# Code Index

## `(root)` — The repository root for SE3 (Software Engineering 3.0), a project-level cross-session framework whose `se3/` Python package provides a Typer CLI flow engine that supervises LLM coding agents via pluggable runners and a persistent state machine, bundled with an optional daemon/FastAPI control-plane server and web frontend, plus a code-first knowledge system (code-index + charter + why-comments), packaging/config manifests, operational scripts, bilingual docs, and a comprehensive test suite. <!--#a9fe0be3ffd98549|07a7c39b2681dbc7-->

### `.gitignore` (text) — Git ignore configuration that takes a whitelist-by-default approach—ignoring everything at the repository root except explicitly un-ignored project files/directories—while also defining global ignore patterns and SE3-specific rules to track committed artifacts but exclude runtime content, scratch files, and local config overrides. <!--#168329740b5bc07f|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `LICENSE` (text) — The full Apache License 2.0 text, granting the project's standard permissive open-source copyright and patent terms. <!--#2f8292753ff1e47a|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `NOTICE` (text) — A project NOTICE file declaring the SE3 software's copyright and authorship by Zhendong Zhang (CRE) for 2026. <!--#91852f8ef9e63e30|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `README.md` (markdown) — The top-level project README introducing SE3 (Software Engineering 3.0) as a project-level, cross-session framework where a CLI engine and persistent state machine supervise an AI coding agent across many sessions and machines, covering its program-as-supervisor philosophy, its code-first knowledge system (code-index + charter + why-comments), installation, quick start, operating modes, full command reference, directory layout, and licensing. <!--#89e2fc6c37c4ca3f|c68bb328c3783ed6-->
- `SE3 — Software Engineering 3.0 Framework` (heading) — Top-level README intro presenting SE3 as a project-level, cross-session CLI flow framework where the program (not the human) supervises an AI coding agent across many sessions and machines until work is complete. <!--#bc60287217a0316c-->
  - `Design Philosophy` (heading) — Parent heading grouping the rationale behind SE3's program-as-supervisor paradigm. <!--#77e6f8f8921f18d9-->
    - `1. A different paradigm: program-as-supervisor, human out-of-the-loop` (heading) — Argues that SE3's unit of work is a multi-session project task supervised by the engine rather than a human-watched single turn, contrasted in a tool-class table. <!--#c9555f96a940c05d-->
    - `2. The real pain: attention is all you need` (heading) — Frames human attention as the true bottleneck and describes the ideal prompt → discover → fire-and-forget → pick-up session that minimizes it. <!--#44bce7dd4e3df92b-->
    - `3. The four moats that make this paradigm work` (heading) — Lists the four capabilities — cross-session state machine, code-first knowledge system, built-in failure recovery, portable substrate — that in-session tools cannot provide. <!--#0904a695288fd8d5-->
    - `se3 vs Claude Code Dynamic Workflows (complementary, not competing)` (heading) — Distinguishes SE3's cross-session governance from Dynamic Workflows' in-session parallelism and explains how the two compose. <!--#3c9f8941e07f7a20-->
  - `The knowledge system: code-index + charter + why-comments` (heading) — Explains how SE3 replaced the old spec-mirror corpus and its sync governance machine with three code-colocated artifacts. <!--#a37585c7f445f66c-->
    - `The three pieces` (heading) — Describes SE3's three code-first knowledge pillars: code-index (a committed, fingerprinted structure map auto-summarized bottom-up), charter (a slimmed high-altitude spec injected in full every step), and why-comments (colocated intent-only comments maintained as a soft prompt convention). <!--#da8e286de1f7c7c7-->
    - `What actually got better (an honest accounting)` (heading) — Honestly accounts for the refactor's real gains — source of truth back in code, eliminated staleness, collapsed governance surface, explicit knobs, higher failure floor. <!--#6791cf42e2126b06-->
    - `A concrete before/after — and why spec-index could never win this` (heading) — Uses the retired spec_index.py to argue code-index wins on navigation because its source of truth is the code, cashing out the coverage-over-depth bet. <!--#c2fda17f39a3a1c0-->
  - `Installation` (heading) — Pip install instructions for the core CLI and the optional server and browser extras. <!--#131c9eece23a2cbf-->
  - `Quick Start` (heading) — A quickstart walkthrough showing the core commands to initialize a project, optionally run discovery, run/resume a full task flow end-to-end, and navigate the codebase via the code-index map. <!--#fc732be510ce6649-->
    - `Three operating modes` (heading) — Describes the --loop worktree mode, the resident daemon, and the central se3-server web console. <!--#c8f7660b10e8560d-->
      - `Web console authentication` (heading) — Outlines the multi-tenant first-run auth flow: break-glass admin token, login, user creation, and daemon-key binding. <!--#04d11c5004095aab-->
  - `Command Reference` (heading) — Parent heading introducing the full CLI command catalog as of the documented version. <!--#572ee8f7044e277a-->
    - `Top-level commands` (heading) — A reference table of SE3's top-level CLI commands (run, init, code-index, migrate, guardrails, merge, merge-respond, salvage) with their purposes and key flags. <!--#25a76810e5ca6a53-->
    - ``se3 history` — flow history` (heading) — Documents the `se3 history` command group for listing, showing, restoring, and filtering past/archived flows. <!--#3e81db08ca44209a-->
    - ``se3 issue` — project issues` (heading) — Documents the `se3 issue` command group for listing, showing, creating, and resetting project issues. <!--#33de25e8833392bc-->
    - ``se3 daemon` — resident control plane` (heading) — Documents the `se3 daemon` command group for starting, stopping, and reporting status of the resident daemon control plane, including optional central-server registration. <!--#a5d50611985cec9b-->
  - `Directory Layout` (heading) — Documents the on-disk project layout under `se3/`, distinguishing git-tracked artifacts (code-index, charter, issues, prompts, version-rules) from gitignored runtime state and logs. <!--#7cf08ea68bc7e931-->
  - `Navigating the codebase` (heading) — Explains how to use the code-index as the primary navigation tool — drilling from the adaptive root map down to file-level symbols — and how it plus the charter are auto-injected into every flow step. <!--#2f772ef9c876139a-->
  - `Version & License` (heading) — States that the version lives in pyproject.toml and is engine-bumped, the Apache-2.0 license, and points to the changelog. <!--#999f2a2712e62082-->

### `README.zh.md` (markdown) — The Chinese-language README for SE3 (Software Engineering 3.0), presenting it as a project-level, cross-session CLI engine + state machine + code-first knowledge system where a program (not a human) supervises AI coding agents, covering its design philosophy, the code-index/charter/why-comments knowledge system, installation, quick-start, run modes, server auth, command reference, directory layout, and versioning/licensing. <!--#e7029b1d8f83632f|fd226a66f0ab7707-->
- `SE3 — Software Engineering 3.0 框架` (heading) — Title/banner section with version, Python, and license badges plus the tagline positioning SE3 above session-level tools as a persistent CLI engine + state machine + code-first knowledge system. <!--#f6025367ed3a8ad0-->

    - `2. 真正的痛点：attention is all you need` (heading) — Argues the real bottleneck is human attention and lays out the ideal fire-and-forget SE3 session (prompt → discover → walk away → collect deliverable). <!--#86c7cbd54fc3ec35-->
    - `3. 撑起这种范式的四件套护城河` (heading) — Lists the four pillars that make program-as-supervisor viable: cross-session state machine, code-first knowledge system, built-in failure recovery, and provider-neutral portability. <!--#3f4f12c0a105cc57-->
    - `se3 vs Claude Code Dynamic Workflows（互补，而非竞争）` (heading) — Distinguishes SE3 (cross-session project governance) from Dynamic Workflows (in-session parallel orchestration) and frames them as composable rather than competing. <!--#b2a83509c7f8e397-->
  - `知识体系：code-index + charter + why-注释` (heading) — Section introducing how the three colocated, code-as-source-of-truth artifacts replaced the old parallel spec corpus and its anti-drift governance machinery. <!--#8ecfda556e767049-->
    - `三件套` (heading) — Describes SE3's three-part orientation system: code-index (the deterministic, version-controlled structure map with embedded fingerprints), charter (high-altitude project conventions injected into every step), and why-comments (colocated intent notes updated only when the why changes). <!--#53526fd8b0fda6e4-->
    - `真正变好了什么（诚实的账）` (heading) — Honest accounting of the refactor's real gains (source-of-truth returns to code, staleness eliminated, governance surface shrinks, explicit knobs, decoupled charter size, higher failure floor) while conceding semantic accuracy is unchanged. <!--#5501353ee7d43418-->
    - `一个具体的前后对照——以及 spec-index 为何永远赢不了这一局` (heading) — Concrete before/after using the retired spec_index.py to argue code-index wins because its source of truth is the code itself, realizing the coverage-over-depth bet. <!--#20a9bcddeb628963-->

  - `快速上手` (heading) — A quick-start walkthrough showing the core CLI flow: `se3 init`, optional `--discover`, end-to-end `se3 run`, `--resume`, and navigating the codebase via `se3 code-index`. <!--#887ed3499a62e78e-->
    - `三种运行形态` (heading) — Describes the three execution modes—--loop (isolated worktree runs), se3 daemon start (resident supervisor), and se3-server (multi-machine central server). <!--#b7f29278060cfa34-->
      - `网页控制台鉴权` (heading) — Explains the central server's multi-tenant auth onboarding flow: bootstrap break-glass admin token, log in, create users, and issue per-owner daemon keys. <!--#dba033d164603542-->
  - `命令清单` (heading) — Heading introducing the command reference tables for version 10.8.1. <!--#09d18905dc6eff15-->

### `VERSIONS.md` (markdown) — The SE3 framework's chronological release-history and changelog document, recording each version's bugfixes and features from the recent 11.2.0 gitignore-hardening release back through major milestones like the 11.0.0 code-index/charter system and 10.0.0 worktree-isolation rewrite. <!--#3ee22dd3f9e9a398|b26afdb831fbab98-->

  - `11.2.0 - 2026-06-30` (heading) — Changelog for release 11.2.0, which hardens gitignore handling by generating root `/*` default-deny plus per-artifact whitelists for new projects, extends `migrate` to apply this default-deny idempotently while re-allowing already-tracked paths, and adds a non-blocking commit-time WARNING when a new top-level path is excluded. <!--#ecc8b082bd3d4f66-->

  - `11.1.0 - 2026-06-29` (heading) — Changelog entry for release 11.1.0 introducing a secondary 'list-fp' fingerprint that limits normal code-index rebuilds to re-summarizing only files/dirs whose direct member name/kind list changed, scopes body-only edits to the edited symbol, preserves full content-fp cascade under --force, and migrates existing indexes lazily at zero LLM cost. <!--#8c7a8c4e38f9bf60-->

### `progress.md` (markdown) — A chronological development log of the SE 3.0 project, recording per-session done/changes/open-issues/next-steps entries that trace the tool's evolution through features like loop branching, collaborative mode, requirement-intake specs, CLI tooling (lint/sync/verify/status), spec cleanup, and tool-enforced progress tracking. <!--#e1332e31ececfbc4|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `pyproject.toml` (text) — Hatchling-based packaging manifest for the `se3` CLI flow-engine package, declaring its core runtime dependencies (typer, pyyaml, rich, psutil, pexpect, etc.), optional `server`/`browser` extras, the `se3` and `se3-server` console scripts, wheel build settings, and pytest configuration. <!--#c3762a0052698019|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `se3.yaml` (yaml) — The project's central se3 configuration file, defining agent registry, LLM caller chain, per-step confirmation/language/version policies, session and human-call escalation settings, workflow fix-loop limits, e2e and critical-test verification, and project-level preset prompts. <!--#86a887377348b8b4|ee539914ac0fcae4-->
- `human_call` (yaml-key) — Configures the human-call escalation channel — where call files live, their language, and how many days before a pending call times out. <!--#e0f1017dd95e7533-->
- `session` (yaml-key) — Session bookkeeping settings naming the progress log file and capping how many progress entries are retained. <!--#c067eb90db8bd1a7-->
- `agents` (yaml-key) — Top-level agent registry mapping logical names (primary/backup/low) to claude-code commands and priorities, resolved by name everywhere else in the config. <!--#2f9b309d4148ee7b-->
- `llm_caller` (yaml-key) — Defines the default agent caller chain plus hard per-step overrides for which agents run the implement and summarize steps. <!--#5e4a39a06783b3ed-->
- `confirmation` (yaml-key) — Per-step review configuration; the presence of a step key enables its confirmation, here enabling LLM review of the plan step with a max-iteration cap. <!--#664dfa6489595c1d-->
- `version` (yaml-key) — Automatic version-bumping settings controlling whether commits bump the version, auto-detect the version file, and embed the version in the commit message. <!--#8864db448db15952-->
- `language` (yaml-key) — Language policy separating the language used for human-facing steps from the language used when writing specs. <!--#fae409e34c1f163b-->
- `e2e` (yaml-key) — Optional end-to-end/visual-regression testing settings for baseline storage, pixel diff threshold, viewport, and URL paths to test. <!--#460af1d4687117b0-->
- `test` (yaml-key) — Registers critical acceptance tests that must genuinely run, so a skipped or missing test marks the verification run as unverified rather than passing. <!--#95f606ea092ea271-->
- `workflow` (yaml-key) — Workflow control settings, here capping the maximum fix-loop iterations as a backstop against runaway fix cycles. <!--#989c560f8df718cd-->
- `presets` (yaml-key) — Declares project-level preset prompts (e.g., doc-sync) that override built-in presets and are runnable via `se3 run --preset`. <!--#8cddb0680aac6aaa-->

## `.claude/` — directory .claude/ <!--#9622d82f73f44a00|ee9fa220890c234d-->

### `.claude/.session.json` (json) — json .claude/.session.json <!--#75a1e2b905ccc3f1|97f010ab8e013eb0-->
- `status` (json-key) — Marks whether the session is currently active. <!--#5768e3a2fd58cd66-->
- `started_at` (json-key) — ISO 8601 timestamp recording when the session began. <!--#6cd43ee6b2d1a12c-->
- `pid` (json-key) — Operating-system process ID of the running session, used to detect whether it is still alive. <!--#6184dd5c70a9c3ce-->

### `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (markdown) — Read-only project guide for the SE3 self-bootstrapping project, explaining that it generates new SE3 specs while being developed with the published (immutable) `.claude/` specs, and documenting the `se3 run` entry point, the `se3/` runtime directory layout, and the optional per-step confirmation/review configuration in `se3.yaml`. <!--#6aef8fe0dc5e296b|24c7dda92181f60f-->
- `SE3 自举项目` (heading) — Document title heading naming the SE3 bootstrapping project. <!--#18e5a852b854462e-->
  - `项目性质` (heading) — Explains the project's nature: it produces new SE3 specs while simultaneously being developed using the existing published SE3 specs. <!--#a108c216d1b6d9f7-->
  - `重要约束` (heading) — States the key constraint that generating new specs must not modify the published, read-only spec files under `.claude/`. <!--#4663a50343327fd5-->
  - `SE3 命令入口` (heading) — Lists SE3's command entry points, notably `se3 run` to start the flow engine. <!--#479eb24aec6d90d6-->
  - `目录结构` (heading) — Describes the runtime directory layout under `se3/` (specs, state, cache, logs, calls, collab) plus `se3.yaml` config and the read-only `.claude/` framework specs. <!--#d3e9ce41d48eaa8c-->
  - `确认步骤配置（可选）` (heading) — Documents the optional per-step confirmation/review model in `se3.yaml`, covering agent registration, llm_caller defaults, and per-step reviewer/max_iterations fields with fail-fast on unregistered agents. <!--#7721b2cce827a2b8-->

## `docs/` — User-facing documentation directory containing English and Chinese reference guides for SE3's optional always-on control plane (the `se3 daemon` and central `se3-server`), covering quickstart, deployment/operations, architecture, multi-tenant authentication, TLS reverse-proxy setup, and the bundled web frontend. <!--#87089fadeadac9f5|4039ef902670e18a-->

### `docs/daemon-and-server.md` (markdown) — Reference documentation for SE3's optional always-on control plane, covering the daemon and central server's quick start, deployment/operations, internal architecture, mandatory multi-tenant authentication, TLS reverse-proxy setup, and bundled web frontend. <!--#c89cb1bb833b73cd|4ed9ae1e6882ff14-->
- `SE3 Daemon & Central Server` (heading) — Top-level intro framing the daemon and central server as an optional always-on control plane layered over the one-shot `se3 run` CLI core. <!--#1fdee38eb50ca15e-->
  - `Table of Contents` (heading) — Navigation index linking to the document's five major sections and their subsections. <!--#5a0492ebebb43e53-->
  - `Quick Start` (heading) — Section heading grouping installation and the basic commands to get the daemon and server running. <!--#629a4900e292c455-->
    - `Installation` (heading) — Explains that the daemon ships with core `se3` while the central server requires the optional `se3[server]` extra for its web dependencies. <!--#26b5cb9fb7ec4589-->
    - `The `se3 daemon` command` (heading) — Documents the `se3 daemon` subcommand group (start/stop/status) with its options and behaviors in a reference table. <!--#6493c17eb101d6ac-->
    - `The `se3-server` command` (heading) — Documents the standalone `se3-server` entry point, its CLI options/defaults, the `bootstrap-token` subcommand, and the mandatory-auth caveat. <!--#b51f88d8f81432c1-->
    - `A typical session` (heading) — End-to-end shell walkthrough of standing up a server, minting tokens/keys, and starting a worker daemon that dials in. <!--#77108cef308c4671-->
  - `Deployment & Operations` (heading) — Section heading grouping the operational topics: connection model, run modes, runtime files, and flow supervision. <!--#7a1eddb2450f7c7a-->
    - `The outbound connection model` (heading) — Describes the daemon-dials-out single-WebSocket design, its NAT-friendliness/resilience benefits, and the scheme-aware default-port handling. <!--#14d0cc53cee04b2a-->
    - `Foreground vs. background (detached) mode` (heading) — Contrasts the default double-fork detached background start with `--foreground`, noting the one-daemon-per-pid-directory rule. <!--#37fb078c285a8f62-->
    - `Runtime files: pidfile and status file` (heading) — Lists the daemon's `~/.se3/` runtime files (pidfile, status JSON, log) and their purposes, noting atomic writes. <!--#bfa213cc1b938792-->
      - `Connection state in `status`` (heading) — Explains the `Connection:` line in `daemon status`, enumerating the local-only / connected / not-connected(reason) states that reveal a silent degrade. <!--#1ea66c3f75c6ea72-->
    - `Flow discovery and supervision` (heading) — Describes how the daemon tracks spawned vs. discovered `se3 run` flows, polls their liveness, and only terminates flows it owns on shutdown. <!--#40d3e10ae65b6483-->
  - `Architecture & How It Works` (heading) — Section heading grouping the internal-design subsections for the daemon, the server, and the end-to-end task-publish path. <!--#37fc459f8df19bd0-->
    - `Inside the daemon` (heading) — Breaks the daemon into its four concurrent asyncio components — supervisor, spawner, aggregator, and outbound client. <!--#a919f7a36e4921ac-->
    - `Inside the central server` (heading) — Describes the FastAPI server's WebSocket pool, in-memory `ServerState`, sqlite identity persistence, REST API, and bundled frontend. <!--#04199faf5e8f8615-->
    - `End-to-end: publishing a task from a remote machine` (heading) — Traces the full task-publish flow from browser/API through the server's `SPAWN_FLOW` instruction to a real `se3 run` child, plus the mirror-image respond path. <!--#ff4c85b228691221-->
  - `Authentication & Multi-Tenant Access` (heading) — Section intro establishing the server as a multi-tenant control plane where every request and daemon must resolve to an owner, with a setup-motion overview. <!--#cb022cc70dbc930b-->
    - `Why authentication is mandatory` (heading) — Explains the fail-closed auth model: the configurable provider chain, `AuthNotConfigured` startup refusal, and HTTP 401 for ownerless requests. <!--#782723d85b178b36-->
    - `The persistence layer (`~/.se3/server.db`)` (heading) — Details the embedded sqlite store and the identity-only facts it persists (owners, bindings, password hashes, daemon-key/break-glass hashes), excluding live state. <!--#49cbf78253e40d42-->
    - `Bootstrapping the first admin (`bootstrap-token`)` (heading) — Describes the re-runnable one-time break-glass admin token as the IdP-independent first entrance into a fresh server. <!--#0dd5fe92e8fe2c99-->
    - `Logging in and creating users` (heading) — Documents the human login ceremony (login/logout/me endpoints) and admin-only user creation, noting no public self-registration in v1. <!--#49803a3994826103-->
    - `Issuing daemon keys and binding machines` (heading) — Explains owner-self-serviced daemon keys, the HELLO handshake that binds a machine to an owner, and WELCOME accept/reject behavior. <!--#f1fd2ca28ef64806-->
    - `Deploying behind a TLS reverse proxy (wss)` (heading) — Explains that `se3-server` speaks plaintext and needs a reverse proxy to terminate TLS and forward both static HTTP and upgraded WebSocket traffic. <!--#1b1d14307a1a3895-->
      - `nginx` (heading) — Provides a concrete nginx reverse-proxy config for WebSocket upgrade (the `map`, HTTP/1.1, long read timeout) with common-pitfall notes. <!--#375efbcea68f4501-->
      - `Caddy` (heading) — Provides the minimal Caddy reverse-proxy config that handles TLS and WebSocket upgrades automatically, plus an optional idle-timeout variant. <!--#adf7a3bf3e207711-->
      - `Verifying the proxy: a `curl --http1.1` handshake probe` (heading) — Shows how to confirm the proxy upgrades a WebSocket end-to-end via a raw `curl` handshake, interpreting the `101` and expected-404 results. <!--#da3245a99a200a4c-->
    - `Owner isolation` (heading) — Describes how both the UI/REST channel and the daemon `/ws` channel are owner-scoped, with cross-owner targets reading as 404 and additive provider linking. <!--#b7529003bf01a4e6-->
  - `The Web Frontend` (heading) — Documents the bundled build-step-free static frontend: login requirement, the `/ws/ui` real-time push channel, and watch/publish/respond capabilities. <!--#893626419c1e6172-->

### `docs/daemon-and-server.zh.md` (markdown) — Chinese-language guide to SE3's optional resident control plane — the `se3 daemon` and `se3-server` — covering quickstart, deployment/operations, daemon and server architecture, mandatory owner-scoped auth and multi-tenancy, TLS reverse-proxy setup, and the bundled web frontend. <!--#ee3ec771277db2d9|9d439bcd17c0dfa0-->
- `SE3 Daemon 与中心服务器` (heading) — Top-level intro framing the daemon and central server as an optional resident control plane layered over the one-shot `se3 run` CLI, both fully optional. <!--#0f154ef35de08826-->
  - `目录` (heading) — Table of contents linking the document's five main sections and their subsections. <!--#614e34e6136a3d7e-->
  - `快速上手` (heading) — Quickstart section header grouping installation, the two commands, and a typical session walkthrough. <!--#d6e457a6857ef50f-->
    - `安装` (heading) — Installation guidance distinguishing the core `pip install se3` (includes daemon) from the heavier `se3[server]` extra needed for the central server and the daemon's outbound WebSocket client. <!--#ee853d60c909a471-->
    - ``se3 daemon` 命令` (heading) — Reference for the `se3 daemon` subcommand group (start/stop/status) with a table of options and behaviors including server-url, daemon-key, and foreground flags. <!--#58276cecdf617578-->

    - `一次典型会话` (heading) — End-to-end shell walkthrough of a typical session: start server, mint a bootstrap token, start a daemon with a key on a worker machine, then observe and dispatch via the browser. <!--#f9a790bc7f65f509-->

    - `出站连接模型` (heading) — Explains the daemon-dials-out-to-server WebSocket model (NAT-friendly, exponential-backoff reconnect) and the scheme-based default port completion for `--server-url`. <!--#c7f0a060e99f2661-->
    - `前台模式 vs 后台(detached)模式` (heading) — Contrasts the default detached background mode (double-fork) with foreground (`--foreground`) mode and notes one daemon per pid directory. <!--#d94c3ae4b745efd5-->
    - `运行时文件:pidfile 与状态文件` (heading) — Describes the daemon's runtime files under `~/.se3/` (daemon.pid, daemon_status.json, daemon.log), their purposes, and atomic-write guarantees. <!--#024f486afbbfe54e-->
      - ``status` 中的连接状态` (heading) — Details how `daemon_status.json` records the real outbound connection result and how `se3 daemon status` renders it on a `Connection:` line with human-readable failure reasons. <!--#ccd0e402cb454fc5-->
    - `流程的发现与监管` (heading) — Explains how the daemon tracks both spawned and discovered `se3 run` processes, polls liveness via flow_id, and only terminates processes it owns. <!--#464fa507d4267135-->
  - `架构与工作原理` (heading) — Architecture section header covering daemon internals, server internals, and the end-to-end task-publishing flow. <!--#f9184f4e8ec18234-->
    - `daemon 内部` (heading) — Describes the daemon's four asyncio components — Supervisor, Spawner, Aggregator, and optional outbound Client — running as concurrent tasks on one event loop. <!--#7165790ef0bb7533-->
    - `中心服务器内部` (heading) — Describes `se3-server` as a FastAPI app that accepts daemon WebSockets at `/ws`, holds an in-memory ServerState aggregate, persists only identity facts to sqlite, and exposes owner-filtered REST APIs. <!--#836c73f22b67eb29-->
    - `端到端:从远端机器发布任务` (heading) — Traces the full chain of publishing a task from the frontend through SPAWN_FLOW to a remote daemon's spawner, plus the mirror path for responding to a call via RESPOND_CALL. <!--#d17668f6e26dbd99-->
  - `鉴权与多租户访问` (heading) — Auth/multi-tenancy section header explaining that since 8.0.0 every request and daemon connection must resolve to an owner, with a setup-flow overview. <!--#99d34537d967189c-->
    - `为什么鉴权是强制的` (heading) — Explains the fail-closed auth model: the server refuses to serve without an available provider (default `local`), throwing AuthNotConfigured at startup and returning HTTP 401 for unresolvable requests. <!--#1fe9f0fb37aa236f-->
    - `持久化层(`~/.se3/server.db`)` (heading) — Describes the embedded single-file sqlite store that persists only identity facts daemon reconnects cannot rebuild (owners, identity bindings, password hashes, daemon-key hashes, break-glass token hashes). <!--#9e5df781761f011c-->
    - `引导首个管理员(`bootstrap-token`)` (heading) — Explains the `se3-server bootstrap-token` command that mints a one-time break-glass admin token (printed once, only its hash stored) as the sole entry point into a fresh server. <!--#f7e57b0100d13f20-->
    - `登录并创建用户` (heading) — Describes the human/UI login flow through the provider chain (login/logout/me endpoints) and admin-only user creation, with no v1 public self-registration. <!--#0acb5b9085ab94d8-->
    - `签发 daemon key 并绑定机器` (heading) — Explains owner-managed daemon keys (mint/list/revoke endpoints), how the daemon presents a key in its HELLO to bind its machine to an owner, and TLS-backed reverse trust. <!--#320850b65c0724a3-->
    - `在 TLS 反向代理后部署(wss)` (heading) — Explains deploying behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy that forwards both static HTTP and WebSocket-upgrade traffic to se3-server's plaintext port via a single `location /`. <!--#c347ebb9feac1faa-->
      - `nginx` (heading) — Provides an annotated nginx config for the reverse proxy, with the `map`-derived Connection header, HTTP/1.1 upgrade, and relaxed read timeouts, plus common pitfalls. <!--#25b2ebd1dc6a95e8-->
      - `Caddy` (heading) — Provides a minimal Caddy config that auto-terminates TLS and transparently proxies WebSockets, with an optional relaxed idle-timeout variant. <!--#a0782c4e347cc06a-->
      - `验证代理:`curl --http1.1` 握手探测` (heading) — Shows how to verify the proxy passes a WebSocket upgrade through to the backend using a raw `curl --http1.1` handshake, with notes on interpreting 101/404 responses. <!--#a88ae4515b8cde06-->
    - `owner 隔离` (heading) — Explains how both channels are owner-scoped — frontend/`/api/*` filtered by owner (cross-owner reads as 404) and daemon `/ws` bound via HELLO key — and how adding a second auth provider is purely additive. <!--#6afda22934aebcb0-->
  - `网页前端` (heading) — Describes se3-server's bundled static web frontend, its mandatory login, the owner-scoped `/ws/ui` WebSocket for live updates, and its capabilities (view progress, publish tasks, respond to calls). <!--#f8667f2c3fe5824d-->

## `scripts/` — A directory of standalone operational scripts: one Bash helper that installs Chromium's shared libraries into a userspace dir so headless-browser tests can run without root, and one Python one-time migration that converts se3/specs/_backlog markdown files into typed Issues via IssueManager. <!--#ce04bf92d4426bf6|a8cca7e2c098a155-->

### `scripts/install_browser_test_libs.sh` (text) — A userspace-fallback Bash script that, without root, downloads and extracts the Debian/Ubuntu shared libraries Chromium needs into a gitignored `.browser-libs/lib` directory so the headless-browser Playwright acceptance test can run via LD_LIBRARY_PATH. <!--#fe72f339a1f471d9|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `scripts/migrate_backlog.py` (python) — A one-time migration script that converts each markdown file in se3/specs/_backlog into a typed Issue (parsing title, phase-inferred type, and description) via IssueManager, deletes the source file, and prints a migration report. <!--#a0845babfc6d9712|760a7a4bef36feb3-->
- `_extract_title` (function) — Returns the first markdown '# ' heading as the issue title, or 'Untitled' if none is found. <!--#5831f459c0a33fa4-->
- `_extract_phase` (function) — Finds and returns the markdown line containing both 'status' and 'backlog' to capture the phase/status info. <!--#5713b308209b36b0-->
- `_infer_type` (function) — Maps a phase/status line to an issue type (phase 1→task, phase 2/3→feature, phase 4/future→idea, default feature). <!--#c7e5b6978408cc9f-->
- `_extract_description` (function) — Collects body text under the Idea/Goal/Motivation section as the issue description, falling back to a default string. <!--#a6e466f1c2d9273a-->
- `migrate` (function) — Main entry point that iterates backlog markdown files, creates a tagged issue for each, deletes the source file, and prints a migration report. <!--#ce12a1e953eb33a1-->

## `src/` — The project's source root, containing the single `se3/` package that implements the entire SE 3.0 framework — a Typer CLI driving an LLM-backed flow engine via pluggable agent runners, project scaffolding, and an optional daemon/FastAPI server bridging local flow state to a control plane. <!--#51aad90b2fb4298b|5f64bb0e9d734a3d-->

## `src/se3/` — The root package of the SE 3.0 framework: a Typer-based CLI (cli.py + commands/) that drives an LLM-backed flow engine through pluggable agent runners (Claude one-shot/interactive, Codex) selected via a layered config and preset-prompt system, scaffolds projects from bundled templates, and is paired with an optional resident daemon and standalone FastAPI server (with web console) that bridge local flow state to a multi-tenant control plane, all atop shared core/utils helpers. <!--#43510a49588f653a|d527c3124a744507-->

### `src/se3/__init__.py` (python) — Package initializer for the se3 package that resolves the package version from installed metadata or pyproject.toml, defaulting to 'unknown' on failure. <!--#9ea621a32fa204c4|52ccc8955ede7d6c-->
- `_get_version` (function) — Helper that determines the package version, preferring installed package metadata and falling back to parsing the `version` field from pyproject.toml, returning 'unknown' if all attempts fail. <!--#ac46b5e4fb58631f-->

### `src/se3/__main__.py` (python) — Package entry point enabling `python -m se3` to launch the CLI app, used as a fallback by the daemon's spawner when the `se3` console script isn't on PATH. <!--#d004d4b47395e15f|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/agent_runner.py` (python) — Defines the abstract AgentRunner base class plus its supporting InfraErrorType enum and RunResult dataclass, establishing the unified contract (synchronous run, monitored run, CLI arg-building, and infrastructure-error detection) that LLMCaller uses to drive any concrete agent runner implementation. <!--#1a75f0c5408d89aa|2d4ad19e73310e39-->
- `InfraErrorType` (class) — Enum classifying infrastructure-level failures (usage limit, timeout, hang, startup failure) that warrant rotating to a different agent. <!--#b4559b2f7002857f-->
- `RunResult` (class) — Dataclass bundling a runner execution's exit code, stdout, stderr, and detected infrastructure-error type. <!--#d425154633ceb3f4-->
- `AgentRunner` (class) — Abstract base class specifying the contract (run, monitored run, arg-building, infra-error detection) that LLMCaller uses to drive any concrete agent runner. <!--#2f605128c1a1406c-->
  - `AgentRunner.run` (method) — Abstract method to run the agent synchronously with optional timeout/cwd/env and a retry callback, returning a CompletedProcess. <!--#36ae2f398d60a19e-->
  - `AgentRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Abstract method to run the agent under wall/inactivity timeouts with output and activity callbacks, returning a monitored result. <!--#b42f4e02affb6ec5-->
  - `AgentRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Abstract method translating caller intent (prompt, read-only flag, context files, spec-guard settings) into agent-specific CLI arguments. <!--#d40b10d9780ce4a7-->
  - `AgentRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Abstract method that inspects a run's exit code and output to classify whether an infrastructure error occurred. <!--#9da392a3d03fdbc7-->

### `src/se3/claude_interactive_runner.py` (python) — Implements the interactive PTY-based AgentRunner adapter that spawns and drives the Claude Code TUI, watching its session transcript JSONL to stream stream-json NDJSON records, accumulate token usage, and detect turn-end/inactivity signals (with a degraded content-tracking fallback when no transcript is available). <!--#ddd47eb78061d0d0|344f409d8cb91096-->
- `_import_pexpect` (function) — Lazily imports the optional pexpect dependency, raising a friendly install hint if it is missing, so the module loads without pexpect installed. <!--#95b977a55b4eb9b4-->
- `_safe_isalive` (function) — Returns whether the PTY child handle is still running, swallowing errors from a dead/reaped handle. <!--#98bcb81ff0b06817-->
- `_ActivityClock` (class) — Thread-safe last-activity timestamp bumped by the drain thread and read by the supervisor to drive inactivity timeouts. <!--#e8dd8801beac4cb5-->
  - `_ActivityClock.__init__` (method) — Initializes the clock to the current time with a lock for thread-safe access. <!--#34f4d6294c29498a-->
  - `_ActivityClock.update` (method) — Sets the stored timestamp to now under the lock (called on each activity tick). <!--#e2f01023ef425bb5-->
  - `_ActivityClock.last` (method) — Returns the last-recorded activity timestamp under the lock. <!--#fc964925b709c931-->
- `_normalize_pty_lines` (function) — Strips ANSI/TUI noise and collapses volatile digits and whitespace so cosmetic spinner/footer re-renders normalize to identical strings while real streamed text stays distinct. <!--#f917aa24c44496b4-->
- `_MeaningfulContentTracker` (class) — Degraded-mode progress detector that, when no transcript JSONL is available, advances an activity clock only on genuinely new PTY content so cosmetic TUI re-renders cannot keep the inactivity timer alive forever. <!--#c7186a35fb511d1e-->
  - `_MeaningfulContentTracker.__init__` (method) — Initializes the tracker's clock, chunk cursor, residual buffer, and bounded seen-line set. <!--#65310c3c1a5b2386-->
  - `_MeaningfulContentTracker.scan` (method) — Consumes newly-appended PTY chunks, holding back partial lines, and bumps the clock only when a normalized line hasn't been seen before. <!--#c5a7dc16b28cd47c-->
- `munge_cwd` (function) — Reproduces Claude Code's cwd→projects-subdir-name munging (replacing non-alphanumeric chars with dashes) to derive the per-project transcript directory. <!--#06a85a49aa34fe85-->
- `claude_projects_dir` (function) — Returns the ~/.claude/projects transcript directory, honoring the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR override. <!--#2e8a3a47b034eaf4-->
- `_safe_mtime` (function) — Returns a path's modification time, or 0.0 if it cannot be stat-ed. <!--#f2c9d08de602063a-->
- `snapshot_session_files` (function) — Best-effort recursive snapshot of all *.jsonl transcript files under the projects tree, used for the pre/post-launch diff. <!--#b3cc6a37d00c01eb-->
- `_file_cwd_matches` (function) — Second-pass check that reads a candidate transcript's leading records to confirm/deny its cwd field matches the target, distinguishing concurrent-flow files. <!--#058ab205a169f36b-->
- `locate_session_file` (function) — Locates this launch's transcript file, binding deterministically to the explicit session-id filename when given, else diffing against the pre-launch snapshot with cwd-match isolation. <!--#8ad402673acf6dbd-->
- `tail_new_records` (function) — Incrementally reads complete JSON records appended past a byte cursor (leaving partial lines unconsumed, resetting on truncation) and returns them with the advanced cursor. <!--#9b6d210df49bb20b-->
- `to_stream_json_ndjson` (function) — Converts one JSONL transcript record into the stream-json NDJSON shape upstream consumers expect, filtering by type and dropping sidechain/non-meaningful records. <!--#a9cebac1c0ff43a0-->
- `extract_usage_from_record` (function) — Reads the four token-count fields from a record's nested or top-level usage payload, defaulting to zeros on any parsing surprise. <!--#d372c353fba00548-->
- `synthesize_result_line` (function) — Builds a terminal stream-json type:"result" line from accumulated usage so interactive-mode tokens flow through the existing usage-accounting chain. <!--#bc3e6e4b7b2cf681-->
- `_is_terminal_record` (function) — Decides whether a record marks turn-end (a result line or an assistant message with a terminal stop_reason), excluding tool_use/tool_result. <!--#f9e8edfb9ee3de7a-->
- `turn_complete` (function) — Single-turn completion check combining a terminal last JSONL record with the transcript having gone idle, deliberately ignoring PTY idleness. <!--#ffa31ba5172c2976-->
- `SessionTranscriptWatcher` (class) — Stateful watcher that snapshots, locates, and incrementally tails one session transcript JSONL, producing stream-json NDJSON, accumulating usage, and exposing write-activity for the turn-end/inactivity signals. <!--#e8241b7e9aff8b46-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.__init__` (method) — Initializes the watcher's cwd, projects dir, session id, file path, cursor, snapshot, record state, and usage accumulator. <!--#10cfb0fd9b41a77d-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.snapshot` (method) — Captures the pre-launch *.jsonl file set (called before spawning the PTY). <!--#a0b057e7f237a0b9-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.locate` (method) — Attempts to locate this launch's transcript file, idempotently caching it once found. <!--#211931ea8b3151e9-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.poll` (method) — Reads new records, advancing the cursor and state, accumulating usage, emitting a leading init line on first model sighting, and returns their stream-json NDJSON lines. <!--#4813007e9cc6466a-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.usage` (method) — Property returning a copy of the token counts accumulated across all assistant messages seen. <!--#670ae7e99550c5a2-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.write_activity` (method) — Returns the best timestamp of the last JSONL write (file mtime, falling back to last record-yielding poll) driving inactivity and turn-idle signals. <!--#a0974012f0252f9d-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.synthesize_result` (method) — Mints the terminal result line from the watcher's accumulated usage. <!--#6dde706e00fdf4ac-->
- `ClaudeInteractiveRunner` (class) — The AgentRunner subclass implementing the interactive PTY adapter: translates call intent into TUI flags, spawns/feeds/drains the PTY, supervises the lifecycle, and classifies infra errors. <!--#d47ccc7a037ac82e-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the runner with a single Claude command, setting-sources config, project root, and per-launch prompt/session-id slots. <!--#385aa73c8852e7ff-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Translates call intent into interactive-mode CLI flags (read-only disallowedTools, context-file --add-dir), stashing the prompt for later PTY feeding rather than placing it in argv. <!--#d3241cf3fe2dabdc-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._build_full_cmd` (method) — Composes the launch argv, injecting --dangerously-skip-permissions, --setting-sources, and the explicit --session-id prefix flags. <!--#ca23609984994b62-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._spawn_pty` (method) — Spawns the interactive claude inside a PTY as a session/process-group leader (via pexpect) so the whole group can later be killed. <!--#4b8a493ca1c400c9-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._feed_prompt` (method) — Background-thread feeder that waits for input-box readiness, then delivers the full multi-line prompt as one bracketed paste followed by an Enter to dispatch the turn. <!--#215fc9a01efb85f5-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._await_input_ready` (method) — Blocks until the PTY has rendered output and gone quiet for the settle window (input box ready) or the readiness timeout elapses. <!--#dec5ee493e266727-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._write_text` (method) — Writes text to the PTY master via a byte-level full-delivery loop on the child fd, falling back to handle.send for test stubs. <!--#f41046c33dca8162-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._write_all_bytes` (method) — Writes every byte of a payload to a fd, retrying the unwritten remainder in chunks with tiny pauses to avoid truncation/overrun. <!--#c7fde4aa2a021e36-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._drain_pty` (method) — Background-thread reader that continuously drains PTY output, bumping activity clocks, buffering, logging, and firing output/activity callbacks until EOF or stop. <!--#d16fff172457c9fa-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._terminate` (method) — Force-terminates the PTY child's whole process group (SIGTERM, grace, SIGKILL) and reaps it via pexpect close, best-effort on every step. <!--#fe6d7710e2b42015-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner.run` (method) — Runs one interactive turn synchronously via the shared monitored path and returns a CompletedProcess carrying the stream-json NDJSON output. <!--#a1823559b550eee5-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Launches interactive claude in a PTY and supervises its full lifecycle (wall/inactivity timeouts, force-kill, reclamation), returning a MonitoredResult with the captured output. <!--#5e0acfb93bb5b043-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._make_watcher` (method) — Constructs the SessionTranscriptWatcher for the run, returning None (degraded PTY-only mode) when cwd is unknown; overridable in tests. <!--#0915cd3f68f49c15-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._run_single_with_monitor` (method) — Core method that spawns the PTY, runs feed/drain threads and the composite PTY+JSONL supervisor loop until turn-complete or a timeout, and guarantees teardown/reclamation in a finally block. <!--#192e1a8f30049e77-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._compose_output` (method) — Selects the output payload, preferring captured stream-json NDJSON and falling back to raw PTY capture when none was produced. <!--#a7dc47d241852098-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._compose_output_with_limit_marker` (method) — Composes the output and appends a usage-limit marker after scanning the raw PTY buffer, so the keyword survives for downstream USAGE_LIMIT classification on timeout paths. <!--#2189ff68cdfcada1-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._exit_code` (method) — Derives a best-effort exit code from a finished pexpect handle (exit status, 128+signal, or 0/1 fallback). <!--#46e170d535bbd994-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._detect_usage_limit` (method) — Scans the output tail for usage/rate-limit keywords on failed runs only. <!--#b846f24a2be97871-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._detect_startup_failure` (method) — Detects whether the output carries a PTY-spawn or never-created-transcript startup-failure marker. <!--#a5d76a6d9e6a9a4e-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Classifies infrastructure errors (USAGE_LIMIT, TIMEOUT, STARTUP_FAILURE, or NONE) for LLMCaller agent rotation, drawing on PTY output and JSONL transcript state. <!--#0c761ec5e68d6538-->
- `MonitoredResult` (class) — Dataclass result of run_with_monitor carrying the return code, output, command metadata, and interrupted/success state. <!--#b12f4f609b402674-->
  - `MonitoredResult.success` (method) — Property reporting whether the return code is zero. <!--#787b46b245897e2b-->
- `_SingleRunResult` (class) — Internal dataclass result of a single monitored PTY run (return code, output, success, should_retry, interrupted). <!--#7fd76b6e9948c7f4-->

### `src/se3/claude_runner.py` (python) — An AgentRunner implementation that executes a single Claude CLI command via subprocess, providing both a synchronous run path and a monitored run path with activity-based stuck/timeout detection, large-prompt-to-stdin rewriting, confirmation-prompt answering, and infra-error (usage-limit/timeout) detection for retry logic. <!--#a6f8225952eaa565|8abf5e983b2a7a07-->
- `_spawn_stdin_writer` (function) — Module helper that writes a large prompt payload to the child's stdin from a daemon thread (then closes it) to avoid pipe-buffer deadlock on the large-prompt path. <!--#19dde2ba6f7be9f0-->
- `_spawn_stderr_reader` (function) — Module helper that drains the child's stderr in a daemon thread, optionally logging to a file and echoing to the parent's stderr, keeping stdout NDJSON clean. <!--#8e701338eb2971f4-->
- `detect_confirmation_prompt` (function) — Module function that conservatively detects an interactive CLI confirmation prompt in a line of child output, returning the prompt text and any inline numeric option labels (or None). <!--#5c28f457ef473dae-->
- `_write_stdin_response` (function) — Module helper that writes a confirmation answer (newline-terminated) back to the child's stdin, swallowing failures so undeliverable answers degrade to a no-op. <!--#a2717e89116de7e9-->
- `ClaudeCodeRunner` (class) — AgentRunner subclass that wraps and executes one specific Claude CLI command (no list traversal or fallback), injecting permission/setting-source flags. <!--#334b3a774d4cc996-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the runner from a single command (with legacy `commands` support) and resolves the Claude CLI setting-sources list from explicit args or project config. <!--#b59445d42c87ca93-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner._resolve_args` (method) — Static method that rewrites oversized `-p`/`--prompt` argv values to stdin (preserving `@file` references) to avoid execve E2BIG limits. <!--#181b40b864d27e84-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.run` (method) — Runs Claude synchronously via subprocess.run for a single command, assembling the full argv, feeding any stdin prompt, and returning a CompletedProcess (124 on timeout). <!--#4f8bee1df17dbf47-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.get_command` (method) — Returns the command string at the given index in the backward-compatibility commands list (clamping to the last entry). <!--#55afbbe111e290a0-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.get_next_command` (method) — Returns the command following a given one in the commands list, or None if it is last or not found. <!--#0f38633a0bb6a7c2-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Builds the Claude CLI argument list from intent-level parameters (prompt, read-only tool restrictions, spec-guard settings, context files). <!--#ce2be31b0dd81519-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.detect_usage_limit` (method) — Static method that inspects the tail of failed-command output for known usage/rate-limit keywords to detect quota exhaustion. <!--#f864b51cf98d6564-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.detect_timeout` (method) — Static method that reports whether a return code (124) indicates a timeout failure. <!--#3e76609d6d367ce6-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Combines usage-limit and timeout detection into a single InfraErrorType verdict for LLMCaller's retry logic. <!--#b63bfc06170b32ad-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Runs Claude with real-time activity-based monitoring (stuck/hang detection, logging, output and confirmation callbacks) and returns a MonitoredResult. <!--#c345b548e48f0a50-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner._run_single_with_monitor` (method) — Internal worker that spawns the child via Popen and runs the monitoring loop — handling stdin feeding, stderr draining, wall/inactivity timeouts, and confirmation-prompt answering. <!--#f6f5b52ec49fdef8-->
- `MonitoredResult` (class) — Dataclass holding the outcome of run_with_monitor (return code, output, command used, retry/interrupt flags) with a `success` property. <!--#c1d4bf7467c22e70-->
  - `MonitoredResult.success` (method) — Property returning True when the monitored run's return code is zero. <!--#787b46b245897e2b-->
- `_SingleRunResult` (class) — Internal dataclass capturing the result of a single monitored command run (return code, output, success, should-retry, interrupted). <!--#3382b4f182bfe583-->

### `src/se3/cli.py` (python) — The Typer-based CLI entry point for se3, defining all top-level commands — run, init, guardrails, daemon (start/stop/status), merge family, salvage, and end-session — plus display/input helpers. <!--#e4902789fb2cf00c|5b9ccdf6646ee539-->
- `_version_callback` (function) — Eager `--version` flag callback that prints the se3 version and exits. <!--#61477e86dd0c60ea-->
- `main` (function) — Root Typer callback that initializes the display console and shows help when no subcommand is invoked. <!--#7d477aaadb07298b-->
- `_init_display` (function) — Initializes the global Rich console for consistent CLI output. <!--#bc1892294d2bdfda-->
- `_read_multiline_input` (function) — Reads multiline user input (interactive prompt_toolkit session or piped stdin) with proper Unicode handling and cancel/accept semantics. <!--#498e1f327fad2edb-->
- `run_cmd` (function) — The `se3 run` command — the unified flow-engine entry point handling task/resume/discovery/preset/from-issue/worktree modes and output-sink selection. <!--#85b5bab960f65743-->
- `init_cmd` (function) — The `se3 init` command that scaffolds a new SE3 project's standard directory structure and config. <!--#becd33a815f4e4ac-->
- `_run_spec_size_guardrails` (function) — Helper that runs project-wide spec size-governance checks and exits warn (0) or enforce (1) per the configured tier. <!--#5de7bd67e20a8955-->
- `guardrails_cmd` (function) — The `se3 guardrails` command that checks a spec file for weakening/deletion diff violations plus size-governance violations. <!--#2788715339155eca-->
- `_project_root_for_spec` (function) — Helper that walks up from a spec file to locate the owning SE3 project root for size governance. <!--#40c3c36bb5ef4490-->
- `_precheck_websockets` (function) — Warns on the CLI front-end when the optional `websockets` dependency is missing and the daemon would fall back to local-only mode. <!--#e39a9a6afc9501e1-->
- `_report_connection_result` (function) — Polls the daemon status file after a detached start to report the real central-server connection outcome, handling staleness and transient errors. <!--#a957641890a8ac7a-->
- `daemon_start_cmd` (function) — The `se3 daemon start` command that launches the daemon (detached or foreground) with server URL/key config and reports connection status. <!--#e51a816a5efaa32f-->
- `daemon_stop_cmd` (function) — The `se3 daemon stop` command that stops the running daemon and reports the outcome. <!--#b7a28c61b0dd75fd-->
- `daemon_status_cmd` (function) — The `se3 daemon status` command that reports the daemon's running state, server connection, and tracked flows (text or JSON). <!--#8c710c27a529974b-->
- `merge_cmd` (function) — The `se3 merge` command that sequentially merges branches into the current branch with a chosen conflict strategy and applied SemVer bumps. <!--#1badf301cad37235-->
- `merge_respond_cmd` (function) — The `se3 merge-respond` command that processes an MCP call response file to execute merge-conflict resolution decisions. <!--#2fd36eaa5b353e65-->
- `merge_unlock_cmd` (function) — The `se3 merge-unlock` command that inspects and releases the project's merge lock, cleaning up stale locks or force-releasing live ones. <!--#7498497616a5d7be-->
- `salvage_cmd` (function) — The `se3 salvage` command that performs best-effort recovery (commit changes, create issues, archive) from an abnormally terminated session. <!--#59b4b4c953d461fe-->
- `end_session_cmd` (function) — The `se3 end-session` command that terminates a live run process and archives the session without merging uncommitted work. <!--#14e623e821083b59-->

### `src/se3/codex_runner.py` (python) — Codex CLI adapter that wraps a single `codex exec --json` command as an AgentRunner, converting codex's JSONL events into Claude-compatible stream-json NDJSON and running it synchronously or with activity-based monitoring, timeout enforcement, and infrastructure-error classification. <!--#3b2f7c5b4390a07d|90b98d81ec878b0d-->
- `_detect_shell_snapshot_failure` (function) — Module-level helper that returns True if the given stderr text contains any known shell-snapshot validation failure pattern. <!--#285b07575c27a81d-->
- `CodexEventConverter` (class) — Stateful converter that turns codex `--json` JSONL events into zero or more Claude stream-json NDJSON lines over the lifetime of one codex invocation, never raising. <!--#ebdd6c4cac5d6f89-->
  - `CodexEventConverter.__init__` (method) — Initializes the converter's internal state: accumulated agent messages, terminal-seen flag, tool-id counter, and touched-files set. <!--#23192a4eaaf62e01-->
  - `CodexEventConverter.touched_files` (method) — Property exposing the set of file paths collected from `file_change` items for dependency tracking. <!--#21dde3ceae6fa2d8-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._next_tool_id` (method) — Generates a unique synthetic tool-use id (`codex_tool_N`) when an event lacks its own call id. <!--#abc4b1e4bae8e685-->
  - `CodexEventConverter.convert_line` (method) — Parses one codex JSONL line and dispatches by event type to the appropriate handler, returning the resulting NDJSON lines. <!--#f5413ff755d808ce-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._handle_item_event` (method) — Converts `item.updated`/`item.completed` events (agent_message, command_execution, file_change, mcp_tool_call) into Claude tool_use/tool_result/assistant NDJSON events. <!--#6a72f173946f2fae-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._map_tool_name` (method) — Maps codex's generic tool/function names (shell, apply_patch, etc.) to the closest Claude tool names for display. <!--#24273fa0354b0a63-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._handle_turn_completed` (method) — Handles `turn.completed` by emitting a Claude `type: result` event built from accumulated agent messages, extracted usage, and cost. <!--#ae84f50b3fd4238f-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._handle_turn_failed` (method) — Handles `turn.failed`/`error` by emitting an error `type: result` event with the extracted error message and usage. <!--#5a23f07f8c5e81ff-->
  - `CodexEventConverter.finalize` (method) — Emits a synthesized terminal `result` event after the process exits if no `turn.completed`/`turn.failed` was ever seen. <!--#0a250218c729af5c-->
- `_spawn_stdin_writer` (function) — Launches a daemon thread that writes a prompt payload to the subprocess stdin and closes it, avoiding pipe-buffer deadlock. <!--#136c5b7ec66b9827-->
- `_spawn_stderr_reader` (function) — Launches a daemon thread that drains the subprocess stderr, optionally logging to a sidecar file and capturing the tail into a bounded buffer. <!--#af4e0e85a2eb715f-->
- `CodexRunner` (class) — AgentRunner subclass implementing the codex CLI adapter, with methods to build CLI args, run synchronously, run with activity monitoring, and classify infrastructure errors. <!--#f120b03d78ce2564-->
  - `CodexRunner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the runner with a single command dict, defaulting to `{cmd: codex, priority: 0}`. <!--#c5b52427c53670a9-->
  - `CodexRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Builds the `codex exec --json` argv from intent-level parameters, handling sandbox mode, inlined context files, and stdin-routing for oversized prompts. <!--#416201dbd82bdb1b-->
  - `CodexRunner.run` (method) — Runs codex synchronously to completion and returns a CompletedProcess whose stdout is codex output converted to Claude NDJSON. <!--#a659dadfbc8ababd-->
  - `CodexRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Runs codex with activity-based monitoring, streaming converted NDJSON to buffer/log/callbacks and returning a MonitoredResult. <!--#a4ed41c0d1b0f6de-->
  - `CodexRunner._run_single_with_monitor` (method) — Core monitoring loop that spawns the codex process, streams and converts stdout, drains stderr, and enforces wall/inactivity (hang) timeouts. <!--#549f31a7c3cfe1be-->
  - `CodexRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Classifies a codex run's exit code and output tail into an InfraErrorType (timeout, usage/auth limit, shell-snapshot startup failure, or none). <!--#d00ad55f4e702f64-->
- `MonitoredResult` (class) — Dataclass holding the outcome of `run_with_monitor` (return code, output, command, retry/interrupt flags, stderr tail) with a `success` property. <!--#6ac9ba61952cbdea-->
  - `MonitoredResult.success` (method) — Property returning True when the return code is zero. <!--#787b46b245897e2b-->
- `_SingleRunResult` (class) — Internal dataclass capturing the result of a single monitored command run (return code, output, success, retry/interrupt flags, stderr tail). <!--#25c02f14463c799c-->

### `src/se3/config.py` (python) — Central SE3 configuration module that loads, validates, and merges global (~/.se3/config.yaml) and project (se3.yaml/se3.local.yaml, with worktree-aware precedence) settings into typed dataclasses for versioning, docs, per-step confirmation, the agent registry and LLM-caller chains, spec loading/governance/write-protection, code-index, merge, Claude-subprocess, and server/auth, while tolerantly handling and warning about malformed or deprecated keys. <!--#4d8cb08c853e4723|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/preset_loader.py` (python) — Loads and merges SE3 preset prompts from a dual-layer registry — packaged built-in prompts overlaid by project-local `se3/prompts/*.md` and `se3.yaml` overrides — exposing functions to list, build, and resolve a preset name to its (task type, prompt text, layer) with explicit errors for unknown names or missing files. <!--#6b084d3aa7add2b9|d2564ec60747f605-->
- `PresetError` (class) — Base exception for any preset resolution failure (e.g. a declared prompt file that does not exist). <!--#6030b307aeecbc5f-->
- `PresetNotFoundError` (class) — Exception raised when a requested preset name is absent from the registry. <!--#58c5c0d2faa5b1d9-->
- `PresetEntry` (class) — Dataclass representing one resolved preset registry entry (name, task type, on-disk prompt file path, and source layer). <!--#02e2f636bc038da6-->
- `_scan_builtin_presets` (function) — Enumerates built-in presets by globbing the packaged templates/prompts directory and attaching declared metadata. <!--#8fc5ae2abd3383b6-->
- `_load_project_presets` (function) — Enumerates project-local presets from se3/prompts/*.md and overlays metadata/path overrides from se3.yaml's presets section. <!--#2e2c97c767f5d773-->
- `load_registry` (function) — Builds the merged name→PresetEntry registry, loading built-ins first then letting project presets override same-named entries. <!--#6fface6d1a6916f9-->
- `list_presets` (function) — Returns all available presets (built-in plus project) sorted by name. <!--#1039d20edae71e6c-->
- `resolve` (function) — Resolves a preset name to its (task_type, prompt_text, layer) tuple, raising explicitly on unknown names or missing prompt files. <!--#e9990726bc48d1f3-->

### `src/se3/utils.py` (python) — Shared SE 3.0 utility module providing helpers for discovering and parsing spec files, syncing/copying outputs, validating documentation and framework versioning, inspecting git-staged framework changes, and parsing status/changelog metadata. <!--#dd440553a674550f|bbb61607537f6fe4-->
- `_resolve_specs_dir` (function) — Resolves the specs directory by preference order: se3/specs/, then specs/, then legacy openspec/specs/. <!--#50cfb7c3c9bc1885-->
- `discover_specs` (function) — Returns a sorted list of absolute paths to spec.md files found in the resolved specs directory. <!--#92b1149753063b4b-->
- `parse_spec` (function) — Parses a spec.md file into structured data (title, purpose, requirements, and WHEN/THEN scenarios). <!--#264118a9b806c560-->
- `get_exit_code` (function) — Maps a list of validation results to a CLI exit code (0 success, 1 errors, 2 runtime error). <!--#61082e083fb6cc05-->
- `discover_outputs` (function) — Lists all regular files directly inside a given directory. <!--#ec09c48061154c4d-->
- `get_file_mtime` (function) — Returns a file's modification timestamp, or None if it doesn't exist. <!--#730f41c0d4c2440a-->
- `copy_file` (function) — Copies a file to a destination, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#78cd0cb36fae02a0-->
- `get_source_mappings` (function) — Returns the (now empty) source-to-output file sync mappings, since runtime files are no longer synced. <!--#6f5c472251f28ed0-->
- `discover_changes` (function) — Discovers changelog/change entry names from se3/specs/_changelog with legacy fallbacks. <!--#ca576176987c4adb-->
- `discover_specs_in_change` (function) — Legacy helper that finds spec.md files nested within a named change directory. <!--#0870a4e8ac7c9751-->
- `find_verification_markers` (function) — Searches Python files for pytest markers or comments verifying a given scenario ID. <!--#7dbaf5c1ee6b6e20-->
- `get_framework_version` (function) — Extracts the SE3 framework version string from pyproject.toml. <!--#1d5ec79da290223b-->
- `check_documentation_consistency` (function) — Validates that README.md and VERSIONS.md exist, cross-reference each other, and reflect the current framework version. <!--#5401b568afd9afa1-->
- `has_framework_file_changes` (function) — Checks git's staged files for changes to known framework source paths. <!--#dbfdb9481646fa39-->
- `parse_status_md` (function) — Parses status.md into structured fields (active change, current task, status, blockers). <!--#2c4ec321050f973f-->

## `src/se3/commands/` — The SE3 CLI command layer, providing every Typer entry point a human or the LLM invokes — project scaffolding (init), issue management (issue), the unified flow driver (run) with its session lifecycle helpers (end-session, salvage), code-index navigation (code-index), the spec→new-system migrator (migrate), flow history inspection (history), and the branch-merge workflow (merge, merge_respond) backed by the dependency-free merge/ foundation package. <!--#e1ebebecc2e5b642|01f017349841f61e-->

### `src/se3/commands/__init__.py` (python) — Package initializer marking the directory as the SE 3.0 CLI commands module. <!--#7bf1513a2bce3e63|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/commands/code_index_cmd.py` (python) — Defines the `se3 code-index` Typer command family that lets humans and the LLM navigate the project structure map, exposing the bare adaptive root view plus `index` (literal one-level drill-in), `show` (full function/method detail for one file), `rebuild` (the only writing command, incrementally or fully re-summarising se3/code-index.md), and `inspect` (on-disk map health stats). <!--#f9b5327bf01ed56a|1302050c2e20f923-->
- `get_project_root` (function) — Locates the project root by walking up from the cwd to the first directory containing a .git folder or an SE3 config marker, falling back to cwd. <!--#05a0e596195334bb-->
- `_render_adaptive_map` (function) — Renders the bare `se3 code-index` adaptive root view — the budgeted zoomable orientation tree built from the configured primary roots and byte budget, emitted exactly to stdout for LLM consumption. <!--#a5942a92675b9b78-->
- `code_index_main` (function) — Typer callback for the `code-index` command group that renders the adaptive root view when invoked with no subcommand and otherwise dispatches to its drill-in/rebuild/inspect subcommands. <!--#475c3ea7659eb429-->
- `index_cmd` (function) — Implements `code-index index [<path>]`, rendering exactly one literal level at the given path (a directory's immediate children, a file's symbols, or the root level) without auto-expansion. <!--#3b6340171d8c0926-->
- `show_cmd` (function) — CLI command that prints one file's full class/function/method detail (or a directory's file one-liners) by loading the authoritative se3/code-index.md render-only. <!--#f1874d87c89d2387-->
- `rebuild_cmd` (function) — CLI command that (re)builds the authoritative se3/code-index.md via load_or_build, re-summarising only fingerprint-changed nodes incrementally or everything with --force, then reports file/symbol counts. <!--#dc6c44c51d070001-->
- `inspect_cmd` (function) — Implements `code-index inspect`, printing summary health stats (file, symbol, degraded-chunk counts and a per-kind file breakdown) from the on-disk map. <!--#6730d9e2e9a202ff-->

### `src/se3/commands/end_session_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `end-session` command that tears down an SE3 flow: it locates the session (worktree or main-branch), terminates the live `se3 run` process tree (SIGTERM-grace-SIGKILL), archives and promotes engine/history state safely outside the doomed worktree, clears resumable snapshots, and renders a colored Rich summary with an aggregate exit code. <!--#366d8121af52f973|eb726bbf0fd6ee8a-->
- `end_session` (function) — Top-level entry point that orchestrates the end-session pipeline: resolve root, find any worktree session, terminate the live process, archive (worktree or main-branch), and render a summary with an aggregate exit code. <!--#03d0f5d7c265dc0e-->
- `_find_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the current directory to locate the project root via a `.git` dir or an SE3 config file. <!--#3c8eb6032ea041a2-->
- `_resolve_main_root` (function) — Resolves the main project root, normalizing a worktree-copy path back to its owning main root so archival writes land outside the worktree being deleted. <!--#62178ee8d8722eaf-->
- `_read_main_flow_id` (function) — Best-effort reads the active `flow_id` from the main project's `se3/state/engine.json`. <!--#811a4a97d453d48b-->
- `_find_worktree_session` (function) — Scans `se3/worktrees/*/.../engine.json` for a worktree session matching the given flow_id (regardless of status), returning its path/branch metadata or None for a main-branch session. <!--#c84340e517fd8c27-->
- `_proc_alive` (function) — Returns whether a pid names a live, non-zombie process (using psutil when available, else `os.kill(pid, 0)`). <!--#afc851908ba03f0c-->
- `_collect_descendants` (function) — Returns the given pids plus all their live recursive descendants, captured up front so a whole process tree can be signalled before the parent is killed and children orphaned. <!--#ef2fff3b2e9e0231-->
- `_any_alive` (function) — Returns whether any pid in the given collection is currently alive. <!--#325a42539d7156fa-->
- `_terminate_one` (function) — Terminates a pid and its entire descendant tree via SIGTERM-grace-SIGKILL, returning (ok, detail) where ok is True only when every process is confirmed dead. <!--#9a8baaa37329a0f9-->
- `_read_run_pidfile` (function) — Reads the live-flow pid recorded in `<state_root>/se3/state/run.pid`, returning None if absent/unreadable/empty. <!--#0cb62ebd8d238460-->
- `_pid_is_live_se3_run` (function) — Guards the run.pid marker against staleness by checking the pid is both alive and (via psutil cmdline) actually an `se3 run` process. <!--#b7281b12398e0885-->
- `_proc_has_descendant_in_dir` (function) — Returns whether a process's tree is anchored inside a worktree path (a descendant cwd or any open file under it), used to identify a `--worktree` flow's parent that stays at the main root. <!--#5e59f4d695e1cf19-->
- `_discover_pids_for_flow` (function) — Discovers live `se3 run` pids belonging to a flow via the run.pid marker, an `--flow-id` cmdline arg, matching cwd + on-disk flow_id, or a tree anchored in the worktree path. <!--#baf6b5daf9fa7b8e-->
- `_terminate_session_process` (function) — Terminates the session's live process(es) — using a supplied pid or discovered candidates — returning (ok, summary) where ok gates the destructive archive path. <!--#ec0cc83d0cb971f5-->
- `_archive_worktree_session` (function) — Archives a worktree session by reusing the merge-cleanup machinery (archive worktree, promote engine state, sync history, clear snapshot, delete branch/worktree), each sub-step independently fault-tolerant. <!--#a3256d422f075bc6-->
- `_archive_main_session` (function) — Archives a main-branch session by clearing engine state and the resumable snapshot, but only clears state when the main engine.json positively belongs to the requested flow_id. <!--#f2058d8d2f43a35d-->
- `_infer_worktree_branch` (function) — Infers the branch checked out at a worktree path by parsing `git worktree list --porcelain`, used when engine.json did not record a worktree_branch. <!--#c0d9e792ab67fa0a-->
- `_sync_worktree_history` (function) — Copies a worktree's per-flow history files into the main project append-only, never overwriting (collisions become `.from-<branch>` sidecars) and skipping byte-identical files for idempotency. <!--#118816cd79f47b90-->
- `_same_file` (function) — Fault-tolerantly returns whether two files have byte-identical content via filecmp. <!--#43129f0a76c9cfd1-->
- `_resolve_history_target` (function) — Resolves where to copy a history file without overwriting, returning the primary path, a uniquified `.from-<branch>` sidecar, or None if an identical copy already exists. <!--#cd2db7cff1fe7516-->
- `_clear_resumable` (function) — Clears the resumable snapshot for a flow_id within a worktree via PersistenceManager. <!--#46bde5cf369c8f72-->
- `_display_results` (function) — Renders the collected (step, status, detail) results as a colored Rich summary table, mirroring the salvage command's output. <!--#050555613facd1c2-->

### `src/se3/commands/history_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `se3 history` CLI command group, providing functions to locate flows across active/archived/history-only data sources and render their summaries and detailed (including LLM-call session) info as Rich tables or JSON, plus subcommands to list, show, restore, and view archived flows. <!--#9e5dfc63cee10708|a350823ac8891575-->
- `get_project_root` (function) — Locates the project root by walking up from the cwd looking for a `.git` directory or an SE3 config marker. <!--#f92ddfc8dfa3425f-->
- `format_datetime` (function) — Converts an ISO datetime string into a human-readable `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` format, falling back to the raw string on error. <!--#0f5d25170fb3009a-->
- `format_duration` (function) — Computes and formats the elapsed duration between two ISO timestamps as minutes/hours/days. <!--#212868504b98e854-->
- `list_all_flows` (function) — Returns all flows from every data source via the PersistenceManager. <!--#6ed7050a4e181cb1-->
- `list_archived_flows_from_disk` (function) — Scans the archive directory for `engine_*.json` files and returns summary dicts of each archived flow. <!--#54c48597e26a4ebf-->
- `_detail_from_flow` (function) — Builds a detailed info dict (metadata, progress, steps, chat session count) from a live FlowInstance object. <!--#eeccd00f334be5a5-->
- `_load_archived_flow` (function) — Searches archive files for one matching the given flow_id and reconstructs a FlowInstance from it. <!--#6fbbe558dca9d15e-->
- `_detail_from_history` (function) — Builds a minimal flow-detail dict from history-only directory data, reconstructing timestamps and self_check pass numbering. <!--#d657d101098e50a4-->
- `get_flow_detail` (function) — Retrieves a flow's detail dict by searching active, archived, then history-only data sources in order. <!--#f197f9de0c0a77c9-->
- `_status_color` (function) — Maps a flow status string to a Rich display color. <!--#d24adeb7ceeee4ff-->
- `_step_status_color` (function) — Maps a step status string to a Rich display color. <!--#8bb2cea2c4630c05-->
- `_render_flows_table` (function) — Renders a list of flow dicts as a Rich table with status colors and a usage hint. <!--#879c364f24bcdb84-->
- `default_cmd` (function) — Default `se3 history` callback that lists flows (with active/archived/JSON filters) unless a subcommand is invoked. <!--#ee56291e672fffd0-->
- `list_cmd` (function) — `se3 history list` subcommand that lists all flows with active/archived/JSON filtering options. <!--#bc1cdce01f476992-->
- `show_cmd` (function) — `se3 history show` subcommand that displays detailed flow info, with prefix matching and optional detailed/verbose LLM-call output. <!--#f2635fcfc804b8ea-->
- `_show_detailed_sessions` (function) — Renders detailed per-step LLM call sessions for a flow using Rich rules and session renderers. <!--#f9b92401ed5c0945-->
- `_show_detailed_json` (function) — Outputs a flow's detail plus full chat history as JSON. <!--#3757b11347d645fd-->
- `restore_cmd` (function) — `se3 history restore` subcommand that validates the flow and delegates to `se3 run --resume` to resume it. <!--#90d23da25a8bcfc9-->
- `archived_cmd` (function) — `se3 history archived` subcommand that lists archived flows as a Rich table or JSON. <!--#60d2fcfc21462bd9-->

### `src/se3/commands/init_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `se3 init` CLI command, which scaffolds a new SE3 project by rendering template files (charter.md, VERSIONS.md, etc.), initializing a git repo if needed, and ensuring .gitignore excludes se3.local.yaml. <!--#d08cb98dd65311a8|7949f85b71a6f43b-->
- `_render_template` (function) — Loads a named template file from TEMPLATES_DIR and substitutes `{key}` placeholders via literal string replacement (not str.format) to avoid choking on incidental braces. <!--#760a3c5ebb7fdbb8-->
- `is_git_repository` (function) — Returns True if the given path lies inside an existing git repository by walking up parents looking for a .git directory. <!--#0d770de078464a79-->
- `init_repository` (function) — Runs `git init` in the given directory and returns a (success, message) tuple, handling git-not-installed and command-failure cases. <!--#6268849a7cbf7dd5-->
- `_normalize_gitignore_pattern` (function) — Strips gitignore anchor/recursive-glob/directory markers (`/`, `**/`, trailing `/`) from a pattern so it can be matched with fnmatch. <!--#a6b579bdc1df51ec-->
- `_gitignore_has_local_pattern` (function) — Returns True when an existing .gitignore already ignores se3.local.yaml via a literal or covering glob line, skipping comments and negations. <!--#d075bf1a25d3b705-->
- `_gitignore_has_local_negation` (function) — Returns True when .gitignore contains a narrow `!se3.local.yaml`-style negation that specifically un-ignores the file (but not se3.yaml), signalling a conflicting append should be refused. <!--#75d9f94ea11cafdf-->
- `create_gitignore` (function) — Ensures .gitignore ignores se3.local.yaml, returning one of five statuses (created/appended/negated/unchanged/error) and writing/appending the ignore block as needed. <!--#53319e9f4a4b90a5-->
- `_get_charter_template` (function) — Builds the initial se3/charter.md content by delegating to charter.render_charter_template with placeholder fill-in prompts for a fresh project. <!--#6d0eb88f593c231f-->
- `_get_versions_md_template` (function) — Renders the initial VERSIONS.md from the versions_md.md template, filling in project name and current date. <!--#80b454c638f9ac34-->
- `run_init` (function) — Core, testable init routine that creates all project artifacts and git setup, returning a dict of created/skipped paths plus git and gitignore status flags. <!--#2371f759850888d6-->
- `init_cmd` (function) — The typer CLI entrypoint for `se3 init` that resolves the project root/name, calls run_init, and prints status messages and next-step guidance. <!--#5025bcd3453b1dca-->

### `src/se3/commands/issue_cmd.py` (python) — Typer CLI command module for managing SE3 issues — listing, showing, creating, editing (via external editor with YAML templates), closing, and resetting issues — with Rich-based colored formatting and helpers for project-root resolution and editor invocation. <!--#5a28e5919377a43d|491264dd703bea1f-->
- `get_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the current directory to locate the project root via a `.git` directory or SE3 config marker, falling back to cwd. <!--#f92ddfc8dfa3425f-->
- `_status_color` (function) — Maps an IssueStatus enum value to a Rich color string for table/detail rendering. <!--#440d3dc2ee8afeb2-->
- `_priority_color` (function) — Maps a priority string (critical/high/medium/low) to a Rich color for display. <!--#decc56c974d7023c-->
- `_type_color` (function) — Maps an issue type string (bug/feature/etc.) to a Rich color for display. <!--#bd6f4aa758834f96-->
- `_format_datetime` (function) — Formats a datetime as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, falling back to its string form on error. <!--#622e5ed38538305d-->
- `_get_editor` (function) — Resolves the editor command from $EDITOR, defaulting to `vi` when unset or malformed. <!--#6da17e089dc60c09-->
- `EditorError` (class) — Exception raised when the external editor binary cannot be found or launched. <!--#5e3c13fe86988091-->
- `_open_editor_with_content` (function) — Writes content to a temp file, opens it in the user's editor, and returns the edited text (None if cancelled, raising EditorError on launch failure). <!--#e47b567354907101-->
- `_issue_to_editor_yaml` (function) — Renders an existing Issue as a human-editable YAML template containing only editable fields plus a read-only id. <!--#b0abf28b8150969b-->
- `_new_issue_editor_yaml` (function) — Generates a blank YAML template for creating a new issue via the external editor. <!--#f32e849fd690fa51-->
- `_parse_edited_issue_yaml` (function) — Parses edited YAML text into a dict, validating it is a non-empty mapping with a non-blank description. <!--#466da3b0f72e14be-->
- `default_cmd` (function) — Default callback that lists open issues when no subcommand is invoked. <!--#78df7f33146891ba-->
- `list_cmd` (function) — Lists issues in a Rich table with optional filtering by status (all/open), type, and source. <!--#53a4b2ce3e820410-->
