- `show_cmd` (function) — Displays detailed information for a single issue by ID in a formatted block, erroring if not found. <!--#0a4092ed73dcf0e8-->
- `create_cmd` (function) — Creates a new issue from a positional/stdin/interactive description or a full YAML editor template, with optional title, type, priority, and tags. <!--#535ab76f334c4c39-->
- `_resolve_description` (function) — Resolves an issue description from a positional argument, piped stdin, or an interactive prompt, returning None on cancel and raising on empty input. <!--#a600847d29781592-->
- `edit_cmd` (function) — Opens an issue in the external editor and applies the edited YAML via update_fields, treating removed fields as cleared to defaults. <!--#ed70b17ee247e3a5-->
- `close_cmd` (function) — Closes an issue by ID with an optional reason, reporting errors via IssueManager. <!--#5894a962b47cdaad-->
- `reset_cmd` (function) — Resets an in-progress issue back to open status by ID. <!--#3c3ce4cfb105b529-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `se3 merge` CLI command that sequentially merges one or more branches into the current branch — validating branch names and a clean/non-in-progress working tree, acquiring the main-worktree merge lock, orchestrating the merge (with optional fast-strategy auto-stash and conflict resolution), and rendering runtime-sync signals, merged-branch buckets, and failure summaries with an exit code. <!--#c54f05d0c7319106|f83c8f62023ac746-->
- `_run_git` (function) — Thin wrapper that runs a git subcommand in a given project root via subprocess, capturing output with configurable check/timeout. <!--#8bdb8c6f53ca2c0b-->
- `_resolve_git_dir` (function) — Resolves the real git directory (handling linked worktrees where .git is a pointer file) via `git rev-parse --git-dir`, returning None if unavailable. <!--#39d970125e3b9d76-->
- `_is_working_tree_clean` (function) — Returns whether the working tree has no uncommitted tracked changes and no in-progress git operation, ignoring untracked files. <!--#0b796ef88d8b0242-->
- `_git_operation_in_progress` (function) — Detects whether git is mid-merge/cherry-pick/revert/rebase by checking for the corresponding marker files in the git directory. <!--#bfe6f2d49513bda6-->
- `_branch_exists` (function) — Checks whether a local branch exists via `git show-ref`, failing closed (False) on any infrastructure error so indeterminate refs are refused. <!--#e9891f12d3b59534-->
- `validate_branch_names` (function) — Validates user-supplied branch names before any git command runs, rejecting empties, dash-prefixes, shell metacharacters, glob chars, and git-ref-invalid patterns with a descriptive ValueError. <!--#526dc4e71b25599b-->
- `_append_runtime_sync_lines` (function) — Appends human-readable runtime-sync signal sections (skipped branches/files, idempotent bypasses, discarded tier-B, collisions) to a CLI output line list. <!--#23ec6910a7f12691-->
- `_split_merged_buckets` (function) — Splits a merge report's merged branches into newly-merged versus already-an-ancestor buckets, with a git-ancestry fallback for legacy reports. <!--#85e42d3a5d245a8d-->
- `_append_split_branch_lines` (function) — Appends the per-bucket 'Newly merged' and 'Already an ancestor' branch listings to a CLI output line list. <!--#46b7a0e52a8e54c2-->
- `_has_user_uncommitted_changes` (function) — Returns whether the user has genuine working-tree WIP (tracked or untracked), filtering out SE3's own runtime artifacts, to decide if a fast-strategy pre-stash is needed. <!--#bf31679b6ab5f671-->
- `_fast_stash_dirty` (function) — Stashes dirty working-tree state (including untracked) before a fast-strategy merge, returning the stash label or None on clean tree/failure. <!--#27f8729d65270986-->
- `_fast_stash_pop` (function) — Pops the fast pre-merge stash, deterministically resolving any conflicts/collisions via take-ours, dropping the stash, and filing an audit issue. <!--#d5be63b456914f42-->
- `run_merge` (function) — Top-level entry point that validates inputs, enforces a clean/non-in-progress tree, acquires the main-worktree merge lock, runs the merge orchestrator (with optional fast auto-stash), and renders results, returning an exit code. <!--#6c99eec5743a23d9-->
- `_failure_title_and_summary` (function) — Maps a merge failure_reason code (including compound prefixed reasons) to a user-facing (title, summary-line) pair distinguishing conflict, guardrail, and fast-mode failure categories. <!--#d31f01806d4f6f2e-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge_respond.py` (python) — CLI module that processes a user's response to a merge guardrail decision (accept/abort/manual), running the locked, version- and guardrail-checking workflow under a MergeLock with support for parked manual-resolution re-entry and rollback. <!--#fb23f5ba961c1ef0|36ad4e88dda4d061-->
- `_is_spec_path` (function) — Thin wrapper that delegates se3 spec-file path detection to the canonical implementation in `se3.engine.merge.guardrails` so the merge subsystem shares one detector. <!--#92631e060c96b704-->
- `_first_parent_sha` (function) — Returns the first-parent SHA of HEAD via `git rev-list --parents`, treating octopus merges like 2-parent merges and raising RuntimeError on git failure or a parentless root commit. <!--#b8325d34356dfe2f-->
- `_head_parent_count` (function) — Returns HEAD's parent count for octopus-merge detection, distinguishing a legitimate `0` (root commit) from `None` (undetermined due to a transient git failure). <!--#a7aa6eaf6327be38-->
- `_extract_version_from_string` (function) — Parses a version string out of TOML (`pyproject.toml`) or JSON (`package.json`) content, returning None (and warning on TOML parse failure) when no version can be extracted. <!--#0322f245c4574684-->
- `_check_version_unchanged` (function) — Compares the project version between a pre-merge SHA and HEAD, returning an error message when the version is unchanged or the post-merge version file is present but unparseable. <!--#3bc84fb050d1d860-->
- `process_merge_response` (function) — Public entry point that validates the call file, resolves the main-worktree lock root, and runs the locked response-processing body under a blocking MergeLock, mapping lock-busy/stale errors to CLI exit codes. <!--#d70cfe2ee3a6e6b3-->
- `_verify_pending_guardrails` (function) — Handles re-entry for a parked manual-resolution merge by reading the `.pending_guardrails` marker, running guardrails against the user's new commit, and either clearing the marker or rolling HEAD back to the pre-merge SHA (auto-stashing first). <!--#fe2c6a53bba0778b-->
- `_process_merge_response_locked` (function) — Lock-protected core that dispatches on the user's choice (accept/abort/manual), handling pending-guardrails re-entry and refusing to accept strict-mode placeholder or orphan-guardrail-violating resolutions. <!--#627aaeb4cb7259b6-->

### `src/se3/commands/migrate_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `se3 migrate` command as a registry-based migration channel whose shipped first migrator runs a salvage-first, fault-tolerant pipeline that cuts a project over from the retired se3/specs/ corpus to the new code-index + charter + colocated why-comment system, landing the whole change as one git-revertable working-tree edit. <!--#347d03e12f8cecbe|89764abbafbff369-->
- `ColocatedWhy` (class) — Dataclass pairing a project-relative source file path with a prose why/intent fragment to be inserted into that file as a comment. <!--#cfd51d5498faf0ca-->
- `SalvageInput` (class) — Dataclass bundling everything the salvager needs (project root, base spec text, non-base spec corpus, admission standard, charter template, project name) so the salvager does no discovery of its own. <!--#a03d93eb1581a162-->
- `SalvageResult` (class) — Dataclass holding the salvaged product: the full assembled charter body, the code-bound colocations, and advisory notes for the reviewer. <!--#a748fffc532da172-->
- `Migrator` (class) — Dataclass describing one registered migration — its id, description, and a `run` callable returning a MigrationReport. <!--#39fc5673b8d53d52-->
- `register_migrator` (function) — Registers a migrator under its unique id in the MIGRATORS registry, raising on duplicate ids. <!--#29ecb08e2108fe0e-->
- `get_migrator` (function) — Looks up and returns a registered migrator by id, or None if not found. <!--#f654e0789ae24328-->
- `list_migrators` (function) — Returns all registered migrators sorted by id. <!--#f112e419974b0265-->
- `StepOutcome` (class) — Dataclass recording one pipeline step's name, status (OK/SKIP/FAIL), and detail string. <!--#b595caa244d380a1-->
- `MigrationReport` (class) — Dataclass accumulating per-step outcomes and notes, exposing overall success (`ok`) and a process `exit_code`. <!--#624b9b55c9e82f75-->
  - `MigrationReport.add` (method) — Appends a StepOutcome with the given name, status, and detail to the report. <!--#5b0f45dfab323d34-->
  - `MigrationReport.ok` (method) — Property that is True only when no recorded step has FAIL status. <!--#c434422828d4983f-->
  - `MigrationReport.exit_code` (method) — Property returning process exit code 0 on success, 1 on any failure. <!--#4299b082776eeaeb-->
- `_load_spec_corpus` (function) — Tolerantly loads the spec corpus from a specs directory, returning the base spec text and a {name: text} map of non-base specs while skipping unreadable, hidden, and underscore-prefixed entries. <!--#1727d96aa1f76583-->
- `_project_name_from_base` (function) — Best-effort extraction of the project name from the base spec's title line, with a fallback. <!--#4208a2781e9fec9b-->
- `_make_llm_salvager` (function) — Builds the default LLM-backed salvager that assembles the charter (pass A) and extracts per-spec code-bound why/intent (pass B), each LLM call degrading defensively rather than aborting the migration. <!--#699d621938e9bb9a-->
- `_strip_code_fence` (function) — Strips a single wrapping triple-backtick code fence from a text body if present. <!--#620f4e9b5e0d1c5d-->
- `_fallback_charter` (function) — Produces a degraded but lossless charter — the rendered template plus the base spec verbatim under a loud review banner — when LLM assembly is unavailable. <!--#13cb999b7c39d7eb-->
- `_comment_prefix` (function) — Returns the line-comment prefix for a file based on its extension, defaulting to `#`. <!--#edaf021548cf685e-->
- `_render_why_comment` (function) — Renders a why/intent fragment into a list of commented lines prefixed by the WHY marker. <!--#4017fdd2f97275ce-->
- `_insert_why_comment` (function) — Inserts a rendered why-comment block at a safe top-of-file location, preserving any leading shebang. <!--#0385c973b5aaea6c-->
- `_apply_colocations` (function) — Inserts each colocation's why-comment into its target file, skipping (with recorded reasons) any missing or unreadable targets, and returns the applied count plus skip reasons. <!--#efcc27bd877d25f5-->
- `_write_charter_once` (function) — Writes the fully-assembled charter body to se3/charter.md in a single atomic write with no overwrite window. <!--#5542c0bfe1b1099e-->
- `_tracked_toplevel_whitelists` (function) — Helper that runs `git ls-files` to enumerate all tracked top-level paths and returns `!/<name>` whitelist lines (dirs with trailing slash, .gitignore first), or None if git is unavailable so callers won't add a root default-deny without existence protection. <!--#a1fd1234efe43966-->
- `_rewrite_gitignore` (function) — Idempotently migrates a project's .gitignore by adding code-index/charter whitelists, removing the retired specs whitelist, and introducing a root `/*` default-deny guarded by existence-protected top-level whitelists, returning a human-readable list of the changes made. <!--#cb922b4e7207863e-->
- `run_spec_to_new_system` (function) — Executes the one-shot, fault-tolerant spec→new-system migration pipeline: assembles the charter, colocates why-comments into source, builds the code-index, deletes the old se3/specs/ tree only after salvage is confirmed, and rewrites .gitignore — all as one uncommitted, git-revertable working-tree change. <!--#5966af45c4291bf7-->
- `_display_report` (function) — Renders a migration report as a Rich table with color-coded step statuses plus any review notes. <!--#ba4c448f26e0b128-->
- `list_command` (function) — Typer command that lists the available registered migrations in a table. <!--#3a65166c9e3f056d-->
- `run_command` (function) — Typer command that resolves and runs a migration by id against the project root, displays the report, and exits with its exit code. <!--#cbe8e3ce48a6f38d-->

### `src/se3/commands/run.py` (python) — The unified `se3 run` CLI command that drives the SE3 3.0 flow engine — creating new flows or resuming interrupted ones, executing each step type through the state machine, and handling human CONFIRM-gate responses (including free-text approvals from the web console) and SIGINT interrupts. <!--#5585e22ac86e0448|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/commands/salvage_cmd.py` (python) — CLI command that rescues an interrupted flow by running five sequential salvage steps — loading session state, assessing git changes, committing uncommitted work, creating tracking issues for unfinished work, and archiving the session — then renders the per-step outcomes in a Rich table and returns an exit code. <!--#e70cd5d8e0d21072|c03e0c8fc18c4581-->
- `salvage` (function) — Top-level entry point that runs the five salvage steps in sequence, each wrapped in its own error handling, then prints a results table and returns an exit code. <!--#31a7bc717491a9e6-->
- `_find_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the current directory to locate the project root by finding a .git directory or an SE3 config file. <!--#3c8eb6032ea041a2-->
- `_load_session` (function) — Tolerantly loads the persisted flow/session state via PersistenceManager, returning the FlowInstance (or None) plus any warnings. <!--#8c64b4dd4cc982ab-->
- `_assess_git_diff` (function) — Runs git status/diff to collect a dict of uncommitted-change info (status lines, changed file count/list, diff stat, truncated diff summary). <!--#c6bf085dac297a44-->
- `_commit_changes` (function) — Stages and commits all uncommitted changes with a generated `[salvage]` message, returning the new commit hash (or None if nothing to commit). <!--#2047b9ff2adde17e-->
- `_create_salvage_issues` (function) — Creates tracking issues for unfinished work, summarizing flow step history, interruption point, and changed files (or just changed files when no session state exists). <!--#782c49e6c54a7315-->
- `_archive_session` (function) — Clears the persisted session state and its per-flow resumable snapshot so the dispositioned flow is no longer resumable, returning whether anything was archived. <!--#1a0e70dd930dbfb2-->
- `_display_results` (function) — Renders the per-step salvage outcomes (name, color-coded OK/SKIP/FAIL status, detail) as a Rich table to the console. <!--#979947d3b3746ba9-->

## `src/se3/commands/merge/` — The foundation layer of the SE3 merge subsystem, bundling lightweight, dependency-free building blocks—typed result models, failure-reason enums, an fcntl-based merge lock, append-only LLM call tracing, secret redaction, and independent merge post-condition assertions—shared by the merge orchestrator, CLI entry points, and engine internals. <!--#8f0ccdf83cd91b04|57c639818844852a-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/__init__.py` (python) — Package init for the SE3 merge subsystem's foundation layer, re-exporting the lightweight building blocks—failure-reason enums, LLM call tracing, concurrency locking, post-condition assertions, typed result models, and secret redaction—shared by the merge orchestrator, CLI entry points, and engine internals. <!--#cf78c40f0e1bc931|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/failure_reason.py` (python) — Defines the FailureReason IntEnum cataloging every reason a merge orchestration can fail or pause, plus helpers to translate between these enum values and their legacy 'prefix: detail' string forms for round-trippable persistence and diagnostics. <!--#0b69a0075f190cd3|216dcac12bc54b0b-->
- `FailureReason` (class) — An IntEnum cataloging every reason a merge orchestration can fail or pause, with subsystem-grouped gap-aware integer values (git, conflict-resolution, fast-strategy, guardrail, rollback, runtime-sync, post-condition, version, repo-state, lock, etc.) and a NONE/UNEXPECTED pair. <!--#793301c5003e27cc-->
  - `FailureReason.legacy_string` (method) — Property returning the canonical legacy-string spelling of a reason as its lower-cased enum name, without any compound diagnostic detail. <!--#c0b7d910ff47c044-->
- `_assert_compound_prefix_order_longest_first` (function) — Test-importable defensive assertion that verifies the _COMPOUND_PREFIXES list is ordered longest-first so no shorter prefix can silently shadow a longer one during matching. <!--#a215f7b873024d92-->
- `from_legacy_string` (function) — Translates a legacy failure_reason string (None, empty, bare reason, or compound 'prefix: detail' form) into a (FailureReason, detail) tuple, falling back to UNEXPECTED with the raw text preserved as detail. <!--#14977706905a8d7c-->
- `to_legacy_string` (function) — Renders a FailureReason back into its legacy string form, mapping None to None and FailureReason.NONE to an empty string to preserve round-trip semantics. <!--#6e4cedb31364c905-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/llm_trace.py` (python) — Module providing append-only JSONL trace logging of individual LLM calls during merge operations, defining an LLMCallRecord dataclass for per-call metadata and a size-rotating, fsync-batching LLMTrace writer that records each call as a line. <!--#8150d7f2ad960f9f|cd3eec9a59d5ee7c-->
- `LLMCallRecord` (class) — Dataclass capturing a single LLM call's metadata (sequence, timestamp, agent, token estimate, prompt/response previews, duration, outcome, error, and arbitrary meta). <!--#6f024f9b4e32d840-->
  - `LLMCallRecord.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the call record into a plain dict ready for JSON encoding into a trace line. <!--#66bd42648a913924-->
- `LLMTrace` (class) — Thread-safe (single-process) append-only JSONL writer that records LLM calls, rotating files by size and batching fsync for durability without IO amplification. <!--#37656d149fdecb08-->
  - `LLMTrace.__init__` (method) — Configures the trace writer with project root, target directory, max file size, and fsync batching thresholds, initializing counters and the lock. <!--#a4d8a0e7c57bdd80-->
  - `LLMTrace._ensure_dir` (method) — Creates the trace output directory (and parents) if it does not yet exist. <!--#bcc55e51d2a7b05f-->
  - `LLMTrace._new_file_path` (method) — Generates a unique rotation-counter-suffixed, UTC-timestamped JSONL file path for a new trace file. <!--#dc1884017308886f-->
  - `LLMTrace._rotate_if_needed` (method) — Closes and reopens a fresh trace file once the current one exceeds the configured size limit. <!--#41851d34db6d1884-->
  - `LLMTrace._open_file` (method) — Ensures the directory exists and opens a new trace file for writing at a freshly generated path. <!--#3f16d51fc8ed6b8e-->
  - `LLMTrace._fsync_now` (method) — Forces a flush plus os.fsync of the current file and resets the fsync throttle counters. <!--#585ae5672b2847f9-->
  - `LLMTrace._close_file` (method) — Flushes the tail to disk via fsync and closes the current trace file so no buffered record is lost. <!--#9b59062c89518c78-->
  - `LLMTrace.start` (method) — Idempotently opens the initial trace file and marks the writer as started. <!--#6d6bb5dfdab16afe-->
  - `LLMTrace.stop` (method) — Closes the trace file (forcing a final fsync) and marks the writer as stopped. <!--#e7137789ab5bc682-->
  - `LLMTrace.record` (method) — Appends one LLM call as a JSONL line (truncating previews, rotating if needed, flushing, and conditionally fsyncing) and returns its sequence number. <!--#ca81df8dded5e875-->
  - `LLMTrace.__enter__` (method) — Context-manager entry that starts the trace and returns the instance. <!--#d1285a98c0961099-->
  - `LLMTrace.__exit__` (method) — Context-manager exit that stops the trace, ensuring the file is closed and synced. <!--#53eaf3af0d2e4827-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/merge_lock.py` (python) — Implements the project's main-worktree mutex as an fcntl.flock-based merge lock, providing the MergeLock dataclass (blocking/non-blocking acquire, release, PID-record management, and stale-lock breaking) plus supporting exceptions and inspection/manual-release helpers. <!--#fdec46d96355d4a4|56091478ba86b620-->
- `is_lock_held_in_process` (function) — Advisory check (no syscalls) that returns whether the current process already holds the merge lock, by consulting an in-memory registry of resolved lock paths. <!--#2bb6fc9e0e7d60d8-->
- `_stale_break_jitter` (function) — Returns a random fraction in [0,1) for stale-break backoff jitter, wrapped as a function so tests can monkeypatch it deterministically. <!--#8652290c3ab2f41a-->
- `MergeLockBusy` (class) — Exception raised when another live process currently holds the merge lock (non-blocking mode), carrying the lock file path and optional holder PID. <!--#1210b7f477ae2254-->
  - `MergeLockBusy.__init__` (method) — Stores the lock file and holder PID and builds a human-readable message that appends the PID when known. <!--#aafc5beb7625e77f-->
- `MergeLockStale` (class) — Exception signaling the lock file appears stale (holder PID absent, no PID recorded, or unparseable/corrupt), letting callers decide whether to break and retry. <!--#4e18a8971b831131-->
  - `MergeLockStale.__init__` (method) — Records the lock file, optional holder PID, and corrupt flag, composing a message that distinguishes dead-holder, empty-record, and corrupt-record cases. <!--#3058bbf691add9d9-->
- `MergeLock` (class) — Dataclass representing an exclusive merge lock over a file via fcntl.flock, providing acquire/release, blocking/non-blocking modes, PID record management, and stale-lock breaking. <!--#71bb3a553ee7ee70-->
  - `MergeLock.__post_init__` (method) — Resolves the configured lock_path against the project root (unless already absolute) into the instance's _resolved_path. <!--#0949665977013300-->
  - `MergeLock.held` (method) — Property reporting whether this specific instance currently owns an open, acquired lock file descriptor. <!--#69f47245bd20560f-->
  - `MergeLock._read_holder_pid` (method) — Reads the fixed-width PID record from the lock file (using O_NOFOLLOW, capped length), returning the holder PID or None and setting _last_read_corrupt when the bytes are unparseable. <!--#cc09b99d86e82597-->
  - `MergeLock._write_pid` (method) — Writes the current process's fixed-width PID record into the held lock fd via pwrite-then-truncate-then-fsync, avoiding any transient empty state for concurrent readers. <!--#04b2b4102bf2452e-->
  - `MergeLock._is_pid_alive` (method) — Probes whether a PID exists using signal 0, treating ESRCH as dead and EPERM (and success) as alive, to drive stale-lock decisions. <!--#009ece408997f3a8-->
  - `MergeLock._try_break_stale_and_acquire` (method) — Encapsulates the bounded, jittered unlink-then-reacquire retry loop for breaking a stale lock, returning the new fd or raising MergeLockBusy/OSError on failure. <!--#9693dfe29daac6dc-->
  - `MergeLock.acquire` (method) — Acquires the exclusive lock, choosing blocking LOCK_EX queueing or non-blocking fail-fast with stale detection and optional break_stale recovery, then records this process's PID. <!--#28984568b2a7ed6e-->
  - `MergeLock.release` (method) — Releases the flock, closes the file descriptor, and removes the path from the in-process held-locks registry, idempotently. <!--#60e5949e76255cfe-->
  - `MergeLock.__enter__` (method) — Context-manager entry that acquires the lock using the instance's configured blocking default and returns self. <!--#4b90db2205610f11-->
  - `MergeLock.__exit__` (method) — Context-manager exit that releases the lock. <!--#8f781b847877252c-->
- `LockStatus` (class) — Read-only snapshot dataclass of the lock file's state (existence, holder PID, liveness, staleness, corruption) shared by inspection and release logic. <!--#713c00e0cca2a814-->
- `ReleaseOutcome` (class) — Result dataclass of a manual release decision, holding an exit code, the observed LockStatus, and a categorical action label. <!--#ecd40e485c6e7e55-->
- `inspect_lock` (function) — Performs a write-free probe of the lock file, reusing MergeLock's PID-read and liveness checks to produce a LockStatus snapshot. <!--#358862de19df1f56-->
- `break_lock_file` (function) — Unlinks the lock file (the only way an external process can clear an flock-held lock), returning whether a file was actually removed. <!--#fcf13b779b14aba0-->
- `release_merge_lock` (function) — Pure decision logic for a manual lock release that inspects state and removes the file for stale or force cases while refusing to evict a live holder without force. <!--#8b93ee87f470279b-->
- `_lock_file_removed` (function) — Removes the lock file and re-probes the path to confirm it is actually gone, distinguishing real removal from a swallowed permission error. <!--#81738d415b225947-->
- `acquire_merge_lock` (function) — function acquire_merge_lock <!--#345e208a00ddaf0b-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/postcondition.py` (python) — Post-condition assertions that independently verify a branch the orchestrator marked 'merged' really was merged — checking ancestry of HEAD, merge-commit shape, and an actual version bump — with hardened git plumbing and typed failure reasons so corruption or commit-hook tampering is distinguished from benign cases. <!--#b734fc587adf0d52|53dfd51b51cc4b95-->
- `_bounded_read_version_file` (function) — Reads a version file with size, duration, and regular-file-only guards so a pathological or streaming version file cannot hang or OOM the post-merge check. <!--#b4ca393bdf6263b1-->
- `PostConditionViolated` (class) — RuntimeError raised when a post-condition fails, carrying a typed FailureReason plus the offending branch and diagnostic detail so callers can route the failure. <!--#0da431b628261e1a-->
  - `PostConditionViolated.__init__` (method) — Constructs the exception from a FailureReason, optional branch, and detail string, assembling them into a human-readable message. <!--#f70bb7761adb86d6-->
- `CorruptCommitGraphError` (class) — RuntimeError signalling that a commit's parent count hit the safety cap, indicating a malformed commit graph rather than a non-merge commit. <!--#1294b6b69466ee14-->
  - `CorruptCommitGraphError.__init__` (method) — Builds the corrupt-graph error from the offending ref and the parent-count cap that was exceeded. <!--#fb3fa4e6616ab5a0-->
- `_run_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand in the project root with captured output, a timeout, and disabled stdin, returning the CompletedProcess. <!--#aec14a50bb4519da-->
- `assert_branch_merged` (function) — Post-condition that a branch is an ancestor of HEAD via git merge-base --is-ancestor, distinguishing a definitive not-merged verdict from unresolvable git errors. <!--#4596f5a4b25b218b-->
- `_resolve_parent_count_cap` (function) — Returns the parent-count safety cap, defaulting to 64 but honoring the SE3_MERGE_PARENT_COUNT_CAP environment override with validation. <!--#a59ca6631aa99934-->
- `_count_parents` (function) — Counts a ref's parents via repeated rev-parse --verify ref^N, reporting whether the ref itself resolves and raising CorruptCommitGraphError past the safety cap. <!--#c41f49fe5bd6b316-->
- `assert_head_is_merge_commit` (function) — Post-condition that HEAD is a merge commit (enough parents), with opt-in tolerance for fix-up commits stacked on top of the merge up to a configurable depth. <!--#1fa9b990dc66c18d-->
- `assert_version_bumped` (function) — Post-condition that the version file contains the expected version, parsing TOML/JSON to avoid substring false-positives and optionally cross-checking the committed HEAD tree. <!--#2da0110c10472f23-->
- `_assert_committed_version_matches` (function) — Verifies HEAD's committed version file matches the expected version, distinguishing transient git-plumbing failures from positive commit-hook tampering signals. <!--#5a603880f7db03aa-->
- `check_all` (function) — Convenience entry-point that runs all applicable post-condition checks (ancestry, merge-commit shape when not a no-op, and version bump when expected) for a merged branch. <!--#4252328eeb6514ee-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/result_model.py` (python) — Defines the typed data model for merge-run results — EvidenceRecord (fail-fast guardrail-violation evidence), MergeOutcome (per-branch terminal result), and MergeReport (top-level aggregation into semantic buckets) — each with dict round-tripping and legacy-compatible accessors for JSON persistence and unmigrated consumers. <!--#f37338f77f3f24ab|c206b4a2bd0ae05b-->
- `EvidenceRecord` (class) — A dataclass enumerating every recognized guardrail-violation evidence field (pairing, deletion, topology, size, etc.) that fails fast on unknown keys and round-trips to/from plain dicts for backward compatibility. <!--#bcfcb240c97cf3e0-->
  - `EvidenceRecord.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the evidence record to a plain dict, omitting fields whose value is None, for JSON-persisted call files and log entries. <!--#a62c823b0bddf6a4-->
  - `EvidenceRecord.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that constructs an EvidenceRecord from a dict (returning None for empty input), letting unknown keys raise TypeError as the fail-fast behavior. <!--#05d79f59c6187865-->
- `MergeOutcome` (class) — A dataclass holding the terminal outcome of a single branch merge attempt, including success, typed failure reason, ancestor/warning flags, merge commit SHA, and the git_merge_succeeded distinction. <!--#7cb496de0e157739-->
- `MergeReport` (class) — The typed top-level merge-run result aggregating per-branch outcomes into semantic buckets plus version aggregation, runtime-sync, cleanup, and rollback state, with legacy-compatible fields and accessors. <!--#474e078c9d665c62-->
  - `MergeReport.failure_reason_enum` (method) — Property returning the typed FailureReason for the report, parsing a legacy string (or passing through an existing enum) and mapping unknown strings to UNEXPECTED. <!--#ee363d13b2f99528-->
  - `MergeReport.add_outcome` (method) — Appends a branch outcome and routes it into the appropriate summary bucket (already-ancestor, newly-merged, with-warnings) while recording the first failed branch. <!--#938bedc6b8a3486a-->
  - `MergeReport.newly_merged` (method) — Backward-compatibility alias property returning newly_merged_branches. <!--#2ddc24cb4dd75dff-->
  - `MergeReport.already_merged` (method) — Backward-compatibility alias property returning already_ancestor_branches. <!--#7aa051f1613716f0-->
  - `MergeReport.all_merged_branches` (method) — Returns the combined backward-compatible view of all branches that were newly merged, already ancestors, or merged with warnings. <!--#cd3e3997fa557f3e-->
  - `MergeReport.call_file_str` (method) — Returns the human-call file path as a string or actual None, avoiding the legacy 'Call file: None' rendering bug. <!--#9ece35c501a4547a-->
  - `MergeReport.to_legacy_dict` (method) — Serializes the typed report into a dict matching the legacy orchestrator.MergeReport shape for JSON persistence, fixtures, and unmigrated consumers. <!--#ef7ee84f6c9d2b81-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/secret_redact.py` (python) — A secret-redaction utility module providing a configurable, thread-safe `SecretRedactor` (plus module-level convenience functions and a cached default singleton) that masks secrets in text and git diffs while preserving diff structure and restoring allowlisted fake values. <!--#b643e520097c799f|d4452133f4d3d1d7-->
- `RedactConfig` (class) — Dataclass holding redaction configuration — an allowlist of exempt strings, extra regex/replacement patterns, and a preview length. <!--#59b0056d5d87e29e-->
- `SecretRedactor` (class) — Stateful, thread-safe redactor that applies the built-in plus configured patterns to mask secrets in text and diffs, restoring allowlisted fakes. <!--#c18072db25b8f560-->
  - `SecretRedactor.__init__` (method) — Initializes the redactor with a config and combines the default patterns with any configured extra patterns. <!--#85ccebb496ffc9a9-->
  - `SecretRedactor.redact` (method) — Applies all redaction patterns to a string, then restores any allowlisted values that were accidentally masked. <!--#fa9c0623cedad71a-->
  - `SecretRedactor._mask_fake` (method) — Static helper that runs the default patterns over a single known-fake value to compute its masked form for allowlist restoration. <!--#4fdd627f585d7c01-->
  - `SecretRedactor.redact_diff` (method) — Redacts secrets in a git diff line-by-line so diff markers and structure are preserved. <!--#eadedc33a38bbaa8-->
- `_get_default` (function) — Lazily constructs and caches a module-level default SecretRedactor singleton. <!--#a18335149677cff0-->
- `redact_text` (function) — Module-level convenience function that redacts secrets from text using the default redactor. <!--#ae56d65c5e441865-->
- `redact_diff` (function) — Module-level convenience function that redacts secrets from a git diff using the default redactor. <!--#c2475d3670220c02-->

## `src/se3/core/` — The SE3 framework's shared core package, currently housing low-level cross-cutting text utilities (e.g. a `truncate_preview` helper for capping strings with an ellipsis) intended for reuse across the codebase. <!--#cd265b7e389a08e3|45daffb5f1e58451-->

### `src/se3/core/__init__.py` (python) — Package initializer marking the src/se3/core directory as the home for SE3's shared core utilities. <!--#48e466c636635268|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/core/utils.py` (python) — A shared utilities module for the SE3 framework providing text helpers, currently a single `truncate_preview` function that caps a string to a max length and appends an ellipsis for consistent console previews. <!--#e3c9d16af367d231|63fffa8987576585-->
- `truncate_preview` (function) — Truncates a string to a maximum length and appends an ellipsis indicator, returning the text unchanged when it already fits, for consistent text previews in console output. <!--#ae15e4e349281ce9-->

## `src/se3/daemon/` — The SE3 daemon package: a resident control-plane process that outlives one-shot `se3 run` flows, composing a supervisor (tracks local processes), spawner (launches/resumes/ends flows), aggregator (polls on-disk artifacts into status snapshots), history reader, and a NAT-friendly outbound WebSocket client/protocol to bridge local project state to the central server and web UI. <!--#0632c7bc2624c4ff|e22be8bd1730fcc1-->

### `src/se3/daemon/__init__.py` (python) — Package entry point for the SE3 daemon — the resident control-plane process that bridges one-shot `se3 run` flows and the central server — re-exporting the public API from its supervisor, spawner, aggregator, daemon, client, and protocol sub-modules. <!--#6949b9b6bea420b2|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/daemon/aggregator.py` (python) — Defines the DaemonAggregator and its snapshot dataclasses (PendingCall, FlowSnapshot, IssueSnapshot, MachineStatus) that poll on-disk SE3 flow, pending-call, and issue artifacts across project roots to build a serializable MachineStatus status snapshot for the webui. <!--#923efcec98253fb1|e71e5b6b67c73ed7-->
- `PendingCall` (class) — Dataclass mirroring one file under a project's `se3/calls/` directory — a queued human-in-the-loop interaction whose `kind` field tells the UI how to render it. <!--#d774b38aee436019-->
  - `PendingCall.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the PendingCall to a plain dict for inclusion in the JSON status snapshot. <!--#5ac307bda7dd0d44-->
- `FlowSnapshot` (class) — Dataclass holding the aggregated state of a single flow as read from its `engine.json`, including progress, status, resumability, and pending calls. <!--#5dcc99b02bc8b563-->
  - `FlowSnapshot.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the FlowSnapshot (and its nested pending calls) to a plain dict for the status snapshot. <!--#d0b8958ac2b84742-->
- `IssueSnapshot` (class) — Dataclass representing a single issue record with all webui-relevant fields for inclusion in MachineStatus. <!--#80d58e94a77654f3-->
  - `IssueSnapshot.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the IssueSnapshot to a dict, omitting optional fields (title/priority/type) when unset. <!--#ac44a97529a64719-->
- `MachineStatus` (class) — Dataclass representing a full status snapshot of one SE3 machine — its flows, pending calls, project roots, and issues. <!--#bb09d7d223f3b84d-->
  - `MachineStatus.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the whole MachineStatus snapshot (with all nested flows/calls/issues) to a plain dict. <!--#eef332c4091b4c31-->
- `_stable_machine_id` (function) — Returns a process-stable machine id composed of the hostname plus a short uuid/node tail. <!--#e773a1e1eb387919-->
- `DaemonAggregator` (class) — Core class that polls on-disk flow artifacts across known project roots and builds them into a MachineStatus snapshot. <!--#6d71d0499e752678-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.__init__` (method) — Constructs the aggregator, wiring optional registry load/persist and live-roots-provider callbacks and initializing the historical-roots TTL cache. <!--#304a6e84f072b54d-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.add_project_root` (method) — Registers a project root for polling, normalizing worktree copies back to their main root and write-through-persisting it to the registry. <!--#e2484cdbc852b09e-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.remove_project_root` (method) — Stops polling the given path and invalidates the historical-roots cache. <!--#4138c922e7fea488-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.set_project_roots` (method) — Replaces the entire polled project-root set and invalidates the historical-roots cache. <!--#b0860aaf9c1796da-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._invalidate_hist_roots_cache` (method) — Drops the cached historical-root enumeration so the next `all_project_roots` re-runs the on-disk history walk. <!--#9f1c834431d818f3-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.project_roots` (method) — Returns a sorted snapshot list of the currently registered active project roots. <!--#424a9b11cd59d976-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.has_changes` (method) — Returns whether any tracked `engine.json` mtime changed since the last call, updating the internal mtime cache as a side effect. <!--#0d911f5dc970cb00-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.get_snapshot` (method) — Builds and returns the current MachineStatus by snapshotting every observable root's flow, calls, issues, and supplemental resumable snapshots. <!--#5fdf22f72c529a8f-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._live_roots` (method) — Resolves the normalized set of roots with a live `se3 run` process via the injected provider, used to gate the resumable flag. <!--#42348cabae23a503-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.all_project_roots` (method) — Returns the deduplicated, sorted union of active, registry, and TTL-cached historical roots that drives the New Task dropdown and history index. <!--#96d5c9ebc5b23cc9-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.all_observable_roots` (method) — Returns `all_project_roots` plus active `--worktree` run subdirectories, the root view used for building flow snapshots. <!--#667d4c7077dc12cb-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._active_worktree_run_roots` (method) — Discovers active `se3 run --worktree` isolation subdirectories (gated on `is_worktree_mode`) so their in-progress flows are observable. <!--#9f80d1d42b7bfcc5-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._historical_roots` (method) — Returns the on-disk historical roots for a base set, reusing a TTL- and fingerprint-guarded cache to keep the expensive history walk off the hot path. <!--#14abb216427621d8-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.pending_calls_signature` (method) — Returns a cheap stat-based (name, mtime, size) fingerprint of every `se3/calls/` file so the daemon can poll for changes without a full snapshot. <!--#b0b4a005f53552b5-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._merge_project_roots` (method) — Produces the snapshot's `project_roots` field by delegating to `all_project_roots`. <!--#f97c43f045028b11-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._snapshot_for_root` (method) — Builds a FlowSnapshot for one root from its `engine.json` (or returns None when nothing is reportable), filtering its calls and computing resumability. <!--#f2f9d5e0862a1d76-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._enumerate_resumable_snapshots` (method) — Builds supplemental FlowSnapshots from `se3/state/resumable/*.json` files for flows not represented by an active engine.json, deduplicating by flow_id. <!--#5e3b78b7d2917a44-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._snapshot_from_resumable` (method) — Builds a single resumable FlowSnapshot from a resumable-snapshot dict, deriving progress and the live-gated resumable flag. <!--#bfbad50cc153b741-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._enumerate_calls` (method) — Lists genuinely-pending human-call files under `se3/calls/`, skipping response files and any call that already has a response sibling. <!--#b1b553058e150ab1-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._filter_calls_for_flow` (method) — Filters a call list to those whose `context.flow_id` matches the given flow, dropping unattributed calls (or returning all when no flow_id is given). <!--#d1420ff6e2ef8337-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._filter_stale_calls` (method) — Drops calls whose owning step the flow has already moved past, with an exemption keeping retry-decision chips visible on a FAILED step. <!--#290a9c80a50fe843-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._dedup_calls_by_step` (method) — Keeps only the newest unanswered call per (flow_id, step_id) so superseded clarification-round leftovers don't pile up as stale chips. <!--#252191d67ed75681-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._parse_call_file` (method) — Builds a PendingCall from one call file, reading its JSON body for display metadata with legacy fallbacks for kind/prompt/flow_id. <!--#8f422e8874df3dbe-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._read_summary` (method) — Returns the most recent `summary-*.json` summary text for a flow, if any. <!--#a4e35352515c5261-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._collect_issues` (method) — Reads open/ and closed/ issue YAML files from `se3/issues/` into IssueSnapshots, skipping worktree-copy roots to avoid double-counting. <!--#438a56a40451673e-->
- `_is_resumable_status` (function) — Returns whether a status string names a resumable flow — everything except `completed` qualifies. <!--#e302c0e8083cfeec-->
- `_normalize_root` (function) — Normalizes a project root to the canonical live-process-gate key by folding worktree copies to their main root and resolving symlinks. <!--#a89e080d5bf58c7b-->
- `_resumable_with_live_gate` (function) — Computes a flow's resumable flag, tightening it to False only for a RUNNING flow whose root still has a live process. <!--#0f5ece84b5759a40-->
- `_safe_mtime` (function) — Returns a path's mtime, or None if it does not exist or is unreadable. <!--#11651aaac368a47d-->
- `_safe_stat` (function) — Returns a path's (mtime, size) tuple, or (0.0, 0) when unreadable, for change-signature fingerprinting. <!--#854c07daef0261c7-->
- `_read_json` (function) — Reads and parses a JSON file, returning None on any OS or parse error. <!--#5d8c043c7c84672b-->
- `_call_step_id` (function) — Resolves the step a PendingCall belongs to, preferring its `step_id` field then `context.step_id`, else None. <!--#6fb85d6e474a8859-->
- `_call_sort_key` (function) — Returns a recency sort key (created_at mtime, then call_id tie-breaker) for a PendingCall. <!--#7c1a397b9866544b-->
- `_current_step` (function) — Resolves a human-readable current-step label from a flow `state` dict. <!--#b7b602ad33735782-->
- `_count_dir` (function) — Counts regular files anywhere under a path (0 if it does not exist). <!--#745c695aa4dafe04-->
- `_count_issues` (function) — Counts open issue YAML records under `se3/issues/` (the open/ subtree). <!--#2150e54506de74da-->

### `src/se3/daemon/client.py` (python) — Defines DaemonClient, the daemon's NAT-friendly outbound WebSocket client that maintains a single auto-reconnecting connection to the central server, pushing STATUS_UPDATE/HISTORY snapshots and dispatching inbound server commands (spawn, respond, interject, end-session, issue, and history requests) to injected handlers. <!--#33f53c8ddf1522d8|3c5e7059aab0f2aa-->
- `_format_exc` (function) — Helper returning a guaranteed-non-empty, key-safe one-line description of an exception (falling back to its type name) for recording as the connection's last-error reason. <!--#6bb7dce1e7c8ec76-->
- `_normalize_ws_url` (function) — Helper that normalizes any user-supplied server URL into a canonical `ws(s)://host:port/ws` form, filling in scheme-aware default ports and preserving explicit ports/paths/IPv6 literals. <!--#b5332febe335055e-->
- `DaemonClient` (class) — The outbound WebSocket client class linking one daemon to the central server, owning the connection lifecycle, push/receive loops, and dispatch of server-issued commands. <!--#34d13b6281afdcd6-->
  - `DaemonClient.__init__` (method) — Constructor wiring in the machine identity, daemon credential, snapshot/history/calls providers, and the spawn/resume/respond/end-session/ensure handlers, plus push-interval configuration. <!--#6cec22787ab7c539-->
  - `DaemonClient.connected` (method) — Property reporting whether an active WebSocket session is currently established. <!--#5831c223727779da-->
  - `DaemonClient.last_error` (method) — Property returning the most recent connection error string, if any. <!--#d8d98d202de9e6d8-->
  - `DaemonClient._next_seq` (method) — Helper that increments and returns a monotonically increasing per-client message sequence number. <!--#f2490b69e1cbed2e-->
  - `DaemonClient.run` (method) — Top-level coroutine that lazily imports `websockets`, then connects/serves/reconnects with capped exponential backoff until the stop event fires or auth is rejected. <!--#11e83456424fefaa-->
  - `DaemonClient._session` (method) — Runs one full WebSocket session: sends HELLO, pushes an initial status/history snapshot, then races the receive, push, stop, and auth-rejection loops. <!--#9cf21569cd90b8ed-->
  - `DaemonClient._receive_loop` (method) — Reads inbound frames off the socket, decodes them, and dispatches each to its handler until the socket closes or shutdown is requested. <!--#eecbd577cc3ed509-->
  - `DaemonClient._push_loop` (method) — Single coroutine driving both STATUS_UPDATE and HISTORY pushes — on the steady heartbeat, on disk/calls signature changes, or on a fast-push trigger — sharing one socket so sends never interleave. <!--#8107e6c4a29107fd-->
  - `DaemonClient._wait_next_tick` (method) — Waits one fast tick racing the timeout against the stop event and the fast-push event, returning whether a fast-push actually woke the loop. <!--#b0d8ca12e0865a9e-->
  - `DaemonClient._calls_changed` (method) — Returns whether the `se3/calls/` directory fingerprint changed since last check (updating cached signature), so a new/drained interjection triggers an immediate status push. <!--#77712dc7033b695c-->
  - `DaemonClient._trigger_fast_push` (method) — Sets the sticky fast-push event to wake the push loop immediately for an out-of-band STATUS_UPDATE after a local side-effect. <!--#f6a684584badbf4c-->
  - `DaemonClient._history_changed` (method) — Returns whether any active flow's on-disk signature changed since last check (updating cached signature), gating incremental history pushes. <!--#06513e0308cc1743-->
  - `DaemonClient._dispatch` (method) — Routes a single decoded inbound server message to the appropriate handler based on its protocol message type. <!--#4fc9438ae2892fdf-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_welcome` (method) — Processes the server's WELCOME, treating `accepted=false` as a credential rejection that records the reason and signals the session to stop reconnecting. <!--#bd8d13ba2607d1c4-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_spawn` (method) — Routes an incoming SPAWN_FLOW to the resume, project-init, or fresh-spawn path, reporting genuine launch failures back to the server as SPAWN_FAILED. <!--#1513026d3992a89f-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_respond` (method) — Routes a RESPOND_CALL to the response-file writer, resolving a missing project root from the history index so worktree/discovery sessions land correctly. <!--#efd813b2ed490d81-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_interject` (method) — Routes an INTERJECT_FLOW to the interjection-file writer (resolving the project root if absent) then fires a fast push so the pending chip surfaces within ~1s. <!--#4de62f88a34aeb37-->
  - `DaemonClient._resolve_interject_root` (method) — Resolves a flow's project root from the current machine snapshot (off-thread), falling back to the history index, for an INTERJECT_FLOW lacking an explicit root. <!--#3be56fff4b123f3b-->
  - `DaemonClient._resolve_flow_root_from_index` (method) — Resolves a flow_id's project root from the TTL-cached history index so respond/interject/end-session writes match the history-read scope. <!--#925a6b4ab18ff7b0-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_end_session` (method) — Routes an END_SESSION to the injected end-session handler (resolving root from the index if omitted), which off-loads terminating the flow and archiving its worktree. <!--#06657bd3cb2169d7-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_issue_command` (method) — Validates and executes a server ISSUE_COMMAND against a registered project via IssueManager (off-thread), replying with an ISSUE_RESULT ack and triggering a fast push. <!--#97331081843b1f9b-->
  - `DaemonClient._execute_issue_operation` (method) — Synchronous dispatcher mapping create/edit/close/reopen issue operations to the corresponding IssueManager method and returning the affected issue ID. <!--#5883f40a7a7e6a85-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_history_request` (method) — Answers a server HISTORY_REQUEST by reading the requested flow's records (off-thread, honoring an optional cursor) and replying with HISTORY_DATA. <!--#33e0763a1fe1535f-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_history_index_request` (method) — Forces a fresh rebuild and re-push of the full history index when a browser enters the history view, bypassing the change debounce. <!--#8960fe7c8bb23353-->
  - `DaemonClient._send` (method) — Low-level helper that JSON-encodes a protocol message and sends it on the WebSocket. <!--#50c8cb5d7bc9fdb7-->
  - `DaemonClient._push_status` (method) — Builds a STATUS_UPDATE from the snapshot provider (off-thread to avoid stalling the loop), caches known project roots, and sends it. <!--#81316f953e552e1b-->
  - `DaemonClient._push_history` (method) — Pushes the history index (only when changed or forced) and ships per-active-flow incremental record deltas, maintaining cursors including retained ones for resumable terminal flows. <!--#12eab942a6e1b9ab-->
  - `DaemonClient._resumable_flow_ids` (method) — Returns the set of flow_ids still resumable from disk (live engine.json flows) via the provider, so a final-flushed FAILED flow's cursor is retained. <!--#d0588d10991a6ff5-->
- `_default_respond_handler` (function) — Default handler that atomically writes a `<call_id>.response.json` file into `<project_root>/se3/calls/` to feed a server response back into a paused flow. <!--#3cc084bfe323f24e-->
- `_default_interject_handler` (function) — Default handler that writes a mid-flow interjection request file into `se3/calls/` for the running `se3 run` process to drain at its next step boundary. <!--#7bf411ef69f626a3-->

### `src/se3/daemon/daemon.py` (python) — The resident SE3 daemon control-plane module: it defines the Daemon class (wiring supervisor, spawner, aggregator, and history reader) and its DaemonConfig, exposing spawn/resume/end-session/respond control surfaces over an async serve loop with a status-aggregation poll loop, plus helpers for pidfile/status-file management, signal handling, atomic JSON writes, and a persistent project-roots registry. <!--#f7c1a3c873a286e1|997766cb2c3400aa-->
- `_configure_daemon_logging` (function) — Installs a single idempotent, timestamped log handler for the daemon process so its log lines are attributable across detached and foreground modes. <!--#9280268fece7609c-->
- `_default_pid_dir` (function) — Returns the directory for daemon runtime files (pidfile/status/log), defaulting to ~/.se3 but overridable via the SE3_DAEMON_DIR env var for test isolation. <!--#64e9a9b21d5ed8cd-->
- `DaemonConfig` (class) — Dataclass holding daemon configuration (server URL, credential, pid_dir, poll cadences, machine id, project roots) with derived path properties for its runtime files. <!--#4f7cb1e690ecf0cf-->
  - `DaemonConfig.__post_init__` (method) — Coerces the configured pid_dir into a Path after dataclass construction. <!--#c8319b96022c643e-->
  - `DaemonConfig.pid_file` (method) — Property giving the pidfile path under pid_dir. <!--#db80f9021d5529bf-->
  - `DaemonConfig.status_file` (method) — Property giving the status-file path under pid_dir. <!--#1d551dccb5cefe59-->
  - `DaemonConfig.log_file` (method) — Property giving the daemon log-file path under pid_dir. <!--#1ad7ba864a0ad3ee-->
  - `DaemonConfig.project_roots_file` (method) — Property giving the persistent project-roots registry file path under pid_dir. <!--#bd196da4c4c0757e-->
- `Daemon` (class) — The resident control-plane class that wires together supervisor, spawner, aggregator, and history reader and exposes spawn/resume/end-session/serve control surfaces. <!--#3e62325a1a6c1890-->
  - `Daemon.__init__` (method) — Constructs the daemon, instantiating the supervisor/spawner/aggregator/history-reader and wiring the project-roots registry load/persist/live-roots callbacks. <!--#426c4d284fa0f563-->
  - `Daemon.request_spawn` (method) — Spawns a new `se3 run` flow (optionally discovery/worktree/from-issue) and registers its project root with the aggregator. <!--#2bbb2d056b412ce6-->
  - `Daemon.request_resume` (method) — Resumes a paused/interrupted flow by locating it in engine.json or the per-flow resumable snapshot, rejecting only COMPLETED flows and guarding against double-spawn into a live root. <!--#7b489448a3abeddb-->
  - `Daemon.request_end_session` (method) — Terminates and archives a supervised (or dangling worktree) flow by dispatching an `se3 end-session` subprocess so grace-waits and archival stay off the event loop. <!--#80a7f53b17992e5a-->
  - `Daemon._live_project_roots` (method) — Returns the set of project roots that currently have a live `se3 run` process, using the same supervisor/is_alive view as the resume double-spawn guard, to gate the RUNNING-flow resumable flag. <!--#7f1555c5a2eb317e-->
  - `Daemon.snapshot` (method) — Returns a fresh MachineStatus aggregation snapshot from the aggregator. <!--#18881f0b4dc950ac-->
  - `Daemon.stop` (method) — Signals the running event loop to shut down gracefully by setting the stop event. <!--#8c421937c52e8b71-->
  - `Daemon.run_forever` (method) — Foreground entry point that configures daemon logging and runs the async serve loop until interrupted. <!--#28c8017c1d0d57e6-->
  - `Daemon.serve` (method) — Async main that writes the pidfile, installs signal handlers, and runs the poll loop plus optional outbound server client concurrently until stopped, then cleans up. <!--#2334b4771bbff6f3-->
  - `Daemon._start_server_client` (method) — Lazily creates the outbound DaemonClient asyncio task (wiring snapshot/spawn/resume/end-session/respond/history handlers) only when a server_url is configured. <!--#266d6b30d3d101a2-->
  - `Daemon._handle_spawn_request` (method) — Adapts an inbound server SPAWN_FLOW message into a request_spawn call. <!--#4fb879526798f301-->
  - `Daemon._handle_resume_request` (method) — Adapts an inbound server SPAWN_FLOW-with-resume_flow_id message into a request_resume call. <!--#a1397f1fc3be07ee-->
  - `Daemon._handle_end_session_request` (method) — Adapts an inbound server END_SESSION message into a request_end_session call. <!--#785f8ebae74029dc-->
  - `Daemon._handle_ensure_request` (method) — Pre-spawn hook that runs `se3 init` on a target directory if needed and registers the freshly-initialized root with the aggregator. <!--#73697a39cd470777-->
  - `Daemon._handle_respond_request` (method) — Adapts a server RESPOND_CALL by writing the response file to se3/calls and then re-spawning the now-answerable PAUSED flow with --resume. <!--#dd2ea42bc295b24b-->
  - `Daemon._resume_paused_flow` (method) — Best-effort re-spawn of a project's flow with --resume when its engine.json shows PAUSED and no live process is already running in that root. <!--#dbe99ca43ec124c4-->
  - `Daemon._poll_loop` (method) — Aggregation poll loop that runs `_poll_once` on a fixed interval until the stop event fires, swallowing per-iteration errors. <!--#6a4660ef372ac9a7-->
  - `Daemon._poll_once` (method) — A single aggregation tick that discovers/attributes flows, reaps the spawner, and builds+persists a status snapshot (offloading the history-sized snapshot build to a worker thread). <!--#cda1de4cb289e0d4-->
  - `Daemon._install_signal_handlers` (method) — Wires SIGTERM/SIGINT to a graceful stop on the event loop, falling back to signal.signal on platforms without loop signal handlers. <!--#49b2ae2f6678bb85-->
  - `Daemon._shutdown` (method) — Terminates any spawned flows within the grace period and removes the status/pid runtime files on shutdown. <!--#943e2b7baa719500-->
  - `Daemon._write_pidfile` (method) — Writes the daemon pidfile (pid/start time/server/machine id), refusing to start if another live daemon already holds it. <!--#4e6caf9c4c17a9d6-->
  - `Daemon._write_status` (method) — Atomically persists the latest snapshot, tracked flows, and real outbound-connection state to the status file for `se3 daemon status` to read. <!--#1cccc946e76d9413-->
- `DaemonAlreadyRunning` (class) — RuntimeError subclass raised when a daemon is started while another instance is alive, carrying the conflicting pid. <!--#da58834df4e58342-->
  - `DaemonAlreadyRunning.__init__` (method) — Initializes the error with a message and stores the conflicting pid. <!--#75516beb68cdd4c3-->
- `_se3_version` (function) — Best-effort lookup of the installed SE3 version string, returning 'unknown' on failure. <!--#4b1a40eeb2d1b705-->
- `_read_pidfile` (function) — Reads and JSON-parses a daemon pid/status file, returning None if absent or corrupt. <!--#5aa376cf77d5cd0f-->
- `_pid_alive` (function) — Returns whether an int-like pid names a live process via os.kill(pid, 0), treating permission errors as alive. <!--#166d012dcd6de729-->
- `_atomic_write_json` (function) — Atomically writes a payload as JSON to a path using a temp-file-plus-rename. <!--#dcff051d0bc329f1-->
- `_read_project_roots` (function) — Reads the persisted project-roots registry document, treating a missing/corrupt/malformed file as an empty list. <!--#b0b841877c011e8d-->
- `_append_project_root` (function) — Appends a realpath-deduplicated (worktree-folded) project root to the registry file, rewriting it atomically only when a genuinely new root appears. <!--#a61acc56a3b3a66a-->
- `_sanitize_project_roots` (function) — One-time startup cleanup that drops any leaked worktree-copy entries from the registry file, rewriting only when something was removed and never blocking startup. <!--#ec9d803d3f0469c4-->
- `start_daemon` (function) — Public entry point that starts the daemon foreground (blocking) or fully detached via double-fork/subprocess, raising DaemonAlreadyRunning if one is already live. <!--#856f4e1148be83db-->
- `_start_detached_fork` (function) — Detaches the daemon via a classic double-fork (reparenting the real daemon onto init) and polls the pidfile before returning to the launcher. <!--#e621687e3abf6b96-->
- `_detach_streams` (function) — Redirects the detached daemon's stdin/stdout/stderr to /dev/null and the log file. <!--#02d4194e10a76e4a-->
- `_start_detached_subprocess` (function) — Fallback detach path for platforms without os.fork, launching `se3 daemon start --foreground` as a new-session subprocess and passing the daemon key via the environment. <!--#64cf11f07fad0ba3-->
- `stop_daemon` (function) — Signals a running daemon to shut down via SIGTERM and waits for it to exit, reporting stopped/not_running/stop_timeout. <!--#def767d191f88bfb-->
- `daemon_status` (function) — Reports whether the daemon is running plus its tracked flows, snapshot, and real outbound-connection state read from the pid/status files. <!--#472f7d019b97062f-->

### `src/se3/daemon/history.py` (python) — Implements `DaemonHistoryReader`, a read-only scanner of each tracked project root's `se3 history` artifacts that builds a per-flow session index (`SessionMeta`) for the central server/web UI and serves incremental, cursor-keyed (line-count) full-or-append reads of a flow's append-only jsonl conversation records, using a running full-prefix hash to detect in-place rewrites and `MAX_RECORDS_PER_REPORT` to bound each read. <!--#ba3cd38b5775647f|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/daemon/protocol.py` (python) — The single source of truth for the daemon↔server WebSocket wire protocol, defining the four-key JSON Message frame plus encode/decode helpers and per-type constructors (HELLO/WELCOME, spawn/respond/interject/end-session control, status/call notifications, issue commands, ping/pong, and history index/data) shared by both daemon and server to keep the schema from drifting. <!--#51374031d4812b5a|41acbd272640929c-->
- `ProtocolError` (class) — A ValueError subclass raised when a wire frame cannot be parsed as a valid protocol message. <!--#8844b8e7e818cf89-->
- `Message` (class) — A dataclass representing one protocol frame (type, payload, seq, timestamp) with serialization/parsing helpers to and from JSON dicts and strings. <!--#6d471563b76576f9-->
  - `Message.to_dict` (method) — Returns the JSON-friendly dict form of the message with its four canonical top-level keys. <!--#759de46712e4b25b-->
  - `Message.to_json` (method) — Serializes the message to a compact JSON string. <!--#4ea1594e9d498330-->
  - `Message.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that validates and builds a Message from a decoded JSON object, raising ProtocolError on a malformed or unknown-type frame. <!--#fc4a7b6821d1c6ea-->
  - `Message.from_json` (method) — Classmethod that parses a JSON string into a validated Message, raising ProtocolError on bad JSON or an invalid frame. <!--#e82ebe85cf35c624-->
- `encode` (function) — Builds a Message of the given type/payload/seq and returns it JSON-encoded in one call. <!--#3f319ca1e3054bfe-->
- `decode` (function) — Parses a raw JSON wire string into a validated Message. <!--#c008cfff05ac0ddc-->
- `make_hello` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server HELLO message announcing a daemon's machine identity, version, and optional secret owner key. <!--#e11c4df49538cc4c-->
- `make_welcome` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon WELCOME message acknowledging a HELLO with server version and acceptance status. <!--#a9085ee42f4fc840-->
- `make_status_update` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server STATUS_UPDATE message carrying an aggregated machine-status snapshot. <!--#7525f2e92673100b-->
- `make_call_notification` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server CALL_NOTIFICATION message reporting a freshly-detected pending human call. <!--#677dd0e2384a7f58-->
- `make_spawn_flow` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon SPAWN_FLOW message instructing a daemon to spawn, resume, or issue-spawn an se3 run flow (with optional discover/worktree flags). <!--#7f6c7841d5e5bfc9-->
- `make_spawn_failed` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server SPAWN_FAILED message reporting that a dispatched spawn/resume/project-init failed after the server already replied 202. <!--#1b569585789302df-->
- `make_respond_call` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon RESPOND_CALL message delivering a human response for a pending call. <!--#8aaa1c0ac739b1bf-->
- `make_interject_flow` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon INTERJECT_FLOW message delivering a mid-flow user interjection to be folded into a running flow. <!--#150211d4be0cc211-->
- `make_end_session` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon END_SESSION message instructing the daemon to terminate and archive a given flow. <!--#5db85a6d8a2b3c14-->
- `make_issue_command` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon ISSUE_COMMAND message requesting an issue write operation (create/edit/close/reopen) with operation-specific fields. <!--#ea7e983f451ab580-->
- `make_issue_result` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server ISSUE_RESULT message acknowledging an issue write command, correlated by request_id. <!--#81cd9f6eebb1d8f3-->
- `make_ping` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon PING heartbeat-probe message. <!--#b2c7fb1f30e8011c-->
- `make_pong` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server PONG heartbeat-reply message. <!--#2b41c9ace39e5f99-->
- `make_history_index` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server HISTORY_INDEX message reporting the list of known history-session metadata. <!--#fa0245e46e8a3b42-->
- `make_history_index_request` (function) — Constructs the payload-less server→daemon HISTORY_INDEX_REQUEST message forcing a fresh rebuild and re-push of the history index. <!--#946e3b425098a9e1-->
- `make_history_request` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon HISTORY_REQUEST message pulling a flow's history records, optionally with a per-step cursor for incremental fetch. <!--#b51051e6cfa89ccd-->
- `make_history_data` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server HISTORY_DATA message delivering a flow's history records as a full snapshot or incremental append, validating the mode. <!--#7644594449ab96a7-->

### `src/se3/daemon/spawner.py` (python) — Module providing the daemon's process-management layer for `se3 run` flows, centered on the `DaemonSpawner` class that resolves the `se3` CLI and a login-shell PATH, ensures projects are SE3-initialized, then spawns/resumes/ends flows as tracked child processes and polls, tails NDJSON logs, terminates, and reaps them. <!--#2abc526d74899ce2|c6c39984755248ef-->
- `resolve_login_shell_path` (function) — Probes `$SHELL -lc 'echo $PATH'` once at startup to recover the full login-shell PATH, returning it as a string or `None` on any failure without raising. <!--#5a7b63a33cc7dea2-->
- `merge_path_env` (function) — Combines a login-shell PATH ahead of the current PATH, deduplicating entries while preserving order, so spawned children inherit the richer PATH idempotently. <!--#97a7fecfa2117609-->
- `SpawnedProcess` (class) — Dataclass wrapping a spawned `se3 run` child's Popen handle plus metadata (project root, task, argv, start time, log files) with convenience properties and a JSON-serializable `to_dict`. <!--#685faf708e7f87df-->
  - `SpawnedProcess.pid` (method) — Property returning the child process's PID. <!--#723aab9ae510a1e7-->
  - `SpawnedProcess.returncode` (method) — Property returning the child's exit code, or `None` while it is still running. <!--#2ae567e522946e10-->
  - `SpawnedProcess.is_running` (method) — Property giving a non-blocking boolean probe of whether the child is still executing. <!--#46892e7692d315b1-->
  - `SpawnedProcess.to_dict` (method) — Returns a JSON-serializable dict of the process's PID, root, task, status, start time, and log paths. <!--#2405a3194bc0f30a-->
- `_resolve_se3_command` (function) — Resolves the argv prefix that invokes the `se3` CLI using same-interpreter-first fallbacks (sibling console script → `-m se3` → `shutil.which`) to avoid picking up a foreign environment's `se3`. <!--#be84eeb3635a4409-->
- `EnsureResult` (class) — Dataclass reporting the outcome of `ensure_se3_project` — whether init ran, any error to short-circuit on, and captured stdout/stderr. <!--#8ece94eff8859192-->
- `_is_se3_project` (function) — Returns whether a directory is already an SE3 project by checking for the durable `se3/charter.md` marker file. <!--#3a5427bfb36e813c-->
- `DaemonSpawner` (class) — The core class that starts, tracks, polls, tails, and terminates `se3 run` child flows for the daemon, caching login-shell PATH and optionally registering with a supervisor. <!--#c03d438af558dcf8-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.__init__` (method) — Constructs the spawner, wiring optional supervisor and spawn/exit callbacks and resolving/caching the login-shell PATH (unless overridden) once at startup. <!--#7eb90569d833fc11-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.ensure_se3_project` (method) — Ensures a directory is SE3-initialized, returning a no-op when the charter marker exists or otherwise spawning `se3 init -p <root>` and surfacing failures as an error result. <!--#f6d3b4fcbdfc5885-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.spawn` (method) — Builds the argv for a new `se3 run` flow (task or `--from-issue`, with optional `--discover`/`--worktree`) and launches it as a tracked child. <!--#8dcf15f1b32b3ed0-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.resume` (method) — Relaunches a paused flow by spawning `se3 run --resume --flow-id <id>` so it continues from persisted state after a human-call answer. <!--#986ef1903d45f4d3-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.end_session` (method) — Spawns `se3 end-session <flow_id>` (optionally with a `--pid` hint) to gracefully terminate and archive a flow off the daemon's event loop. <!--#eae1bede7b559482-->
  - `DaemonSpawner._launch` (method) — Shared launcher that builds the child env with merged PATH, opens per-flow log files, starts the Popen child, then tracks it and fires supervisor registration and the on-spawn callback. <!--#c47ee0388e45bb8a-->
  - `DaemonSpawner._allocate_log_paths` (method) — Computes timestamped stdout (`.ndjson`) and stderr log paths under `<root>/se3/logs/daemon/`, returning `(None, None)` if the directory can't be created. <!--#2972143c96485bbf-->
  - `DaemonSpawner._open_log_targets` (method) — Opens the stdout/stderr log files for Popen redirection (falling back to DEVNULL on failure) and returns the targets plus handles for the caller to close. <!--#f4e9be468f03f95c-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.get` (method) — Returns the tracked `SpawnedProcess` for a given PID, or `None`. <!--#afe4d346453eb0a2-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.processes` (method) — Returns a snapshot list of all currently tracked spawned processes. <!--#98f0b6899e671ee8-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.poll` (method) — Non-blocking exit-code probe for a tracked PID, returning `None` while it runs or is untracked. <!--#9ddea01204faba20-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.wait` (method) — Blocks up to a timeout for a tracked PID to exit and returns its code, raising `TimeoutExpired` if still running. <!--#1e54bd90cc51f142-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.iter_events` (method) — Tails a child's stdout log file, yielding each line parsed as an NDJSON event dict and stopping once the child has exited and the log is drained. <!--#b4e8468ca8557bde-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.terminate` (method) — Gracefully stops a tracked PID via SIGTERM, waits the grace period, then escalates to SIGKILL, returning the exit code. <!--#a3530ad10bca19d0-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.terminate_all` (method) — Gracefully terminates every still-running tracked process. <!--#2c13b58e7138e052-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.orphans` (method) — Returns the tracked processes still running that would be orphaned if the daemon exited. <!--#b330fd95d71db3f9-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.reap` (method) — Drops tracking for finished children, firing supervisor de-registration and the on-exit callback, and returns the reaped processes. <!--#e777ee62d549b294-->

### `src/se3/daemon/supervisor.py` (python) — Implements the SE3 daemon's process-supervision layer: a thread-safe DaemonSupervisor that maintains a PID→FlowRecord map of local `se3 run` processes, polling for liveness to reap dead ones and fire exit callbacks, registering daemon-spawned flows, and discovering externally-started ones via best-effort psutil command-line scanning (attributing worktree sandbox copies back to their main project root). <!--#9d97ba5e6eaca8f2|a64a9787734b2ab8-->
- `FlowRecord` (class) — Dataclass holding metadata for one supervised `se3 run` process (pid, project root, flow id, task, origin, start time). <!--#c0bf1436f2eb3589-->
  - `FlowRecord.to_dict` (method) — Returns a JSON-serializable dict of the record's fields. <!--#db07055256e060a1-->
- `_is_alive` (function) — Returns whether a pid names a live process using `os.kill(pid, 0)`, treating permission errors as alive. <!--#cefb5946976f093c-->
- `resolve_worktree_main_root` (function) — Maps a `<main>/se3/worktrees/<name>` isolation-sandbox path back to its main project root (or None if the path isn't such a worktree), so worktree copies aren't registered as standalone projects. <!--#abf7cf1fc461bcce-->
- `is_worktree_copy_root` (function) — Returns whether a path is an se3 worktree isolation copy directory, i.e. whether resolve_worktree_main_root would attribute it back to a main root. <!--#3d0c3c74dfc13264-->
- `_read_flow_id` (function) — Best-effort read of `flow_id` from a project's `se3/state/engine.json`. <!--#75acae2e5c6e9449-->
- `DaemonSupervisor` (class) — Thread-safe registry that tracks, reaps, and discovers local `se3 run` processes, firing exit callbacks when supervised processes die. <!--#d8f99d6e40c1f51e-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.__init__` (method) — Initializes the empty flow map, re-entrant lock, and exit-callback list. <!--#df9c702e787b6a06-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.register` (method) — Tracks a pid as a supervised flow (updating metadata in place if already known) and returns its FlowRecord. <!--#553d17a1289ca485-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.unregister` (method) — Stops tracking a pid, returning its record if it was tracked. <!--#974100ca92149eb8-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.on_exit` (method) — Registers a callback invoked once per process found dead during reaping. <!--#bf51ed3636e3c140-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.is_alive` (method) — Static wrapper exposing `_is_alive` to report whether a pid is a live process. <!--#92412c191d795dea-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.reap` (method) — Prunes records for exited processes, firing exit callbacks (errors swallowed) and returning the reaped records. <!--#e3b14bf6bd4807b3-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.discover_flows` (method) — Reaps dead processes, optionally scans for external `se3 run` processes, and returns all tracked flows sorted by start time. <!--#8c7c75225573f74f-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor._scan_external` (method) — Best-effort psutil scan that finds externally-started `se3 run` processes and registers them (attributing worktree sandboxes back to their main root). <!--#39314f3967af3eb8-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.get` (method) — Returns the FlowRecord for a pid, or None if untracked. <!--#8e9bd7dae72840c9-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.flows` (method) — Property returning a snapshot list of all tracked records. <!--#e98310c8ea90711a-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.count` (method) — Property returning the number of currently-tracked records. <!--#7a98b600786cd252-->
- `_cmdline_is_se3_run` (function) — A structural predicate that inspects a process's psutil-observed argv to decide whether it is a genuine `se3 run` invocation, matching only the console-script (`se3 run`) and module (`python -m se3 run`) launch shapes where `run` immediately follows the se3 program/module token, while excluding Python inline `-c` stubs and unrelated subcommands to prevent false-positive WebUI aggregation. <!--#176b92a5d4a3ad4a-->

## `src/se3/engine/` — The core SE3 flow-engine package: a program-controlled state machine that drives LLM-backed task execution (discovery → analyze → plan → implement → test → commit/summarize) through pluggable step handlers, formatters, merge, and utility subpackages, supported by context assembly, an incremental code-index/render subsystem, charter and chat-history management, an event-stream/interaction-call human-in-the-loop channel, DAG-based parallel scheduling, baseline-fix memory, docs/version syncing, and Rich console display. <!--#d5e76123ac94dddf|f0513d711ebc37a1-->

### `src/se3/engine/__init__.py` (python) — Public package interface for the SE3 flow engine, re-exporting the core state-machine, persistence, LLM-caller, schema, logging, and event-stream/sink types (and aliasing EventEmitter as EventStream) that drive program-controlled workflow execution. <!--#bdee0c4d523b5958|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/baseline_fix_memory.py` (python) — A cross-flow persistent store (schema-versioned, atomically-written, LRU-bounded JSON at se3/state/baseline_fix_attempts.json) recording which inherited baseline test failures the fix loop has given up on, so future flows skip re-attempting the same un-fixable failures. <!--#c501d64f879331ae|4b4720d265c83075-->
- `memory_path` (function) — Returns the path to the baseline-fix memory JSON file (se3/state/baseline_fix_attempts.json) under a given project root. <!--#9eec86eaec770cfb-->
- `_read_entries` (function) — Corruption-tolerant reader that loads the memory's entries map, returning an empty dict on any missing/corrupt/schema-mismatched file rather than raising. <!--#d3d6de9e35eb54ba-->
- `load_given_up` (function) — Returns the set of test ids already given up on, reading an empty set when the store is missing or corrupt. <!--#27086faf5a83f3a9-->
- `load_given_up_details` (function) — Returns the full per-test_id metadata map (attempts/reason) so callers can surface why a baseline failure was abandoned. <!--#62d3a0c6091dc142-->
- `record_given_up` (function) — Atomically marks test ids as given-up, accumulating attempt counts and latest reason while LRU-trimming the store to MAX_ENTRIES. <!--#e31f6cbd4ec5c077-->

### `src/se3/engine/charter.py` (python) — Module managing se3's project charter: locating, loading, and rendering the charter.md file, plus a non-blocking altitude gate that warns when a changed charter exceeds a byte-size threshold. <!--#fdd8144b525c3736|a5d98fa17461a9b0-->
- `AdmissionResult` (class) — Dataclass capturing the outcome of the charter altitude gate: byte size, threshold, advisory over-threshold flag, the normative admission-standard text, and an optional monitoring-light warning. <!--#254a712e6734b8f1-->
- `charter_path` (function) — Returns the absolute path to se3/charter.md for a given project root. <!--#65a9fce46453f1c5-->
- `load_charter` (function) — Reads the full charter text for whole-text injection, degrading to an empty string (never raising) when the file is missing or unreadable. <!--#dfbea1c686094d59-->
- `load_charter_template` (function) — Returns the raw packaged charter.md template text without any placeholder substitution. <!--#14e46cbcc4abd4d3-->
- `render_charter_template` (function) — Renders the packaged charter template by literal-replacing {key} placeholders, leaving incidental braces untouched, for use by init/migrate. <!--#30f6fa7d05c57c78-->
- `_changed_paths_touch_charter` (function) — Helper that returns True iff se3/charter.md appears among the changed files, matching on the path tail to tolerate relative/absolute and Windows-separator forms. <!--#44ee47271579de1f-->
- `admission_check_for_changes` (function) — Trigger point that runs the altitude gate only when the charter was actually changed, returning the AdmissionResult or None when the charter is untouched. <!--#82c6810331ea6f27-->
- `check_admission` (function) — Runs the charter altitude gate against given text, computing a non-blocking monitoring-light warning when the UTF-8 byte size exceeds the threshold and attaching the normative admission standard. <!--#d2630d46b30139ac-->

### `src/se3/engine/chat_history.py` (python) — Chat history subsystem that records each flow step's LLM prompts and responses as JSON-serialized ChatMessage lines in se3/history/{flow_id}/{step_id}.jsonl, supporting retry-context injection, per-turn token/agent/model metadata, user interjections, and human-readable conversation browsing. <!--#aae32e64b5ddcf98|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->
