### `src/se3/engine/code_index.py` (python) — The code-index engine that builds a deterministic, gitignore-respecting structure map of the project — enumerating directories, files, and within-file symbols (via AST/markdown/yaml/json extraction or last-resort chunk degradation), fingerprinting each node for incremental staleness detection, and bottom-up LLM-summarising them into the single authoritative, self-sufficient `se3/code-index.md` written atomically under an advisory build lock. <!--#28cc73f025c77584|0d15b6b6f30c1992-->
- `Fingerprint` (class) — A dataclass holding one file's content fingerprint — cheap mtime/size signals plus the authoritative sha256 prefix used as the change signal. <!--#9451c48c84db3103-->
- `Symbol` (class) — Dataclass for one within-file node (class/function/method, structural unit, or degraded chunk) carrying its id, kind, location, hash, summary, and optional verbatim content. <!--#a009f18727b02756-->
- `FileEntry` (class) — Dataclass holding one enumerated file's path, kind, fingerprints (whole-file plus a direct-symbol-roster 'list' fingerprint that gates reuse without cascading on body edits), summary, and extracted child symbols. <!--#c08141b42a516794-->
  - `FileEntry.symbol_id` (method) — Returns a symbol's full id by joining the file's relpath and the symbol's local id with '::'. <!--#c3974e13d18e0fdf-->
- `CodeIndex` (class) — Dataclass representing the in-memory structure map — a relpath→FileEntry table plus per-directory summaries, recursive content fingerprints, and direct-child list fingerprints — and able to reconstruct a render-only instance from the authoritative md via from_md. <!--#45de87d959de8cc5-->
  - `CodeIndex.from_md` (method) — Classmethod that rebuilds a render-sufficient CodeIndex by parsing directory headings, file headings, and symbol bullets out of the authoritative md, capturing only structure and summaries (fingerprints left zeroed). <!--#1ad25495637898a3-->
- `_split_fp` (function) — Helper that strips an md line's embedded fingerprint comment, returning the bare line plus its parsed content-fp and (optional) list-fp before any heading/bullet regex runs. <!--#fca7095dc35bd53e-->
- `_fp_comment` (function) — Helper that renders the trailing fingerprint HTML comment for an md line, emitting the legacy single-fp shape or the dual content|list shape when a list-fp is supplied. <!--#af268880669ba2d9-->
- `SummaryTarget` (class) — A dataclass describing one node (symbol, file, or directory) that needs an LLM summary, carrying its id, owning path, kind, name, and content to summarise. <!--#784c7c0812cd97aa-->
- `_sha256_prefix` (function) — Returns a hex sha256 of the given bytes truncated to a configurable prefix length. <!--#4a3d0b21f35268a9-->
- `_sha256_text` (function) — Hashes a string by UTF-8 encoding it and delegating to _sha256_prefix. <!--#4f7607d84cf5f60a-->
- `_fp` (function) — Helper that truncates a node's sha256 to the first `_FP_LEN` hex chars for embedding in the md. <!--#7dc034e8bbda50ba-->
- `_slice_lines` (function) — Returns the 1-based inclusive line range of a list of lines joined by newlines, clamping out-of-range bounds. <!--#b6d736c0ae3a5c02-->
- `_extract_python` (function) — Extracts top-level classes/functions and class methods from Python source via AST, stopping at the function/method level. <!--#8977c5a354cfcd6a-->
- `_extract_markdown` (function) — Extracts markdown headings (ignoring fenced code blocks) as structural units, each spanning to the next heading. <!--#e78a2c67046c83eb-->
- `_line_of_top_key` (function) — Best-effort lookup of the 1-based line number where a top-level YAML/key declaration appears. <!--#cf55f29734a6211c-->
- `_extract_yaml` (function) — Extracts top-level YAML mapping keys as symbols, carrying each key's serialized value as content. <!--#03759e3e86c28e59-->
- `_extract_json` (function) — Extracts top-level JSON object keys as symbols, carrying each key's serialized value as content. <!--#915a274e73e1db64-->
- `_extract_structure` (function) — Dispatches structural extraction to the right per-extension extractor, returning [] when none applies or none is found. <!--#25e24dfeb6fb8a76-->
- `_file_kind` (function) — Classifies a file as python/markdown/yaml/json/text by its extension. <!--#8090ae4dd5164009-->
- `is_degrade_eligible` (function) — Returns whether a file qualifies for last-resort chunk degradation by requiring all three conditions: text, no structure, and over a size threshold. <!--#08b26f76b777e5f6-->
- `_chunk_degraded` (function) — Splits a structure-less oversized file into line/byte-bounded chunks, each emitted as one degraded symbol. <!--#93818e7aaf52f59e-->
- `_index_file` (function) — Builds a structural FileEntry for one path (no summaries) — handling binary/unreadable files, structural symbol extraction, oversized-file collapsing, and structure-less degradation to chunks. <!--#d4b21d66db7f2546-->
- `md_path` (function) — Returns the path to the authoritative se3/code-index.md under the project root. <!--#f147cb0ac2d3f6ee-->
- `lock_path` (function) — Returns the path of the advisory build-lock file under the gitignored `se3/cache/` directory. <!--#d9a84f9915e55bf2-->
- `_build_lock` (function) — Context manager holding an exclusive advisory flock across a build's load→enumerate→write critical section to serialize concurrent rebuilds, falling back to unlocked when fcntl is unavailable. <!--#bfdd14e1fa8107ed-->
- `_atomic_write_text` (function) — Writes text to a path atomically via a unique per-write temp file plus os.replace, so concurrent writers never clobber each other. <!--#b1565ce44f841b76-->
- `_dir_of` (function) — Returns the directory key of a file's immediate parent directory. <!--#29c094ab2953dd41-->
- `_parent_dir` (function) — Returns the parent directory key of a directory key (None for the root). <!--#a3be6ae8fa72d759-->
- `_depth` (function) — Returns the nesting depth of a directory key (root = 0). <!--#106ed76edc8752c9-->
- `_all_dir_keys` (function) — Computes the set of every directory key in the tree — every ancestor of every file plus the root. <!--#a754c18a54352d82-->
- `_child_files` (function) — Returns the sorted relpaths of files whose immediate parent directory is the given directory key. <!--#a60e7ddda26ff7ca-->
- `_child_dirs` (function) — Returns the sorted directory keys whose immediate parent is the given directory key. <!--#336d66009c59273a-->
- `_compute_dir_fps` (function) — Computes a recursive per-directory content fingerprint bottom-up so any change in a subtree propagates up and re-summarises every ancestor while untouched siblings reuse cached summaries. <!--#eb5bf3ca6ead4260-->
- `_compute_file_list_fp` (function) — Computes a file's mechanical 'list' fingerprint by hashing only its direct symbols' sorted (kind, name) roster — ignoring bodies, summaries, position, and order — so body-only edits don't change it. <!--#06db726193d7e3a4-->
- `_compute_dir_list_fps` (function) — Computes each directory's non-recursive 'list' fingerprint by hashing only its direct child names (immediate files and subdirs), so a deep edit never bubbles up and each level reuses independently. <!--#51135b8b8c0187f7-->
- `render_full` (function) — Renders the complete authoritative md map — every directory level, file, and symbol — embedding each node's content (and list) fingerprint only when it already has a real summary so partial flushes stay safe resume points. <!--#4b2fc507f56d93d1-->
- `_write_md` (function) — Atomically writes the rendered authoritative md for an index to its md path. <!--#e0d9f93ae34e6f6a-->
- `_parse_md` (function) — Parses the authoritative md into three node-id-keyed maps (reusable summaries, content fingerprints, and migrated file/dir list fingerprints), reading everything from the committed md with no out-of-band cache. <!--#75f859777f45cf86-->
- `_parse_md_summaries` (function) — Convenience wrapper returning just the `{id: summary}` map from the parsed md. <!--#7b2c20ea52847695-->
- `_flatten_summary` (function) — Collapses an LLM summary's whitespace (including newlines) to a single physical line so the one-node-per-line md format isn't corrupted. <!--#ab4fda75898c4eba-->
- `_heuristic_summary` (function) — Produces a deterministic placeholder summary used when no LLM is available or a call fails, keeping builds from crashing. <!--#5e95c0cfd0580e7b-->
- `_make_llm_summarizer` (function) — Constructs the default LLM-backed summariser that batches targets per owning path into one LLMCaller call requesting a JSON id→summary map, degrading to heuristic summaries on any failure. <!--#f2caca61766d0821-->
- `_make_target` (function) — Builds the summary target for a symbol (using its own content or a line slice) or, as a fallback, a file node from its own source. <!--#3bcb90fc368a7d51-->
- `_make_file_target` (function) — Builds a file's summary target bottom-up — from a digest of its symbols' one-line summaries, or its own source when it has no symbols. <!--#303ef86543b2fdf0-->
- `_make_dir_target` (function) — Builds a directory's summary target bottom-up from its immediate child subdirectory and file summaries. <!--#0490470f87f95416-->
- `_summarize_wave` (function) — Summarises one dependency wave of targets and assigns the results back onto their directory, symbol, or file nodes, skipping the LLM entirely for an empty wave. <!--#10d6a3897e48eae1-->
- `build_index` (function) — The single (re)build entry point that enumerates the project, extracts structure, incrementally summarises changed nodes bottom-up, and writes the authoritative md, all under the advisory build lock. <!--#3168b57596673d1d-->
- `_build_index_locked` (function) — The locked body of build_index: parses the prior md, deterministically enumerates files and computes all fingerprints, defines the content-fp and list-fp reuse gates, then seeds reused summaries before incrementally re-summarising only changed nodes bottom-up. <!--#5ff2bb1a6adc9131-->
- `load_or_build` (function) — Lazy-incremental (re)build entry point that delegates to build_index, refreshing only changed nodes (or everything when forced). <!--#98bae63f723837c9-->

### `src/se3/engine/code_index_render.py` (python) — Renders the authoritative `se3/code-index.md` into two display views over a CodeIndex: `render_adaptive`, a byte-budgeted zoomable root tree always injected into flow steps, and `render_path`, a deterministic one-level drill-in at a given path. <!--#1a3403083146467c|ab45c8f67a44ae70-->
- `load_for_display` (function) — Reconstructs a render-only CodeIndex from the authoritative `se3/code-index.md` on disk, returning None when no build has produced that file yet. <!--#efdde682055b6a2a-->
- `_top_of` (function) — Returns the top-level ancestor directory key of a given directory key (or the key itself if already top-level). <!--#42c3cefff4559ca3-->
- `_auto_primary_roots` (function) — Auto-detects the code-bearing top-level directories to treat as primary expansion roots, falling back to all top-level dirs when none contain code. <!--#6ea444b4ecf816de-->
- `_subtree_file_counts` (function) — Computes, in one pass, the number of files contained in the subtree of every directory by incrementing each file's ancestor directories. <!--#7afffc3c5eead1ed-->
- `_render_view` (function) — Renders the directory tree as a bulleted markdown map, descending only into the expanded directories and showing files under expanded parents. <!--#ef2c6ecc16fafe5c-->
- `_expansion_costs` (function) — Precomputes the byte cost of expanding each directory (its immediate children block) so the render budget can be checked incrementally in O(1) per candidate. <!--#af7dd118de471c22-->
- `render_adaptive` (function) — Produces the byte-budgeted zoomable root view, expanding frontier directories shallowest-and-densest-first within primary roots until the budget is exhausted. <!--#d164459ab4fc6ed8-->
- `_render_file_detail` (function) — Helper that formats a single file's heading plus its indented function/method symbol tree, marking degraded symbols. <!--#68467cdf328f6577-->
- `_render_one_level` (function) — Renders exactly the immediate children (subdirs and files) of a single directory key as a markdown section. <!--#0ecd37d78e015b3a-->
- `render_path` (function) — Renders the one-level drill-in view for a given path — root level, a file's full symbol tree, a directory's immediate children, or a not-found note. <!--#e9351a5830007db3-->

### `src/se3/engine/context.py` (python) — Defines the read-only Context class that wraps a workflow State to expose display-friendly task-type properties (task_description, task_type, display_type, is_type_pending) for use during step execution and in the UI. <!--#dfe0eb26098689ec|20549d4ad681ed99-->
- `Context` (class) — Read-only context object that wraps workflow State and exposes display-friendly task-type properties for step execution and UI. <!--#eeb1bd891048e5a1-->
  - `Context.__init__` (method) — Constructor storing the original task description and the workflow State reference. <!--#8242df2429226234-->
  - `Context.task_description` (method) — Property returning the original task description string. <!--#9ad8135cc0823e21-->
  - `Context.task_type` (method) — Property resolving the current task type by checking resolved type, explicit --type flag, flow attribute, then falling back to 'pending'. <!--#49a739a8909c96df-->
  - `Context.display_type` (method) — Property returning the resolved task type for UI display, or None when still pending. <!--#9a4275ef7830af06-->
  - `Context.is_type_pending` (method) — Returns whether the task type is still unresolved, delegating to State's method when available. <!--#a8174bd77d016406-->
  - `Context.__repr__` (method) — Debug string representation showing the task type and pending status. <!--#ac43d00ede6802c8-->

### `src/se3/engine/context_builder.py` (python) — Central context-assembly module that builds the per-step prompt injections for run-engine LLM calls — language instructions, charter, code-index, spec-names, runtime-environment/issue-discovery fragments, read-only and spec-write-protection constraints, and worktree runtime context — and provides the ContextBuilder class plus the LLM-review prompt builder for loading spec content and reviewing step output. <!--#e9eb10c259da6cac|3ff4c561df5a4882-->
- `get_step_language_instruction` (function) — Returns the language instruction to append to a run-engine step's prompt, routing spec steps to spec_language, human-facing/confirmed steps to the general language, and everything else to no injection. <!--#69f7354a76473892-->
- `get_spec_language_instruction` (function) — Gives the sync_* modules (which write specs outside the run state machine) the same spec_language instruction that update_spec gets. <!--#49b519e028c50c1e-->
- `_load_runtime_environment_markdown` (function) — Reads and process-caches runtime_environment.md, returning empty string with a one-time warning on read failure. <!--#c69d2cc539e7ddc0-->
- `_reset_runtime_environment_cache` (function) — Test-only helper that clears the runtime_environment.md cache so reload paths can be exercised. <!--#8fcfcfa91ac8350c-->
- `get_runtime_environment_injection` (function) — Returns the se3 runtime-environment capability markdown for whitelisted steps (default list overridable via se3.yaml, minus always-forbidden steps). <!--#e2ac12eb9ac7a402-->
- `get_issue_discovery_injection` (function) — Returns the B-class issue-discovery prompt fragment for steps in the configurable whitelist and not in the forbidden set. <!--#bbb89699dda1eaf7-->
- `get_spec_names_injection` (function) — Builds the 'available specifications' injection listing all specs and which are already loaded, instructing the LLM to consult others on demand via the read-only `se3 spec` index commands. <!--#f54620f6f99f8ee6-->
- `get_charter_injection` (function) — Returns the project charter (se3/charter.md) wrapped in a labelled section, injected in full on every step as the authoritative convention channel. <!--#2427642e166932b4-->
- `get_code_index_injection` (function) — Builds the per-step prompt injection that orients the agent to the project's code-index, returning the drill-down protocol header plus either the adaptive byte-budgeted root-map tree (read from se3/code-index.md) or a note explaining how to build the map when it doesn't yet exist. <!--#d89f20fa7ce38fde-->
- `ensure_code_index_fresh` (function) — Best-effort lazy-incremental rebuild of se3/code-index.md (only if already built) so consuming steps inject a fresh map. <!--#0fbc8b2e65fe72d8-->
- `is_step_read_only` (function) — Predicate that determines whether a given step type runs under read-only constraints by consulting STEP_POOL attributes plus sync-engine and internal pure-data step sets, serving as the single source of truth for both prompt-level read-only injection and tool-level enforcement. <!--#06ae86fbd04076e4-->
- `get_read_only_injection` (function) — Returns the read-only constraint prompt fragment (forbidding any file modification) for steps that is_step_read_only flags. <!--#c0de90dc60e4cd0c-->
- `_is_spec_write_protected_step` (function) — Returns True for non-read-only LLM steps not in SPEC_WRITE_ALLOWED_STEPS, identifying steps that must be barred from writing spec files. <!--#6cf953afe2ce2135-->
- `get_spec_write_protection_injection` (function) — Returns the spec-file write-protection prompt fragment for spec-write-protected steps, forbidding edits under se3/specs/ while leaving code changes free. <!--#f405841f29eb8970-->
- `get_runtime_context_injection` (function) — When running in a worktree, injects context about gitignored runtime state (open issues, flow state, history) that exists only in the main repository. <!--#40ad7d8911426794-->
- `_detect_main_repo_root` (function) — Detects the main repository root from a worktree path via git's --git-common-dir, returning None if detection fails. <!--#d5041cfe6374379d-->
- `ContextBuilder` (class) — Class providing specs-directory resolution and spec-content loading for the analyze and discovery handlers. <!--#9edf18ec74038306-->
  - `ContextBuilder.__init__` (method) — Initializes the builder with a project root and resolves its specs directory. <!--#7c2a9e8da739c1ae-->
  - `ContextBuilder._resolve_specs_dir` (method) — Static helper resolving the specs directory, preferring se3/specs/ then specs/ then the legacy openspec/specs/. <!--#1d639c614f0c5fc6-->
  - `ContextBuilder._load_spec_content` (method) — Loads a spec's text by name, trying several candidate paths and returning None if none exist. <!--#8cd7e0c8ec088d86-->
- `build_llm_review_prompt` (function) — Builds the structured prompt for LLM-based review of a step's output, formatting the output, optional revision feedback, evaluation criteria, and required JSON response format. <!--#bf66f623e57bd0bb-->

### `src/se3/engine/dag_scheduler.py` (python) — Module implementing DAG-based parallel execution of task groups, classifying graph topology into a relay/fork/convergence plan and driving concurrent group execution (via a thread pool) with worktree relay contexts, failure propagation, and topological merge ordering. <!--#9f4a305db6d4857c|8e398420b3a80b98-->
- `ConvergenceInfo` (class) — Dataclass capturing, for a node with multiple predecessors, which predecessor's worktree is inherited (primary) and which predecessors' branches are merged in (secondary). <!--#1b7a60866faacf8e-->
- `RelayContext` (class) — Runtime context handed to the executor telling a group how to obtain its worktree — reuse a predecessor's, fork a new branch, or create fresh — plus any convergence branches to merge. <!--#05abe19424a373e2-->
- `RelayPlan` (class) — Dataclass holding the full relay execution strategy (relay map, fork sources, leaf/root nodes, convergence points) produced by classify_chains and consumed by the scheduler. <!--#06c133c34947e5d3-->
- `classify_chains` (function) — Analyzes DAG topology to produce a RelayPlan, deciding per group whether to create a new worktree, relay from a primary predecessor, fork, or merge at a convergence point. <!--#a14041499502d9b6-->
- `_relay_plan_is_linear` (function) — Helper returning True when a RelayPlan describes a single-root, fork-free linear chain, letting callers skip DAG-parallel execution that would yield no parallelism. <!--#195dd89fd4eb9574-->
- `GroupResult` (class) — Dataclass representing the outcome of executing one task group (status, files/tests changed, branch, worktree, completion details) with skipped/failed constructor helpers. <!--#c16bb24282ecaca3-->
  - `GroupResult.skipped` (method) — Classmethod constructing a GroupResult marked as skipped because an upstream dependency failed. <!--#41b078e164946dde-->
  - `GroupResult.failed` (method) — Classmethod constructing a GroupResult marked as failed with the given error message. <!--#fb9f926def640ccf-->
- `DAGScheduler` (class) — Core class that builds a validated DAG from group dependencies and drives parallel execution via ThreadPoolExecutor + Condition, emitting per-group lifecycle status and building relay contexts. <!--#2a8c65cc167d157f-->
  - `DAGScheduler.__init__` (method) — Initializes the scheduler's config and DAG bookkeeping structures and builds the DAG from the supplied groups. <!--#7fbf3b1d94a456b5-->
  - `DAGScheduler._emit_status` (method) — Safely invokes the optional on_group_status callback, swallowing and logging any exception so a faulty status sink cannot disrupt scheduling. <!--#6944feb1a073cafa-->
  - `DAGScheduler._build_dag` (method) — Builds the group map, forward/reverse adjacency, and in-degrees from depends_on edges and validates the graph is acyclic. <!--#1d7fc2a08282d9bd-->
  - `DAGScheduler._kahn_topo_sort` (method) — Computes a topological ordering of groups via Kahn's algorithm, with a short result signaling a cycle. <!--#e8ecf8fb870b4c2b-->
  - `DAGScheduler._build_relay_context` (method) — Constructs a RelayContext for a group from the relay plan and completed predecessor results, resolving worktree reuse, fork source, and convergence merge branches. <!--#50778ecfac8bbe73-->
  - `DAGScheduler.run` (method) — Executes all groups in dependency order, submitting ready groups to a thread pool, propagating failures to downstream groups, and returning their GroupResults. <!--#a61ec96384e2fe46-->
  - `DAGScheduler.get_fallback_leaves` (method) — Returns completed groups whose downstream all failed or were skipped (excluding normal leaves), so their valid work can be merged back as fallback. <!--#516fb66a7a14bfae-->
  - `DAGScheduler.topological_merge_order` (method) — Returns groups in topological order to guide the sequence of branch merges back to the main branch. <!--#277ba115a8b5b1be-->

### `src/se3/engine/display.py` (python) — A Rich-based console rendering module that displays LLM outputs, specs, proposals, designs, code, diffs, markdown, and token-usage summaries in full without truncation, using reverse-color title/footer blocks for visual framing. <!--#9a57487a4d8def77|542b7c7ad2425872-->
- `get_console` (function) — Lazily creates and returns the module-global Rich Console singleton. <!--#34af9b63623b3216-->
- `set_console` (function) — Overrides the module-global Console instance, mainly for testing. <!--#3c900a44fe46127f-->
- `_reverse_title` (function) — Builds a reverse-color ` ## Title ` heading as a Rich Text object on a colored background. <!--#548f67b20e68a7ec-->
- `_reverse_footer` (function) — Builds a fixed-width reverse-color whitespace block used as a block's bottom boundary marker. <!--#b3b374c4e5cfae09-->
- `render_block_header` (function) — Public wrapper that prints a reverse-color block title followed by a blank line. <!--#6bc1573d1ddb863c-->
- `render_block_footer` (function) — Public wrapper that prints the fixed-width reverse-color block footer followed by a blank line. <!--#b02ffd2b25f0e7e4-->
- `render_usage_block` (function) — Renders a UsageTotals/dict/None as an aligned two-column token-and-cost summary in a cyan reverse-color block, printing nothing when usage is empty. <!--#f3feaa318bfa6c55-->
- `render_full` (function) — Prints arbitrary content in full without truncation, optionally wrapped in a blue title/footer block. <!--#cc2bafbda92f1b83-->
- `render_proposal` (function) — Formats and renders a proposal dict (summary, files to modify/create, rationale, extra fields) as a styled block. <!--#002534cc42d11146-->
- `render_design` (function) — Formats and renders a design-document dict (overview, components, interfaces, decisions, extras) with section headers. <!--#693dd10657726d53-->
- `render_spec_content` (function) — Formats and renders a spec dict (metadata header, description, requirements, extra sections) as a styled block. <!--#6824d1fe5aa32281-->
- `render_text` (function) — Renders plain text left-aligned with an optional title block and optional Rich style. <!--#02638b45c952b7be-->
- `render_code` (function) — Renders code with syntax highlighting and line numbers under an optional green title block. <!--#5b51ac6cd6788d16-->
- `render_diff` (function) — Renders a unified diff with red/green/cyan coloring and line numbers, truncating after max_lines. <!--#73c936866411a923-->
- `render_markdown` (function) — Renders markdown content via Rich's Markdown under an optional magenta title block. <!--#57673343920809b3-->

### `src/se3/engine/docs_updater.py` (python) — Module providing a template-driven DocumentationUpdater that keeps a project's README.md version badge/header and VERSIONS.md changelog in sync via configurable, precedence-ordered templates. <!--#3ff5229bed399a3f|1664cf9bff7dfad6-->
- `_versions_md_template_path` (function) — Module-level helper returning the path to the packaged versions_md.md template (resolved relative to this module so tests can monkeypatch it). <!--#76ac7c1506576aea-->
- `_versions_entry_template_from_file` (function) — Reads the first ## section of the packaged versions_md.md template and returns it as a fallback entry template only if it contains the required {{version}} and {{changes}} placeholders, else None. <!--#fcd606d5ab77c4ed-->
- `Template` (class) — Simple template holder that substitutes {{key}} placeholders with merged default and context values. <!--#aa02c2559079b161-->
  - `Template.__init__` (method) — Stores the template content string and an optional dict of default placeholder values. <!--#4aeb58f2bd29890e-->
  - `Template.render` (method) — Returns the content with each {{key}} replaced by its value from the merged placeholder/context dictionary. <!--#3ea1ee9e956e5b1b-->
- `DocumentationUpdater` (class) — Updates a project's README.md (version badge/header) and VERSIONS.md (changelog entries) using configurable, precedence-ordered templates. <!--#77d34d9f26420f69-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.__init__` (method) — Stores the project root and config, then loads the template set via _load_templates. <!--#bdedeb61dfc386a6-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._load_templates` (method) — Builds the readme_badge, optional readme_header, and versions_entry templates from config with file/default fallbacks. <!--#92a84c251a5f850e-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.update_readme` (method) — Reads README.md, replaces its version badge (and header if configured), and writes back only if the content changed; raises if README.md is missing. <!--#04e75a628f5ca34d-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._build_context` (method) — Constructs the base render context (version, current date, year) merged with any additional context. <!--#df355d4c1e939574-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._replace_version_badge` (method) — Replaces an existing version badge by regex, or inserts a freshly rendered badge after the title heading (skipping YAML front-matter and leading HTML comments). <!--#b5f47aef81a18505-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._replace_version_header` (method) — Replaces the first matching version-header line in README content using the configured readme_header template, leaving content unchanged if none exists. <!--#5eba858b38211444-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.update_versions_md` (method) — Renders a new changelog entry and inserts it into an existing VERSIONS.md (or creates the file with a header if absent). <!--#9d948f317e8bb930-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._format_changes` (method) — Formats a list of change strings into markdown bullet lines, returning a placeholder line when the list is empty. <!--#cc657081348cb54d-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._insert_version_entry` (method) — Inserts a new entry after the VERSIONS.md header while skipping duplicates of an already-present version. <!--#d40abdb7e31b4267-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._create_new_versions_md` (method) — Returns brand-new VERSIONS.md content with a 'Version History' header followed by the first entry. <!--#1f2a677e05d7bc42-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.render_template` (method) — Renders a named template with the given context, raising KeyError if the template is not registered. <!--#ed1913f03093bd06-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.add_template` (method) — Registers a custom named template with optional default placeholders. <!--#a2e403c04c0432e5-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.update_both` (method) — Convenience method that updates both README.md and VERSIONS.md, returning a dict of per-file success flags and tolerating missing files. <!--#e95fc6040805098f-->

### `src/se3/engine/event_stream.py` (python) — Defines the SE3 flow engine's unified in-memory event stream: an EventType enum of flow/step lifecycle events, an Event dataclass with dict round-trip serialization plus a new_event factory, and an EventEmitter pub/sub hub that fans each event out to subscribed rendering sinks with failure isolation and scoped subscriptions. <!--#bb8c44fc6ab62e7c|a0e685a12504c7b1-->
- `EventType` (class) — A str-backed Enum enumerating every flow-lifecycle event type (flow started/paused/completed/failed, step started/output/completed/failed, interjection/call needed) with JSON-serializable string values. <!--#5042d02dff7f81ca-->
- `Event` (class) — Dataclass representing one structured stream event (type, timestamp, flow/step ids, step type, arbitrary data payload) with dict serialization round-trip helpers. <!--#8025abee4638212c-->
  - `Event.to_dict` (method) — Serializes an Event to a plain JSON-friendly dict, reducing the type enum to its string value and passing data through verbatim. <!--#c81b31aedb4967c2-->
  - `Event.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that reconstructs an Event from a to_dict payload, supplying defaults for missing optional fields. <!--#e7515b91e274fa52-->
- `new_event` (function) — Convenience factory used by run_flow that builds an Event, collecting keyword payload arguments into its data dict. <!--#3da965c97a496c47-->
- `EventEmitter` (class) — In-memory pub/sub hub holding an ordered list of subscribed sinks and fanning each emitted Event out to them, with isolation against failing sinks and a scoped-subscription context manager. <!--#13f76d85d2b8b4ac-->
  - `EventEmitter.__init__` (method) — Initializes the emitter with an empty subscriber-sink list. <!--#777bfe63b8aa5014-->
  - `EventEmitter.sinks` (method) — Property returning a copy of the currently subscribed sinks in subscription order. <!--#6eaaeda2e99bfed6-->
  - `EventEmitter.subscribe` (method) — Registers a sink to receive future events, ignoring duplicate subscriptions of the same instance. <!--#91dda552eaf06e71-->
  - `EventEmitter.unsubscribe` (method) — Removes a sink from the subscriber list, silently ignoring sinks that aren't subscribed. <!--#7e72619f09833308-->
  - `EventEmitter.emit` (method) — Delivers an event to every subscribed sink in order, swallowing any sink exception so one rendering fault can't break delivery or the flow. <!--#8494582ed4c615e6-->
  - `EventEmitter.scope` (method) — Context manager that snapshots the subscriber list on entry and restores it on exit, so subscriptions made inside the block are automatically undone. <!--#c65503c1b0064a8d-->

### `src/se3/engine/file_enum.py` (python) — Enumerates the deterministic, sorted set of files the code-index should cover—combining git-tracked and untracked-non-ignored paths, applying se3/ and configured glob exclusions, and providing helpers to measure file size and detect binary files. <!--#d6d81694c0b30a0d|7524aebd7fe113ac-->
- `_is_se3_path` (function) — Predicate returning True when a relative path lies inside the always-excluded `se3/` runtime directory. <!--#894fc5809a6f598a-->
- `_git_ls_files_paths` (function) — Runs `git ls-files` to return the index view of every tracked file's relative path, returning empty on git failure. <!--#d5658f06054df9fb-->
- `_git_ls_files_other` (function) — Runs `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` to return untracked-but-not-ignored files so new files are picked up without registration. <!--#056a2ea4677d010d-->
- `matches_exclude` (function) — Secondary glob-based guard testing whether a relative path matches any explicit `code_index.exclude` pattern, with basename and directory-subtree conveniences. <!--#65ebacc0b391b57e-->
- `is_binary` (function) — Sniffs a file's leading bytes to classify it as binary (NUL byte or largely-undecodable UTF-8) so the indexer keeps it at a single file-level line. <!--#25bf9ae9141d17de-->
- `FileSize` (class) — Dataclass holding a text file's cheap size measurement as line count and byte count. <!--#47930e403c8c718f-->
  - `FileSize.from_bytes` (method) — Classmethod constructing a FileSize from already-read content without re-reading the file. <!--#4179f5c88553b475-->
- `measure_file` (function) — Reads a file and returns its FileSize, or None if it cannot be read. <!--#cfe51f3a660821c6-->
- `enumerate_index_files` (function) — Top-level entry point returning the deterministic, sorted set of absolute file paths the code-index should cover (tracked ∪ untracked-non-ignored, minus se3/, excludes, and deleted ghosts). <!--#e76522edfbc770fc-->

### `src/se3/engine/interaction_calls.py` (python) — The single producer/consumer helper for the unified `se3/calls/` file channel, atomically reading and writing kind-tagged JSON call files and their sibling response files that represent every human-in-the-loop interaction in a running flow (MCP calls, mid-flow interjections, retry/failure decisions, and CLI-subprocess confirmations) in a backward-compatible format the daemon and web console can route. <!--#1ce1f12dc54766b8|0634ff752c4ef491-->
- `calls_dir_for` (function) — Returns the `se3/calls/` directory path for a given project root. <!--#652a81f197a424a6-->
- `classify_kind` (function) — Resolves a parsed call dict's interaction kind, defaulting legacy or unrecognized files to `CALL_KIND_CALL` so old artifacts work without migration. <!--#880f7c9758d2615c-->
- `write_call` (function) — Atomically writes a call file of a given kind with prompt/context/options payload, returning its path. <!--#5eb93b7be0ca617f-->
- `read_call` (function) — Parses a call file into a dict (always carrying a `kind` key), returning `None` on any read/parse error. <!--#a51ef169b9c2eacf-->
- `response_path` (function) — Returns the canonical sibling `.response` path for a given call file. <!--#6943622212596f29-->
- `read_response` (function) — Returns the parsed sibling answer file, recognizing both `.response` and `.response.json` variants, or `None` if none exists. <!--#f16ade7359cac25c-->
- `write_response` (function) — Atomically writes a sibling `.response` answer file (wrapping non-dict values) and returns its path. <!--#8d02ff1e8ce9e6d0-->
- `write_interjection_request` (function) — Daemon-side producer that queues a mid-flow interjection as a `CALL_KIND_INTERJECTION` call file for the running `se3 run` to consume. <!--#965c0f08272a7e6a-->
- `drain_interjection_requests` (function) — The `se3 run` consumer that scans for unanswered interjection call files and returns them oldest-first, sealing each via an idempotent write-response-then-delete protocol. <!--#3dedded011a0e8c7-->
- `write_retry_decision_call` (function) — Writes a `CALL_KIND_RETRY_DECISION` call file for a failed step on the no-TTY path, externalizing the Retry/Skip/Abort prompt for a web console to answer. <!--#92af625ef122d099-->
- `write_interaction_call` (function) — A project-root-addressed convenience wrapper around `write_call` that folds extra keywords into the call payload. <!--#c59f01ec4147bea5-->
- `read_interaction_response` (function) — Returns the bare answer value for a call (unwrapping `{response: ...}` envelopes from either `.response.json` or plain `.response`), or `None` when no answer exists yet. <!--#318712f1706b9339-->
- `make_cli_confirm_handler` (function) — Builds an `on_confirm` callback for the agent runner that writes a `cli_confirm` call file, polls for the sibling response while the subprocess lives, and marks orphaned calls consumed if the child exits unanswered. <!--#1f5d19c172a19a06-->

### `src/se3/engine/issue_discovery.py` (python) — Flow-engine module implementing automatic issue discovery via A-class system triggers (e.g. fix-loop exhaustion, pre-existing failures) and B-class whitelist-based prompt injection/collection, plus a scoped executor for LLM-emitted create/update/delete issue operations, with title-based deduplication and zero-padding-tolerant ID matching. <!--#370d7905d149a5d6|fbd916824bfc4e68-->
- `_normalize_issue_id` (function) — Helper that strips leading zeros from an issue ID so zero-padded variants like '5' and '005' compare equal in membership checks. <!--#3d9056ee5983eaff-->
- `apply_discovery_issue_operations` (function) — Engine-side executor that runs LLM-emitted create/update/delete issue intents for a discovery step, enforcing the tracking-set scope guarantee and isolating each operation so one failure doesn't abort the batch. <!--#ffeb9af8ec081bdb-->
- `_apply_create` (function) — Creates a new issue with source='human' and adds its ID to the discovery step's tracking set. <!--#3c972612bf74020d-->
- `_apply_update` (function) — Updates a tracked issue's editable fields (title/description/priority/type/tags only), rejecting out-of-scope IDs and dropping malformed non-list tags. <!--#8108bd67f54f0192-->
- `_apply_delete` (function) — Deletes a tracked issue and removes its ID from the tracking set, rejecting out-of-scope IDs. <!--#cebe0d8a0b5000ed-->
- `IssueDiscovery` (class) — Class managing per-flow automatic issue discovery (A-class system triggers and B-class prompt-injection collection) with title-based deduplication. <!--#eef0d8fdc803f19f-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.__init__` (method) — Initializes the discovery instance with an IssueManager, flow ID, and an empty list of created titles for deduplication. <!--#1292078f24c6befe-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.create_from_fix_loop_exhaustion` (method) — A-class trigger that builds and creates a high-priority bug issue (source=system) when the fix loop hits max iterations, embedding flow context, test output, and fix history. <!--#0857f45fd5b99585-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.create_from_pre_existing_failures` (method) — A-class trigger that creates a medium-priority issue documenting inherited baseline test failures not introduced by the current change. <!--#bf9800b8f2e5bb00-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.get_injection_prompt` (method) — Returns the issue-discovery prompt fragment for whitelisted step types (B-class injection), or None otherwise. <!--#2979579ce1738652-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.collect_issues_from_output` (method) — B-class collector that parses a whitelisted step's discovered_issues output and creates deduplicated source=system issues from each valid entry. <!--#2b8bce29a5aede95-->
  - `IssueDiscovery._is_duplicate` (method) — Checks whether a title matches any already-created title in this flow using normalized similarity comparison. <!--#1a096e2f501e6ea8-->
  - `IssueDiscovery._normalize_title` (method) — Normalizes a title for comparison by lowercasing, stripping punctuation, and collapsing whitespace. <!--#28516bc357948272-->
  - `IssueDiscovery._titles_similar` (method) — Determines if two normalized titles are near-duplicates via exact match or >70% token-overlap ratio. <!--#16f9009715e698f8-->

### `src/se3/engine/issue_manager.py` (python) — Module implementing the SE3 issue tracker: an Issue dataclass plus an IssueManager that creates, loads, lists, edits, and transitions issues stored as YAML files across open/ and closed/ directories with monotonic ID allocation. <!--#2612385733255c69|6e31e636104dfff2-->
- `IssueStatus` (class) — Enum of the five issue lifecycle states (open, in-progress, resolved, won't-fix, closed). <!--#decbedd5a7c9f2d6-->
- `Issue` (class) — Dataclass representing a single issue record with serialization helpers and a derived display title. <!--#ff53e1ff54ead2d9-->
  - `Issue.display_title` (method) — Property that returns a human-readable title, falling back from explicit title to the first non-empty description line to "untitled". <!--#1a19b1f1da95d214-->
  - `Issue.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the issue to a YAML-ready dict, including optional fields only when set. <!--#5baf46152d4ccfe9-->
  - `Issue.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that deserializes an issue from a dict, tolerating missing/legacy fields and parsing timestamps defensively. <!--#1fb4f2a14503faab-->
- `_make_slug` (function) — Helper that converts a title into a lowercase, hyphenated URL/filesystem-friendly slug. <!--#0de7a9734d3c82a6-->
- `_derive_slug_for_issue` (function) — Helper that derives a filename slug for an issue using the same title-priority logic as display_title. <!--#f32424f3c00139e5-->
- `IssueManager` (class) — Class managing the full issue lifecycle—create, load, list, update status, edit fields, and move files between open/ and closed/ directories. <!--#aa158747baa1b981-->
  - `IssueManager.__init__` (method) — Initializes the manager with the project root and resolves the issues, open, and closed directory paths. <!--#072700a6b770b364-->
  - `IssueManager._ensure_dirs` (method) — Creates the open/ and closed/ issue directories if they don't already exist. <!--#8e38a3b44bcd372f-->
  - `IssueManager._next_id` (method) — Allocates the next monotonic zero-padded issue ID using an flock-serialized counter file, falling back to scanning existing files. <!--#4128a9bd22de5140-->
  - `IssueManager._find_issue_file` (method) — Locates an issue's YAML file by ID across open/ and closed/, tolerating zero-padding differences. <!--#395484abb8bf782f-->
  - `IssueManager.create` (method) — Creates a new open issue from a required description (plus optional metadata), writing its YAML to open/. <!--#fe8f1910d7c1a7a6-->
  - `IssueManager.adopt_issue` (method) — Adopts an externally-originated issue under a freshly-allocated ID while preserving all other fields, used by merge runtime-sync. <!--#c267b3f816d023a3-->
  - `IssueManager.load` (method) — Loads and returns an issue by ID from open/ or closed/, or None if not found. <!--#020eb18913a1d3ab-->
  - `IssueManager.list_issues` (method) — Lists issues (open by default, optionally closed) with optional type and source filters, sorted by ID. <!--#83ee845dc598e516-->
  - `IssueManager.update_status` (method) — Validates and applies a status transition, updating the YAML and moving the file between open/ and closed/ as needed. <!--#d96cdeb912e9e247-->
  - `IssueManager.reset_to_open` (method) — Resets an in-progress issue back to open, erroring if it is in any other state. <!--#a22f7bfa163b4e22-->
  - `IssueManager.find_open_by_title` (method) — Finds an open issue whose display title case-insensitively matches the given title. <!--#83a2c1627c6282c0-->
  - `IssueManager.close_issue` (method) — Closes an open issue (falling back to resolved when needed) and moves its file to closed/. <!--#77684cefd8dabbd4-->
  - `IssueManager.delete_issue` (method) — Permanently deletes an issue's YAML file by ID with no status transition or file move. <!--#25390c6a0d56a160-->
  - `IssueManager.list_by_tags` (method) — Lists issues that contain all of the specified tags, optionally including closed ones. <!--#a4ef3ff5e8af3ded-->
  - `IssueManager.update_fields` (method) — Updates editable issue fields and renames the YAML file when the derived slug changes. <!--#712c1fc23aaca8f1-->
  - `IssueManager.reopen_issue` (method) — Reopens a closed/resolved/won't-fix issue back to open, moving its file to open/. <!--#53e5b2dd713901f3-->
  - `IssueManager._read_issue` (method) — Reads and parses an issue YAML file into an Issue, returning None on parse failure. <!--#33a506ffef4077af-->
  - `IssueManager._write_issue` (method) — Serializes an issue and writes it as YAML to the given filepath. <!--#26627c78c08ec256-->

### `src/se3/engine/json_extractor.py` (python) — Module providing JSONExtractor, a class that recovers a JSON dict from raw LLM output via a fast direct-parse path with a fallback second LLM pass (including stream-json assistant-text stripping), plus a convenience function wrapping the two-phase extraction. <!--#aaed016a6e055540|1d927ac6d6a985f9-->
- `JSONExtractor` (class) — Class that extracts a JSON dict from raw LLM output, trying a direct parse first and a lightweight second LLM pass as fallback. <!--#16dfa7c498bda86b-->
  - `JSONExtractor.__init__` (method) — Constructor storing the project root (for the LLM caller) and the extraction call timeout. <!--#5c1837782c47b8c5-->
  - `JSONExtractor.extract` (method) — Public entry point that returns parsed JSON via the direct-parse fast path, or delegates to LLM extraction when that fails. <!--#08106d958854572b-->
  - `JSONExtractor._try_direct_parse` (method) — Helper that attempts to parse the raw output directly using the shared json_parser utility without invoking an LLM. <!--#c74809bed98aaa51-->
  - `JSONExtractor._extract_text_from_stream_json` (method) — Helper that parses stream-json (NDJSON) output and concatenates the text content of assistant messages, dropping tool calls and results. <!--#1c3d95c718342e3c-->
  - `JSONExtractor._extract_with_llm` (method) — Fallback that strips stream-json to assistant text, prompts a non-JSON LLMCaller to restructure it into schema-complete JSON, and parses the result. <!--#903e5a4227f7fd73-->
- `extract_json_two_phase` (function) — Module-level convenience function that constructs a JSONExtractor and runs two-phase extraction in one call. <!--#f6b6bb2c3227af8b-->

### `src/se3/engine/json_modes.py` (python) — Defines the JsonMode enum of JSON extraction strategies (STRICT, EXTRACT, TWO_PHASE, OFF) and the get_json_mode resolver that picks one from explicit and legacy parameters by a fixed backward-compatible priority order, centralizing how LLM calls select structured-output handling. <!--#cb3ab8a5a880eec8|92767f0284f446eb-->
- `JsonMode` (class) — Enum enumerating the available JSON extraction strategies (STRICT, EXTRACT, TWO_PHASE, OFF) used to control how an LLM call produces structured output. <!--#3c44b448f5440910-->
- `get_json_mode` (function) — Resolves a JsonMode from a mix of explicit and legacy parameters (json_mode, two_phase_json, require_json), applying a fixed priority order for backward compatibility. <!--#45eacf3bde2932c4-->

### `src/se3/engine/llm_caller.py` (python) — Module that executes step prompts by invoking the Claude CLI via subprocess, handling retry/fallback logic, agent selection and rotation on infrastructure errors, and prompt deduplication with a defensive safety cap that truncates the retry-history head to keep prompts under a size limit while preserving the current prompt. <!--#f65493c1a0a56fc7|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/logging_config.py` (python) — Defines the flow engine's structured logging subsystem — log level/event-type enums, a serializable log-entry value object, and a singleton StructuredLogger that writes daily JSON-lines files with an in-memory buffer, console output, per-flow/step/LLM convenience methods, and log retrieval/export. <!--#2fb132f11a8b0f4c|7c79a7fcdeb5af16-->
- `LogLevel` (class) — String enum defining the five severity levels (debug through critical) used for log entries and filtering. <!--#0afc90c8e31e38f7-->
- `LogEventType` (class) — String enum enumerating the categories of flow-engine log events across flow, step, LLM, persistence, and tool operations. <!--#e6e9c091fe6eacd7-->
- `StructuredLogEntry` (class) — Value object representing a single structured log event with metadata and serialization to dict/JSON. <!--#b3501160ecd27907-->
  - `StructuredLogEntry.__init__` (method) — Constructs a log entry, stamping the current UTC timestamp and storing event type, level, and optional flow/step/LLM context. <!--#059a51e6b392ac75-->
  - `StructuredLogEntry.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the entry to a dictionary, omitting unset optional fields and rounding the duration. <!--#234f02f7ff69c0bf-->
  - `StructuredLogEntry.to_json` (method) — Serializes the entry to a JSON string via its dict representation. <!--#6f39524c89de5837-->
- `StructuredLogger` (class) — Logger that writes structured entries to a daily JSON-lines file, keeps an in-memory buffer, and optionally prints to the console. <!--#a23456e4a4234c8a-->
  - `StructuredLogger.__init__` (method) — Initializes the logger, setting up the log directory, daily log file, recent-log buffer, and timing trackers. <!--#64bdeda4cd028cef-->
  - `StructuredLogger._get_log_file` (method) — Returns the date-stamped JSON-lines log file path for the current day. <!--#4f29bb52bebeaebd-->
  - `StructuredLogger._should_log` (method) — Determines whether a given level meets the configured minimum threshold. <!--#60722b42c6fbf2cb-->
  - `StructuredLogger._write_log` (method) — Appends an entry to the current log file, updates the bounded in-memory buffer, and emits console output if enabled. <!--#845a6fa3db9a39bb-->
  - `StructuredLogger._console_output` (method) — Prints a human-readable, color-coded one-line summary of an entry to stderr. <!--#3428059cb34f263a-->
  - `StructuredLogger.log` (method) — Core logging method that builds a StructuredLogEntry and writes it if the level passes the threshold. <!--#b5c689d8f1d507d8-->
  - `StructuredLogger.flow_started` (method) — Convenience method logging a flow-started event with the task and task type. <!--#010d617a47430eb6-->
  - `StructuredLogger.flow_completed` (method) — Convenience method logging a successful flow-completion event with its duration. <!--#6334121e6557f6d8-->
  - `StructuredLogger.flow_failed` (method) — Convenience method logging a flow-failure event with the error and optional duration. <!--#19591ad845bb411a-->
  - `StructuredLogger.step_started` (method) — Starts a per-step timer and logs a step-started event. <!--#c898e0b04a6e3713-->
  - `StructuredLogger.step_completed` (method) — Logs a step-completion event with computed duration and optional outputs. <!--#16ba47376084468d-->
  - `StructuredLogger.step_failed` (method) — Logs a step-failure event with duration, error, and retry indication, downgrading severity when a retry will follow. <!--#b8368ebbb9097a76-->
  - `StructuredLogger.llm_call_started` (method) — Starts an LLM-call timer and logs the call-started event with model and prompt size. <!--#0b2900cc5c77e4b3-->
  - `StructuredLogger.llm_call_completed` (method) — Logs an LLM-call-completed event with duration and input/output token counts. <!--#634b0aa95a7ac233-->
  - `StructuredLogger.llm_call_failed` (method) — Logs an LLM-call-failure event with duration, model, and error. <!--#1a7b3576bbc26ef7-->
  - `StructuredLogger.state_saved` (method) — Convenience method logging a state-saved event referencing the persisted state file. <!--#593c9924dc51089d-->
  - `StructuredLogger.get_recent_logs` (method) — Returns recent buffered log entries, optionally filtered by event type and flow ID and capped by a limit. <!--#8c123a66b7b211f9-->
  - `StructuredLogger.export_logs` (method) — Reads all daily log files and exports matching entries (filtered by time and event type) to a JSON file, returning the count. <!--#cbed0084601dd847-->
- `get_logger` (function) — Module-level accessor that lazily creates and returns the singleton StructuredLogger instance. <!--#45e4799fe4cca297-->
- `reset_logger` (function) — Resets the global logger singleton, primarily for testing. <!--#1cb3faeb6146c533-->

### `src/se3/engine/models.py` (python) — Defines the flow engine's core serializable data models — the Step/StepType/StepStatus, Transition, State, and FlowInstance dataclasses and enums that hold a workflow run's steps, runtime state, review/fix iteration tracking, token usage, and lifecycle status, plus STEP_POOL lookup and default step-sequence helpers. <!--#41af8223064195c2|ed84091c78ea4db0-->
- `StepType` (class) — Enum enumerating every workflow step type in the step pool (analyze, plan, implement, test, invariant_check, commit, etc.), including ones deprecated by the charter refactor. <!--#d69394f16486bb4a-->
- `StepStatus` (class) — Enum of a step's execution lifecycle states (pending, running, completed, partial, failed, retrying, paused, revision_needed). <!--#38d6ab911468a93f-->
- `Step` (class) — Dataclass for a single workflow step holding its type, status, retry/model config, inputs/outputs, artifacts, and error tracking. <!--#9b413ca9a5717441-->
  - `Step.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a Step to a JSON-primitive dictionary. <!--#937fbe0c54931cab-->
  - `Step.from_dict` (method) — Reconstructs a Step from its serialized dictionary form. <!--#983c5b3b82ce612e-->
- `Transition` (class) — Dataclass describing a state-machine transition rule from one step type to another with an optional condition. <!--#7a2689d2166206ee-->
  - `Transition.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a Transition to a dictionary. <!--#4540da1b0410523c-->
  - `Transition.from_dict` (method) — Reconstructs a Transition from its serialized dictionary form. <!--#cdfa73691c44022b-->
- `State` (class) — Dataclass holding the engine's runtime state — current/selected steps, history, shared context, review/fix iteration tracking, test baseline, and cumulative token usage. <!--#25951dc7cfb0127d-->
  - `State.get_current_step` (method) — Returns the currently active Step, or None if none is set. <!--#918e318297b74364-->
  - `State.add_step` (method) — Registers a Step in the state, auto-generating a sortable human-readable step_id and appending it to history. <!--#8764118b5d041b38-->
  - `State.get_step_to_review` (method) — Finds the step preceding a given confirm step (the one being reviewed) from history. <!--#7a52d05a0edb06c5-->
  - `State.increment_review_iteration` (method) — Increments and returns the review-cycle iteration count for a given step. <!--#7dcf9130950ebe0b-->
  - `State.get_review_iteration` (method) — Returns the current review iteration count for a step (0 if never reviewed). <!--#19414144af977a06-->
  - `State.increment_fix_iteration` (method) — Increments the test-verify-fix loop counter, appends a capped history entry, and mirrors the count into context. <!--#3550ebf4a7e40719-->
  - `State.get_fix_iteration` (method) — Returns the current fix-loop iteration count. <!--#6b71e3bdd412a0bc-->
  - `State.update_task_type` (method) — Stores the analyze-step-resolved task type in the shared context. <!--#a1d6daf59f1e228d-->
  - `State.is_type_pending` (method) — Reports whether the task type has not yet been resolved. <!--#4e7aadf82393a590-->
  - `State.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the full State (including nested steps and token usage) to a dictionary. <!--#09070887b8ba08b2-->
  - `State.from_dict` (method) — Reconstructs a State from a dictionary, re-applying the fix-history cap and preserving tri-state baseline/usage backward compatibility. <!--#7d2b515cf04009e6-->
- `FlowStatus` (class) — Enum of a flow instance's overall lifecycle status (init, running, paused, completed, failed, recovering). <!--#2e96c050c86ed8d4-->
- `FlowInstance` (class) — Top-level dataclass for a single workflow run, bundling task info, the State, metadata/timestamps, change tracking, and worktree/lock state. <!--#e154c32133bf518d-->
  - `FlowInstance.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the flow instance to a dictionary, emitting waiting_for_lock only when actually waiting. <!--#39bfc2e2a3eb1289-->
  - `FlowInstance.from_dict` (method) — Reconstructs a FlowInstance from its serialized dictionary, defaulting newer fields for backward compatibility. <!--#78e16df247ad23b5-->
  - `FlowInstance.get_progress` (method) — Returns flow completion as a (completed_count, total_count) tuple. <!--#382fd14e9da0d282-->
- `get_step_info` (function) — Looks up a step type's metadata entry from the STEP_POOL. <!--#9d66a58a6cd35598-->
- `get_default_step_sequence` (function) — Returns the default ordered list of step types for a given task type (feature, bugfix, review, small, directive, discovery). <!--#79a8090f0e6cd94a-->

### `src/se3/engine/output.py` (python) — Utility module providing helpers to format arbitrary data into strings, log internal messages, and render formatted error/success output through the display module. <!--#ea4a9cc3154a0357|c0b1b9557353d0db-->
- `format_output` (function) — Converts any data type (string, dict/list as pretty JSON, else str) to a string representation without truncation, ignoring the deprecated truncate flag. <!--#1fb8dc97c460cf5b-->
- `log_output` (function) — Logs a message at a named level via the module logger, used for internal logging output that bypasses the display module. <!--#bcd99a66853b242d-->
- `format_error` (function) — Builds a formatted error string from an exception or message plus optional context dict, using rich markup for display. <!--#bde57deb611612c1-->
- `display_error` (function) — Formats an error with optional context and renders it in full under an 'Error' title via the display module. <!--#133e319df0e4d82e-->
- `display_success` (function) — Formats a success message with optional details and renders it in full under a 'Success' title via the display module. <!--#aaea6f8f9a0bdd98-->

### `src/se3/engine/output_formatter.py` (python) — Defines a FormatterRegistry class and module-level convenience functions providing a singleton name-to-formatter-class registry and factory for registering, looking up, instantiating, and listing output formatters (seeded with the default 'tasks' TaskFormatter). <!--#4dcdfd93fddf90e8|eca8291d052da2a1-->
- `FormatterRegistry` (class) — Class that maintains a name-to-formatter-class mapping and acts as a factory for instantiating formatters, seeded with default formatters on construction. <!--#059002186071d632-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.__init__` (method) — Initializes the empty formatter mapping and registers the default formatters. <!--#d42322823229516e-->
  - `FormatterRegistry._register_default_formatters` (method) — Registers the built-in default formatters (currently the 'tasks' TaskFormatter). <!--#e0ff2860430fe51d-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.register_formatter` (method) — Stores a formatter class under a given name, warning if it overwrites an existing registration. <!--#8566348c910c841e-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.get_formatter` (method) — Looks up and instantiates a formatter by name with optional constructor kwargs, returning None (and logging) on missing name or instantiation failure. <!--#56a1016d3a6b9cd2-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.list_formatters` (method) — Returns a dict mapping each registered formatter name to its class name. <!--#ad7a2621dacf661f-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.unregister_formatter` (method) — Removes a formatter by name, returning whether it was present. <!--#ec59bc018e1528a2-->
- `get_registry` (function) — Lazily creates and returns the module-level singleton FormatterRegistry. <!--#0450178df4985dc7-->
- `register_formatter` (function) — Module-level convenience that registers a formatter class on the global registry. <!--#defcad979b65f3de-->
- `get_formatter` (function) — Module-level convenience that retrieves a formatter instance from the global registry by name. <!--#f3cc7acf1ada4e92-->
- `list_formatters` (function) — Module-level convenience that lists all formatters registered in the global registry. <!--#cb28e95009c9c96e-->

### `src/se3/engine/persistence.py` (python) — Defines PersistenceManager, the flow engine's state persistence layer that uses atomic temp-file-then-rename writes to durably manage engine.json, per-flow resumable snapshots, context exports, backups, archiving, and fault-tolerant flow loading/listing. <!--#d0840887fa156f0c|e317b181f2546b75-->
- `PersistenceManager` (class) — Class that manages all flow-engine state persistence — the active engine.json, per-flow resumable snapshots, context exports, backups, archiving, and flow listing — using atomic temp-file-then-rename writes. <!--#69f0ff4aa4073478-->
  - `PersistenceManager.__init__` (method) — Constructor that derives the state directory layout (engine.json, context.json, resumable/) from the given project root. <!--#a532038611cca8d5-->
  - `PersistenceManager.ensure_directories` (method) — Creates the se3/state directory tree if it does not yet exist. <!--#b8a17d8d37aa3ed9-->
  - `PersistenceManager.save_flow` (method) — Atomically writes the flow to engine.json and, as the single convergence point, refreshes or clears its resumable snapshot based on completion status. <!--#b5ec0974777a2a21-->
  - `PersistenceManager.save_resumable_snapshot` (method) — Atomically writes a durable per-flow snapshot to resumable/<flow_id>.json that survives a later run overwriting the single-slot engine.json. <!--#8f60ffb2f83671dc-->
  - `PersistenceManager.load_resumable_snapshot` (method) — Loads and validates the resumable snapshot for a flow_id, rejecting mismatched-id or corrupt files by returning None instead of raising. <!--#96f71a2f842b21af-->
  - `PersistenceManager.clear_resumable_snapshot` (method) — Best-effort deletion of a flow's resumable snapshot file (used on normal completion). <!--#b0c25381c0f25e04-->
  - `PersistenceManager.list_resumable_snapshots` (method) — Returns all readable, id-consistent resumable snapshots as FlowInstances, skipping corrupt or mismatched ones. <!--#d409844219776f22-->
  - `PersistenceManager.load_flow_by_id` (method) — Locates a flow by id, preferring the active engine.json and falling back to its resumable snapshot. <!--#97f34e4b8cf52189-->
  - `PersistenceManager.load_flow` (method) — Loads the active flow from engine.json, falling back to the .bak backup if the main file is corrupted. <!--#e670c037e597284b-->
  - `PersistenceManager.load_flow_tolerant` (method) — Maximally fault-tolerant load that repairs truncated JSON, fills missing fields, falls back to backup, and never raises — returning the flow plus warning messages. <!--#7ba13678d79019a5-->
  - `PersistenceManager._try_repair_json` (method) — Helper that attempts to fix truncated JSON by trimming partial trailing data and closing unbalanced braces/brackets. <!--#45fdbf54c5b23a71-->
  - `PersistenceManager._tolerant_from_dict` (method) — Helper that builds a FlowInstance from a possibly incomplete dict, injecting defaults for missing required fields and recording warnings. <!--#03b6a0398ef4cc96-->
  - `PersistenceManager.create_backup` (method) — Copies the current engine.json to a .bak backup file, returning its path or None on failure. <!--#b7bea4c92cf007e5-->
  - `PersistenceManager.clear_state` (method) — Archives the current engine.json into state/archive with a timestamped name rather than deleting it. <!--#f4d954bd8823df76-->
  - `PersistenceManager.list_active_flows` (method) — Returns metadata for the single currently-active flow held in engine.json, if any. <!--#48ea8fd793831682-->
  - `PersistenceManager.list_all_flows` (method) — Aggregates flow metadata across active, archived, and history-only sources, de-duplicating by flow_id and sorting by most-recently-updated. <!--#262bca29b70bfb60-->
  - `PersistenceManager.extract_history_summary` (method) — Derives a short task-description title from a history directory's first JSONL file using a three-tier (user-marker / task-block / raw) priority. <!--#4499ec791bdb034d-->
  - `PersistenceManager.save_context` (method) — Atomically writes an AI-consumable context dictionary to context.json for handoff/resumption. <!--#71b404bb79559768-->
  - `PersistenceManager.export_context_from_flow` (method) — Builds context.json from a flow instance via the schema transformation and saves it. <!--#31ea57981e30f20b-->
  - `PersistenceManager.load_context` (method) — Loads the saved context.json, handling both the new direct and old nested formats. <!--#587d5c82f36df771-->
  - `PersistenceManager.export_progress_markdown` (method) — Renders a flow's steps and context as human-readable progress markdown derived from the JSON state. <!--#2d591e3b31f21aa2-->

### `src/se3/engine/project_context.py` (python) — Defines ProjectContextCollector, which aggregates project-wide context (git status, flow engine history, parsed backlog items, and available spec names) into a structured dict, plus a helper to list spec subdirectory names. <!--#e9c1f298e9b07b81|0c4f9aaf972f0d55-->
- `ProjectContextCollector` (class) — Class that gathers project-wide context from multiple sources (git, flow engine, backlog, specs) rooted at a project directory. <!--#68f3c4ac3bc2422e-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector.__init__` (method) — Constructor storing the project root path as a Path. <!--#9812ec98f69838a9-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector.collect` (method) — Aggregates git, flow_engine, backlog, and specs context into a single structured dict. <!--#837254f0d8b3e685-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._collect_git` (method) — Returns git status via the commands/status helper, falling back to an unknown-branch default on error. <!--#acb96af4ae25b142-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._collect_flow_engine` (method) — Returns flow engine history via the commands/status helper, or None on failure. <!--#056dd30cb3a17c33-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._collect_backlog` (method) — Scans se3/specs/_backlog/*.md files and returns a list of parsed backlog items. <!--#152900683ae6176d-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._parse_backlog_item` (method) — Parses a backlog markdown file's first lines to extract title, status, and phase. <!--#512c11b5f66af35a-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._collect_specs` (method) — Lists available spec names by delegating to ContextBuilder's specs directory. <!--#2d1aaf9b24d7374a-->
- `list_spec_names` (function) — Returns a sorted list of spec subdirectory names, excluding internal dirs prefixed with underscore. <!--#b4e64d015a4eff4f-->

### `src/se3/engine/prompt_dedup.py` (python) — A utility module that detects and collapses repeated contiguous line blocks in a prompt, replacing duplicate occurrences with content-hash `[DUPLICATED CONTENT:...]` markers to shrink redundant prompt text. <!--#14e7b640b0b10a2c|72b2d7612e58296b-->
- `deduplicate_prompt_lines` (function) — Scans a prompt for repeated contiguous line blocks of at least `min_block_lines`, keeping the first occurrence and replacing duplicates with content-hash-based `[DUPLICATED CONTENT:...]` markers via fingerprint-based O(n) matching. <!--#371239b146ce980e-->

### `src/se3/engine/prompt_history.py` (python) — Provides the project's prompt_toolkit input-history backing, exposing get_prompt_history() to return a FileHistory at se3/history/prompt_history while capping the file to the most recent MAX_ENTRIES. <!--#5f5aa17c2519ba66|04bd12b146c2d87e-->
- `_truncate_history` (function) — Helper that parses a prompt_toolkit history file and rewrites it to retain only the most recent MAX_ENTRIES entries, failing silently on I/O errors. <!--#2200a06d776996fb-->
- `get_prompt_history` (function) — Returns a FileHistory for the project's se3/history/prompt_history path, creating the directory and truncating the file before use. <!--#9ccd7eb15cdd0929-->

### `src/se3/engine/prompt_markers.py` (python) — Pure-function utility module for inserting, detecting, and extracting the marker-delimited user-content segment in prompt templates and jsonl records, supporting both the preferred three-segment (prefix/user/suffix) layout and legacy two-marker forms with idempotent, defensive wrapping. <!--#4a6d5f8d5b5676be|2ad3dabcf08b54e5-->
- `_strip_edge_newlines` (function) — Helper that strips only leading/trailing CR/LF (preserving other whitespace) from a marker-bounded segment, mirroring the JS console's newline-stripping. <!--#c325d55079417749-->
- `extract_user_content` (function) — Pure function that locates the three markers in canonical order and returns the middle user-content segment, or None when the full three-segment layout is absent or empty. <!--#8530e9db818b2b45-->
- `first_user_content` (function) — Scans a bounded number of jsonl lines forward, skipping event/non-user/empty records, and returns the content of the first genuine user-content record (or None). <!--#2906efc562d20f94-->
- `_marker_pair_present` (function) — Predicate returning True only when text already contains all three markers in canonical order, used to make wrapping idempotent and distinguish the legacy two-marker form. <!--#7264f000ac385a29-->
- `wrap_user_section` (function) — Wraps user_content as an explicitly marked middle segment between prefix and suffix (the preferred three-segment layout), idempotently skipping re-wrapping if markers already exist. <!--#32884d24dfcf9446-->
- `inject_boundary` (function) — Legacy two-segment helper that splices the marker pair into a template just before a given anchor substring, idempotent and defensive when the anchor or markers are absent. <!--#85d4d148f339ac22-->
- `wrap_user_content` (function) — Legacy two-segment helper joining a template prefix and user content with the marker pair (no suffix), with empty-side and idempotency fallbacks. <!--#f94f37a3057dc0f6-->

### `src/se3/engine/retry_context.py` (python) — Provides retry/dedup context configuration, exposing a helper that resolves the post-dedup safety limit from the SE3_POST_DEDUP_SAFETY_LIMIT environment variable with a built-in default fallback. <!--#a5a0cbe752a64910|d1925360b2c56d65-->
- `_load_safety_limit` (function) — Resolves the post-dedup safety limit from the SE3_POST_DEDUP_SAFETY_LIMIT env var, falling back to the built-in default when the value is missing, non-integer, or non-positive. <!--#273086c8defce832-->

### `src/se3/engine/runtime_environment.md` (markdown) — A prompt-injected reference document that orients an se3-managed agent on which se3 CLI commands are safe to call proactively (read-only history, issue, and code-index navigation/search workflows) versus state-mutating commands (restore, issue create/reset, salvage, merge, sync, init) it must not invoke unless the user explicitly requests them. <!--#c8cd6cc4efe63afd|2c90375074fd2184-->
  - `se3 Runtime Environment` (heading) — Top-level heading introducing the document and stating that the agent is running inside an se3-managed project with command-safety lists following. <!--#de743451af2ef77e-->
    - `Safe to call proactively (read-only)` (heading) — Documents the read-only commands an agent may freely run to orient itself—viewing past session history, consulting related issue context, and locating code via the code-index—with preferred overview/navigation commands, free-form search fallbacks, and recommended workflows for each. <!--#0ff7039abc560fdd-->
    - `Do NOT call proactively` (heading) — Section enumerating state-mutating se3 commands (history restore, issue create/reset, salvage, merge, sync, init) that the agent must not invoke unless the user explicitly requests them. <!--#d89cfba2610ed611-->

### `src/se3/engine/schema.py` (python) — Defines the typed schema for SE3 flow persistence — status/type enums plus TypedDicts for engine.json (flow instance, state, steps) and the AI-optimized context.json export, along with helpers that distill a full flow into that context structure. <!--#d630d7008b3a87ef|f113fab8169e125b-->
- `StepStatusValue` (class) — String enum of valid step lifecycle statuses (pending, running, completed, failed, retrying, paused). <!--#5f5e227669391abd-->
- `StepTypeValue` (class) — String enum of valid flow step types (analyze, plan, implement, test, commit, etc.), with several deprecated aliases that map to PLAN. <!--#ab6ca712b072d46c-->
- `FlowStatusValue` (class) — String enum of valid overall flow statuses (init, running, paused, completed, failed, recovering). <!--#39df2b604e1da00c-->
- `StepSchema` (class) — TypedDict describing the structure of a single step record in engine.json (id, type, status, timestamps, retries, model, inputs/outputs, artifacts, errors). <!--#84a1ed043310dd80-->
- `StateSchema` (class) — TypedDict describing the state object in engine.json that tracks current step, step history, steps map, context, and selected-step progression. <!--#44c3054fd28dca3b-->
- `FlowInstanceSchema` (class) — TypedDict for the root engine.json object capturing one flow execution's identity, status, task, nested state, timestamps, and worktree/locking metadata. <!--#a1d6c901eb2faac7-->
- `ContextStepInfo` (class) — TypedDict holding a condensed per-step summary (type, status, timestamps, key outputs) used inside context.json. <!--#44e8c429cad17650-->
- `ContextSchema` (class) — TypedDict for the root context.json object — an AI-optimized, distilled export of flow state for handoff and resumption. <!--#04a6cbdc2923d71f-->
- `build_context_from_flow` (function) — Function that transforms a full flow instance dict into the distilled context.json structure with step summaries, key outputs, and progress. <!--#d5345fcc8d8a18af-->
- `_summarize_outputs` (function) — Helper that selects and truncates the key output fields per step type for inclusion in a context step summary. <!--#8d53669a401b3363-->
- `_extract_key_outputs` (function) — Helper that extracts the most important output values for each step type into the context's key_outputs map. <!--#38f86a01943d8f20-->

### `src/se3/engine/sink.py` (python) — Defines pluggable event-stream sinks — an abstract Sink base plus concrete CliSink (Rich CLI rendering), JsonSink (NDJSON for daemon), and HistorySink (persists step lifecycle to per-step jsonl) — that consume the unified event stream and turn each event into a concrete output. <!--#4ca8fb3bda5af1e5|c74fbe7a84cd7382-->
- `Sink` (class) — Abstract base class for an event-stream consumer that subscribes to an EventEmitter and receives every emitted event. <!--#056bd1888e33fe98-->
  - `Sink.consume` (method) — Abstract method each concrete sink overrides to perform its side effect on a single event. <!--#bb2390a15e6f138f-->
- `CliSink` (class) — Sink for CLI mode that delegates to the existing Rich step renderers to keep `se3 run` output identical, applying per-step-type usage rules and treating flow-level events as no-ops. <!--#a09a1686239092b7-->
  - `CliSink.__init__` (method) — Constructor that optionally installs a supplied Rich Console as the global display console for all delegated renderers. <!--#7670536357cf51e0-->
  - `CliSink.consume` (method) — Dispatches terminal step events to `_render_step` and STEP_OUTPUT events to `_render_step_usage`, ignoring all other event types. <!--#4fb42242ff9754f9-->
  - `CliSink._render_step` (method) — Routes a terminal step event to the step-output renderer, skipping full reports for confirm/discovery/plan but still surfacing their token usage via per-type renderers. <!--#c17bf533ba7cf189-->
  - `CliSink._render_step_usage` (method) — Renders per-step token usage for a non-terminal STEP_OUTPUT event, applying the same per-type (discovery/confirm/default) rules as the terminal path. <!--#02ac269cfbbc8c1d-->
  - `CliSink._render_confirm_usage_footer` (method) — Renders confirm's token usage as a compact dim single-line footer (round equals cumulative since confirm calls the LLM at most once), rendering nothing when usage is empty. <!--#d0d721be80846166-->
  - `CliSink._render_discovery_cumulative_usage` (method) — Renders the whole-discovery cumulative token usage as a dim single-line via `format_usage_line`, rendering nothing when discovery made no LLM calls. <!--#ed61c7ee6fcebab5-->
- `JsonSink` (class) — Sink for daemon mode that serializes each event to one line of JSON (NDJSON, or pretty-indented), degrading non-serializable payloads to their str() form. <!--#b3473271b7b32503-->
  - `JsonSink.__init__` (method) — Constructor selecting the destination text stream (default stdout) and compact-vs-pretty serialization mode. <!--#f494e6176cbf27cf-->
  - `JsonSink.consume` (method) — Serializes an event via `to_dict` and writes it as a newline-terminated JSON line, flushing while swallowing closed/unflushable-stream errors. <!--#620cbdd2cd131156-->
- `HistorySink` (class) — Sink that persists step-lifecycle events (started/completed/failed/output) into per-step chat-history jsonl so the web console can render anchors and report cards, swallowing filesystem failures. <!--#ef6b304ba013539b-->
  - `HistorySink.__init__` (method) — Constructor that records the project root used to locate the per-step history files. <!--#72ade7501cf2da27-->
  - `HistorySink.consume` (method) — Records STEP_STARTED via `_record_started` and persists terminal/output events' full step dict through `record_step_event`, ignoring other event types. <!--#85f85df1bccb1bbe-->
  - `HistorySink._record_started` (method) — Persists a STEP_STARTED event as a state-aware `running` anchor, skipping when a terminal record exists or the last anchor is already running, and re-arming '进行中' when a paused step resumes. <!--#091c894d34c9cc7a-->

### `src/se3/engine/spec_format.py` (python) — Module implementing the spec format v1 parser and validator: parse_spec() decomposes spec markdown into a structured ParsedSpec (shared header plus Requirement items with their tags, keywords, and extracted references, while flagging content-loss hazards), and validate() checks the result against v1 rules to return error/warning Issues. <!--#68fe61c069d82482|ad5f94024bcdb848-->
- `Issue` (class) — Dataclass representing a single validation finding with its severity, message, and source location. <!--#83b25fba29c9c8a5-->
- `Requirement` (class) — Dataclass holding one parsed Requirement item: its name, body, tags, keywords, references, and starting line. <!--#05f4aeb020c89af3-->
- `ParsedSpec` (class) — Dataclass capturing the full parse result — shared header, Requirements, v1 marker flag, and content-loss hazards like orphan H2s, trailing text, and deep headings. <!--#2e1a351c3b5d3bd8-->
- `_find_code_block_ranges` (function) — Helper that locates the character ranges of fenced code blocks so parsing can skip their contents. <!--#be98a62dfece2077-->
- `_is_inside_code_block` (function) — Helper that tests whether a character position falls within any fenced code-block range. <!--#8a533901a897c653-->
- `_is_inside_table_row` (function) — Helper that tests whether a position lies inside a markdown table row. <!--#841d46f55f6d4171-->
- `_split_values` (function) — Helper that splits a comma-separated tags/keywords string into a trimmed list. <!--#0534b827650457a7-->
- `_clean_ref_name` (function) — Helper that truncates an extracted reference name at stop-words or a word limit to avoid over-capturing prose. <!--#8f4a6f0ef4729236-->
- `_extract_refs` (function) — Helper that extracts deduplicated intra-spec and inter-spec references from a Requirement body, skipping code blocks and tables. <!--#2ab0ac5cf93ce57b-->
- `_extract_tags_and_keywords` (function) — Helper that pulls all tags and keywords declared in a Requirement body. <!--#a38457bf73f7ba5f-->
- `parse_spec` (function) — Top-level function that parses raw spec markdown into a ParsedSpec, splitting header from Requirements and detecting orphan/trailing/deep-heading hazards. <!--#76fb3994bd0231e0-->
