- `validate` (function) — Top-level function that checks a ParsedSpec against format v1 rules and returns a list of error/warning Issues. <!--#d2b1f64c2542a1f1-->

### `src/se3/engine/spec_governance.py` (python) — Defines the authoritative normative text and small constants (domain header markers, base-spec admission standard, per-Requirement/per-spec writing discipline, and cohesion-first split criteria) that govern spec volume/content, injected into update_spec and `se3 sync` prompts so every LLM step shares one description of the governance rules, with no thresholds, behaviour, or import-time side effects. <!--#7667af3fe28bd09e|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/spec_validator.py` (python) — A stdlib-only, pure-function module that structurally validates whether a spec.md file conforms to the spec-format v1 contract (v1 marker, title, Purpose, Requirement section, no narrative prose) and extracts the real spec body from sub-agent output, used by sync paths and the CLI audit. <!--#d5fbca240b1620b9|c04ceb4ce144aea5-->
- `ValidationResult` (class) — Dataclass holding the outcome of a structural validation — a `passed` boolean plus an ordered list of human-readable error strings. <!--#7654e5f86acdea05-->
- `validate_spec_structure` (function) — Top-level validator that runs all five spec-format v1 structural rules (v1 marker, title heading, non-empty Purpose, a Requirement section, no narrative prose) and returns a non-short-circuiting ValidationResult. <!--#d50e58263018def4-->
- `extract_spec_body` (function) — Pure transform that slices the real spec body out of sub-agent output by dropping everything before the first structural anchor (v1 marker, valid title, or any level-1 heading). <!--#0c3fc23b04302c7d-->
- `_line_offset` (function) — Helper returning the character offset of the first line (from keepends-split lines) whose stripped form satisfies a predicate, or None. <!--#8c57691b144ae603-->
- `_first_non_blank` (function) — Helper returning the index of the first non-blank line at or after a start index, or None. <!--#e36c52c1fcb0f668-->
- `_first_non_blank_noncomment` (function) — Helper returning the first non-blank line index that is also not a self-contained HTML comment, used to skip header markers when locating the title. <!--#9cef8bcd96c2a4f2-->
- `_is_valid_title` (function) — Helper deciding whether a line is a valid case-insensitive `# <spec_name> Specification` title, with token-tolerant matching for legacy human-authored titles. <!--#7b638e24391d4985-->
- `_find_heading` (function) — Helper returning the index of the first line exactly matching a given heading string, or None. <!--#027eef02d7887b7c-->
- `_section_has_body` (function) — Helper returning whether the section starting at a heading index has any non-blank, non-heading content before the next heading or EOF. <!--#0c4356cb276e0e77-->
- `_has_requirement` (function) — Helper returning whether any line begins with the `### Requirement:` heading. <!--#ce96c41febce9768-->
- `_first_prose_line` (function) — Helper returning the first non-blank, non-comment, non-heading line's stripped content, or None. <!--#4baaf5be448346e5-->
- `_looks_narrative` (function) — Helper returning whether a line begins with one of the narrative-prose prefixes (English or Chinese) that signal sub-agent prose instead of spec content. <!--#ce5b66df03816acc-->

### `src/se3/engine/spec_write_hook.py` (python) — A standard-library-only module providing the PreToolUse hook entry point and controlled-settings generator that block sub-agent writes to spec files under se3/specs/, plus content-hash snapshot/diff/restore helpers used by the post-step fallback guard to detect and revert spec writes that bypass the hook. <!--#efe70f4f5b95eb74|ede64b5b7aa9be54-->
- `_specs_dir` (function) — Returns the absolute, normalized se3/specs directory path for a given cwd without checking existence. <!--#820e65f393a68a60-->
- `_resolve_target` (function) — Resolves a possibly-relative file path against cwd into a normalized absolute Path, returning None on empty input or error. <!--#796c32141d866a6c-->
- `_is_spec_target` (function) — Returns True when a given file path resolves to somewhere under the cwd's se3/specs directory. <!--#51c3f95bed41c685-->
- `_emit_deny` (function) — Emits a PreToolUse deny decision (both the structured JSON protocol and an exit-2/stderr backstop) explaining the spec write is rejected, then exits. <!--#15e3859220f183cd-->
- `main` (function) — Hook entry point that reads the stdin payload, denies a write targeting a spec file, and otherwise safely allows the call (failing open on any error). <!--#ff237bb752e3f93f-->
- `_guard_settings_payload` (function) — Builds the minimal Claude settings dict carrying only the PreToolUse spec-write hook, with the interpreter path shell-quoted for safe launch. <!--#08294da053c96064-->
- `ensure_guard_settings` (function) — Idempotently generates/caches the controlled settings file under se3/tmp/ and returns its absolute path for llm_caller to pass via --settings. <!--#c574ede2ecdba446-->
- `snapshot_spec_files` (function) — Walks se3/specs recursively and returns a map of project-relative path to sha256 content hash for before/after change detection. <!--#e88c238e08d4ad1f-->
- `diff_spec_files` (function) — Compares two spec snapshot/content maps and returns the sorted list of paths that were added, removed, or modified. <!--#6d7b39d46828be66-->
- `capture_spec_contents` (function) — Byte-level counterpart of snapshot_spec_files, mapping each spec path to its raw bytes so the fallback guard can revert illegal writes. <!--#fe4a82c02e1e6b95-->
- `restore_spec_files` (function) — Reverts each changed spec path to its pre-step bytes (or deletes newly-created ones) and returns paths that could not be restored. <!--#e5e8dd0422656775-->

### `src/se3/engine/stash_utils.py` (python) — Helpers for resolving `git stash pop` conflicts by parsing the pop output for files git reports as 'already exists' and force-staging the merged HEAD (--ours) version of each conflicting file. <!--#b93530f955fdfa36|d01bca0223b7123f-->
- `parse_stashpop_already_exists` (function) — Parses `git stash pop` output to extract file paths reported as 'already exists, no checkout', which git doesn't mark as unmerged. <!--#740f82b591b8253f-->
- `take_ours_for_stashpop` (function) — Resolves stash-pop conflicts in a best-effort manner by keeping the merged HEAD (--ours) version of each conflicting file and staging it. <!--#b3673861c462abf6-->

### `src/se3/engine/state_machine.py` (python) — Core flow-engine state machine that drives step transitions and execution flow, composing effective task descriptions (discovery refinements + user interjections), managing fix/revision loops with retry-counter resets, and bounding accumulated state like previous_output and fix_history. <!--#cd636f6239cc3d72|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/step_renderers.py` (python) — A registry-based rendering module whose single public entry point (render_step_output) dispatches each completed step to a per-StepType custom renderer (or a generic default) to print its outputs, then appends a per-step token-usage block. <!--#2f2f26d66573e244|d54d67bf3501a24e-->
- `register_renderer` (function) — Decorator factory that registers a function as the custom renderer for a given StepType in the STEP_RENDERERS registry. <!--#d32f2f04d911965a-->
- `render_step_output` (function) — Public entry point that renders a completed step by dispatching to its registered renderer (or the default), then appends the step's token-usage block. <!--#f8c10e874f60ccb1-->
- `render_step_usage` (function) — Renders the per-step token-usage block from outputs.token_usage when present, exposed so CliSink can show usage for steps whose full report it skips. <!--#9e174cc43cf6545a-->
- `_format_value` (function) — Helper that formats an arbitrary output value into a display string, JSON-encoding dicts/lists and stringifying everything else. <!--#de91dc9da5c3e62f-->
- `_default_render` (function) — Generic fallback renderer that iterates step.outputs printing each key/value (with previews for long strings), status, and any error message. <!--#3950ced25ad3c496-->
- `_render_remaining` (function) — Helper that renders any step.outputs keys not already handled by a specialized renderer, under an 'Additional Details' panel. <!--#1e71813763f00346-->
- `_render_version_analyze` (function) — Custom renderer for the version-analysis step showing the current→suggested version, bump type/confidence, and reasoning. <!--#116453776569f134-->
- `_render_summarize` (function) — Custom renderer for the summarize step that renders the work-summary output as markdown. <!--#738ac7f62d030ce2-->
- `_build_test_summary_lines` (function) — Helper that builds summary lines (overall status, per-phase pass/fail counts, command) from a test_results dict, shared by the test and spec_gate renderers. <!--#229b1bfa19c9b13f-->
- `_render_test` (function) — Custom renderer for the test step that presents a summary-only view of test_results, falling back to default rendering when absent. <!--#637eb9831e26a9dc-->
- `_render_spec_gate` (function) — Custom renderer for the spec_gate step showing the gate conclusion (passed/failed/skipped), fallback route, fix instructions, and re-test summary. <!--#bdf1eeb6ff95cd9e-->
- `_render_propose` (function) — Custom renderer for the propose step that renders the structured proposal dict and any remaining outputs. <!--#52e3d565fe61294f-->
- `_render_design` (function) — Custom renderer for the design step that renders the structured design document dict and any remaining outputs. <!--#8f2bf6445475b377-->
- `_render_plan` (function) — Custom renderer for the plan step that renders its proposal, design, and task-group sections plus any remaining keys. <!--#5d7e000280fbba46-->
- `_group_files_by_directory` (function) — Helper that groups a list of file paths by their top-level directory into a sorted OrderedDict for display. <!--#f9bc34f5641dd2ca-->
- `_render_implement` (function) — Custom renderer for the implement step showing a status bar, summary, files changed, tests added, incomplete tasks, restricted edits, and errors. <!--#6d5d0bca3552ff37-->
- `_render_analyze` (function) — Custom renderer for the analyze step showing task type/complexity/scope, reasoning, and relevant spec items. <!--#5e2f32cab33f6a3e-->
- `_render_self_check` (function) — Custom renderer for the self-check step showing pass/fail status, summary, and issues grouped by severity. <!--#4938c1b337cfbba8-->
- `_render_verify_spec` (function) — Custom renderer for the verify-spec step showing verified status, summary, issues grouped by scope/priority, and recommendations. <!--#b4386901686444b9-->
- `_render_update_spec` (function) — Custom renderer for the update-spec step listing updated specs and new capabilities, or a no-op message. <!--#ed67188a732c36d3-->
- `_render_commit` (function) — Custom renderer for the commit step showing the commit hash, optional version bump, and commit message, or a no-changes message. <!--#8ef524737da51f8e-->

### `src/se3/engine/task_description.py` (python) — A small helper module that builds a task description by appending an optional '## Additional Instructions' section, composed from non-empty interjection entries, to a base description. <!--#5bfbec42e2f34e85|86c2c9cd1e02d20d-->
- `compose_task_description_with_interjections` (function) — Renders a list of interjection dicts into a '## Additional Instructions' section appended to the base task description, skipping empty entries and returning the base unchanged when none are usable. <!--#0330964a0329ae3c-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_baseline.py` (python) — Captures a pre-implementation test-suite baseline — running the full suite in a background subprocess to record the set of already-failing test ids — and caches that failing-set keyed by git HEAD plus working-tree dirty hash so post-change runs can distinguish new regressions from pre-existing failures. <!--#458c1e367e315aa7|3a16cb9889dc135e-->
- `compute_baseline_key` (function) — Builds a deterministic cache key from the git HEAD sha plus a working-tree dirty hash, so any commit or content change invalidates a stale baseline. <!--#8dd9a8fe1224c6b5-->
- `_git_head_sha` (function) — Returns the current git HEAD sha, degrading to the literal "no-head" when the directory isn't a git repo or git is unavailable. <!--#6d07afeb323ea303-->
- `_file_content_hash` (function) — Returns the SHA-256 hex digest of a file's bytes, or None if it can't be read. <!--#857a05eb3f930681-->
- `_working_tree_dirty_hash` (function) — Hashes the working tree's dirty state — the raw `git diff HEAD` plus the names and content hashes of untracked non-ignored files — into a content-sensitive digest. <!--#695425e98c6d4c13-->
- `_git_untracked_files` (function) — Returns the sorted relative paths of untracked, non-ignored files via `git ls-files --others`, or an empty list on failure. <!--#64b04d87e8a279d9-->
- `cache_path` (function) — Returns the on-disk path of the baseline cache file (se3/state/test_baseline_cache.json) under a project root. <!--#c7e65d5b0cdc7682-->
- `_read_cache_entries` (function) — Best-effort reader of the cache's `entries` map that returns an empty dict on any problem (missing/corrupt/wrong-shape/schema-mismatch) so a damaged cache reads as a clean miss. <!--#e5a6072715306eca-->
- `load_cached` (function) — Looks up the cached failing-test-id set for a key, returning a (possibly empty) set on a hit or None on any miss. <!--#e3cd6b779c7a8b44-->
- `save_cache` (function) — Atomically persists a failing-set under a key (preserving other keys, LRU-bounded to MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES) via tempfile + os.replace. <!--#5c020aadea086148-->
- `resolve_baseline_timeout` (function) — Resolves the wall-clock bound for a baseline run by reusing `test.timeout` from se3.yaml, falling back to DEFAULT_BASELINE_TIMEOUT on any config error. <!--#cf0c6e1d36901294-->
- `BaselineCapture` (class) — Class that runs the full test suite as a background subprocess and later resolves the failing-id set, returning the None sentinel when the capture itself failed. <!--#575545a1c87e3780-->
  - `BaselineCapture.__init__` (method) — Initializes the capture's project root, optional command override, and the process/result/timeout bookkeeping state. <!--#496945c492d18e32-->
  - `BaselineCapture.launch` (method) — Starts the background test subprocess (with SE3_TEST_RUNNING=1 to prevent recursion), idempotently and without raising, recording any launch failure for later. <!--#e3d786d17860ee0e-->
  - `BaselineCapture.is_ready` (method) — Returns True when `wait` would resolve without blocking — i.e. the subprocess finished, launch failed, or nothing was ever launched. <!--#cf4e7fa49e0f2d9f-->
  - `BaselineCapture.wait` (method) — Blocks until the capture finishes and returns the cached failing-id set, or None on capture failure, raising TimeoutExpired (resumable) if a timeout is given and hit. <!--#e1642a76f1abaa60-->
  - `BaselineCapture.timed_out` (method) — Reports whether the capture was killed for exceeding its time bound, letting the caller skip a synchronous retry that would just hang again. <!--#f66c64ed5690fb8f-->
  - `BaselineCapture.wait_or_kill` (method) — Bounded wait that kills the subprocess on timeout and resolves to the None sentinel (setting timed_out), instead of leaving the capture resumable like `wait`. <!--#58778a3528d13e61-->
  - `BaselineCapture.kill` (method) — Best-effort, idempotent teardown that terminates and reaps the subprocess, cleans up the temp output file, and marks the capture as a failed (None) measurement. <!--#5d1609d8c4dcd876-->
  - `BaselineCapture._resolve_command` (method) — Resolves the test command from se3.yaml or the test step's auto-detection, ensuring a pytest command carries a verbose flag so per-test results are parseable. <!--#a732a2702ddbe0ce-->
  - `BaselineCapture._parse_result` (method) — Parses the captured output into a failing-id set, returning None when a non-zero exit produced no parseable per-test results (a collection/infra error) to signal fallback. <!--#0b6275a2089ff0ef-->
  - `BaselineCapture._close_stdout_file` (method) — Closes the open stdout temp-file handle, swallowing any OSError. <!--#b5e92b79a12c5410-->
  - `BaselineCapture._cleanup_stdout_file` (method) — Closes and deletes the temp stdout file once it has been read, ignoring errors. <!--#59ca266f4db1a002-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_code_index_degrade.py` (python) — Unit tests for the code-index degrade path, verifying when a structure-less file becomes degrade-eligible (the three-condition gate plus an independent byte-size trigger) and how it is split into line-limited degraded chunks that surface a DEGRADED marker in rendered output. <!--#66c3611511c6f6b5|71775928e2399a22-->
- `_small_cfg` (function) — Test helper returning a CodeIndexConfig with tiny line/chunk thresholds so tests can trip degrade with only a few lines. <!--#53bc45df86825aa9-->
- `TestDegradeGate` (class) — Test class covering when a file becomes degrade-eligible — the three-condition gate and independent byte-threshold triggering. <!--#d0d6098b67194f0e-->
  - `TestDegradeGate.test_all_three_conditions_required` (method) — Asserts degrade eligibility requires structure-less AND over-threshold, voided by either having structure or being under threshold. <!--#2199039eeb4e2357-->
  - `TestDegradeGate.test_byte_threshold_trips_independently` (method) — Verifies the byte-size threshold can trip degrade on its own, even for a single-line file under the line threshold. <!--#46459083602a0c70-->
- `TestChunking` (class) — Test class covering chunk production: per-chunk line limits, degraded marking, and file-level vs chunked indexing outcomes including render output. <!--#ed0c09850d45ad3e-->
  - `TestChunking.test_chunks_respect_line_limit_and_mark_degraded` (method) — Checks _chunk_degraded splits text into degraded 'chunk' units that each stay within the configured chunk_lines limit. <!--#e1f3a47db522d4b6-->
  - `TestChunking.test_small_structureless_file_stops_at_file_level` (method) — Verifies a small structure-less file stays a single file-level text entry with no chunk symbols. <!--#6740dfa1b46eb647-->
  - `TestChunking.test_large_structureless_file_degrades_to_chunks` (method) — Verifies a large structure-less file is indexed into degraded chunk symbols. <!--#95e53b825cb305cd-->
  - `TestChunking.test_degraded_marker_in_render` (method) — Confirms the DEGRADED_MARKER appears in the rendered output for a degraded, chunked file. <!--#5fcb0faef565ff1c-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_e2e.py` (python) — End-to-end pytest suite for the flow engine that drives complete documentation, feature, and bugfix flows through all steps (with mocked subprocess/LLM responses) to verify completion, interruption-and-resume, step-failure recovery, and state consistency across persistence cycles. <!--#f4568184475538f1|639ab78885c981d9-->
- `MockSubprocessResult` (class) — Test double mimicking a subprocess.run result with stdout, stderr, and returncode attributes. <!--#7cd9e8f256499683-->
  - `MockSubprocessResult.__init__` (method) — Initializes the mock subprocess result with given stdout, stderr, and returncode defaults. <!--#a5da8ba30e1e20a5-->
- `create_mock_llm_responses` (function) — Helper returning a dict of canned LLM responses keyed by StepType for a documentation-task flow. <!--#03aedc206121439a-->
- `TestEndToEndSmallTask` (class) — Test class covering a small task's full flow execution and its interruption/resume behavior. <!--#68c4ca59b6e8986c-->
  - `TestEndToEndSmallTask.test_complete_small_flow` (method) — Runs a small documentation flow with mocked subprocess and handlers, asserting it reaches COMPLETED. <!--#c26ddf8f7d77721a-->
  - `TestEndToEndSmallTask.test_flow_with_interruption` (method) — Saves a flow, recreates fresh manager/state-machine instances, and asserts the flow resumes from persistence. <!--#6a17973c7dc1db29-->
- `TestRealWorldScenarios` (class) — Test class exercising realistic feature-request and bugfix flows end to end. <!--#7f1bc8fab797c09f-->
  - `TestRealWorldScenarios.test_feature_request_flow` (method) — Drives a feature-task flow through all steps and asserts completion with at least five steps taken. <!--#9581d9848cdc769c-->
  - `TestRealWorldScenarios.test_bugfix_flow` (method) — Drives a bugfix-task flow to completion using success handlers for every step type. <!--#993335182c66a65a-->
- `TestErrorRecovery` (class) — Test class covering step-failure recovery and state consistency across persistence cycles. <!--#aa6f34f92cacf389-->
  - `TestErrorRecovery.test_recovery_after_step_failure` (method) — Uses a flaky handler that fails once then succeeds to verify a retried step recovers to COMPLETED. <!--#5fa7662358f09216-->
  - `TestErrorRecovery.test_state_consistency_across_persistence` (method) — Progresses and saves a flow, then reloads in fresh instances to assert step outputs and current step survive intact. <!--#dc2c8d56fc423f1f-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_engine.py` (python) — Unit-test suite for the flow engine, covering data models, persistence, the state machine, crash/interrupt recovery, full state transitions, and post-charter-refactor step-sequence routing. <!--#7e620f771413a9e1|7c7a05a1ed1b99c1-->

  - `TestModels.test_default_sequences_end_with_summarize` (method) — Asserts SUMMARIZE is the single final step of every default sequence (right after COMMIT for non-review types) and that the unknown-type fallback matches feature. <!--#8be39b0610d798b8-->
- `TestPersistence` (class) — Tests the PersistenceManager — saving/loading flows, atomic writes, listing active flows, and context file round-trips. <!--#4bbcf88fcd7adab4-->
  - `TestPersistence.test_save_and_load` (method) — Verifies a saved flow can be reloaded with its flow_id and task description preserved. <!--#3a7087926038fa1e-->

  - `TestStateMachine.test_create_flow` (method) — Asserts create_flow seeds a flow with the task fields, INIT status, selected steps, and a current step id. <!--#b91b112b6d75210c-->
  - `TestStateMachine.test_load_or_create_new` (method) — Confirms load_or_create_flow creates a fresh flow when none exists (not resumed). <!--#e32b5e7e0542ec9b-->
  - `TestStateMachine.test_load_or_create_resume` (method) — Confirms load_or_create_flow resumes a previously persisted flow by id. <!--#0a45052783b903ee-->

  - `TestStateMachine.test_run_step_no_handler` (method) — Confirms a step with no registered handler fails gracefully with an explanatory error message. <!--#8c9a60b7097ad62a-->

  - `TestStateMachine.test_run_step_on_running_not_called_without_handler` (method) — Confirms on_running is never invoked when a step fails before entering RUNNING due to a missing handler. <!--#bd686d879e5dbd5b-->
- `TestRecovery` (class) — Tests interrupt/crash recovery — resuming flows after a simulated crash, mid-step interruption, and scanning for multiple persisted flows. <!--#54dd5e46dc1d60b5-->
  - `TestRecovery.test_recovery_after_crash` (method) — Verifies a new StateMachine resumes a persisted flow and restores the current step after a simulated crash. <!--#706a66871174803d-->

  - `TestRecovery.test_multiple_flow_recovery` (method) — Checks that saved flow state files can be discovered by scanning the state directory. <!--#eb6761daf283ad9f-->

  - `TestStateTransitions.test_complete_flow_transitions` (method) — Drives a small flow through every step with mock handlers and asserts it reaches COMPLETED. <!--#370ba5bbabad6678-->
  - `TestStateTransitions.test_completion_advances_step_index_to_total` (method) — Verifies completion advances current_step_index to the total step count for unified total/total progress reporting. <!--#3e7c9a2d219c8fbc-->
  - `TestStateTransitions.test_resume_completed_flow_does_not_raise` (method) — Confirms transition_to_next on an already-completed flow self-heals the out-of-range index instead of raising. <!--#b5fed906e3c98d54-->

  - `TestCharterRefactorRouting.test_invariant_check_revision_routes_to_implement_fix_loop` (method) — Verifies an INVARIANT_CHECK REVISION_NEEDED routes back to IMPLEMENT, bumps the fix iteration, and re-runs to completion. <!--#95614723fa7eb6b7-->
  - `TestCharterRefactorRouting.test_invariant_check_shares_max_fix_iterations_exhaustion` (method) — Confirms an always-failing INVARIANT_CHECK exhausts the shared fix-iteration bound and fails the flow. <!--#8e19b6d57a6af023-->
  - `TestCharterRefactorRouting.test_charter_freshness_is_non_blocking` (method) — Verifies CHARTER_FRESHNESS advisory output never diverts the flow into a fix loop. <!--#b1bab9680a232e89-->
  - `TestCharterRefactorRouting.test_freeze_invariant_anchors_idempotent` (method) — Confirms invariant anchors are frozen once at flow start and not re-read on a subsequent init. <!--#005ac88de9bbd6e7-->

  - `TestStreamProgressHistory.test_read_flow_incremental_cursor_over_progress` (method) — Tests the daemon reader advancing its per-file cursor across progress lines in full then append mode without losing or duplicating records. <!--#cca0aa5c5f344548-->
- `TestStreamJSONTrackerUsage` (class) — Tests StreamJSONTracker capturing token usage and cost from result NDJSON lines, ignoring non-result/malformed input, and folding into the step accumulator. <!--#7710f60803b78ce3-->

  - `TestStreamJSONTrackerUsage.test_malformed_usage_does_not_raise` (method) — Confirms a non-dict usage payload is swallowed without error, leaving usage empty. <!--#875205ac5b9566cd-->

- `TestSessionTokenUsageModel` (class) — Tests State.session_token_usage — default emptiness, serialization round-trip as a primitive dict, backward compatibility with old engine.json, and non-interference with other fields. <!--#4596b53ce8081225-->
  - `TestSessionTokenUsageModel.test_default_session_usage_is_empty` (method) — Asserts a default State has empty session token usage. <!--#c8def32349991da0-->

- `TestRunStepTokenAggregation` (class) — Tests run_step folding per-step token usage into step.outputs and session totals, including multi-call merges, no-call cases, exceptions, and non-terminal (paused/revision) carry-over without double-counting. <!--#c2a8a9257880d762-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation._make_usage` (method) — Helper constructing a UsageTotals from keyword fields. <!--#61d9bd91f9c0d33a-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_single_step_merges_multiple_calls` (method) — Verifies two calls within one step merge into the step's token_usage and the session total. <!--#c39903bd03e6bf4d-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_no_call_step_writes_no_usage_field` (method) — Confirms a step making no LLM call writes no token_usage field and leaves the session total empty. <!--#f7afd427ad3b2dbf-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_multi_step_session_accumulation` (method) — Verifies the session total equals the sum of usage across multiple separately-run steps. <!--#d0f0e4c88a4e0921-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_exception_step_still_aggregates_and_resets_scope` (method) — Confirms a raising handler still records usage gathered before the raise and resets the step scope (no contextvar leak). <!--#498168edce99d8ce-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_paused_run_usage_carried_into_next_emitted_record` (method) — Verifies paused rounds publish both token_usage and carried_token_usage, the final round sums all rounds and clears the carry, and the session total stays consistent. <!--#2a522c6d2150f888-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_aggregated_usage_survives_persistence` (method) — Confirms both step-level and session token usage round-trip through engine.json persistence. <!--#e87aadc8e5ee2ef4-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_revision_needed_step_publishes_visible_token_usage` (method) — Verifies a REVISION_NEEDED step publishes visible token_usage (the G2 fix) alongside carried_token_usage. <!--#23c0cc57791d6903-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_non_terminal_then_terminal_usage_equals_sum_of_rounds` (method) — Confirms after a revision then a completion round the terminal token_usage and session total equal the sum of both rounds' increments. <!--#a6bfda3a51da181c-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_session_usage_not_duplicated_by_combined_totals` (method) — Verifies the session total sums each round's per-round increment rather than combined carry totals, avoiding double-counting across re-entries. <!--#5fd1b8051bd165b1-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_steps.py` (python) — Pytest suite for the flow engine's step handlers, covering analyze/test/commit step behavior, the STEP_HANDLERS registry, LLMCaller retry logic, ContextBuilder pruning, issue-discovery injection gating, ANALYZE-to-downstream input mapping, and default step-sequence ordering — with emphasis on confirming retired spec-governance steps and outputs are fully removed. <!--#5cc1d551d866257c|0bf363a7f8127195-->

  - `TestSetupPyHandler.test_read_version_with_other_args` (method) — Checks reading the version when setup() has additional arguments. <!--#b0f8f4ed26e4d25e-->

  - `TestSetupPyHandler.test_read_version_missing` (method) — Checks that a setup() call with no version raises a ValueError. <!--#bd15d132a61a1528-->
  - `TestSetupPyHandler.test_write_version_simple` (method) — Verifies updating the version in a minimal setup() call. <!--#82a5532572564742-->
  - `TestSetupPyHandler.test_write_version_preserves_structure` (method) — Verifies a version write leaves the rest of setup.py (imports, other args, file reads) intact. <!--#9b272c00956ab9e7-->
- `TestVersionBumper` (class) — Test class for the VersionBumper orchestrator covering version parsing, semantic bumping, file detection, and backup/rollback. <!--#af9af38811041594-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_parse_version_simple` (method) — Checks parsing of plain major.minor.patch version strings into tuples. <!--#7daf35ca23c56c6a-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_parse_version_with_v_prefix` (method) — Checks parsing of versions with a leading v/V prefix. <!--#2e7007dd8752666f-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_parse_version_with_prerelease` (method) — Checks parsing strips prerelease suffixes to the numeric core. <!--#cb02118379737ed6-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_parse_version_two_components` (method) — Checks parsing a two-component version defaults patch to 0. <!--#daa030f2be2cafa5-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_parse_version_invalid` (method) — Checks that malformed version strings raise ValueError. <!--#2d10a479f5a321bd-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_bump_version_string_major` (method) — Checks a MAJOR bump increments major and resets minor/patch. <!--#7a4532a6998fdbb7-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_bump_version_string_minor` (method) — Checks a MINOR bump increments minor and resets patch. <!--#509fd258feafaaf1-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_bump_version_string_patch` (method) — Checks a PATCH bump increments only the patch component. <!--#c9bf0432147403b9-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_detect_version_file_priority` (method) — Checks that package.json is detected first by the file-detection priority order. <!--#800c23eec1a4baaa-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_detect_version_file_pyproject` (method) — Checks detection of pyproject.toml as the version file. <!--#eab8f0213179d5cf-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_detect_version_file_configured_path` (method) — Checks that an explicitly configured file_path overrides auto-detection. <!--#5ca9989f488ddc7c-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_bump_version_with_bump_type` (method) — Checks end-to-end bumping of a file with an explicit bump type. <!--#6b813fcf542e2198-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_bump_version_creates_backup` (method) — Checks that bump_version records a backup path and prior version for rollback. <!--#a674c77c14b69314-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_rollback_restores_version` (method) — Checks that rollback restores the original version after a bump. <!--#1edc28e64d5ee1f9-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_rollback_without_backup` (method) — Checks that rollback is a safe no-op when no backup exists. <!--#1ba05a6ea38e482b-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_clear_backup` (method) — Checks that clear_backup resets the stored backup path and version. <!--#92114194e8380157-->
  - `TestVersionBumper.test_bump_version_disabled` (method) — Checks that bumping raises RuntimeError when version bumping is disabled in config. <!--#a374b55fff375ef0-->
- `TestVersionConfig` (class) — Test class for VersionConfig validation. <!--#2228776d17000967-->
  - `TestVersionConfig.test_validate_nonexistent_file` (method) — Checks that validate() reports an error for a nonexistent configured version file. <!--#566c0988aeaf4da0-->

### `src/se3/engine/token_usage.py` (python) — Central token/cost accounting module providing the additive UsageTotals dataclass, ContextVar-based step-scoped accumulators for folding per-call LLM usage, and formatting helpers that render compact usage/cost lines for CLI and display layers. <!--#55569bbbe56edfd9|a60fafda9217ec4b-->
- `_coerce_int` (function) — Best-effort coerces any value to an int, returning 0 for None/missing/unparseable input so malformed usage payloads never raise. <!--#c97b0fddc8bb6dee-->
- `_coerce_float` (function) — Best-effort coerces any value to a float, returning 0.0 for None/missing/bad input. <!--#9a7b6843df4c055e-->
- `UsageTotals` (class) — Additive dataclass holding the four token counts plus USD cost for a step or session, with field-wise merging and tolerant JSON round-tripping. <!--#375cd06ef41c59d1-->
  - `UsageTotals.add` (method) — Folds another UsageTotals into self field-by-field (ignoring None) and returns self, the merge primitive for combining many LLM calls or steps. <!--#fdfadb75f6c63a01-->
  - `UsageTotals.total_tokens` (method) — Property returning the sum of all four token counts (input + output + both cache kinds). <!--#7b66453eb3751841-->
  - `UsageTotals.is_empty` (method) — Returns True when every token field and the cost are (near) zero, used by display to suppress an empty usage block. <!--#418f023efc3e6d45-->
  - `UsageTotals.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the tally to a stable-keyed JSON-primitive dict for persistence and read-back by both display ends. <!--#8a5404e456cc4012-->
  - `UsageTotals.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod reconstructing a UsageTotals from a possibly-partial/None mapping, defaulting missing fields to zero via the coerce helpers. <!--#0886740f6509abf2-->
- `accumulate_step_usage` (function) — Context manager that opens a fresh step-scoped accumulator (via ContextVar) for its body and yields it so the caller can read the merged step total afterward. <!--#cc56e3c1d6f5a823-->
- `current_step_usage` (function) — Returns the currently in-scope step accumulator, or None when no step scope is active. <!--#7fd09ce3743acedc-->
- `use_step_usage` (function) — Context manager that re-binds a given existing accumulator into the current context, used to carry a parent step's scope across ThreadPoolExecutor thread boundaries (no-op for None). <!--#3dbb8ce677b8dd31-->
- `add_call_usage` (function) — Best-effort folds one LLM call's usage (UsageTotals or raw dict) into the in-scope step accumulator under a lock, a safe no-op outside any scope and on any error. <!--#638e1c5fbd6b3f82-->
- `format_cost` (function) — Renders a USD cost as a 4-decimal-place string (e.g. $0.0123), tolerant of None/non-numeric input. <!--#1d2dadbbbc3b7703-->
- `_format_tokens` (function) — Renders a token count with thousands separators (e.g. 12,345). <!--#6ac1c2bfe7972253-->
- `format_round_usage_footer` (function) — Renders a compact single-line per-round usage footer (this round's vs cumulative in/out tokens) for CLI interactive multi-round steps. <!--#cfbfdeb0753e1d42-->
- `format_usage_line` (function) — Renders a compact single-line labelled usage summary (in/out/cache/cost), safe for None or empty input. <!--#9315ed6455ff9aa6-->

### `src/se3/engine/tool_formatters.py` (python) — A tool-aware formatting module that renders previews, merged success/failure chip headers, structured detail payloads, and console diffs for agent tool calls (Edit, Write, Read, Bash, Grep, Glob) via a per-tool formatter registry with generic fallbacks, plus path/text truncation helpers. <!--#c54dd61994655562|91e7162fb2ba2d74-->
- `set_project_root` (function) — Sets the module-level project root used for relative-path truncation. <!--#dfcc75f6b64065c1-->
- `get_project_root` (function) — Returns the currently configured module-level project root. <!--#7154a7b54664f7dd-->
- `truncate_path` (function) — Shortens a file path by converting to project-relative and abbreviating middle segments while always preserving the filename. <!--#af68e886ed526bb5-->
- `truncate_preview` (function) — Collapses text to a single line and truncates it to a max length with an ellipsis. <!--#430e41a2779956b6-->
- `_generic_tool_use_preview` (function) — Fallback formatter rendering a tool name plus up to three key=value input parameters. <!--#5381c07435a555b6-->
- `_generic_tool_result_preview` (function) — Fallback formatter producing a short preview of an arbitrary tool result, handling errors, dicts, lists, and strings. <!--#48f2fbefea36c20f-->
- `_format_edit_use` (function) — Formats an Edit tool_use preview showing the path and old→new line counts. <!--#f71eb442b30a57a8-->
- `_format_edit_result` (function) — Formats an Edit tool_result preview with a success/failure check mark. <!--#85c9245a8efa4b63-->
- `_format_write_use` (function) — Formats a Write tool_use preview showing the path and content line count. <!--#cbf2c6850db84c36-->
- `_format_write_result` (function) — Formats a Write tool_result preview with a success check mark. <!--#bb864e49ebf169af-->
- `_format_read_use` (function) — Formats a Read tool_use preview showing the path and optional offset/limit line range. <!--#033bed8e51562302-->
- `_format_read_result` (function) — Formats a Read tool_result preview reporting the number of lines read. <!--#64139de5213892f1-->
- `_format_bash_use` (function) — Formats a Bash tool_use preview showing a truncated command string. <!--#1d81716ea4607e32-->
- `_format_bash_result` (function) — Formats a Bash tool_result preview reporting the output line count. <!--#cadb1cac2322ffa6-->
- `_format_grep_use` (function) — Formats a Grep tool_use preview showing the pattern and search path. <!--#f358d0cddd652f2f-->
- `_format_grep_result` (function) — Formats a Grep tool_result preview reporting the number of matches. <!--#db18d2ecd441d75f-->
- `_format_glob_use` (function) — Formats a Glob tool_use preview showing the pattern and search path. <!--#a5fb2a263b26c807-->
- `_format_glob_result` (function) — Formats a Glob tool_result preview reporting the number of matched files. <!--#15d57808a43d6f30-->
- `_extract_text` (function) — Normalizes a tool result of varied shapes (string, dict, content-block list) into plain text. <!--#9ccecf462228bddd-->
- `format_tool_use_preview` (function) — Public entry point that routes a tool_use to its registered formatter or the generic fallback. <!--#384bca508e74b524-->
- `format_tool_result_preview` (function) — Public entry point that routes a tool_result to its registered formatter or the generic fallback. <!--#be3e1b30f642fff2-->
- `generate_edit_diff` (function) — Produces unified-diff lines from an Edit tool's old and new strings. <!--#12314b9f4beec6e1-->
- `format_tool_chip_in_flight_header` (function) — Returns the chip header string for an in-flight (not-yet-settled) tool call. <!--#1f543073fd4bdc05-->
- `_error_preview` (function) — Extracts a short error description from a failed tool_result payload. <!--#355770af1dbe4956-->
- `_success_combined_edit` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for an Edit call (path plus line-count delta). <!--#c1da397fa166012e-->
- `_success_combined_write` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Write call (path plus line count). <!--#dd4ee8b0ac44b368-->
- `_success_combined_read` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Read call (path, range, and lines read). <!--#8301d4b64ec2f5f6-->
- `_success_combined_bash` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Bash call (command plus output line count). <!--#7244951a7d393507-->
- `_success_combined_grep` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Grep call (pattern, path, and match count). <!--#2cf5893c148f574d-->
- `_success_combined_glob` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Glob call (pattern, path, and file count). <!--#a0ffe282c52331a7-->
- `_failure_use_body` (function) — Returns the use-side summary body for a chip with the tool-name prefix stripped off. <!--#42b4af467d9e996a-->
- `format_tool_chip_header` (function) — Builds the merged success (✓) or failure (✗) chip header combining input and result/error summaries for a settled tool call. <!--#0289b350323d1bb4-->
- `_parse_first_hunk_start` (function) — Parses the first hunk's old/new starting line numbers from unified-diff lines. <!--#9423216a302e5b77-->
- `_maybe_truncate_text` (function) — Tail-truncates text to a max character count, returning the text and a truncation flag. <!--#ec5a2a60e03451e2-->
- `_maybe_truncate_lines` (function) — Truncates a list of lines to a max item count, returning the list and a truncation flag. <!--#2fbed4dc3f10a384-->
- `_build_edit_detail` (function) — Builds the structured edit_diff detail payload (diff text and hunk line numbers) for an Edit call. <!--#5af5b189f4951526-->
- `_build_write_detail` (function) — Builds the write_full or write_diff detail payload for a Write call depending on whether prior content existed. <!--#5ef63ac28351f7e8-->
- `_build_read_detail` (function) — Builds the read_text detail payload (file text and start line) for a Read call. <!--#0cd9954a4b3a9156-->
- `_build_bash_detail` (function) — Builds the bash_output detail payload (command, stdout, stderr) for a Bash call. <!--#92b7bb8c3d4fd9bf-->
- `_build_grep_detail` (function) — Builds the grep_matches detail payload (pattern, path, match lines) for a Grep call. <!--#f8f884afae6d79fa-->
- `_build_glob_detail` (function) — Builds the glob_matches detail payload (pattern, path, file list) for a Glob call. <!--#f5ce9cb5e0ed9cdc-->
- `_build_generic_text_detail` (function) — Builds the fallback kind="text" detail payload from extracted result text for unregistered tools. <!--#4d3ee4f1226cb7d4-->
- `build_tool_detail_payload` (function) — Public entry point producing a JSON-safe structured detail dict (with a kind discriminator) for the web chip's expandable panel. <!--#343f99f9c9ff70ee-->
- `format_tool_diff` (function) — Renders unified-diff or created-file output to the console for Edit/Write tools, no-op for others. <!--#17b73d59cfd2d12c-->

### `src/se3/engine/transitive_reduction.py` (python) — Module that computes the transitive reduction of a group dependency graph, stripping redundant direct dependencies that are already reachable through longer paths while preserving the original input. <!--#e9031a4a3db90475|0f08cb4ec581ddce-->
- `transitive_reduce` (function) — Public function returning a deep copy of the input groups with each redundant direct dependency (one reachable via a longer path) removed from its `depends_on` list, leaving the originals untouched. <!--#41aca8aef443ed63-->
- `_has_long_path` (function) — Internal BFS helper that reports whether the adjacency graph has an indirect path of length ≥ 2 from source to target, ignoring the direct source→target edge. <!--#d3ec927b055eff6d-->

### `src/se3/engine/truncation.py` (python) — A central module of named character-limit constants for truncating LLM-consumed content (test/self-check/verify stdout-stderr tails, fix instructions, failures sections, task-group summaries, and web tool-chip payloads) so the limits stay consistent and adjustable in one place. <!--#ef740dc558517a20|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/version_bumper.py` (python) — Semantic-versioning toolkit providing an immutable SemVer Version value object plus pluggable, format-specific version-file handlers (JSON, TOML, Python, setup.py) and a VersionDetector that classifies a project's type and locates/reads/bumps its version file. <!--#f10ee1578849d135|febbe367307b6b96-->
- `ProjectType` (class) — Enum of supported project types (Python, Node.js, Unknown) used to drive version-file detection. <!--#2c6662747efb04b7-->
- `BumpType` (class) — Enum naming the three semantic-versioning bump kinds: major, minor, and patch. <!--#da8d688705155657-->
- `Version` (class) — Immutable SemVer 2.0.0 value object that parses, validates, stringifies, compares, and bumps version components. <!--#6343759176871ea6-->
  - `Version.parse` (method) — Classmethod that parses a SemVer string into a Version, raising ValueError on empty or malformed input. <!--#96dad270505dc81c-->
  - `Version.validate` (method) — Classmethod returning True if a string is a valid SemVer version (parse succeeds), else False. <!--#a520043f7f23f28d-->
  - `Version.__str__` (method) — Renders the Version back to its canonical MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-prerelease][+build] string form. <!--#ba5738e57d5afb3e-->
  - `Version.bump_major` (method) — Returns a new Version with major incremented and minor/patch reset to zero. <!--#f3339b07dd8dfb40-->
  - `Version.bump_minor` (method) — Returns a new Version with minor incremented and patch reset to zero. <!--#3d59389e3f5867ab-->
  - `Version.bump_patch` (method) — Returns a new Version with patch incremented. <!--#ddc46dd1a9d0bc33-->
  - `Version.with_prerelease` (method) — Returns a copy of the Version with the prerelease identifier replaced. <!--#6da00fb8dfe0907e-->
  - `Version.with_build` (method) — Returns a copy of the Version with the build metadata replaced. <!--#c78c75cdc85a37d8-->
  - `Version.bump` (method) — Dispatches to bump_major/minor/patch based on the given BumpType. <!--#1621340211520461-->
  - `Version.__eq__` (method) — Equality comparison against another Version (ignoring build metadata) or a 3-tuple of numbers. <!--#60b50cf04371f68a-->
  - `Version.__hash__` (method) — Hashes the Version on its numeric components and prerelease, excluding build metadata. <!--#0d62c0a2d0e94ec0-->
  - `Version.__lt__` (method) — Implements SemVer precedence ordering, including prerelease identifier comparison rules. <!--#08963aa698cc60d5-->
  - `Version.__le__` (method) — Less-than-or-equal comparison derived from __eq__ and __lt__. <!--#abc20a7cc2141ee0-->
  - `Version.__gt__` (method) — Greater-than comparison derived from __le__. <!--#00451315f65f92a1-->
  - `Version.__ge__` (method) — Greater-than-or-equal comparison derived from __lt__. <!--#24ebfdfd27ae87fc-->
- `VersionInfo` (class) — Dataclass bundling detected project type, version-file path, raw version string, and parsed Version. <!--#802e8ec3419df566-->
- `VersionFileHandler` (class) — Abstract base class defining the read/write/ensure/create interface for format-specific version file handlers. <!--#a07b8f65236b1ffc-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.can_handle` (method) — Abstract predicate indicating whether the handler supports a given file path/format. <!--#db58566b8a10520b-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.read_version` (method) — Abstract method to read and return the version string from a file. <!--#5035056e002230d5-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.write_version` (method) — Abstract method to write a new version string into the file. <!--#a475c00f546c0bb6-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.ensure_version` (method) — Optional hook (default unsupported) that idempotently inserts a version field if one is missing. <!--#c9a4431ce5153943-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Optional hook (default unsupported) that creates a new version file with an initial version. <!--#6a4f7c21938ff82f-->
- `JsonVersionHandler` (class) — Version file handler for JSON files like package.json, reading/writing the top-level version field. <!--#ce928dc45bec4d5f-->
  - `JsonVersionHandler.can_handle` (method) — Returns True for .json files or files named package.json. <!--#2bf682d38aefb50b-->
  - `JsonVersionHandler.read_version` (method) — Loads the JSON and returns its version field, raising if absent. <!--#83346fccd78f5315-->
  - `JsonVersionHandler.write_version` (method) — Updates the JSON version field and rewrites the file with 2-space indentation. <!--#de1b95612151f94f-->
  - `JsonVersionHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Creates a minimal package.json with name/version/description fields, erroring if one already exists. <!--#a274cb9243bcc633-->
- `TomlVersionHandler` (class) — Version file handler for TOML files like pyproject.toml, supporting PEP 621 and Poetry version fields. <!--#6fe3d2c4bfecb0f0-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.can_handle` (method) — Returns True for .toml files or files named pyproject.toml. <!--#cf5108c660cb6332-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.read_version` (method) — Parses the TOML and returns project.version or tool.poetry.version, raising if neither is present. <!--#09f2a22b558ba011-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.write_version` (method) — Regex-replaces the version string in the [project] or [tool.poetry] section while preserving formatting. <!--#1992edca58aa8de2-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.ensure_version` (method) — Adds a version field under [project] (creating the section if needed) when none exists. <!--#ae9fafd9dd9ff935-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Creates a minimal PEP 621 pyproject.toml with build-system and project sections. <!--#5ecc875d7ab5fac3-->
- `PythonVersionHandler` (class) — Version file handler for .py files exposing __version__, version, or VERSION assignments. <!--#16a991b3b7e0ddb0-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.can_handle` (method) — Returns True for any .py file. <!--#b096d66b4d0a6776-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.read_version` (method) — Regex-extracts the version from __version__, version, or VERSION assignments. <!--#20c1d195b1aab75d-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.write_version` (method) — Regex-replaces the version in __version__, version, or VERSION assignments. <!--#d549e76c5f9c361d-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.ensure_version` (method) — Prepends a __version__ assignment to the file if no version is found. <!--#6dfb4e1ab685ea1d-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Creates a version.py with __version__ inside the detected package or src/ directory. <!--#ad58a4cb4acc90dd-->
- `SetupPyHandler` (class) — Version file handler for setup.py that reads/writes the version keyword of the setup() call via AST. <!--#b8ea17a61702ecba-->
  - `SetupPyHandler.can_handle` (method) — Returns True only for files named setup.py. <!--#faafe99ad3e31b2c-->
  - `SetupPyHandler.read_version` (method) — Walks the AST to locate the setup() call's version keyword and returns its constant value. <!--#a7cd71c89280a9c8-->
  - `SetupPyHandler._get_func_name` (method) — Helper extracting a callable's name from an AST Name or Attribute node. <!--#bec71767409a06e2-->
  - `SetupPyHandler.write_version` (method) — Locates the version argument via AST positions and replaces its string, falling back to regex for multi-line cases. <!--#a009ee54b96ba372-->
  - `SetupPyHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Creates a minimal setup.py invoking setuptools.setup() with name and version. <!--#f241b6ce5dd61c41-->
- `VersionDetector` (class) — Detects a project's type and locates/reads its version file by checking known markers and file locations in priority order. <!--#4fea9be4e65f2ddf-->
  - `VersionDetector.__init__` (method) — Initializes the detector with its ordered list of TOML/JSON/Python/setup.py handlers. <!--#48f8b1a48b142f73-->
  - `VersionDetector.detect_project_type` (method) — Classifies the project as Python, Node.js, or Unknown by checking characteristic marker files. <!--#d0ebb06157a824d2-->
  - `VersionDetector.detect_project_type_without_version_file` (method) — Classifies project type from language/framework markers and source structure when no version file exists yet. <!--#54ca047bc8b24a52-->
  - `VersionDetector.get_version_file_path` (method) — Returns the first known version-file location that both matches a handler and yields a readable version. <!--#3714d693e64ea4a4-->
  - `VersionDetector.read_version` (method) — Reads a version string from a path by delegating to the first capable handler. <!--#d4769f408e454856-->
  - `VersionDetector.detect` (method) — Main entry point that detects project type, finds the version file, and returns a populated VersionInfo. <!--#4a30496f59d5ac93-->
- `VersionConfig` (class) — Configuration dataclass controlling whether bumping is enabled, an explicit version-file path, and commit-message inclusion. <!--#014d4efef42053a3-->
  - `VersionConfig.validate` (method) — Returns a list of validation errors, e.g. when the configured version file path does not exist. <!--#9d8ace4382297af9-->
- `VersionBumper` (class) — High-level orchestrator that detects, reads, bumps, sets, and rolls back versions via file handlers or an optional version script. <!--#511ac50dd45ecfd1-->
  - `VersionBumper.__init__` (method) — Initializes the bumper with config, handler list, detector, backup state, and script-mode flags. <!--#987a05dfe1c3fdb4-->
  - `VersionBumper.register_handler` (method) — Appends a custom version file handler to the bumper's handler list. <!--#32122fd9d619e3d1-->
  - `VersionBumper.detect_version_file` (method) — Locates the version file, preferring a version script, then an explicit config path, then auto-detection. <!--#16c556251b1d2a5c-->
  - `VersionBumper._find_and_init_script` (method) — Searches for a version script and, if found, switches the bumper into script mode with a VersionScriptRunner. <!--#adc59518a3995bb0-->
  - `VersionBumper.initialize_version_system` (method) — Bootstraps versioning for a project by generating a version script or creating/updating an appropriate version file. <!--#f85719e10f4d362b-->
  - `VersionBumper._get_handler_for_new_file` (method) — Returns a handler capable of creating a new file with the given suffix. <!--#2ab4976ca4b6c6d7-->
  - `VersionBumper.detect_project_type` (method) — Delegates to the detector to classify the project's type. <!--#aec769c16a3c72d1-->
  - `VersionBumper._get_handler` (method) — Returns the first registered handler that can process the given file path, raising if none apply. <!--#c46fafc4e8a5aaa4-->
  - `VersionBumper.read_version` (method) — Reads the current version via the script runner in script mode, otherwise via the detected file's handler. <!--#fe3a2746035c133f-->
  - `VersionBumper.parse_version` (method) — Static convenience wrapper delegating to Version.parse. <!--#55545ad66a6934ff-->
  - `VersionBumper.validate_semver` (method) — Static convenience wrapper delegating to Version.validate. <!--#b4dfccabd4c8fb35-->
  - `VersionBumper.bump_version_string` (method) — Static helper that parses a version string, applies a bump, and returns the new string. <!--#5a9b2633882efb56-->
  - `VersionBumper.bump_version` (method) — Bumps the version in the file or script, capturing a backup for rollback and returning the new version. <!--#53f37d782d5be3e5-->
  - `VersionBumper.set_version` (method) — Validates and writes an explicit version directly (no bump computation), capturing a rollback backup. <!--#b2acecbc992d2fa9-->
  - `VersionBumper.save_original_version` (method) — Records the current version and its path as a backup for potential rollback. <!--#58bfbb0699c085d9-->
  - `VersionBumper.rollback` (method) — Restores the backed-up version via handler or script, then clears the backup state. <!--#059becaee9ad1190-->
  - `VersionBumper.clear_backup` (method) — Discards the saved backup so the last bump becomes permanent, typically after a successful commit. <!--#a854889561986177-->
  - `VersionBumper.atomic_bump` (method) — Context manager that applies a bump and yields the new version, auto-rolling back on exception and clearing the backup on success. <!--#8520e55a31d36db5-->

### `src/se3/engine/version_script_interface.py` (python) — Module for managing project version scripts: provides VersionScriptRunner to invoke a script's get/bump/set subcommands via subprocess and parse the results, plus helpers to locate, validate, and LLM-generate a version script tailored to the project. <!--#0e53153b3b79a7fc|c410e6e037c8df3a-->
- `VersionScriptRunner` (class) — Class that runs a version script's get/bump/set subcommands via subprocess and returns parsed Version objects. <!--#98b4f61a5c96e0ff-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the runner with a script path and project root (used as cwd), raising FileNotFoundError if the script is missing. <!--#0928b5697a4b7343-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner._run_script` (method) — Invokes the version script (via python/bash/direct) with given args and a timeout, returning stripped stdout or raising RuntimeError on failure. <!--#dea2c93f7c197c77-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner.get_version` (method) — Calls the script's 'get' command and returns the parsed current Version. <!--#f9aaac75f0d15371-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner.bump_version` (method) — Calls the script's 'bump' command with the given bump type and returns the new Version. <!--#f094221c393e8096-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner.set_version` (method) — Calls the script's 'set' command to explicitly set a version string and returns the resulting Version. <!--#2e00806c0b7fe690-->
- `find_version_script` (function) — Locates the project's version script, checking a configured path first then the default se3/scripts locations, returning its Path or None. <!--#dffe245a479cd4ad-->
- `validate_script` (function) — Validates a version script by running its 'get' command, returning a (is_valid, error_message) tuple. <!--#98058fd72961d58c-->
- `generate_version_script` (function) — Uses an LLM to generate a version script tailored to the project structure, writing it to disk, validating it, and making it executable. <!--#4042aeeaa878b170-->
- `_validate_generated_script` (function) — Checks that the LLM-written script exists, is non-empty, has valid Python syntax, and contains a read_version() function. <!--#16d30943aaff6188-->
- `_scan_project_for_generation` (function) — Scans the project to detect its type, candidate version files, and current version to inform script generation. <!--#de357e474966dba1-->
- `_load_template` (function) — Loads the bundled version script template from the templates directory, or a placeholder if absent. <!--#4965c6c93641fa49-->
- `_build_generation_prompt` (function) — Constructs the LLM prompt instructing it to write a version script to the target path based on project info and the template. <!--#3a98ca7c38f412ef-->

### `src/se3/engine/worktree.py` (python) — Git worktree lifecycle utility module providing helpers to create, fork, remove, and force-clean worktrees and branches, plus merge-conflict detection and LLM-assisted resolution, all wrapped by an exception-safe WorktreeContext manager. <!--#c4d85ecb353d3b4c|dc4c498fcd3567b3-->
- `_run_git` (function) — Internal helper that runs a git subcommand in a given project root via subprocess, with configurable error-checking and timeout. <!--#fde166d981df8704-->
- `has_commits` (function) — Returns whether the repository has at least one commit by checking if HEAD resolves. <!--#eedc238ff332a101-->
- `get_current_branch` (function) — Resolves the current branch name, working on both populated and empty repos via symbolic-ref with a rev-parse fallback. <!--#2e6f604688447f87-->
- `_branch_safe_name` (function) — Converts a branch name into a filesystem-safe directory name by replacing slashes with hyphens. <!--#cc8e98cb43f0ac71-->
- `create_worktree` (function) — Creates a git worktree for a branch under se3/worktrees/, with pruning and timeout-doubling retries. <!--#46f06f633b1f8f67-->
- `fork_worktree` (function) — Creates a new branch from a source branch and sets up a worktree for it (used by the relay strategy). <!--#f48d9ef83b40d95d-->
- `remove_worktree` (function) — Removes a git worktree resiliently, handling already-deleted directories, locked worktrees (double-force), and stale metadata via pruning. <!--#1829e020bd67d3d9-->
- `_force_remove_if_still_registered` (function) — Force-removes a worktree entry when git still tracks it after pruning, by inspecting porcelain worktree-list output. <!--#89eb514629084d02-->
- `_cleanup_git_worktree_metadata` (function) — Last-resort helper that directly deletes the internal .git/worktrees/<safe_name> metadata directory. <!--#5b0e5d350a7da2a3-->
- `force_cleanup_worktree` (function) — Forcefully and fault-tolerantly removes a branch's worktree through a six-step sequence (unlock, remove, rmtree, prune, metadata cleanup, verify) for inconsistent-state recovery. <!--#c7aba362e1be00dd-->
- `delete_branch` (function) — Deletes a local branch, first force-cleaning any worktree still registered for it. <!--#eef8cbd9d7138774-->
- `has_new_commits` (function) — Returns whether a branch has any commits ahead of a given base branch. <!--#f4edc123aabe5a25-->
- `exists_for_branch` (function) — Returns whether a worktree is already registered for a given branch by parsing porcelain worktree-list output. <!--#74103a50bb9fc065-->
- `get_conflicting_files` (function) — Returns the list of files with merge conflicts via a worktree-vs-index unmerged diff. <!--#3f1832ae28ca0082-->
- `detect_unmerged_paths` (function) — Returns deduped paths in unmerged-index state by reading the index directly (catching modify/delete cases that get_conflicting_files misses). <!--#e556cc1055c95525-->
- `merge_in_progress` (function) — Returns whether a real git merge/cherry-pick/rebase/revert is mid-flight by checking for marker files in the resolved git directory. <!--#9ced3782cc2dca53-->
- `recover_stale_unmerged_paths` (function) — Auto-resolves stale unmerged-index entries left by a prior failure when safe (working tree matches HEAD), returning resolved and human-needing-attention path lists. <!--#50f627f74a09fbdd-->
- `get_diff_stat` (function) — Returns the `git diff --stat` summary string between a branch and a base branch. <!--#d14c134710526000-->
- `resolve_merge_conflicts_with_context` (function) — Resolves merge conflicts via the LLM using full task/group/spec context, verifying marker-free output and retrying without falling back to --theirs. <!--#8b1d0c0949972df5-->
- `WorktreeContext` (class) — Context manager providing exception-safe worktree lifecycle—creating one on enter and removing it (but preserving the branch) on exit. <!--#bd0659262faa940f-->
  - `WorktreeContext.__init__` (method) — Initializes the context manager with project root, branch, and an empty worktree-path slot. <!--#bc42ff0de12cc5de-->
  - `WorktreeContext.__enter__` (method) — Validates no existing worktree for the branch, creates one, and returns its path. <!--#a4162b03623770c5-->
  - `WorktreeContext.__exit__` (method) — Removes the created worktree on exit (including on exceptions), logging the cleanup. <!--#0c7666626a47f293-->

## `src/se3/engine/formatters/` — Package providing the SE3 engine's task-formatting API, which validates task-list data (required fields, complexity, dependency integrity, cycle detection) and renders task groups into Rich tree, table, detail, summary, dependency-map, and implementation-plan views. <!--#1b4c84e5ed9a1175|2ce50dddb72b1f1f-->

### `src/se3/engine/formatters/__init__.py` (python) — Package init for the SE3 engine formatters, re-exporting the task formatting API (TaskFormatter, TaskDataValidator, TaskValidationError, and format_task_groups) from task_formatter. <!--#22f9c3569771702b|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/formatters/task_formatter.py` (python) — Rich-based task formatting module that validates task-list data (required fields, complexity, dependency integrity, and cycle detection) and renders task groups into tree, table, detail, summary, dependency-map, and implementation-plan views including DAG topology, execution-strategy, and LOC statistics. <!--#795b2307acac071e|50c6e24d6bc0f0be-->
- `_md_heading` (function) — Helper that builds a reverse-color block heading Text via _reverse_title. <!--#f1f52807a66af571-->
- `_heading_group` (function) — Helper that wraps body renderables with a reverse-color heading and matching footer into a Rich Group. <!--#9d666073ce164827-->
- `TaskValidationError` (class) — Exception type raised when task-data validation fails. <!--#868e99ba0adf3b5e-->
- `TaskDataValidator` (class) — Class that validates and normalizes task-list structure, including required fields, complexity, and dependency integrity. <!--#dff249dc1c22b374-->
  - `TaskDataValidator.validate` (method) — Validates a full task list, normalizing each task, rejecting duplicate IDs, and checking dependencies. <!--#2f2a9aad43fa2dc0-->
  - `TaskDataValidator._validate_task` (method) — Validates one task dict, enforcing required fields and filling optional fields with defaults. <!--#e9a09cff2880eb69-->
  - `TaskDataValidator._validate_dependencies` (method) — Checks that dependency/depends_on fields are lists of known task IDs and triggers cycle detection. <!--#ab8aa6e10809309e-->
  - `TaskDataValidator._check_circular_dependencies` (method) — Detects circular dependencies among tasks via a three-color DFS over the dependency graph. <!--#849b5c958fd28e7d-->
- `TaskFormatter` (class) — Main formatter class that renders task groups into Rich tree, table, detail, summary, dependency, and implementation-plan views. <!--#626f5a864fa11b3e-->
  - `TaskFormatter.__init__` (method) — Initializes the formatter with a Rich console and a TaskDataValidator instance. <!--#d4734cdcc8d08064-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_tasks` (method) — Dispatches task-group formatting to tree or table view based on the requested mode. <!--#f39588af93915899-->
  - `TaskFormatter._format_tree_view` (method) — Renders task groups as a hierarchical Rich Tree with complexity badges, files, dependencies, and a summary line. <!--#9291f474a280033f-->
  - `TaskFormatter._format_table_view` (method) — Renders task groups as a flat Rich Table with ID, group, description, complexity, and dependency/criteria counts. <!--#31203a0e9b8178cf-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_task_detail` (method) — Renders a detailed single-task view as a key/value table under a per-task heading with complexity icon. <!--#18fe44ea3fef9117-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_summary` (method) — Renders aggregate statistics (group/task counts, complexity breakdown, deps, criteria, effort estimate) as a summary table. <!--#79e56750824aa7e5-->
  - `TaskFormatter._calculate_avg_complexity` (method) — Computes the weighted average complexity score across tasks (small=1, medium=2, large=3). <!--#2ac50f195b62aa79-->
  - `TaskFormatter._estimate_effort` (method) — Derives a human-readable effort estimate (hours/days/weeks) from task count and average complexity. <!--#732f9190234d3afd-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_implement_plan` (method) — Renders the implement-step plan with execution-strategy summary, task tree, optional DAG topology, and LOC statistics. <!--#6003cca7d82a7f66-->
  - `TaskFormatter._format_strategy_line` (method) — Builds the execution-strategy summary line (single/dag_parallel/sequential) with icon, LOC context, and optional reason. <!--#709f0931b93fee7d-->
  - `TaskFormatter._build_implement_tree` (method) — Builds a Rich Tree of task groups for the implement plan, annotating tasks with complexity, estimated LOC, and files. <!--#4f9b3fb564ea37ce-->
  - `TaskFormatter._compute_topo_waves` (method) — Computes topological execution waves of parallelizable groups via Kahn's algorithm, ordered by group_order. <!--#60000bbf915c98d5-->
  - `TaskFormatter._build_dag_topology` (method) — Builds a layered DAG topology diagram showing waves, LLM call numbering, and relay/fork/merge annotations from a RelayPlan. <!--#85583c02477a7016-->
  - `TaskFormatter._format_loc_summary` (method) — Builds the total and per-group LOC statistics line for the implement plan. <!--#90bd438f64d33add-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_dependencies` (method) — Renders a dependency map table listing each task's dependencies and computed dependents across all groups. <!--#a264942af6747829-->
- `format_task_groups` (function) — Module-level convenience function combining task, summary, and dependency sections into a single renderable view. <!--#1a59b24466bca805-->

## `src/se3/engine/merge/` — The SE3 merge engine package that sequentially merges branches into the current branch with LLM-assisted conflict resolution, coordinating an orchestrator, three-way conflict context/resolver, spec guardrail checking and repair, a safe/strict/fast strategy decider, MCP human-call escalation, git-ignored runtime sync, SemVer version aggregation, and worktree/branch cleanup. <!--#545fd03ebc5d7d40|a67785448f4a4237-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/__init__.py` (python) — Public API surface of the SE3 merge engine package, re-exporting the orchestrator, conflict context/resolver, guardrails, runtime sync, version aggregation, strategy decider, and cleanup components for sequential branch merging with LLM-assisted conflict resolution. <!--#4e72180f7fb9722b|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/cleanup.py` (python) — Implements the `--delete-merged` cleanup for `se3 merge`, providing CleanupManager and helpers that safely archive and remove worktrees, promote completed engine state, and delete merged branches while protecting current/unmerged/configured branches, all tallied in a CleanupReport. <!--#bb018bc6f0569a75|ec2efc301829c05f-->
- `_read_init_default_branch` (function) — Reads git's `init.defaultBranch` config value (or None) so a repo's custom integration branch can be auto-added to the protected set. <!--#c6d785bb210037c8-->
- `_load_protected_branches` (function) — Builds the effective protected-branch set by combining the hardcoded baseline, git's `init.defaultBranch`, and `merge.protected_branches` from se3.yaml, falling back to the baseline on any config-load error. <!--#186e605ef95b66ac-->
- `_build_locale_env` (function) — Returns a copy of the environment with `LC_ALL`/`LANG` pinned to C (and `LANGUAGE` cleared) so git stderr stays English for reliable keyword matching (J2). <!--#695fbdcf800c9c55-->
- `_run_git_locale` (function) — Wrapper that runs a git command against a project root in the locale-pinned C environment with captured output and DEVNULL stdin (J2). <!--#fa3542eba6c79592-->
- `CleanupReport` (class) — Dataclass tallying the outcome of a cleanup run — deleted branches plus per-reason skip lists, archived worktree paths, and promoted terminal-state snapshots. <!--#d678524803e55ce2-->
- `_WorktreeRecord` (class) — Dataclass holding one parsed `git worktree list --porcelain` entry (path, head, branch, detached/bare flags, and a non-local-ref flag for J7). <!--#28d19ef401ec29c8-->
- `_parse_worktree_porcelain` (function) — Parses `git worktree list --porcelain` output block-by-block into validated `_WorktreeRecord`s, logging and dropping malformed blocks instead of silently skipping them (J1, J7). <!--#9922630aafe049fa-->
- `_get_worktree_path_for_branch` (function) — Returns the filesystem path of the local-branch worktree bound to a given branch (or None), skipping non-local-ref records (J7). <!--#2906c7bf2f8b62fe-->
- `_archive_worktree` (function) — Copies a worktree directory into `se3/worktrees/.archive/<slug>-<ts>/` (excluding `.git`) with recovery metadata before destructive deletion, raising on filesystem failure. <!--#2db4baae034fab97-->
- `_promote_completed_engine_state` (function) — Copies a worktree's COMPLETED `engine.json` (any status when `force=True`) into the main project's state archive before deletion so the daemon/webui can report the flow's completed lifecycle. <!--#35fd60c5bd1e68e1-->
- `_is_worktree_clean` (function) — Returns whether a worktree has no uncommitted or untracked changes (treating a missing dir as clean and an unreadable one as dirty) so `git worktree remove` can run without `--force`. <!--#13fcb50dbcbbb210-->
- `_is_branch_ancestor_of_head` (function) — Returns True/False/None for whether a branch is an ancestor of HEAD via `merge-base --is-ancestor`, with None meaning undecidable and treated by callers as do-not-delete (J4). <!--#b716a8e760161657-->
- `CleanupManager` (class) — Class that orchestrates safe deletion of merged branches and their worktrees, exposing a partial report for recovery if the run raises mid-way. <!--#283ba581e89bbe65-->
  - `CleanupManager.__init__` (method) — Stores the project root and initializes the `_current_report` field that exposes in-progress cleanup state to callers' exception handlers. <!--#80bf35838fa3650d-->
  - `CleanupManager.delete_merged_branches` (method) — Main routine that, per branch, skips protected/current/unmerged branches, archives and removes clean bound worktrees, promotes completed state, and runs `git branch -d`, recording each outcome in the CleanupReport. <!--#aa451a3bf03434ef-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/conflict_context.py` (python) — Read-only builder that gathers complete three-way merge context — branch names, SHAs, commit messages, oneline logs, and per-file conflict data (four versions, hunks, binary/spec classification, text decoding) — into a ConflictContext for LLM-based conflict resolution. <!--#19ef5218619ec0d0|3f4381af5c45f195-->
- `ShaResolutionError` (class) — Exception raised when a git ref cannot be resolved to a commit SHA, so the merge halts visibly instead of silently continuing with an empty SHA. <!--#14181aca2a4ac79d-->
- `ConflictHunk` (class) — Dataclass holding the 1-based start/end line range of a single `<<<<<<<`...`>>>>>>>` conflict block. <!--#bd6d9147dc8b0d55-->
- `ConflictFile` (class) — Dataclass capturing all per-file conflict data: the four content versions, existence flags, hunks, spec/binary classification, and decoding (encoding/lossy) status. <!--#741937ea92d50ab0-->
- `ConflictContext` (class) — Top-level dataclass aggregating one merge's full context — branch names, merge-base, head SHAs/messages, oneline logs, and the list of conflicting files. <!--#efc05225f8fefe19-->
- `_git_show_bytes` (function) — Runs `git show <ref>` (including `:N:<path>` index stages) and returns the raw bytes plus an existence flag, handling timeouts and errors gracefully. <!--#46008387dee37aaf-->
- `_decode_text` (function) — Decodes bytes to text by detecting UTF-32/16/8 BOMs and falling back to lossy UTF-8 replacement, returning the text, encoding name, and a lossy flag. <!--#bc0a2e7c3743390d-->
- `_decode_lossy` (function) — Backwards-compatible wrapper around `_decode_text` that returns only the decoded text for external callers. <!--#b45b47dcee7b2866-->
- `_looks_binary` (function) — Heuristic that classifies bytes as binary by matching known magic-byte signatures (at offset 0 and within the first 512 bytes) or detecting NUL bytes. <!--#a9ab25300ea6b325-->
- `_read_gitattributes_binary_paths` (function) — Parses the project's `.gitattributes` to return glob patterns explicitly marked binary (`binary`/`-text`/`-diff`). <!--#ee82061393628243-->
- `_path_matches_binary_pattern` (function) — Returns whether a relative path matches any of the given binary glob patterns, testing both the full path and the bare basename. <!--#ae169f13c2436b9c-->
- `_is_spec_path` (function) — Returns whether a path matches the `se3/specs/**/spec.md` spec-file pattern. <!--#52ac92675013ccc1-->
- `_parse_hunks` (function) — Scans conflict-marker text to find `<<<<<<<`...`>>>>>>>` blocks and return their line ranges, tolerating diff3 markers and unmatched starts. <!--#b2f42f8ef9ca0ce8-->
- `_read_working_tree` (function) — Reads the working-tree version of a file as bytes, returning an existence flag and handling missing/unreadable files. <!--#a833da06d43a858d-->
- `_resolve_sha` (function) — Resolves a ref to a full commit SHA via `git rev-parse`, raising `ShaResolutionError` on any failure or empty result. <!--#ca2413026b4efe5f-->
- `_commit_message` (function) — Returns the full commit message (subject + body) for a ref, or an empty string on failure. <!--#e964eb7f6f75ff78-->
- `_merge_base` (function) — Returns the merge-base commit SHA between two refs, raising `ValueError` on empty input arguments. <!--#14f71f9b25b208c8-->
- `_oneline_log` (function) — Returns the `git log <base>..<head> --oneline` commits (up to a limit) as a list of strings. <!--#19cd724550e13c5d-->
- `_build_conflict_file` (function) — Collects and assembles a complete `ConflictFile` for one path — fetching all four versions, classifying binary/spec, decoding text, and parsing hunks. <!--#73182d7958538926-->
- `build` (function) — Public entry point that builds a full `ConflictContext` for an in-progress merge by resolving SHAs, logs, and per-file conflict data (read-only). <!--#6ebd8dd8afc3bc7e-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/conflict_resolver.py` (python) — Module that resolves git merge conflicts by iteratively prompting an LLM to edit conflicted working-tree files in place—rescanning for residual conflict markers each round (with Unicode-whitespace-hardened detection) until resolved or a configured iteration cap is reached—and synthesizing the outcome into a structured LLMResolution that flags unresolved files for human review. <!--#486016d8e39fa843|2b9ebe4a720c4c46-->
- `_normalize_unicode_whitespace_for_marker_detection` (function) — Helper that maps a set of Unicode whitespace prefix characters (NBSP, zero-width, BOM, etc.) to ASCII spaces for marker detection only, so disguised conflict markers can't evade the regexes. <!--#b53f346f2ca1d839-->
- `_has_conflict_markers` (function) — Returns whether a text blob still contains git conflict markers, tolerating up to 7 leading spaces/tabs and normalized Unicode whitespace, and also catching a stray ======= divider. <!--#917d39cfa8592ae6-->
- `_has_any_conflict_marker` (function) — Reads the file at a path and reports whether it still has conflict markers, treating a missing file as resolved and a read error as unresolved. <!--#ff273679e9eaf157-->
- `_scan_unresolved` (function) — Filters a list of paths down to those whose files still contain conflict markers, preserving input order. <!--#4914e931eee5f132-->
- `_load_max_conflict_resolve_iterations` (function) — Reads the configured max conflict-resolution iteration count from project config, falling back to 10 on any error. <!--#71204d72e0685063-->
- `_preview` (function) — Trims a string to a short truncated preview (with a remaining-char suffix) for storing on outcome records. <!--#a08e37d395298bcd-->
- `HunkValidationError` (class) — Exception raised when a HunkResolution payload (e.g. line numbers) is malformed. <!--#fdd34bd771c38197-->
- `ResolvedContentTooLargeError` (class) — Exception raised when an LLM resolution's content exceeds the configured size cap. <!--#d03720d1f58c1128-->
- `Confidence` (class) — String enum of resolution confidence levels (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW). <!--#dc02a14650d6e871-->
- `MergeStrategy` (class) — String enum of the three conflict-resolution strategies (fast/safe/strict) with a from_str classmethod that fails loudly on the removed default/robust names. <!--#57850004c153e35d-->
  - `MergeStrategy.from_str` (method) — Parses a string into a MergeStrategy, raising migration-friendly errors for the removed 'default'/'robust' names and listing valid options otherwise. <!--#13accfbe29a410a4-->
- `HunkResolution` (class) — Dataclass holding the resolution result for a single conflict hunk (validated 1-based line range, confidence, reasoning). <!--#b764faf99e100832-->
  - `HunkResolution.__post_init__` (method) — Validates the hunk's start/end line numbers and enforces end_line >= start_line, raising HunkValidationError on bad values. <!--#1014dae11a150b03-->
