  - `HunkResolution._validate_line` (method) — Classmethod that coerces/validates a line-number field to a positive bounded int, rejecting None, bools, non-ASCII numerals, and out-of-range values. <!--#472cc527f6b2bbe5-->
- `FileResolution` (class) — Dataclass holding the resolution result for a single file (path, resolved content, hunks, confidence, flags, spec marker). <!--#3177741ae28eddb2-->
- `LLMResolution` (class) — Dataclass aggregating the complete LLM resolution result across all conflict files, with overall confidence, flags, and raw response/parse-error fields. <!--#43b3a064635d1b4c-->
- `BatchContext` (class) — Dataclass carrying merge-level metadata (branches, SHAs, logs, strategy) for a resolve_batch call, decoupled from the per-file list. <!--#ff3a9ad8b2a2f3ca-->
- `IterationFailure` (class) — Dataclass recording one iteration's failure mode and affected files, fed back into the next iteration's prompt instead of triggering take-theirs. <!--#0bfe4e4812133b90-->
- `BatchResolveOutcome` (class) — Dataclass summarizing a resolve_batch run: resolved/unresolved paths, iterations used, escalation reason, failure history, timing, and prompt/response previews. <!--#29444bc8647cbf34-->
  - `BatchResolveOutcome.success` (method) — Property returning True when no escalation occurred and no files remain unresolved. <!--#0d36d6f331e2183b-->
- `ConflictResolver` (class) — Main class that resolves merge conflicts by iteratively prompting an LLM to edit working-tree files in place, judging success by whether markers remain. <!--#5545d5037f1d9f90-->
  - `ConflictResolver.__init__` (method) — Constructs the resolver with a project root, optional shared LLMCaller/trace, and a positive resolved-content byte cap. <!--#24d0499556e2b012-->
  - `ConflictResolver.resolve` (method) — Thin wrapper that builds a BatchContext from a ConflictContext, runs resolve_batch, and synthesizes the result into an LLMResolution. <!--#a46441d349a1f254-->
  - `ConflictResolver._synthesize_resolution_from_outcome` (method) — Translates a BatchResolveOutcome into an LLMResolution, reading back on-disk content for cleared files and flagging unresolved or unreadable files for human review. <!--#1ffbb06151dfa253-->
  - `ConflictResolver.resolve_batch` (method) — Core iteration loop that repeatedly builds an editor prompt, calls the LLM, and rescans files for markers until resolved or max_iterations is hit, returning a BatchResolveOutcome with the appropriate escalation reason. <!--#009706a6d1f4d769-->
  - `ConflictResolver._build_editor_prompt` (method) — Constructs the LLM-as-editor prompt for one iteration, assembling merge metadata, spec warnings, prior-failure history, and per-file base/ours/theirs/working blocks. <!--#f8074b4f31a2d971-->
  - `ConflictResolver._call_llm` (method) — Sends a prompt to the (shared or lazily-built) LLMCaller and optionally records a timed, redacted entry to the LLM trace. <!--#e893a70c18916891-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/guardrail_repair.py` (python) — Module providing GuardrailRepairer, which drives LLM-based repair of post-merge spec guardrail violations by building a prompt, parsing corrected spec content, writing it back under se3/specs/**/spec.md, committing (fix-up commit preferred over amend), and re-verifying—with a strict amend/rollback safety contract and test-mode gating. <!--#dbb48c0557ca91b9|778140db357c6e4b-->
- `RepairResult` (class) — Dataclass holding the outcome of a repair attempt: success flag, repaired files, error text, whether amend was used, and files skipped for missing content. <!--#8a4277828d8b3791-->
- `_is_test_environment` (function) — Helper that detects whether code is running under a test harness via the PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST or SE3_GUARDRAIL_REPAIR_TEST_MODE env vars. <!--#1a59ca252d7b649f-->
- `GuardrailRepairResponseParseError` (class) — ValueError subclass marking that the LLM responded but its output could not be parsed as JSON, distinct from transport errors. <!--#5b0723fa04585374-->
- `GuardrailRepairInconsistentState` (class) — RuntimeError raised when rollback cannot be performed safely, carrying an INCONSISTENT_REPAIR_STATE failure reason to hard-stop the merge sequence. <!--#759538f0ae2a61a2-->
  - `GuardrailRepairInconsistentState.__init__` (method) — Constructor that sets the message and attaches the INCONSISTENT_REPAIR_STATE failure_reason enum. <!--#04d331b235aac86d-->
- `GuardrailRepairer` (class) — Main class that orchestrates LLM repair of spec guardrail violations—building prompts, writing corrections back, committing, and re-verifying—with test_mode safety gating. <!--#393d4bab6122927f-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer.__init__` (method) — Initializer storing project root, optional shared LLM caller and trace, and validating that test_mode is only enabled inside a real test environment. <!--#bd408905c6a97528-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer.repair_violations` (method) — Entry-point method that sends violations and spec contents to the LLM, validates the response, writes corrected files back, commits, and re-checks guardrails. <!--#47a45121494ff4e9-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._probe_branch_verifiable` (method) — Helper that checks whether a branch is a verifiable git ref, treating timeouts and git failures as unverifiable so the silent-loss check fires conservatively. <!--#e085aa5ae817e2c5-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._amend_preserved_merge_topology` (method) — Helper verifying an amended HEAD retains the original merge commit's parent set, distinguishing real topology violations from transient git failures. <!--#83a5eea5de34a7a7-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._format_violations` (method) — Helper that renders the violation list (with evidence such as strong/weak lines, deleted clauses, and topology) into prompt text. <!--#f94d2d94be695007-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._format_spec_contents` (method) — Helper that formats a path-to-content spec dict into a labeled text block for the repair prompt. <!--#84016bcd9d96a331-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._restore_merged_content` (method) — Cleanup helper that best-effort restores merged spec content (or removes hallucinated tracked files) after a failed repair, re-raising the first restore error. <!--#429fea1c9124eae9-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._rollback_commit` (method) — Helper that rolls back a repair commit by soft-resetting to the captured pre-repair SHA, refusing to use HEAD~1 and raising inconsistent-state when no safe target exists. <!--#b80f76abf1f4ffd9-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._call_llm` (method) — Helper that invokes the LLM caller with the repair prompt, optionally records a trace, and extracts/validates the JSON response. <!--#6ced7b4774497bce-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._parse_response` (method) — Helper that normalizes the LLM response (dict or string) into a parsed JSON dict containing a 'files' key, or None on failure. <!--#addb6af6de17705e-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/guardrails.py` (python) — Pure-logic module that enforces spec-protection guardrails on a merge by diffing changed `se3/specs/**/spec.md` files between two git refs to detect requirement weakening, quantifier weakening, deletions, size-budget overruns, and bad merge topology, returning a fail-closed GuardrailReport of stably-hashed violations. <!--#e28bd859f5ba97d0|b1a37a332205ddf6-->
- `_evidence_dict` (function) — Helper that builds a violation evidence dict via EvidenceRecord so unknown keys fail fast with a TypeError. <!--#eaa7ac8fdd6d88a4-->
- `GuardrailViolation` (class) — Dataclass representing a single guardrail violation with its file path, type, message, and diagnostic evidence. <!--#f07c968360073291-->
- `GuardrailReport` (class) — Dataclass holding the overall result of a guardrails check (passed flag, violations list, and fail-closed incomplete flag). <!--#f8059de2a6f52afd-->
- `_tokenize_for_pairing` (function) — Tokenizer that strips role words and stop words to extract content tokens for strong↔weak line similarity comparison. <!--#934ca71c228fe4c9-->
- `_tokenize_for_deduplication` (function) — Tokenizer that keeps role words (but drops stop words) so a strong line can be distinguished from its weakened variant during deduplication. <!--#cf6567000bdaf281-->
- `_jaccard_similarity` (function) — Computes Jaccard similarity between two token sets, returning 0.0 when either set is empty. <!--#b593fcbb81531c9e-->
- `_pair_strong_weak_lines` (function) — Greedily pairs missing strong lines with new weak lines by descending Jaccard similarity above a threshold, each line used at most once. <!--#66341ebe0796c5be-->
- `_extract_weak_role_word` (function) — Extracts the weak role keyword (e.g. SHOULD/MAY) from a line, or None if none is present. <!--#ac436197e33bb640-->
- `_weak_line_is_new` (function) — Determines whether a weak-only line is genuinely new (not a pre-existing or whitespace-only variant), treating a changed weak role word as new. <!--#f4d445ef165be61a-->
- `_precompute_orig_data` (function) — Precomputes stripped strings and both token-set variants for original lines to avoid re-tokenizing across pattern checks. <!--#04754242eadc2a13-->
- `_compute_pairing_evidence` (function) — Builds evidence for a strong→weak transition by pairing a disappeared strong line with a new weak-only (or optionally mixed) line via token similarity. <!--#3f633a92b160dd36-->
- `_first_missing_strong_line` (function) — Returns the first strong line that disappeared and its line number, used as minimal evidence for DELETE violations. <!--#8263d772aeedefff-->
- `_normalize_message` (function) — Normalizes a violation message for stable hashing by stripping line numbers, attempt counters, and SHA-like tokens while preserving counts. <!--#89507c9bc0b6dcf7-->
- `_stable_hash_short` (function) — Returns a short deterministic SHA-256 hex digest of text for sentinel keys. <!--#5c8683f0a1767008-->
- `_stable_key_from_violation` (function) — Derives a stable, format-insensitive hash key from a violation's evidence (strong/deleted/WHEN-clause lines), falling back to the normalized message. <!--#b16564cfe3c8a4d7-->
- `_normalize_for_comparison` (function) — Normalizes text into a sorted role/stop-word-free token string for identity comparison so role-word or punctuation differences collapse. <!--#01bfe89cc9fe74fd-->
- `violation_set_hash` (function) — Computes an order-independent stable hash over a set of violations from their file path, type, and evidence-derived stable key. <!--#8498b3f3ca3361dd-->
- `check_spec_diff` (function) — Core pure function that compares two spec versions and returns all weakening, quantifier-weakening, and deletion violations using two-layer detection. <!--#c35d13da507651d2-->
- `_rel_spec_path` (function) — Best-effort conversion of a spec path to a posix path relative to the project root. <!--#6f104b491084f943-->
- `check_spec_sizes` (function) — Pure, LLM-free check that walks every spec file and reports size-budget violations for base spec, per-file, and per-Requirement byte limits. <!--#0b377d27a9f7d4a0-->
- `_next_non_blank_line` (function) — Advances to the next non-blank line from a start index, raising StopIteration at end-of-file. <!--#3f4a6c956a546a12-->
- `_extract_when_clauses` (function) — Extracts WHEN clauses from spec lines, joining reflowed indented continuation lines to avoid spurious deletion detection. <!--#44a3d34afd8833b4-->
- `_normalize_when_clause` (function) — Normalizes a WHEN clause for identity comparison, preserving short tokens and role/stop words unlike the general normalizer. <!--#21c5f6075c9dd681-->
- `_is_spec_path` (function) — Canonical predicate returning True when a path matches `se3/specs/**/spec.md`, rejecting empty intermediate segments. <!--#faf60cbfd38edafb-->
- `ChangedSpecFilesIncomplete` (class) — Exception raised when the git diff for changed spec files fails, so callers fail closed instead of assuming no changes. <!--#31e4a8dbb4724810-->
- `_get_changed_spec_files` (function) — Returns the spec files changed between two git refs, distinguishing a real empty diff from a failed diff by raising ChangedSpecFilesIncomplete. <!--#54d50811dd02db3d-->
- `_read_file_from_ref` (function) — Reads a file's content from a git ref via `git show`, returning None when unavailable. <!--#858bd66e15a18942-->
- `_check_spec_file_against_ref` (function) — Compares a single spec file between an old and new ref (or worktree), emitting DELETE/CHECK_INCOMPLETE markers and delegating content checks to check_spec_diff. <!--#eb639d60c4d88238-->
- `_check_merge_topology` (function) — Validates that the post-merge commit is a descendant of the pre-merge HEAD and is a real merge commit (with opt-in fix-up tolerance), returning topology violations. <!--#ef56fdec0d6f393c-->
- `MergeGuardrailsCheck` (class) — Class orchestrating guardrail checks over the spec files touched by a merge between two commits, including merge-topology validation. <!--#b500f2c5e16d6cfa-->
  - `MergeGuardrailsCheck.__init__` (method) — Initializes the check with the project root path. <!--#fc13bde9d61f7a1d-->
  - `MergeGuardrailsCheck.check` (method) — Deprecated backward-compatible entry point that delegates to check_merge_result. <!--#3b0761d4bf0d92b5-->
  - `MergeGuardrailsCheck.check_merge_result` (method) — Lists changed spec files between two commits, validates merge topology, runs spec-diff checks on each, and returns a fail-closed GuardrailReport. <!--#ed91003073421d48-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/human_call.py` (python) — Module that writes MCP human-call files for merge conflicts and post-merge guardrail violations into a project's se3/calls/ directory, providing the HumanCallWriter class plus helpers for collision-resistant call filenames, atomic JSON writes, orphan-file guardrail validation, and printing reviewer instructions. <!--#a64f40b367ffa284|76047dd2fafeb843-->
- `_reset_call_seq_after_fork_in_child` (function) — os.register_at_fork child handler that reinitializes the process-level call-sequence counter and its lock so a forked child cannot reuse the parent's seq values. <!--#93f0ed501bc55d98-->
- `_generate_call_filename` (function) — Builds a collision-resistant call filename from prefix, UTC microsecond timestamp, pid, an atomic sequence number, an 8-char SHA, and a sanitized branch label. <!--#c8159a35d9364bee-->
- `_atomic_write_json` (function) — Atomically writes call JSON via a temp file plus os.replace with fsync, symlink-refusal protection, and original-mode/0o644 permission preservation. <!--#b6cfa9d212432913-->
- `_read_original_for_orphan` (function) — Fetches a file's original content from base_ref (falling back to HEAD) via `git show` to support orphan guardrail diffing, returning None if absent. <!--#1a3016dadf670813-->
- `_is_spec_path` (function) — Thin delegator to guardrails._is_spec_path so spec-path detection (se3/specs/**/spec.md) stays canonical across the merge subsystem. <!--#85efc2ce33848333-->
- `_scan_orphan_content_for_evidence` (function) — Scans a rejected orphan file's resolved content for suspicious patterns (conflict markers, smuggled spec keywords, oversize, spec-like paths) and returns structured evidence for the reviewer. <!--#23ec339de6d50e50-->
- `HumanCallWriter` (class) — Class that writes MCP human-call files for merge conflicts and post-merge guardrail violations under a project's se3/calls/ directory. <!--#499a0803273b63c6-->
  - `HumanCallWriter.__init__` (method) — Stores the project_root path used to locate the se3/calls/ output directory. <!--#fc13bde9d61f7a1d-->
  - `HumanCallWriter.write_call` (method) — Assembles per-file conflict context plus LLM resolution proposals, validates orphan files against guardrails, and writes a merge-conflict human-call file. <!--#5b1a005995de8417-->
  - `HumanCallWriter.write_guardrail_call` (method) — Writes a human-call file for guardrail violations detected after a merge, validating violation dicts and embedding rollback/repair instructions. <!--#0e938f6d349fbff9-->
  - `HumanCallWriter.print_instructions` (method) — Reads a call file and prints user-facing instructions, response format, and a summary of violations/next steps to the console. <!--#1d1be8ad87b70e5b-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/orchestrator.py` (python) — The MergeOrchestrator module that sequentially merges branches into the current branch, coordinating git merge calls, conflict resolution, guardrail checks/repair, version aggregation, runtime sync, and result aggregation, plus a crash-safe atomic file-write helper. <!--#77589d74c3f95b1c|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/runtime_sync.py` (python) — Synchronizes git-ignored tier-A runtime content under se3/ from a source branch's worktree into the current branch after a git merge, using hardened atomic file writes (renameat2/RENAME_NOREPLACE to close symlink-swap TOCTOU windows), bounded I/O caps against hostile files, and collision auditing with sidecar tracking. <!--#ab909ed0fb8194f2|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/strategy.py` (python) — Module implementing the safe/strict/fast decision matrix that, given an LLM conflict resolution's confidence and spec-guardrail flags, decides whether to ACCEPT, REJECT, or escalate a merge to a HUMAN_CALL, via both a legacy single-resolution path and a newer batch resolve-and-decide path. <!--#a81da339556b94d6|fd94ea476199f009-->
- `DecisionAction` (class) — String enum of the three terminal decisions a strategy can reach: ACCEPT, HUMAN_CALL, or REJECT. <!--#bc263ff5be2b5d9d-->
- `StrategyDecision` (class) — Dataclass bundling a strategy's chosen action, a human-readable reason, and optional batch outcome / unresolved-file details for downstream orchestration. <!--#5a5765bc74c70683-->
- `StrategyDecider` (class) — Class that decides whether to accept, reject, or escalate a conflict resolution, dispatching across the safe/strict/fast merge strategies. <!--#28e18589511ef908-->
  - `StrategyDecider.decide` (method) — Legacy single-resolution entry point that routes an LLMResolution to the safe/strict/fast decision method based on the merge strategy. <!--#f9aaf33cc2ed29ae-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_safe` (method) — Safe-strategy logic that accepts a resolution unless explicit requires_human_review or spec_guardrail_concern flags (global or per-file) demand a human call. <!--#c9297b94ee3d7092-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_strict` (method) — Fallback strict-strategy logic requiring every hunk and overall confidence to be HIGH with no guardrail flags, else escalating to a human call. <!--#240c886d0f935bbd-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_fast` (method) — Fast-strategy logic that aggressively accepts non-spec files but rejects spec files on human-review or low-confidence signals, never calling a human. <!--#5e80c2888b04a526-->
  - `StrategyDecider.resolve_and_decide` (method) — Newer batch entry point that runs the resolver and dispatches to the per-strategy *_batch deciders, translating the outcome into a StrategyDecision. <!--#ea291ee351b07a3d-->
  - `StrategyDecider._run_resolver` (method) — Helper that drives ConflictResolver.resolve, builds a ConflictContext, and derives a BatchResolveOutcome (preferring an attached outcome or re-scanning for unresolved markers). <!--#c9c0ce846deffd61-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_fast_batch` (method) — Fast batch decider that ACCEPTs when all markers clear (subject to fast flag gates) and REJECTs on iteration exhaustion, never escalating to a human. <!--#0e356fb39af47485-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_safe_batch` (method) — Safe batch decider that ACCEPTs when all markers clear (subject to safe flag gates) and escalates to HUMAN_CALL on iteration exhaustion. <!--#3bb1d80eec3d777c-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_strict_batch` (method) — Strict batch decider that short-circuits the resolver and routes every conflict file straight to a human MCP call without invoking the LLM. <!--#49e4c40caceb9a2d-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/version_aggregator.py` (python) — Computes the aggregated SemVer bump for a set of merged branches by comparing pyproject.toml versions at each merge-base and tip, then atomically rewrites the version field and amends the last merge commit, with section/triple-quote-aware TOML parsing and fail-loud rollback handling for no-op, corrupt, and write/git failure paths. <!--#61210775f690c3eb|d5342d20e0b318f0-->
- `VersionNotAdvanced` (class) — Documentation-only RuntimeError describing the fail-loud 'on-disk version already at or above target' condition that callers may raise instead of accepting a false success. <!--#147a2fa2febe45c7-->
  - `VersionNotAdvanced.__init__` (method) — Stores the pre-merge, current, and target version strings and builds the explanatory 'no bump applied' message. <!--#b12259069490d4d2-->
- `_slice_to_next_section` (function) — Returns TOML content from a section start up to the next line-anchored section header, skipping over triple-quoted strings. <!--#199ed868d02d591f-->
- `_strip_triple_quoted_strings` (function) — Returns the content with all triple-quoted string blocks removed so embedded version-like literals aren't matched. <!--#f9d97057fabebb37-->
- `_find_triple_quoted_regions` (function) — Returns half-open (start, end) offset ranges of every triple-quoted block in the content. <!--#c934417522f7a342-->
- `_find_version_match_in_section` (function) — Returns the first `version = "..."` regex match that lies outside any triple-quoted region, or None. <!--#bfaf31411e2b9cdc-->
- `_parse_pyproject_version` (function) — Extracts the version string from pyproject.toml content, preferring [project] over [tool.poetry] with section and triple-quote awareness. <!--#a1708031992d7430-->
- `read_version_at_ref` (function) — Reads and parses pyproject.toml's version as it existed at a given git ref, returning None when absent or unparseable. <!--#dfc1c3ff78c29e16-->
- `_diff_bump` (function) — Returns the BumpType (MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH) going from a base Version to a branch Version, treating prerelease→release as PATCH and None when not advanced. <!--#0a2cdd1198ba4f38-->
- `InferResult` (class) — Dataclass pairing an inferred bump type (or None) with a human-readable reason string. <!--#4a852784336bceba-->
- `infer_branch_bump` (function) — Infers a branch's SemVer bump by comparing pyproject versions at the merge-base and branch tip, returning None (with a reason) on missing/unreadable/non-advancing versions. <!--#607a0a1cb38faaad-->
- `max_bump` (function) — Returns the highest-priority bump from a list, defaulting to PATCH for an empty list. <!--#ae0a425b7d47d771-->
- `AggregateResult` (class) — Dataclass capturing the outcome of aggregate_and_apply, including success, before/after versions, bump type, error, and the already-at/higher-than-target anomaly flags. <!--#5a2fc7e603d44e55-->
- `_atomic_write_text` (function) — Writes text to a path atomically via temp-file + fsync + os.replace, preserving mode, guarding against destination symlinks, and flushing the parent directory. <!--#a93e22e5d1af0a4a-->
- `_safe_write_version` (function) — Locates the version field's byte offset and rewrites pyproject.toml's version atomically, optionally reusing a caller-supplied content snapshot to avoid cross-read drift. <!--#fad8303d4e307893-->
- `_reset_staged_pyproject` (function) — Runs `git reset HEAD pyproject.toml`, logging and returning an error string on timeout/OSError/non-zero exit so a failed amend leaves no stale staged change. <!--#49cd07058d20978d-->
- `aggregate_and_apply` (function) — Top-level entry point that computes and applies the aggregated bump to pyproject.toml and amends the last merge commit, with rollback and fail-loud handling for no-op, corrupt, and write/git failure paths. <!--#496f8f107da329c8-->

## `src/se3/engine/steps/` — The flow engine's step-handler package, providing one module per pipeline step type (discovery, analyze, plan/plan_tasks, confirm, implement, test, self_check, invariant_check, charter_freshness, version_analyze, commit, summarize, project_summary) plus a registry in __init__.py that maps StepType values to handlers and shims deprecated step types, driving the LLM-backed task-execution flow from clarification through code generation, verification, and committing. <!--#77bd473f0af0bc62|e23856fe4b0e64c2-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/__init__.py` (python) — Package init for the flow engine's step handlers that registers step-type handler functions and provides backward-compatibility stubs (PROPOSE, DESIGN, PROJECT_SUMMARY) which warn and forward to their current replacement handlers so old persisted flows can still resume. <!--#3af01ae499045cf0|4b179c6ca8599baf-->
- `propose_stub_handler` (function) — Backward-compatibility stub for the deprecated PROPOSE step type that logs a warning and forwards to plan_handler so old persisted flows can resume. <!--#6fb89b174cba579c-->
- `design_stub_handler` (function) — Backward-compatibility stub for the deprecated DESIGN step type that logs a warning and forwards to plan_handler so old persisted flows can resume. <!--#ab925d0e54c6959b-->
- `project_summary_stub_handler` (function) — Backward-compatibility stub for the deprecated PROJECT_SUMMARY step type (now merged into ANALYZE) that logs a warning and forwards to project_summary_handler so old persisted flows can resume. <!--#0ddfcccc8427c3ad-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/_fix_context.py` (python) — Helper module that renders the fix-context prompt block for a step's fix iterations, providing utilities to format the iteration/cap counter, schema-tolerantly extract issue fields (severity/description/location) across old and new schemas, and assemble the multi-line reviewer message while omitting fix_history to avoid bias. <!--#879eff276f120e3b|e1e167a8536068b1-->
- `format_fix_iteration_display` (function) — Formats a fix iteration and cap as a compact `<n>/<cap>` (or `<n>/unlimited`) string for log lines. <!--#20f94d99307f7201-->
- `extract_issue_display_fields` (function) — Schema-tolerant reader that pulls (severity, description, location) out of an issue dict whether it uses the new self_check schema or the legacy verify_spec one, defaulting missing fields to empty strings. <!--#7c6be96c5a8cbcf4-->
- `render_fix_context` (function) — Builds the multi-line fix-context prompt block for a step (initial-pass message, iteration count, final-attempt warning, and previously-reported issues), deliberately omitting fix_history to avoid biasing reviewers. <!--#8395e1ce73d6743f-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/analyze.py` (python) — Implements the flow's read-only "analyze" step, which collects programmatic project context, makes one LLM call to classify the task's type and complexity (injecting charter and code-index orientation maps), and rebuilds the flow's step sequence accordingly — with helpers for task-type extraction, --type override conflicts, project-summary collection, and step-sequence reconstruction. <!--#24241d270a13abaf|a69fafa2342119ec-->
- `analyze_handler` (function) — Executes the flow's read-only "analyze" step by collecting project context, making a single LLM call to classify the task type (feature/bugfix/review/small/directive) and complexity, injecting charter and code-index orientation maps, and updating the flow's task type and step sequence accordingly. <!--#4dafc25f409f1c22-->
- `_extract_task_type` (function) — Extracts and validates the task_type from the LLM output, downgrading 'discovery' to 'feature' unless the --discover flag was explicitly set and defaulting invalid values to 'feature'. <!--#4b0f5f2da387e239-->
- `_handle_type_conflict` (function) — Returns the explicit --type flag value when set, overriding the task type the LLM analysis resolved. <!--#581b4b10d216bb7d-->
- `_collect_project_summary` (function) — Gathers structured project context (git status, active flows, backlog, specs) via ProjectContextCollector and formats it into a concise text block, replacing the former PROJECT_SUMMARY LLM step. <!--#b083896bf9f5f700-->
- `_update_flow_steps` (function) — Rebuilds the flow's selected step sequence from the default sequence for the resolved task type, applying se3.yaml step config and inserting confirmation steps. <!--#3ccce3367c21b7e1-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/charter_freshness.py` (python) — A non-blocking flow step that judges whether code changes leave the charter stale: it cheap-passes empty diffs, otherwise asks the LLM for a freshness verdict, runs an advisory charter admission/altitude gate when charter.md itself was edited, and always returns COMPLETED with the verdict recorded as advisory output. <!--#5fb77ead98eafe10|38e432be0c07e528-->
- `_changed_files` (function) — Helper that extracts a flat list of changed file paths from the `changes_made` payload, tolerating both string and dict `files_changed` entry shapes. <!--#8b6c4d2c442424e0-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Helper that renders the diff's changed-files list (with actions and explanations) into a human-readable string for the freshness prompt. <!--#63fed8bbe4faa206-->
- `_run_admission_trigger` (function) — Helper that runs the charter admission/altitude gate only when the diff edited `se3/charter.md`, recording its size/threshold/warning results into `step.outputs` without ever blocking. <!--#43861c20be7d9a0d-->
- `charter_freshness_handler` (function) — The step handler that cheap-passes on empty diffs, otherwise calls the LLM to judge charter freshness, always returning COMPLETED and recording the verdict plus admission results as advisory, non-blocking outputs. <!--#18539b09f227e3d0-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/commit.py` (python) — The commit step module: it stages and git-commits flow changes, writes the authoritative version from version_analyze to the project version file (with rollback/repair fallbacks), decorates the commit message from upstream-step summaries, and runs two fault-tolerant backstops that strip se3 runtime-leak paths and warn about root-whitelist-excluded files. <!--#c311e33011fc8f2a|8cab713cb294031d-->
- `_detect_runtime_leaks` (function) — Pure path-signature predicate that returns which staged paths carry an se3 runtime signature (a top-level `.se3/`, or a nested `se3`/`.se3` followed by a known runtime-subtree name) outside the legitimate top-level `se3/` root. <!--#c5e4e71e671d9029-->
- `_strip_runtime_leaks` (function) — Fault-tolerant backstop run between `git add` and `git commit` that unstages detected runtime-leak paths and warns, never failing the commit, returning whether any leak was found. <!--#2effffb256a8aef8-->
- `_index_has_staged_changes` (function) — Checks whether anything remains staged after leak-stripping, returning True (assume committable) on any git error so it never short-circuits a legitimate commit. <!--#4ef01544d2b8b91f-->
- `_root_deny_excludes` (function) — Helper that uses `git check-ignore -v` to confirm whether a given path is ignored specifically by the root `/*` default-deny rule (versus some ordinary gitignore rule), returning False fault-tolerantly on any subprocess error. <!--#114ca63636e40293-->
- `_detect_root_whitelist_exclusions` (function) — Diagnostic-only backstop run between `git add -A` and commit that enumerates top-level untracked paths swept up by the root `/*` whitelist rule and logs a single WARNING listing them, without modifying .gitignore, staging, or commit control flow. <!--#905992454b796cf0-->
- `commit_handler` (function) — The commit step entry point that stages and git-commits flow changes, optionally writing the authoritative `suggested_version` from version_analyze to the project version file (with auto-repair/initialization fallbacks) and invoking the root-whitelist guard, returning COMPLETED or FAILED. <!--#23c788f716772a52-->
- `_load_version_config` (function) — Thin wrapper that lazily imports and loads the project's VersionConfig to avoid circular imports. <!--#4c9c3fe4b832d2e3-->
- `_resolve_target_version` (function) — Resolves the authoritative target version from the version_analyze step's suggested_version, raising RuntimeError (halting the commit) if that step failed or produced none. <!--#7106e85fbee3d03f-->
- `_stage_file` (function) — Stages a single file via `git add`, resolving it relative to the project root and raising RuntimeError on failure. <!--#23f43a7c6b6b7a0b-->
- `_update_docs` (function) — Best-effort mechanical update of the README.md badge and VERSIONS.md changelog via DocumentationUpdater, staging both, swallowing any failure so docs never abort the commit. <!--#56d644ab0a00578e-->
- `_rollback_version` (function) — Restores the version file to its original value via VersionBumper.rollback, re-raising if the rollback itself fails. <!--#25140dabaebd94dc-->
- `_has_changes` (function) — Determines whether there is anything to commit, diffing a baseline commit against HEAD when available and falling back to `git status --porcelain`. <!--#c3879be18295377b-->
- `_generate_commit_message` (function) — Builds the full commit message via a priority chain of upstream-step summaries, decorating it with bump type, changed files, incomplete-task notes, version, and flow reference. <!--#28aec61a19bdf37e-->
- `_get_commit_hash` (function) — Returns the current HEAD commit hash via `git rev-parse`, yielding 'unknown' on empty repos or any git failure. <!--#fb0dc536f4bf1449-->
- `_generate_template_summary` (function) — Produces and writes a non-LLM markdown work-summary document (to se3/state/) from commit outputs and flow state when no summarize step is present. <!--#fb953b360092015a-->
- `_collect_changes_from_flow` (function) — Gathers the list of changed file paths from all implement-step outputs in the flow history. <!--#9eb8c57d96e672be-->
- `_collect_test_results_from_flow` (function) — Returns the most recent test step's test_results dict from the flow history, or an empty dict if none exists. <!--#dc428ebd61d1ef28-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/confirm.py` (python) — The CONFIRM step handler that gates a reviewed step through either synchronous LLM review (capped by a cross-revision iteration counter) or an asynchronous human-in-the-loop flow that writes a call file and polls for a response sidecar, returning COMPLETED, REVISION_NEEDED, or PAUSED. <!--#b04040131349aaad|ebc50be1da48293f-->
- `TimeoutError` (class) — Custom exception raised when polling for a human review response exceeds the allotted time. <!--#a6c6b7f03a421c70-->
- `_check_existing_response` (function) — Reads a `.response` sidecar file (if present) for a given call file and returns the parsed approval/feedback dict, used to detect human responses on resume. <!--#9723ee1681b75054-->
- `_wait_for_human_response` (function) — Blocks by polling for a human response file at a fixed interval, returning the response or raising TimeoutError when a timeout elapses. <!--#2d3854fcd84f716d-->
- `_create_call_file` (function) — Writes a uniquely-named JSON call file under `se3/calls/` describing the step under review, signaling that human confirmation is requested. <!--#aa0a2e4d2b361003-->
- `_llm_review` (function) — Performs LLM-based review of the reviewed step's output (with a max-iteration cap from the persisted cross-revision counter), returning COMPLETED or REVISION_NEEDED plus a review-result dict. <!--#b91cb2ace03799dd-->
- `confirm_handler` (function) — Top-level CONFIRM dispatcher that routes to synchronous LLM review or the human call-file/response flow, returning COMPLETED, REVISION_NEEDED, or PAUSED. <!--#8c46893f0eb1f6cb-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/conftest.py` (python) — A pytest configuration file that excludes step-handler implementation modules (test.py and test_with_fail_loop.py) from test collection, since their `test`-prefixed names would otherwise be mistaken for test modules. <!--#93a55fa5e88f5424|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/discovery.py` (python) — The discovery step handler that drives a multi-turn, PAUSED-based conversation with the user — building prompts enriched with charter/code-index/project context, calling the LLM in two-phase JSON mode to ask clarifying questions and propose a refined task description, executing emitted issue operations, rendering each turn to the console, and resolving to COMPLETED once the user confirms via the '1'/GUI confirmation gate. <!--#de96b9204c86fbcf|575927fe9f5fa660-->
- `discovery_confirm_metadata` (function) — Builds the (prompt, options) display metadata — a Markdown instruction with the '输入 1 确认' fallback plus a one-click confirm button valued '1' — shown when a non-interactive discovery step pauses at the confirmation gate. <!--#7e3ff5e798341b2e-->
- `_gather_project_context` (function) — Detects and formats basic project context (project type/name, test framework, git remote and branch) from files in the project root for inclusion in the discovery prompt. <!--#2efc5e2fb07052a6-->
- `discovery_handler` (function) — Main step entry point that drives one discovery round per call, manages multi-turn conversation state via PAUSED, executes any emitted issue operations, and returns COMPLETED once the user confirms. <!--#259e516927633f5b-->
- `_run_discovery_round` (function) — Executes one round of the multi-turn discovery conversation by building the prompt (with charter, code-index, language, issue, and runtime-environment injections), invoking the LLM in two-phase JSON mode, then parsing, validating non-empty, and returning the structured result alongside the raw response text. <!--#e863e7c8efc84287-->
- `_format_conversation_history` (function) — Formats the accumulated conversation history list into a plain ROLE: content text block for prompt inclusion. <!--#ce6ad351fc217e64-->
- `_format_issue_op_engine_note` (function) — Builds an engine note summarizing this round's executed issue operations and the current set of in-scope tracked issue IDs, to append to the conversation history for the LLM. <!--#15b7d36de96e91b3-->
- `_generate_summary` (function) — Produces a short summary string counting assistant rounds and user inputs from the discovery conversation history. <!--#3e9395a1b38195a0-->
- `_extract_narrative_from_raw` (function) — Strips fenced and bare JSON blocks out of the raw LLM result text to recover any surrounding narrative prose for display. <!--#951c0061d894ad35-->
- `_proposed_description_block` (function) — Builds a nested cyan Rich reverse-color block that wraps the LLM's proposed refined task description with clear se3-rendered boundaries. <!--#9760a3663ed57bcc-->
- `_display_discovery_message` (function) — Renders the discovery turn to the console — narrative, content, proposed description, questions, issue-operation summary, and a token-usage footer — across question/synthesis/confirmation modes. <!--#2adde47662411e5c-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/implement.py` (python) — Implement step handler that drives LLM-based code generation for task groups via the DAG scheduler, managing worktrees, merge-conflict recovery, version-bump guardrails, the why-comment convention, and fix iterations for the test-verify-fix loop. <!--#02a86af5277fd5bf|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/invariant_check.py` (python) — An engine step handler that detects violations of documented code invariants by harvesting why-comments and charter anchors from touched files, prompting an LLM to flag issues, and returning COMPLETED or REVISION_NEEDED to drive the fix loop (cheap-passing when there is no diff or no anchors). <!--#49e49bb82ad639ba|d782ef85fc2a655d-->
- `_extract_comments` (function) — Best-effort textual harvest returning the bodies of single-line `#`/`//` comments from a block of text. <!--#90739f6db8d26015-->
- `_read_baseline_file` (function) — Reads a file's original pre-implementation content at the flow's frozen baseline commit via `git show`, returning None when there is no baseline or the file is unavailable. <!--#2e17a8cbfdf0c653-->
- `_harvest_why_comments` (function) — Collects colocated why-comments from each touched file, merging baseline and working-tree content so original invariant-documenting comments survive even if the diff deleted or rewrote them. <!--#d9851e8426c286b3-->
- `_build_anchor_inputs` (function) — Assembles the synthetic step_inputs (task text, charter, why-comments, changed files) that drive self_check's validators, sourcing anchors from frozen step inputs with on-disk/harvest fallbacks. <!--#69b66727417e5344-->
- `_anchor_pool_is_empty` (function) — Returns True when the frozen anchor set normalizes to no usable text, signaling the anchor-less case where the check must be refused. <!--#1bdb8c1632821713-->
- `_has_changed_files` (function) — Returns True iff the `changes_made` payload reports at least one changed file/path. <!--#cbe8e49e3e236b70-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Renders the diff's changed-file list into prompt text mirroring self_check's view. <!--#68b655da37aa3b06-->
- `invariant_check_handler` (function) — Entry-point handler that cheap-passes on no diff or no anchors, otherwise prompts the LLM, validates issues against the anchor pool, and returns COMPLETED or REVISION_NEEDED to drive the fix loop. <!--#a3cfb67e8ca7e621-->
- `_build_fix_outputs` (function) — Populates the step's fix-loop outputs (issues, fix instructions, iteration counts) from validated invariant violations and returns REVISION_NEEDED, mirroring self_check's fix output shape. <!--#259888a25e114e3e-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/plan.py` (python) — The unified 'plan' step handler that, in a single depth-adapted LLM call (depth chosen from task_type, with charter/code-index/issue/language/runtime injections and a version-bump guardrail), generates and stores a complete plan—proposal, design, and task groups—on the step outputs and renders it to the console. <!--#3768aa619d568e8e|a8c2aea47989b8ff-->
- `_get_prompt_depth` (function) — Maps a task_type string to a prompt-depth level ('full' for feature/discovery, 'medium' for bugfix, 'shallow' otherwise). <!--#ce8cd3dfad9063df-->
- `_build_prompt` (function) — Assembles the final plan prompt by composing the header with proposal/design/tasks sections and the matching JSON schema according to the chosen depth. <!--#739f8fa1c96d7334-->
- `plan_handler` (function) — The handler for the unified 'plan' step that, in a single depth-adapted LLM call (with charter/code-index/issue/language/runtime injections), generates and stores the full plan (proposal, design, task groups) on the step outputs, returning COMPLETED on success or FAILED on missing input or errors. <!--#ddca62978c2788fc-->
- `_display_plan` (function) — Renders the generated proposal, design, and task groups to the console using Rich formatters for human-readable output. <!--#4d18d096d6926809-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/plan_tasks.py` (python) — The plan_tasks flow-step handler module: it builds a task-planning prompt from the design doc, proposal, and spec content (synthesizing a minimal design when DESIGN was skipped), augments it with charter/code-index/issue-discovery/runtime-environment/revision injections, calls the LLM to break the work into structured task groups with complexity and LOC estimates, and stores the parsed groups as step outputs. <!--#ca86700f219dd22f|082d773d725c8833-->
- `plan_tasks_handler` (function) — The handler for the plan_tasks flow step: it assembles a prompt from the design doc, proposal, and spec content (synthesizing a minimal design when the DESIGN step was skipped), augments it with charter/code-index/issue-discovery/revision injections, calls the LLM to break the work into task groups, and stores the parsed task groups and complexity estimates as step outputs. <!--#a255324e82e7a76c-->
- `_format_design_doc` (function) — Helper that renders a design-document dict into a readable prompt string covering overview, key decisions, components, and implementation plan. <!--#408d2cc21b753960-->
- `_format_proposal` (function) — Helper that renders a proposal dict into a prompt string summarizing the proposal and the files to modify and create. <!--#8f0ab84037ee5337-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/project_summary.py` (python) — A flow step module that generates a natural-language project summary by collecting raw project context, formatting it into an LLM prompt, and exposing both the shared generation core and a step handler that stores the result and reports COMPLETED/FAILED. <!--#87a77e1e3755f333|90d3d47590cc5270-->
- `generate_project_summary` (function) — Shared core function that collects raw project context, formats it into the summary prompt, and calls the LLM to return a natural-language project summary. <!--#574424aa7919551e-->
- `project_summary_handler` (function) — Step executor that runs the project summary generation for a flow, stores the result in step outputs, and returns COMPLETED or FAILED. <!--#4b56d7159393f684-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/self_check.py` (python) — Implements the LLM-based self_check step that, after tests pass, code-reviews the changes for logic completeness, robustness, and test-coverage gaps (explicitly excluding spec compliance), with a structural validation pipeline that grounds each issue against authoritative source quotes and changed-file evidence, plus prompt-building, change/test/spec formatting, multi-pass convergence detection, dedup, and fix-loop output assembly that routes to COMPLETED or REVISION_NEEDED. <!--#d6104343207c88eb|0665297121138aaa-->
- `_normalize_for_quote_match` (function) — Symmetrically normalizes a string (literal-\n expansion, NFKC, smart-quote folding, whitespace collapse) so an LLM's verbatim_quote can be substring-matched against the source pool despite cosmetic drift. <!--#8db8997a3a87e3a5-->
- `_build_source_pool` (function) — Assembles the list of authoritative source strings (task description, original/refined task, user interjections, non-base spec content) that an issue's verbatim_quote must be found within. <!--#a7b0735db1950583-->
- `_changed_paths` (function) — Extracts the set of changed file paths from changes_made.files_changed, tolerating string or dict entries and malformed input. <!--#8ff815377519db66-->
- `_validate_evidence` (function) — Returns whether an issue is properly grounded — a well-formed `path:N` evidence line pointing at a changed file, or a non-empty missing_in entry. <!--#f21f74dd92a232db-->
- `_describe_issue` (function) — Renders a kept issue as a single bullet line (location plus actual/expected/divergence) for the fix_instructions output. <!--#3a2af65715d0ea40-->
- `_validate_and_filter_issues` (function) — Runs the full structural validation pipeline over raw LLM issues, returning the kept issues and a stats dict of per-reason rejection counts. <!--#7faf7dc8d43fa903-->
- `_format_task_groups` (function) — Renders plan task_groups into a compact, head-truncated Markdown summary for the self_check prompt, returning empty string when there is nothing to show. <!--#88ebb9032601e706-->
- `_build_task_groups_section` (function) — Wraps the task-groups Markdown summary in its `## Plan Task Groups` prompt section, or returns empty string to avoid an orphan heading. <!--#fd3b5a4b04262bff-->
- `self_check_handler` (function) — Executes the self_check step: builds a prompt (task, changes, test results, charter, code-index map) and invokes the LLM for a code-review of logic completeness, robustness, and test coverage—excluding spec compliance—then returns COMPLETED when no issues are found or REVISION_NEEDED when issues exist, with support for multi-pass convergence and deferred-fix batching. <!--#210ce07a118a9b94-->
- `_normalize_description` (function) — Normalizes a free-text issue description (lowercase, strip punctuation, drop stopwords, sort tokens) so paraphrased issues compare equal during convergence detection. <!--#37733267f0004aa3-->
- `_issue_signature` (function) — Computes a set of (location, normalized-description) signatures for a list of issues, handling both new and legacy schemas, for dedup and convergence detection. <!--#d3cc36127f3969cb-->
- `_merge_dedup_issues` (function) — Merges incoming issues into an existing list, dropping mechanical duplicates by signature while keeping signature-less issues. <!--#764d50d7676ea599-->
- `_has_critical_or_high` (function) — Returns True if any issue in the list is of critical or high severity (case-insensitive). <!--#a3574497faf32b13-->
- `_build_fix_outputs` (function) — Populates the step's consolidated fix-loop outputs (fix_instructions, issues, iteration counters) from the accumulated issue set and returns REVISION_NEEDED. <!--#13a9625d04f948ee-->
- `_issues_converged` (function) — Returns True when the current issues largely repeat the previous set (by signature subset or shared locations), signaling the fix loop has stalled. <!--#b28509e30f468b66-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Formats the changes_made dict into a human-readable bulleted list of changed files for the prompt. <!--#2f76c452cbec9dff-->
- `_format_test_results` (function) — Formats test_results (phased or flat) into a prompt-ready text summary including pass/fail status and truncated stdout/stderr tails. <!--#094f63f9a19ee178-->
- `_format_spec_content` (function) — Formats spec_content (string or name→content dict) into a Markdown-sectioned block for the prompt. <!--#5b2f381c19897610-->
- `_format_fix_context` (function) — Thin wrapper delegating fix-context rendering to the shared render_fix_context helper, inlining previous issues for the self_check prompt. <!--#ac764dd7d21d35f4-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/summarize.py` (python) — The summarize flow step that gathers prior-step outputs (changes, tests, verification, completion status) to build and run an LLM summary prompt, with a deterministic fallback summary and persistence to `se3/state/summary-{flow_id}.md`, while gating against false 'complete/all-green' claims when verification fails. <!--#bc6c2d29bcdb8cb2|eeb4a0406fb7b6be-->
- `summarize_handler` (function) — Entry-point handler that gathers prior-step outputs, builds the summarize prompt, calls the LLM (falling back to a basic summary on empty/error), stores and saves the result, and always returns COMPLETED. <!--#e8889178ade8b70d-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Renders the changes_made dict into a Markdown bullet list of modified files, tolerating both plain-string paths and structured change dicts. <!--#e9f2222313255a7b-->
- `_gated_tests_passed` (function) — Returns the gated test pass/fail verdict, preferring critical-acceptance-gated `overall_passed` over the legacy raw `passed` key so skipped critical tests aren't reported green. <!--#b3909e825e66b5f8-->
- `_format_test_results` (function) — Formats test results into a one-line 'Tests passed: <bool>' string using the gated verdict. <!--#fc3da81113dda393-->
- `_format_verification` (function) — Formats the verification_result dict into prompt text covering the verified flag, summary, and issue/error counts. <!--#d8353e5d6198d067-->
- `_resolve_verified` (function) — Extracts the authoritative boolean `verified` verdict from verification_result, returning None when no verify_spec step ran. <!--#f1b90fb72a3da192-->
- `_verification_gate_lines` (function) — Returns prompt instruction lines forbidding 'complete/all-green' claims, but only when verification explicitly failed (verified is False). <!--#77b6a8199fa1459e-->
- `_build_completion_section` (function) — Assembles the optional completion-status prompt section (incomplete tasks, restricted edits, and the verification gate), returning empty for the clean complete-and-verified case. <!--#7577870ce91e6575-->
- `_create_basic_summary_text` (function) — Builds a deterministic Markdown summary without the LLM, used as a fallback that honors completion status and the verified=False gate. <!--#6b90098f2cdf6697-->
- `_save_summary` (function) — Writes the summary text to `se3/state/summary-{flow_id}.md` with header metadata, logging a warning on failure. <!--#c990539ad0295730-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/test.py` (python) — The test-step module: runs the project's test command(s) with dynamic timeouts, parses and classifies results across runners (pytest/jest/go/cargo), separates inherited-baseline from newly-introduced failures, applies a critical-acceptance gate, drives the bounded fix loop, records history, files pre-existing-failure issues, and returns a shared TestVerdict mapped to a StepStatus. <!--#c760a796c2734875|e04201ea4a2400cc-->
- `TestVerdict` (class) — Dataclass capturing the classified result of one test-suite run (results dict, pass flag, fix trigger, fix guidance/context, inherited failures), shared so the test step and SPEC_GATE consume one identical verdict. <!--#2fe28d757ce5a9dd-->
- `_extract_failures_section` (function) — Extracts the pytest FAILURES/ERRORS diagnostic section from stdout, per-block-truncating it to fit a character budget while preserving assertions and traceback tails. <!--#48ac6719f45bd66e-->
- `_parse_test_summary_counts` (function) — Best-effort parses aggregate passed/failed counts from a runner's summary line (pytest/cargo/jest) when per-test lines are unavailable, summing across multiple summary lines. <!--#268b30edce88f897-->
- `_summarize_passed_phase_output` (function) — Builds a compact archive summary (count line plus output tail) for a PASSED phase's otherwise-noisy verbose stdout/stderr, using a three-tier count fallback. <!--#1659723ff3b743eb-->
- `_slim_passed_phase_archive` (function) — Mutates a test_results dict in place to replace each passed phase's (and the top-level) stored stdout/stderr with the slimmed summary, leaving failed phases intact. <!--#c54a963da6a47643-->
- `_render_estimate` (function) — Formats an estimated_test_duration value for display, rendering whole floats as ints and None as 'not set'. <!--#ab9da39a8180758d-->
- `test_handler` (function) — The test step entry point: a thin shell that loads config, runs+classifies via run_and_classify_tests, then writes outputs, records history, files the once-per-flow inherited-failure issue, and maps the verdict to a StepStatus. <!--#4e502bca496a33cc-->
- `run_and_classify_tests` (function) — The shared core that runs the primary command plus configured phases with dynamic timeout, applies the critical-acceptance gate, splits inherited vs introduced failures, applies bounded baseline looping, and returns a TestVerdict. <!--#15856b5e490f16e0-->
- `_build_baseline_fix_section` (function) — Constructs the prepended fix-instruction text (mechanism B) listing active baseline failures the fix loop must also repair, with a tightly-scoped relaxation of focus limits. <!--#89d08ebc963cfce8-->
- `_extract_failure_reason` (function) — Extracts a brief failure reason string for a given test id from pytest's short summary output, falling back to a generic message. <!--#8b7946881d8e5999-->
- `_report_pre_existing_issues` (function) — Files inherited (pre-implement baseline) test failures as a single medium-priority A-class discovery issue, relying on the caller for the once-per-flow guard. <!--#11f4592b36f9fb6f-->
- `_is_timeout_result` (function) — Classifies a command result as a timeout-class failure via the structured flag, stderr marker, or -1 returncode sentinel, short-circuiting to False for any passing run. <!--#5cf69f14034df1cf-->
- `_run_command_with_timeout_retry` (function) — Runs a command and, on a timeout-class failure only, retries it once in place (without incrementing the fix iteration), returning the result and whether a retry occurred. <!--#118ae307f8169959-->
- `_run_command` (function) — Spawns a test command via Popen with a dot progress indicator and enforced timeout, guarding against recursive invocation, and returns a structured result dict with distinct sentinel returncodes for timeout (-1) vs spawn error (-2). <!--#b08b8490246aadfd-->
- `_classify_results` (function) — Splits parsed test ids into new_tests vs regression buckets (passed/failed) based on whether each id matches the implement step's added test files. <!--#1198d5758658cb17-->
- `_parse_test_ids` (function) — Parses individual (test_id, passed) tuples from pytest/jest/go/cargo runner stdout, trying each format in turn. <!--#b0d7d24039c585c4-->
- `_parse_skipped_test_ids` (function) — Parses deduplicated SKIPPED test ids from pytest verbose per-test output (ignoring the -rs short-summary form that lacks the file::test form). <!--#aff2a440b23db006-->
- `_critical_pattern_matches` (function) — Returns whether a critical-test pattern matches a test id by substring (covering exact and prefix forms). <!--#ec1772ef7be60c0f-->
- `_detect_critical_failures` (function) — Detects critical acceptance tests that were skipped or silently un-collected/missing (which would otherwise exit 0 falsely green), returning the skipped and missing lists. <!--#37c95ee988a1a3c4-->
- `_is_pytest_command` (function) — Heuristic check for whether a command invokes pytest (bare, path-suffixed, or via python -m pytest). <!--#daec89699f707a0a-->
- `_ensure_verbose_pytest` (function) — Appends -v to a pytest command when critical tests are configured but no verbose flag is present, so per-test SKIPPED lines become parseable (warning if the command isn't pytest). <!--#a56631f4701dbfd3-->
- `_resolve_cwd` (function) — Resolves a phase's optional cwd to an absolute path relative to the project root. <!--#df0454357359e938-->
- `_detect_test_command` (function) — Auto-detects the test command from project marker files (pyproject/pytest.ini → pytest, package.json → npm, Cargo.toml → cargo, go.mod → go), defaulting to pytest. <!--#2ffafee5e990e5d8-->
- `_record_test_history` (function) — Records the test execution as synthetic prompt/response entries in the chat-history system so results persist across worktree isolation and fix-loop iterations. <!--#f051597e9473e28c-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/test_with_fail_loop.py` (python) — A test-only step handler that deliberately injects a bug into the target project on the first run (tracked via a persisted run-count file) so tests fail, exercising the engine's fix loop, then runs pytest normally on subsequent runs. <!--#c94ccfc50f81af48|8fff20a98050d566-->
- `test_handler_with_fail_loop` (function) — Step handler that introduces an intentional bug on the first run before running pytest, then runs tests normally on later runs, to force the fix loop to trigger. <!--#576bd7d1fef5b377-->
- `_get_run_count` (function) — Reads the persisted run count from the tracker JSON file, returning 0 if missing or unreadable. <!--#7a98a6120b25eac3-->
- `_increment_run_count` (function) — Increments the run count and writes it back to the tracker file, returning the new count. <!--#bc0552dcc5f0422e-->
- `_introduce_temporary_bug` (function) — Edits the target project's calculator.py to replace addition with subtraction, deliberately breaking tests on the first run. <!--#46937d61991f40e5-->
- `_run_pytest` (function) — Runs `pytest -v` in the project root via subprocess and returns the completed process result. <!--#675f6b2ee4815506-->
- `reset_test_tracker` (function) — Deletes the run-count tracker file to reset state before starting a new test. <!--#da1a842a593e2517-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/version_analyze.py` (python) — The version-analyze flow step that assembles change, spec, verification, and session-commit context (plus optional project version rules) into an LLM prompt to determine the appropriate SemVer bump, then parses, validates, and writes the authoritative suggested_version and commit-message outputs. <!--#d506323c760ba722|629d4860c789e3f0-->
- `version_analyze_handler` (function) — Step entry point that gathers change/spec/verification/session-commit inputs plus optional project rules, calls the LLM, and writes the authoritative suggested_version and related fields into step outputs. <!--#630a335c713b0ad6-->
- `_read_version_rules_file` (function) — Reads the optional `se3/version-rules.md` project rules file (size-capped, error-swallowing) for verbatim injection into the prompt, returning None when absent or unreadable. <!--#3979c0847245e97e-->
- `_get_current_version` (function) — Detects the project's current version string via the configured VersionBumper, returning an "unknown" sentinel when disabled or no version file is found. <!--#0a9d200f2ca8c0e8-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Renders the implement step's changed-files and implementation-group data into a markdown block for the prompt's "Changes Made" section. <!--#6c7938dd04d95393-->
- `_format_spec_changes` (function) — Renders update_spec's spec/API-change data (dict or list forms) into a markdown block highlighting API-contract changes for the prompt. <!--#5d210c649f528bc0-->
- `_format_session_commits` (function) — Renders implement-stage commits already landed on the main branch as a capped, file-folded markdown list so the prompt can treat them as the baseline-excluded session changes. <!--#916117384c2b9364-->
- `_format_verification` (function) — Renders the verification step's pass/summary/issue results into a markdown block for the prompt's "Verification Results" section. <!--#2ae548847100d2c2-->
- `_parse_response` (function) — Parses the raw LLM response into a JSON object requiring suggested_version, then delegates to _validate_result, raising ValueError on empty or unparsable output. <!--#c3afd53b11854623-->
- `_validate_result` (function) — Validates and normalizes the parsed result — requiring a non-empty suggested_version, defaulting bump_type/confidence, and filtering versions_changes to clean strings. <!--#717fd3589621d384-->
- `_fallback_commit_message` (function) — Builds a fallback commit-subject line from the task type and description (first sentence, 72-char capped) when the LLM omits or fails to produce one. <!--#8502a2c669ba9cb5-->

## `src/se3/engine/utils/` — A small package of standalone engine helper modules, currently centered on robust parsing and repair of JSON payloads extracted from LLM responses. <!--#7ead5ec392afa505|97edfdb0427111b2-->

### `src/se3/engine/utils/__init__.py` (python) — An empty package initializer that marks src/se3/engine/utils as a Python package for grouping engine utility modules. <!--#e3b0c44298fc1c14|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/utils/json_parser.py` (python) — A robust JSON-parsing utility for LLM responses that extracts JSON payloads from stream-json, markdown blocks, or raw text and recovers from common LLM formatting errors (trailing commas, single quotes, unescaped quotes, truncation) through a repair chain, exposing parse and lenient is-JSON predicate helpers. <!--#41772d21d16224bb|d655d5bc22787606-->
- `parse_json_response` (function) — Public entry point that parses JSON from an LLM response, collecting text from stream-json assistant messages when multi-line, otherwise parsing the response directly. <!--#bfc1ed6667139fbc-->
- `_extract_and_parse_json` (function) — Helper that extracts a JSON string from text, parses it through the repair chain, and validates that required keys are present. <!--#70254293e3b33aea-->
- `_extract_json_string` (function) — Locates the JSON payload within text by stripping tool-preview lines, unwrapping markdown code blocks, and falling back to first-brace-to-last-brace or trailing-object extraction. <!--#20dcab890ff12010-->
- `_extract_trailing_json_string` (function) — Walks backwards from the last '}' to find its matching '{' (respecting strings and escaped quotes) to extract the rightmost complete JSON object. <!--#ad42bc21e87f46a3-->
- `_count_unescaped_quotes` (function) — Utility that counts unescaped double quotes in a string, skipping backslash-escaped characters. <!--#8be78ab15a58c787-->
- `_repair_unescaped_quotes` (function) — Iteratively escapes unescaped interior double quotes in JSON string values using json.loads error positions to fix LLM quoting mistakes. <!--#c7f178fd4cf6cc12-->
- `_repair_json` (function) — Repairs common LLM JSON errors by removing trailing commas, converting single quotes to double quotes, and closing truncated structures. <!--#fedcf1c86d1564bc-->
- `_close_truncated_json` (function) — Attempts to make length-truncated JSON parseable by closing open strings and balancing unclosed objects and arrays. <!--#cfd0092566cd7de7-->
- `_validate_keys` (function) — Checks that the parsed data is a dict containing all required keys (trivially true when no keys are required). <!--#a69714e9aba6d385-->
- `_try_parse_with_repairs` (function) — Shared parsing core that tries strict json.loads then escalates through the structural and quote repair chain, returning the parsed object or None. <!--#2529ab7af10ffe44-->
- `looks_like_json_object` (function) — Lenient predicate returning whether text parses as a JSON dict after the full repair chain, mirroring parse_json_response's dict-only semantics. <!--#5fa87d39d7511b7c-->
- `looks_like_json` (function) — Lenient predicate returning whether text parses as any valid JSON value via the repair chain, with a strict fallback to distinguish literal `null` from failure. <!--#9155397a29d59ee8-->

## `src/se3/server/` — The standalone `se3-server` control-plane backend package (a separate `se3[server]` extra, never imported by the core CLI): a FastAPI app that accepts outbound WebSocket connections from any number of SE3 daemons, aggregates their machines/flows/history into in-memory state, and re-exposes it through multi-tenant auth, owner-scoped REST and `/ws/ui` routes, a SQLite persistence/identity layer, and a bundled vanilla-JS web console. <!--#6ec6baf137db97fa|648c461bd923f6b5-->

### `src/se3/server/__init__.py` (python) — The `se3-server` console-script entry point that handles `--version` and `bootstrap-token` directly, then verifies the optional FastAPI/uvicorn `server` extra is installed (printing an install hint and exiting non-zero if missing) before delegating to `se3.server.app.main`. <!--#100d9dbc5eb7b9e6|f583c61a40c09d3b-->
- `main` (function) — The `se3-server` console-script entry point that handles `--version` and `bootstrap-token` on the lightweight path, then verifies the FastAPI/uvicorn `server` extra is installed (printing an install hint and exiting non-zero if not) before delegating to `se3.server.app.main`. <!--#e7924e3140aae035-->

### `src/se3/server/app.py` (python) — Defines the SE3 central-server FastAPI application module: a set of Pydantic request-body models for the flow/auth/user/issue REST endpoints plus the create_app factory and run/main entry points that wire up multi-tenant persistence, the auth-provider chain, session/state management, and all WebSocket and /api/* routes aggregating state across SE3 daemons. <!--#9e9ee58239f6bc04|546df5c430e00062-->
- `NewFlowRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for POST /api/flows that publishes a new task to a machine, optionally sourcing the flow from an existing issue via from_issue_id. <!--#b38f1b8e587353be-->
- `RespondRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for POST /api/flows/{id}/respond carrying the response value (and optional call_id) that answers a flow's pending interjection/call. <!--#601bc82ec8e99653-->
- `InterjectRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for POST /api/flows/{id}/interject carrying the text of a mid-flow instruction to inject. <!--#e6a8c6f221e6506a-->
- `EndSessionRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for POST /api/flows/{id}/end carrying an optional reason for terminating and archiving the session. <!--#6f88c386232572bc-->
- `LoginRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for POST /api/auth/login carrying the local username and password. <!--#5e295e1dd04eb1e1-->
- `BreakglassRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for POST /api/auth/breakglass carrying the one-time admin escape-hatch token. <!--#6a332b8c7ba524b7-->
- `CreateDaemonKeyRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for POST /api/daemon-keys carrying an optional label for the newly minted owner daemon key. <!--#013bfda2cf7d2e7e-->
- `CreateUserRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for POST /api/users by which an admin creates/invites a local user with username, password, display name, and admin flag. <!--#c7cedd123fc6194c-->
- `SetPasswordRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for POST /api/users/{owner_id}/password carrying the new password an admin sets for a user. <!--#6a22fa5f8e56b44b-->
- `SetAdminRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for POST /api/users/{owner_id}/admin carrying the boolean toggling a user's admin flag. <!--#d6a09ebe1f2102e5-->
- `CreateIssueRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for POST /api/issues carrying the machine, project, description, and optional metadata to create a new issue on a daemon. <!--#925faf35202fbc99-->
- `EditIssueRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for PATCH /api/issues/{id} carrying the optional fields to edit on an existing issue. <!--#cbb937a0f0df77c5-->
- `CloseIssueRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for POST /api/issues/{id}/close carrying the machine/project context and optional close reason. <!--#aedcc15c9f4772ba-->
- `ReopenIssueRequest` (class) — Pydantic request body for POST /api/issues/{id}/reopen carrying the machine/project context to reopen a closed issue. <!--#837bf7d54f6446cd-->
- `_scope_for` (function) — Helper that maps an authenticated identity to its owner-scoping value for queries, returning None (unscoped operator view) for admins and the owner_id otherwise. <!--#a7097f3c8ebc134a-->
- `_ensure_breakglass_admin` (function) — Helper that resolves or lazily creates the single stable break-glass admin owner bound to the reserved (breakglass, admin) identity. <!--#ebd011659136c965-->
- `create_app` (function) — Factory that builds and returns the fully wired, fail-closed multi-tenant FastAPI app, assembling persistence, auth provider chain, session/state managers, and all WebSocket and /api/* routes. <!--#8dd184c9c9a983ef-->
- `_create_app_kwargs_from_server_config` (function) — Helper that translates a ServerConfig (server.auth.* and db_path) into the create_app kwargs (auth_config, session_store, rate_limiter, db_path) so configuration actually takes effect. <!--#3a7807a2517fe797-->
- `run` (function) — Builds the app via create_app and starts the SE3 central server with uvicorn (blocking), threading through db_path and auth/session/rate-limiter configuration. <!--#5f5319528c05d32b-->
- `main` (function) — The se3-server console-script entry point that parses CLI args, loads server config, and runs the server with the resolved auth/cookie/lockout/db-path settings. <!--#e047ffea027b0a75-->

### `src/se3/server/bootstrap.py` (python) — A dependency-light module implementing the `se3-server bootstrap-token` CLI subcommand, which mints the one-time break-glass admin escape-hatch token by persisting only its SHA-256 hash and revealing the plaintext to the console exactly once. <!--#117c67460bfbfc86|aa87810d05a4dd59-->
- `issue_breakglass_token` (function) — Mints a break-glass token against a given store, persisting only its hash and returning the (plaintext, token_id) pair with an optional TTL. <!--#43a92d1a8aa0f88a-->
- `print_breakglass_token` (function) — Opens the sqlite store at a path, mints a token, prints it once to a stream (the design-mandated single console reveal), and returns the plaintext. <!--#4e816632366833c2-->
- `_print_banner` (function) — Formats and writes the boxed console banner that reveals the token plaintext, id, and optional expiry exactly once. <!--#3b167444ad0773f8-->
- `main` (function) — Argparse entry point for the `se3-server bootstrap-token` subcommand, parsing --db-path/--ttl and triggering the one-time token print. <!--#cc33210abb24b513-->

### `src/se3/server/crypto.py` (python) — Server security utility module providing password hashing/verification (argon2id with bcrypt fallback), token generation, hashing, and constant-time verification, plus credential fingerprinting and redaction helpers for safe logging. <!--#6cb4d5475664c3ed|7f035102747c14d4-->
- `PasswordBackendUnavailable` (class) — Exception raised when neither argon2-cffi nor bcrypt is installed, signaling the missing se3[server] extra on the password hash/verify path. <!--#8099c2e82c0aa84f-->
- `_argon2_hasher` (function) — Lazily import argon2 and return a PasswordHasher instance, or None if the backend is unavailable. <!--#fc52a7d3aa6dc5df-->
- `_bcrypt_module` (function) — Lazily import and return the bcrypt module, or None if it is unavailable. <!--#307a490487c8b7a8-->
- `_bcrypt_prep` (function) — Normalize a password into a fixed-length, NUL-free bytes value (SHA-256 + base64) to work around bcrypt's 72-byte and NUL-byte limitations. <!--#bb06af56be76fe88-->
- `hash_password` (function) — Hash a password with a slow salted algorithm, preferring argon2id and falling back to bcrypt, raising PasswordBackendUnavailable if neither exists. <!--#dec0485d3794dc2f-->
- `verify_password` (function) — Verify a password against a stored hash by dispatching on its algorithm prefix, returning False rather than raising on any mismatch or malformed input. <!--#647d73f726c8eeb8-->
- `token_hash` (function) — Return the hex SHA-256 of a token plaintext for fast, deterministic hashed storage and lookup. <!--#439625ff8bcb39f8-->
- `generate_token` (function) — Generate a high-entropy random token (optionally prefixed) and return its one-time plaintext alongside its storage hash. <!--#4604b91686f646f1-->
- `verify_token_hash` (function) — Constant-time check that a token plaintext hashes to a given stored hash. <!--#1e8b2fd48a378aaa-->
- `const_eq` (function) — Constant-time equality wrapper over hmac.compare_digest that accepts str or bytes and returns False on unsupported types. <!--#0378385214c29b7c-->
- `token_fingerprint` (function) — Return a short, non-reversible SHA-256-derived fingerprint of a secret for safe identification in logs/UI. <!--#07765d495538db1c-->
- `redact` (function) — Return a fixed placeholder for a credential that reveals neither its value nor its length. <!--#593a6a3cb211b8ef-->

### `src/se3/server/identity.py` (python) — Server-side identity service module that maps daemon keys and external auth identities to owners, enforces a trust gate on cross-provider identity linking to prevent account takeover, and tracks the live in-memory machine→owner bindings. <!--#38cf14a8062afaee|3948191864038871-->
- `UntrustedIdentityLink` (class) — Exception raised when an external identity is linked to an existing owner without passing the trust gate, guarding against account-takeover via blind auto-merge. <!--#f5020a578fd0f10a-->
- `IdentityService` (class) — Service that resolves owners from daemon keys and external identities, gates cross-provider identity linking, and maintains the live in-memory machine→owner binding index. <!--#e688faa5f37e4f48-->
  - `IdentityService.__init__` (method) — Initializes the service with a backing Store, an empty machine→owner dict, and a lock guarding that live index. <!--#949331c4e76504ed-->
  - `IdentityService.resolve_owner_for_key` (method) — Hashes a daemon key plaintext and delegates to the Store to resolve its owner_id, returning None for missing or non-matching keys. <!--#19b0bdb7d1db42ab-->
  - `IdentityService.resolve_owner_by_identity` (method) — Resolves a (provider, external_id) auth identity to its owner_id via the Store. <!--#874d22333f39d734-->
  - `IdentityService.link_identity_to_owner` (method) — Links an external identity to an existing owner only through the trust gate (admin override or both-sides-verified claim), staying idempotent for the same owner and rejecting conflicts. <!--#40178afed914ab1d-->
  - `IdentityService.bind_machine` (method) — Records under lock that a machine_id is currently owned by a given owner_id in the live index. <!--#bbba8ed39a3d379a-->
  - `IdentityService.owner_of_machine` (method) — Returns the owner bound to a machine_id, or None if unbound. <!--#80b6670164d240c6-->
  - `IdentityService.unbind_machine` (method) — Drops a machine's owner binding, e.g. on daemon disconnect. <!--#92a047a6ee556f74-->
  - `IdentityService.machines_for_owner` (method) — Returns the list of machine ids currently bound to a given owner_id. <!--#8c16d5f8ea6b335b-->
  - `IdentityService.snapshot_bindings` (method) — Returns a copy of all current (machine_id, owner_id) bindings under lock. <!--#aa1ad1922a731355-->

### `src/se3/server/persistence.py` (python) — SQLite-backed persistence layer for the multi-tenant server, defining the thread-safe Store repository (with schema migrations) and its Owner/DaemonKey records that encapsulate all SQL for owners, identity bindings, passwords, daemon keys, and break-glass admin tokens. <!--#90a534427104698e|70468e33a16ab4b9-->
- `Owner` (class) — Dataclass record for a persisted owner (stable owner_id, optional display name, admin flag, creation time) returned by the repository instead of a raw Row. <!--#bfe14bf8541354b0-->
- `DaemonKey` (class) — Dataclass record for a persisted daemon-key hash bound to an owner, with metadata and a revoked-at timestamp. <!--#b89b153a17848a21-->
  - `DaemonKey.revoked` (method) — Convenience property reporting whether the daemon key has been revoked (revoked_at is set). <!--#fb4bc884e0c8e4a4-->
- `Store` (class) — SQLite-backed repository encapsulating all SQL for the server's persisted facts, thread-safe via per-thread connections (or one shared lock-serialized connection for in-memory DBs). <!--#6a71c6a3e84c8889-->
  - `Store.__init__` (method) — Initializes the store for a file or in-memory DB, setting up locking/thread-local connection state, ensuring the parent dir exists, and running schema init. <!--#1d462c82a964e6e5-->
  - `Store._new_connection` (method) — Creates a new sqlite3 connection configured with Row factory, WAL journaling (file DBs), busy timeout, and per-connection foreign-key enforcement. <!--#1f7d9b1eb489947a-->
  - `Store._conn` (method) — Returns the appropriate connection for the caller — the shared one for in-memory DBs, otherwise a lazily-created thread-local connection. <!--#7be1eb71508e7627-->
  - `Store.close` (method) — Closes the shared and current-thread connections, clearing their stored references. <!--#9378a1bb19b255bb-->
  - `Store._init_schema` (method) — Reads the DB's user_version under lock and applies migrations if it is behind the current SCHEMA_VERSION. <!--#c387f248c591076c-->
  - `Store._apply_migrations` (method) — Applies the ordered (target_version, sql) migration steps from the current version up to SCHEMA_VERSION, bumping user_version after each. <!--#a3afc0d69e77afc3-->
  - `Store._now` (method) — Static helper returning the current wall-clock time for created/updated timestamps. <!--#194cd7b5e7248d18-->
  - `Store._new_id` (method) — Static helper generating a fresh opaque hex UUID for primary-key identifiers. <!--#205e13ff4affe569-->
  - `Store.create_owner` (method) — Inserts a new owner row and returns its stable internal owner_id. <!--#cfda8cc79821f6eb-->
  - `Store.get_owner` (method) — Fetches a single owner by owner_id, returning an Owner record or None. <!--#9805ae3e143bce5f-->
  - `Store.list_owners` (method) — Returns all owners as Owner records ordered by creation time. <!--#d9e1988a56e1e133-->
  - `Store.delete_owner` (method) — Deletes an owner (cascading to its bindings/credentials/keys) and reports whether a row was removed. <!--#711d2b75fecce53e-->
  - `Store.set_admin` (method) — Updates an owner's is_admin flag, returning whether the owner existed; backs the admin toggle-admin endpoint. <!--#e69d5b897d58e73f-->
  - `Store._count_real_admins` (method) — Lock-held helper counting admin owners excluding the break-glass subject, used to enforce the last-real-admin invariant in the same critical section as a write. <!--#1f3d3d282a0a0e14-->
  - `Store.delete_owner_guarded` (method) — Deletes an owner but atomically refuses if it is the last real admin, returning a 'not_found'/'last_admin'/'deleted' status. <!--#dc19e70db5cc369c-->
