  - `Store.set_admin_guarded` (method) — Sets an owner's admin flag but atomically refuses a last-real-admin demotion, returning a 'not_found'/'last_admin'/'updated' status. <!--#7dfd730f059f977d-->
  - `Store.create_local_user` (method) — Atomically creates an owner, its (provider, external_id) identity binding, and its local password-hash credential in one transaction, raising IdentityAlreadyBound on a duplicate identity. <!--#dd9973ad116e60a4-->
  - `Store.link_identity` (method) — Attaches a (provider, external_id) binding to an owner (idempotent for the same owner), raising IdentityAlreadyBound if it maps to a different owner. <!--#fff8ca88f8ed33c9-->
  - `Store.resolve_owner_by_identity` (method) — Looks up the owner_id bound to a given (provider, external_id) identity, or None. <!--#f213f5753de9638b-->
  - `Store.list_identities` (method) — Returns the list of (provider, external_id) identity bindings attached to an owner. <!--#a8842435882279b8-->
  - `Store.set_password` (method) — Upserts the already-hashed local password for an owner, never handling plaintext. <!--#76f08302cd060b3c-->
  - `Store.get_password_hash` (method) — Returns the stored local password hash for an owner, or None. <!--#4b6e3684831998cf-->
  - `Store.issue_daemon_key` (method) — Persists a daemon-key hash bound to an owner and returns its generated key_id. <!--#df3f970b9328badd-->
  - `Store.resolve_owner_by_daemon_key` (method) — Returns the owner_id a non-revoked daemon-key hash belongs to, or None. <!--#d7a862790a09dda3-->
  - `Store.revoke_daemon_key` (method) — Marks a daemon key revoked by key_id (idempotent), returning False only if the key_id genuinely does not exist. <!--#910630e46c88ad28-->
  - `Store.list_daemon_keys` (method) — Returns an owner's daemon keys as DaemonKey records, optionally excluding revoked ones, ordered by creation time. <!--#92d3d96ccd59c1e2-->
  - `Store.put_breakglass` (method) — Persists a break-glass admin token hash (with optional expiry) and returns its token_id. <!--#d0cf28881699ea5b-->
  - `Store.consume_breakglass` (method) — Atomically consumes a break-glass token by hash, returning True exactly once for a valid/unexpired/unconsumed token and marking it consumed. <!--#42e03299c1a89b1d-->
  - `Store.purge_breakglass` (method) — Deletes all break-glass tokens (e.g. before re-issuing) and returns the number removed. <!--#e0a39cb75dfc461e-->
- `IdentityAlreadyBound` (class) — Exception raised when linking an external identity that is already bound to another owner. <!--#e57ce650eec6fb27-->

### `src/se3/server/state.py` (python) — Defines the central server's non-persisted, asyncio-lock-guarded in-memory state (ServerState plus MachineRecord/FlowSnapshot dataclasses and signed progress-token codecs) that aggregates every dialed-in daemon's machines, flows, history bundles, and issue mirror, exposing owner-scoped ingestion and query methods for the REST/WebSocket handlers. <!--#ae545a1f191151f0|e3b690294f4e0735-->
- `_is_worktree_session_path` (function) — Structural-only helper that returns whether a project_root path's last two segments are `se3/worktrees`, used to recognize an orphan worktree session for end/cleanup without filesystem access. <!--#c1e37948c9c27c2a-->
- `_progress_payload` (function) — Builds the canonical sorted-key JSON byte payload binding (version, generation, offset, machine_id) that backs a history progress token. <!--#252830f5782afc92-->
- `encode_progress` (function) — Encodes an opaque base64url history progress token from (generation, offset, machine_id), optionally HMAC-signed with a process-local secret. <!--#262f2db866a0e3b7-->
- `decode_progress` (function) — Decodes and (when a secret is given) verifies a progress token, returning its scalars or `None` so the caller falls back to a full snapshot on any malformed/tampered input. <!--#4e36bdfbed16f8af-->
- `FlowSnapshot` (class) — Plain dataclass mirroring the daemon aggregator's per-flow view (id, root, status, progress, step history, waiting_for_lock, resumable) so the server never imports daemon types. <!--#70ef16bc3f25802c-->
  - `FlowSnapshot.from_payload` (method) — Classmethod constructing a FlowSnapshot from a daemon-supplied per-flow dict with defensive type coercion and defaults. <!--#ce402e5424df45a9-->
  - `FlowSnapshot.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a FlowSnapshot back to a plain dict for REST/WebSocket payloads. <!--#db43ea80cd9d0565-->
- `MachineRecord` (class) — Dataclass recording one connected/recently-seen machine — identity, liveness, owner trust-domain key, project roots, and its dict of flows. <!--#a32bb8e2197538f8-->
  - `MachineRecord.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a MachineRecord to a summary dict, optionally embedding its nested flow list. <!--#20ac0e5f5451afcf-->
- `_owned` (function) — Predicate deciding whether a MachineRecord is visible to an owner-scoped query, treating `owner is None` as the unscoped/admin view and unbound machines as fail-closed. <!--#bf5a165d13bea0cf-->
- `ServerState` (class) — The asyncio-safe in-memory aggregate store: machine records, history index/bundle relay caches with generation tracking, issue mirror, and all owner-scoped query and ingestion methods. <!--#866705f2f3842e31-->
  - `ServerState.__init__` (method) — Initializes the empty machine map, history relay caches, generation counter, process-local progress-token secret, issue mirror, and the guarding asyncio.Lock. <!--#616c0197209f4176-->
  - `ServerState.register_machine` (method) — Registers or refreshes a machine on HELLO, marking it online and scrubbing the prior owner's flows/history if the resolved owner changed (forgeable-machine_id takeover defense). <!--#fbe47161dca76309-->
  - `ServerState._discard_machine_state` (method) — Lock-held helper dropping a machine's cached history index, history bundles, and issues on an owner change to prevent cross-owner leakage. <!--#9315b3c1af09361f-->
  - `ServerState.mark_offline` (method) — Marks a machine offline and stamps last_seen when its daemon disconnects. <!--#43d1590c93817888-->
  - `ServerState.touch` (method) — Refreshes a machine's last_seen timestamp on a heartbeat/PONG. <!--#ef0a38b4a686f648-->
  - `ServerState.update_status` (method) — Applies a daemon STATUS_UPDATE snapshot, fully replacing the machine's flows, project roots, and per-root issue mirror. <!--#adecb141e2c5fabc-->
  - `ServerState.get_machine_owner` (method) — Returns the owner id bound to a machine (or `None`), used by owner-scoped WebSocket push paths to gate UI clients. <!--#58c587dbd12e0fb6-->
  - `ServerState.get_machines` (method) — Returns owner-filtered summary dicts for all known machines without nested flows. <!--#a201d1372466ec52-->
  - `ServerState.get_machine` (method) — Returns the full record for one machine, reporting cross-owner machines as `None` (no existence leak). <!--#4c36428df7cb705f-->
  - `ServerState.get_machines_full` (method) — Returns owner-filtered full machine dicts including nested flows, for the realtime frontend broadcast payload. <!--#5b36c9138f71224d-->
  - `ServerState.get_machine_flows` (method) — Returns a machine's flow list, or `None` for unknown/cross-owner machines. <!--#0c0e3b88a8a832c8-->
  - `ServerState.get_flow` (method) — Finds a flow by id across all (owner-scoped) machines, returning `(machine_id, flow_dict)` or `None`. <!--#ca2ca5af43bb1987-->
  - `ServerState.find_machine_for_flow` (method) — Returns just the machine id owning a given flow id, via get_flow. <!--#67d6bf5d911f2fc8-->
  - `ServerState.is_flow_resumable` (method) — Owner-scoped resumability gate returning `(machine_id, flow)` when the daemon's resumable flag (or legacy status fallback) holds and the flow is not terminally completed. <!--#f4314f239b674e05-->
  - `ServerState.is_flow_endable` (method) — Owner-scoped end gate returning `(machine_id, flow)` for any non-completed flow or a completed-but-orphaned worktree session still needing cleanup. <!--#c0edeab68b29eae2-->
  - `ServerState.update_history_index` (method) — Replaces the cached history-session index reported by a machine (full list, not a delta). <!--#4667089086e5275b-->
  - `ServerState.get_history_index` (method) — Returns the owner-scoped history index aggregated across machines, annotated with machine_id and sorted by updated_at descending. <!--#18d426e5d9a0826c-->
  - `ServerState.append_history` (method) — Caches history records for a flow in full-replace or append mode, rejecting first-sighting/cross-machine/unanchored appends and managing the requires-full flag and bundle generation. <!--#88c66f8f738b6040-->
  - `ServerState._next_generation` (method) — Lock-held monotonic counter handing out a fresh bundle generation id. <!--#610006147e1ecc92-->
  - `ServerState._ensure_generation` (method) — Returns a bundle's stable generation, back-filling and persisting a fresh one for old-format/zero-generation bundles so progress tokens stay durable. <!--#30e037fa41d8b591-->
  - `ServerState.get_history` (method) — Returns a defensive copy of a flow's cached history bundle (with ensured generation), or `None` on cache miss. <!--#fb2ab42ac81f6797-->
  - `ServerState.get_history_snapshot` (method) — Atomically (under one lock) validates ownership and the client's progress token to return either a delta tail or full bundle plus a fresh token, or `None` on cache miss/ownership mismatch. <!--#2f329c0525ce68f9-->
  - `ServerState.find_machine_for_history_flow` (method) — Resolves which owner-scoped machine owns a flow for an on-demand history pull, checking index, cached bundle, then live flows. <!--#bca10b5c804a637b-->
  - `ServerState._find_machine_for_history_flow_locked` (method) — Lock-held implementation of find_machine_for_history_flow with the owner-acceptance helper. <!--#39f3c7b9a40fd99b-->
  - `ServerState.get_history_flow_project_root` (method) — Resolves a flow's authoritative project_root (from history index then live flows) so an on-demand pull reads the correct root rather than the daemon's first-match guess. <!--#dafe09bc4f8c02f0-->
  - `ServerState.get_issues` (method) — Returns issues from the in-memory mirror filtered by owner, machine, project_root, open/closed status, source, and type. <!--#ac44934ad011ae08-->
  - `ServerState.get_issue_by_id` (method) — Finds a single issue by id within owner/machine/root scope, returning `(machine_id, project_root, issue)` or `None`. <!--#cba188f129587422-->
  - `ServerState.find_machine_for_project` (method) — Returns the owner-scoped machine owning a project_root, checking the issue mirror first then registered project_roots. <!--#7f5359f80a65f72b-->

### `src/se3/server/ws.py` (python) — The SE3 central server's WebSocket layer: it owns the machine_id→daemon connection pool and downlink routing, plus the registries and hubs that let REST handlers park futures awaiting on-demand history pulls, index refreshes, and issue-command replies, diff interjection lifecycle events across status snapshots, and fan out owner-scoped frames to /ws/ui browser clients. <!--#bb413fb5704f5b7c|a735c31279690ad9-->
- `ConnectionManager` (class) — The machine_id→WebSocket pool that tracks live daemon connections and routes downlink messages to a specific daemon. <!--#52883ae113acca4b-->
  - `ConnectionManager.__init__` (method) — Initializes the empty connection dict and the registry lock. <!--#c8a7812d8fac2f5d-->
  - `ConnectionManager.connect` (method) — Registers a websocket as the live connection for a machine, closing any superseded stale socket. <!--#c5c144b4702079b9-->
  - `ConnectionManager.disconnect` (method) — Removes a machine from the pool, only if the given socket still matches the registered one. <!--#58ba5caa6ac7783b-->
  - `ConnectionManager.is_connected` (method) — Reports whether a machine currently has a live connection. <!--#3704a66dd2030bd9-->
  - `ConnectionManager.machine_ids` (method) — Returns a snapshot list of currently-connected machine ids. <!--#8a072e798cee7d62-->
  - `ConnectionManager.send_to` (method) — Sends a message to one daemon by machine id, returning False if it isn't connected. <!--#d5b93cf92f1ef9e1-->
  - `ConnectionManager.get_connection` (method) — Returns the currently registered socket for a machine under the lock. <!--#4fdc29e4e0e3773e-->
  - `ConnectionManager.is_current_connection` (method) — Reports whether a given websocket is still the registered connection for a machine. <!--#372d03c4bcef83de-->
  - `ConnectionManager.send_to_connection` (method) — Sends a message through an exact previously-validated socket, checking identity under the lock but releasing it before the awaited send. <!--#3b22a25df9b0f000-->
- `_PullAbandoned` (class) — Internal exception signaling that a shared-pull leader failed before dispatching, so parked followers retry as a fresh leader. <!--#471918e71d2f3711-->
- `HistoryRequestRegistry` (class) — Tracks in-flight on-demand history pulls (keyed by flow/machine) so cache-miss REST handlers park futures and share one daemon pull. <!--#21a1b382b7c990ec-->
  - `HistoryRequestRegistry.__init__` (method) — Initializes the per-key waiter lists and the in-flight pull-key set. <!--#8c9c543f4c98a904-->
  - `HistoryRequestRegistry.register` (method) — Parks and returns a future for a flow id, optionally pinned to a machine. <!--#3e0b5d3d6442b58d-->
  - `HistoryRequestRegistry.begin_pull` (method) — Registers a waiter and reports whether this caller is the leader that must send the daemon pull versus a follower that just awaits. <!--#1dd90155a26972ea-->
  - `HistoryRequestRegistry.resolve` (method) — Resolves all waiters for a flow/machine with the data, returning whether any waiter existed (i.e. an on-demand pull was answered). <!--#b2eeadcb2c32dea4-->
  - `HistoryRequestRegistry.discard` (method) — Drops a single waiter (e.g. on timeout) without resolving it, clearing the in-flight marker when the last waiter is gone. <!--#2f769c1df1ec47e8-->
  - `HistoryRequestRegistry.fail_pull` (method) — Wakes every follower of a key with _PullAbandoned and unconditionally clears the in-flight marker when the leader fails before dispatch. <!--#30701d48accab21d-->
- `IndexRefreshRegistry` (class) — Tracks in-flight history-index refreshes (keyed by machine) so GET /api/history can await each daemon's forced re-push. <!--#80fcc54c38dfd466-->
  - `IndexRefreshRegistry.__init__` (method) — Initializes the per-machine waiter dict. <!--#fba411afdbd02f01-->
  - `IndexRefreshRegistry.register` (method) — Parks and returns a future that resolves when the given machine re-pushes its index. <!--#302b0786491eb472-->
  - `IndexRefreshRegistry.resolve` (method) — Resolves every waiter parked for a machine (no-op when none). <!--#0c36de37f9b5eef3-->
  - `IndexRefreshRegistry.discard` (method) — Drops a single index-refresh waiter without resolving it. <!--#36aa54710f132bf9-->
- `IssueCommandRegistry` (class) — Tracks in-flight issue write commands (keyed by request_id) awaiting a daemon's MSG_ISSUE_RESULT reply. <!--#6a315b72f8d1966e-->
  - `IssueCommandRegistry.__init__` (method) — Initializes the per-request_id waiter dict. <!--#fba411afdbd02f01-->
  - `IssueCommandRegistry.register` (method) — Parks and returns a future that resolves when the given request_id's result lands. <!--#5bc82f55890f883b-->
  - `IssueCommandRegistry.resolve` (method) — Resolves every waiter parked for a request_id with the daemon's result data. <!--#f08143665a94daa3-->
  - `IssueCommandRegistry.discard` (method) — Drops a single issue-command waiter without resolving it. <!--#ae6c1a2ef504cad2-->
- `broadcast_index_refresh` (function) — Sends a history-index-rebuild request to every connected daemon and returns a {machine_id: future} map for the caller to await. <!--#0ff3d4f3fc8dddf4-->
- `request_history` (function) — Sends a MSG_HISTORY_REQUEST to the daemon owning a flow, optionally pinned to a machine or a specific still-current socket. <!--#25fc977fc0d0efa5-->
- `InterjectionEventTracker` (class) — Per-machine differ that compares interjection chips across STATUS_UPDATE snapshots to emit pending/consumed interjection lifecycle events exactly once. <!--#0c203a5637217100-->
  - `InterjectionEventTracker.__init__` (method) — Initializes the per-machine→flow→{call_id:prompt} seen-state map. <!--#30dd654c458d4ee8-->
  - `InterjectionEventTracker.reset_machine` (method) — Forgets a machine's tracked interjection state, e.g. on disconnect. <!--#228a98d249085fcc-->
  - `InterjectionEventTracker.diff_machine` (method) — Diffs a machine's snapshot against prior state to produce new pending/consumed interjection events and atomically replaces the stored state. <!--#0639105045c12747-->
- `_make_interjection_event` (function) — Builds a single interjection_event UI payload dict (no I/O). <!--#784734196502da32-->
- `UiHub` (class) — Owner-scoped fan-out hub for /ws/ui browser clients that broadcasts machine/history/event frames filtered to each client's trust domain. <!--#d0def5976edd3e9b-->
  - `UiHub.__init__` (method) — Initializes the websocket→owner client map and the hub lock. <!--#97ad5aa825b8a131-->
  - `UiHub.register` (method) — Registers a UI websocket under the owner it authenticated as. <!--#0879cab8ba866508-->
  - `UiHub.unregister` (method) — Removes a UI websocket from the client map. <!--#ff838ffb7369e1a8-->
  - `UiHub.client_count` (method) — Returns the number of currently-connected frontend clients. <!--#b5ac032cea5428a5-->
  - `UiHub.distinct_owners` (method) — Returns the set of distinct owners currently connected (may include None for admin views). <!--#374af16ce9d49e25-->
  - `UiHub.broadcast` (method) — Sends a payload to every UI client unfiltered (retained for owner-agnostic frames). <!--#362bc72b9acb32d4-->
  - `UiHub.broadcast_scoped` (method) — Sends each connected owner the per-owner payload precomputed for it, skipping owners with no payload. <!--#62e1c2afeb67ebef-->
  - `UiHub.broadcast_owned` (method) — Sends a payload only to clients allowed to see a given owner's data (its owner plus the admin view), fail-closed for unowned data. <!--#fb273a5dd096ed5e-->
  - `UiHub._send_map` (method) — Internal helper that resolves each client's payload from an owner→payload map and fans out the resulting targets. <!--#d4298dda42992670-->
  - `UiHub._fan_out` (method) — Internal helper that JSON-encodes and sends each (client, payload) target, pruning sockets that fail. <!--#bae295926de76376-->
- `_push_state` (function) — Broadcasts the per-owner-filtered machine list to UI clients (best effort). <!--#c374fcd82209c536-->
- `_push_history_index` (function) — Broadcasts the per-owner-filtered history index to UI clients (best effort). <!--#bb9a52fa787fb446-->
- `_push_history_data` (function) — Broadcasts a history-data delta for a flow only to its originating machine's owner (plus the admin view). <!--#251cc141ccb29934-->
- `_push_spawn_failed` (function) — Broadcasts a spawn-failure event to the reporting machine's owner UI clients so the frontend can flip a published task into a visible error. <!--#744ca8a4efd1dc0e-->
- `handle_ui_connection` (function) — Serves one /ws/ui frontend connection: sends an owner-scoped snapshot, registers the client, and idles reading frames to detect disconnect (fail-closed when an owner is required but absent). <!--#0e50a0ce83312936-->
- `handle_daemon_connection` (function) — Serves one daemon connection end to end: accepts the socket, authenticates/validates HELLO, registers and binds the machine, answers WELCOME, then runs the serve loop until disconnect. <!--#c87b3352ffbf6886-->
- `_serve_loop` (function) — Runs the daemon receive loop alongside a heartbeat PING/timeout loop concurrently and stops when either task finishes. <!--#b3872cd8de1ec9d1-->
- `_handle_message` (function) — Applies one inbound daemon message (status update, pong, call notification, history index/data, etc.) to server state and fans the result out to UI clients and waiters. <!--#9085f14be8d8c95f-->

## `src/se3/server/auth/` — The pluggable A-layer authentication package for the multi-tenant server, composing local/OIDC/proxy-header providers into a fail-closed chain that resolves each request to an owner identity, with supporting session store, rate limiter, and the FastAPI `require_owner` dependency. <!--#6e244101855f68c0|003a260a1c4d9026-->

### `src/se3/server/auth/__init__.py` (python) — Package init for the multi-tenant server's pluggable A-layer authentication seam, re-exporting the provider ABC, session store, local/rate-limit/registry components that resolve the current request owner (distinct from the B-layer owner_id/authorization model). <!--#5b334a33c957b94b|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/server/auth/base.py` (python) — Defines the server's pluggable authentication core: an OwnerIdentity dataclass for a resolved request owner, an abstract AuthProvider interface that resolves a request to an owner (or None), and a fail-closed ProviderChain that composes enabled providers and returns the first successful resolution. <!--#b73ff7cf4addf079|cd9faafc057e0b60-->
- `OwnerIdentity` (class) — Frozen dataclass holding the resolved owner of a request: the stable internal owner_id used for authorization, plus display_name, the resolving provider, and an is_admin flag. <!--#e6f4d0b299c020c0-->
- `AuthProvider` (class) — Abstract base class for the unified 'resolve the current owner' interface, carrying a name discriminator and an enabled flag for registry/chain participation. <!--#32eaf7eb12361308-->
  - `AuthProvider.resolve_owner` (method) — Abstract method that resolves a request-like object to an OwnerIdentity or returns None (could-not-authenticate, never authorize-anonymous). <!--#519521172c8b189d-->
- `ProviderChain` (class) — Ordered composition of AuthProviders that drops disabled ones, returns the first non-None resolution, and is falsy when empty to enforce fail-closed. <!--#8c9764f1b32445c0-->
  - `ProviderChain.__init__` (method) — Builds the chain by filtering the given providers down to those whose enabled flag is truthy. <!--#111e6b192e809c5b-->
  - `ProviderChain.providers` (method) — Property returning a copy of the chain's enabled providers list. <!--#9fed3349e6dcd43c-->
  - `ProviderChain.resolve_owner` (method) — Iterates the enabled providers in order and returns the first non-None OwnerIdentity, else None. <!--#f6ba975245faf121-->
  - `ProviderChain.__bool__` (method) — Truthiness reflecting whether the chain has any enabled providers (used to enforce fail-closed serving). <!--#fc551b5bfab86264-->
  - `ProviderChain.__len__` (method) — Returns the number of enabled providers in the chain. <!--#a0fd978e084ff45a-->

### `src/se3/server/auth/local.py` (python) — Defines LocalAuthProvider, a session-based authentication provider that verifies owner credentials against the local store with rate limiting and timing-equalized protection against user enumeration. <!--#cd69c77c32718f02|039a69b633851c14-->
- `LocalAuthProvider` (class) — Session-based auth provider that authenticates owners against the local store using username, password, and rate limiting. <!--#b5a7149cd171a8d3-->
  - `LocalAuthProvider.__init__` (method) — Constructs the provider with a store, session store, and an optional (else default) login rate limiter, deferring the dummy timing hash. <!--#10228702a0a41f9c-->
  - `LocalAuthProvider.rate_limiter` (method) — Property exposing the provider's login rate limiter. <!--#97b7c30b9d9fae0f-->
  - `LocalAuthProvider._dummy_verify` (method) — Best-effort dummy password verification that equalizes login timing on the unknown-user path to mitigate user enumeration. <!--#516f8841211cbaef-->
  - `LocalAuthProvider.login` (method) — Authenticates a username/password — rate-gating, resolving the owner, verifying the hash, and minting a session on success or recording a failure otherwise. <!--#6c686daae20099f1-->

### `src/se3/server/auth/oidc.py` (python) — Defines the OIDC authentication provider — a disabled-by-default, fail-closed auth backend that composes stable `{issuer}|{sub}` external identities, resolves owners via session cookies when enabled, and stubs out the login/callback ceremony as unimplemented seams for v1. <!--#ed99ce6366d1dc58|6ed5aab56df6cf65-->
- `oidc_external_id` (function) — Composes the globally stable OIDC external identity as `"{issuer}|{sub}"`, the key used to bind an OIDC subject to an owner_id. <!--#4ce6c3586d1745a6-->
- `OidcProvider` (class) — A disabled-by-default OIDC auth provider that enables only when explicitly opted in and fully configured, otherwise failing closed and leaving the login ceremony unimplemented. <!--#32c9223628687a08-->
  - `OidcProvider.__init__` (method) — Validates the required OIDC config keys and sets `enabled` only when the operator opts in and all keys are present, logging a fail-closed warning on incomplete config. <!--#9f166fbf12760eee-->
  - `OidcProvider.resolve_owner` (method) — Returns None when disabled (never inspecting the request) and otherwise delegates to the standard session-cookie owner resolution. <!--#0b7f86218d50c7cd-->
  - `OidcProvider.begin_login` (method) — Seam for building the authorization-endpoint redirect URL with state/nonce; raises NotImplementedError in v1. <!--#d9ab4af1dc1c8197-->
  - `OidcProvider.complete_login` (method) — Seam for handling the OIDC callback (validate state/nonce, exchange code, link owner, mint session); raises NotImplementedError in v1. <!--#fa4c032f2483c13e-->

### `src/se3/server/auth/proxy_header.py` (python) — Defines the `ProxyHeaderProvider` AuthProvider that resolves a request owner from a proxy-injected identity header, gated behind a fail-closed, operator-affirmed trust flag and backed by an owner store with no auto-creation. <!--#5c4747182c6d7b05|c97844013e24d778-->
- `_read_header` (function) — Helper that safely extracts a named header value from a request's headers mapping, returning None when absent or on any access error. <!--#5f41b5f49adf1583-->
- `ProxyHeaderProvider` (class) — AuthProvider implementation that resolves an owner from a proxy-injected identity header, enabling only when the operator opts in and affirms trust. <!--#fbcc83a32474b846-->
  - `ProxyHeaderProvider.__init__` (method) — Reads config to set the header name and computes the fail-closed enabled flag, warning and staying disabled if enabled without an affirmed trust precondition. <!--#40b36c30c2f1b731-->
  - `ProxyHeaderProvider.header` (method) — Property exposing the configured (lowercased) identity header name. <!--#83cc214723e36afc-->
  - `ProxyHeaderProvider.resolve_owner` (method) — Resolves the request's header value to an OwnerIdentity via the store, returning None when disabled, header missing, or no owner is bound (no auto-creation). <!--#99444a685b125cf3-->

### `src/se3/server/auth/ratelimit.py` (python) — A thread-safe, sliding-window login rate limiter that records per-key failures, trips a configurable lockout once a threshold is reached, raises LoginRateLimited (with a Retry-After delay) while locked, and clears on success. <!--#73e31186e06a45dc|f04b6c8845ceaf3e-->
- `RateLimitConfig` (class) — Dataclass holding the tunable thresholds — max failures, lockout duration, and sliding window — for the rate limiter. <!--#a6a5eb383f7136a0-->
- `_Entry` (class) — Private per-key state record holding the list of recent failure timestamps and the time until which the key is locked. <!--#10591451905b3f36-->
- `LoginRateLimited` (class) — Exception raised when a login key is currently locked out, carrying a retry_after delay suitable for an HTTP 429 Retry-After header. <!--#1dd2b3f40fd525d2-->
  - `LoginRateLimited.__init__` (method) — Constructs the exception with a human-readable message and stores the retry_after seconds. <!--#ba5a287e1e640a20-->
- `LoginRateLimiter` (class) — Thread-safe per-key failure counter that records attempts, trips a lockout once over threshold, and clears on success. <!--#dc80045151f25360-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.__init__` (method) — Initializes the limiter with a config, an injectable clock, an empty entry map, and a lock for thread safety. <!--#61fee3463d2384b5-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter._prune` (method) — Drops failure timestamps older than the sliding window from an entry. <!--#cb829de6f8f922c0-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.is_locked` (method) — Returns whether the given key is currently within its lockout period. <!--#1a4772931c2f9874-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.retry_after` (method) — Returns the seconds remaining on a key's lockout, or 0 if not locked. <!--#b9a0362606992fb2-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.check` (method) — Raises LoginRateLimited if the key is currently locked, otherwise returns silently. <!--#3c7783c70f3655b5-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.record_failure` (method) — Registers a failed attempt and trips the lockout once the failure count reaches the configured threshold. <!--#b1e2b4c4f685ed5f-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.record_success` (method) — Clears a key's entire failure history on a successful login. <!--#e931a75cb8fbf1f7-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.reset` (method) — Drops all tracked keys, as a test helper or administrative clear. <!--#af382ab8e4ab2f2c-->

### `src/se3/server/auth/registry.py` (python) — Auth provider wiring module that normalizes `server.auth` config into an ordered, fail-closed `ProviderChain` of local/OIDC/proxy-header providers and exposes the FastAPI `require_owner` dependency that resolves the request's `OwnerIdentity` or returns HTTP 401. <!--#7b974058ccca3293|462425ce67bb7394-->
- `AuthNotConfigured` (class) — Exception raised when configuration yields no usable auth provider, signaling the server to refuse serving rather than fall back to an identity-unaware open control plane. <!--#18ef78762ac12051-->
- `_normalize_entry` (function) — Helper that normalizes a providers-list entry (bare type string or mapping with `type` plus options) into a `(type, options)` tuple. <!--#4006889c26eb61dc-->
- `build_provider_chain` (function) — Constructs the ordered `ProviderChain` from `server.auth` config, keeping only enabled providers and raising `AuthNotConfigured` (fail-closed) if the chain ends up empty. <!--#86279238c9bb36f0-->
- `_construct_provider` (function) — Factory that instantiates the appropriate provider (local, OIDC, or proxy-header) for a given type discriminator, returning None for unknown types. <!--#40a7f3b75d64da4f-->
- `make_require_owner` (function) — Builds the FastAPI `require_owner` dependency that resolves the current `OwnerIdentity` via the chain and raises HTTP 401 when none resolves, wiring up annotations so FastAPI injects the request. <!--#6b40cb227e95e093-->

### `src/se3/server/auth/session.py` (python) — Provides server-side session management for the UI — defining secure session cookies, a thread-safe in-memory store of hashed, expiring sessions with create/resolve/destroy/sweep operations, and a SessionAuthProvider base class that resolves the current owner from the session cookie. <!--#6b660897af44e2cd|cf36262b4e3d8f0f-->
- `CookieConfig` (class) — Dataclass holding the secure-cookie attributes (name, HttpOnly, SameSite, Secure, Path, Max-Age) for the UI session cookie. <!--#c7b2a206e0272a4d-->
- `Session` (class) — Dataclass representing one live server-side session, storing the session id's hash, owner, and creation/expiry timestamps. <!--#88ed149b1e808cda-->
  - `Session.is_expired` (method) — Returns whether the session's absolute expiry time has been reached at the given clock value. <!--#3e82312554a4481a-->
- `read_cookie` (function) — Best-effort, fail-closed helper that reads a named cookie from a request-like object, returning None on missing/malformed input. <!--#61826ca40012c71a-->
- `SessionStore` (class) — Thread-safe, in-memory table of hashed, expiring sessions keyed by session-id hash, providing create/resolve/destroy/sweep operations. <!--#cb3f9ac1c88e95b1-->
  - `SessionStore.__init__` (method) — Initializes the store with a TTL, cookie config, injectable clock, empty session dict, and a lock. <!--#0b8b8aab7201d1e2-->
  - `SessionStore.cookie_config` (method) — Property exposing the store's CookieConfig. <!--#7a7d3c67f0add4a8-->
  - `SessionStore.create` (method) — Mints a new session for an owner, returning the plaintext session id (cookie value) plus the stored hash-only Session. <!--#1d7f5f94d8a13d82-->
  - `SessionStore.resolve` (method) — Resolves a presented session-id plaintext to a live Session via hash lookup, constant-time compare, and expiry check, evicting expired ones. <!--#569b377aa1f11fde-->
  - `SessionStore.destroy` (method) — Idempotently invalidates a single session by its plaintext id (logout). <!--#d991cc867c95d63f-->
  - `SessionStore.destroy_owner` (method) — Invalidates all sessions belonging to an owner (e.g. on account disable) and returns the count removed. <!--#1ca7efc34f2a4fdc-->
  - `SessionStore.sweep_expired` (method) — Prunes all expired sessions from the table and returns how many were removed. <!--#59bf4dc9b4eb8817-->
  - `SessionStore.__len__` (method) — Returns the current number of stored sessions under the lock. <!--#0852865572e6c842-->
- `SessionAuthProvider` (class) — AuthProvider base class that resolves the current owner from the session cookie, shared by all providers whose login establishes a server-side session. <!--#492550690251601d-->
  - `SessionAuthProvider.__init__` (method) — Initializes the provider with the owner store and the SessionStore. <!--#3b6497b6377e6176-->
  - `SessionAuthProvider.sessions` (method) — Property exposing the provider's SessionStore. <!--#4282f203f8e12aba-->
  - `SessionAuthProvider.store` (method) — Property exposing the provider's owner store. <!--#2a6b2d7f5dc053b4-->
  - `SessionAuthProvider.resolve_owner` (method) — Reads the session cookie, resolves it to a session and owner, and returns an OwnerIdentity (failing closed and dropping the session if the owner is gone). <!--#a647ecb75f2dd934-->
  - `SessionAuthProvider.logout` (method) — Idempotently destroys the session referenced by the request's cookie. <!--#41bf329b337e43e8-->

## `src/se3/templates/` — The template package backing `se3 init`/`se3 migrate` project scaffolding and `se3 run` injection—bundling the high-altitude project charter (plus its retired base-spec ancestor), README/VERSIONS changelog/version-script scaffolds, and an agent prompts subdirectory for documentation-sync—exposing the canonical charter filename via CHARTER_TEMPLATE. <!--#8160cf3e132b8065|2231a8ebe8aa0d05-->

### `src/se3/templates/__init__.py` (python) — Package marker for SE3's project-initialization templates (charter, README, VERSIONS, version script, and legacy base-spec) that exposes the canonical charter template filename via the CHARTER_TEMPLATE constant. <!--#c244c02c91dc2554|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/templates/base_spec.md` (markdown) — Template for the auto-generated project base specification, defining project identity, structure, conventions, constraints, and a SemVer-based version-management policy with example scenarios, parameterized by project name and loaded into all `se3` runs. <!--#00d742d6e9b0c964|a3af382958bb3a94-->
- `{project_name} — Base Specification` (heading) — Top-level document title parameterized by the project name. <!--#d111501fa2c349b2-->
  - `Purpose` (heading) — States that this spec captures the project's base conventions and is generated by `se3 init` then auto-loaded in all runs. <!--#89c4e90a8f22c56c-->
  - `Requirements` (heading) — Container heading grouping all the requirement subsections of the spec. <!--#d8416f1863ce5290-->
    - `Requirement: Project Identity` (heading) — Records the project's name, description, and primary languages/frameworks via placeholders. <!--#8f8680697bd5dba4-->
    - `Requirement: Directory Structure` (heading) — Placeholder requirement describing the project's directory layout. <!--#fda3fd8b0889a9d0-->
    - `Requirement: Coding Conventions` (heading) — Placeholder requirement capturing the project's coding style conventions. <!--#c4a2c6cbe902bea6-->
    - `Requirement: Key Constraints` (heading) — Placeholder requirement listing the project's key constraints. <!--#224404c163fbb0c3-->
    - `Requirement: Workflow Conventions` (heading) — Placeholder requirement describing the project's workflow conventions. <!--#ccc10176db969929-->
    - `Requirement: Version Management` (heading) — Defines the SemVer 2.0.0 versioning policy, the single-source version file per project type, and the `version_analyze`→`commit` decision model with no silent patch-bump fallback. <!--#d362c5fe36acb63d-->
      - `Scenario: 版本自动更新` (heading) — Example scenario where completing a feature task auto-bumps the version (1.2.3→1.3.0) and syncs README/VERSIONS during commit. <!--#819f03a8342b11e0-->
      - `Scenario: 手动版本控制` (heading) — Example scenario where disabling `version.enabled` skips auto-bumping and requires manual version updates. <!--#e32e0fdc9402eb4c-->

### `src/se3/templates/charter.md` (markdown) — The interpolated project-charter template that se3 init/migrate populates and se3 run unconditionally injects into every step (and into the sandbox subprocess as its conventions channel), carrying only high-level cross-cutting content—project identity, top-level architecture, project-wide coding conventions, key constraints, workflow conventions, and SemVer-based version management—while deliberately delegating per-module/per-symbol location info to code-index. <!--#8588351519c858d3|a25ae194c9b872cd-->
- `{project_name} — Charter` (heading) — Top-level title heading naming the charter for the interpolated project. <!--#5fec8c4721218303-->
  - `Purpose` (heading) — Explains that the charter is unconditionally injected into every step and serves as the sandbox subprocess's conventions channel, holding only high-level cross-cutting content (not per-module location info, which belongs to code-index). <!--#013d4260326cc74e-->
  - `Requirements` (heading) — Container heading grouping the charter's requirement subsections. <!--#d8416f1863ce5290-->
    - `Requirement: Project Identity` (heading) — Records the project's name, description, and primary languages/frameworks via placeholders. <!--#8f8680697bd5dba4-->
    - `Requirement: Top-Level Architecture` (heading) — Captures the global architectural picture and subsystem-grouping rationale, explicitly excluding mechanical per-module location info (delegated to code-index). <!--#fa7a503fd6769af5-->
    - `Requirement: Coding Conventions` (heading) — Holds project-wide, cross-cutting coding conventions every step should follow. <!--#9d68141915bc34f0-->
    - `Requirement: Key Constraints` (heading) — Lists hard project-level constraints whose violation is treated as an error. <!--#d6e0ccfe4259b72e-->
    - `Requirement: Workflow Conventions` (heading) — Placeholder section for project workflow conventions. <!--#ccc10176db969929-->
    - `Requirement: Version Management` (heading) — Charter section mandating SemVer 2.0.0 versioning, defining the single-source version file per project type, the version-number format, and the version-decision model where version_analyze's suggested_version is the sole authority (optionally guided by se3/version-rules.md) that commit writes verbatim with no silent patch-bump fallback, plus README/VERSIONS doc-update requirements. <!--#7d849389d954389d-->

### `src/se3/templates/readme_md.md` (markdown) — A scaffolding template for a generated project's README, with placeholder tokens (project name, overview, version) and standard sections covering quick start, directory structure, and documentation links. <!--#55c8d680b6a802c7|a110ba4f79dab588-->
- `{project_name}` (heading) — Top-level title heading carrying the project name placeholder, a version badge, and the project description token. <!--#516e411a1b099380-->
  - `Overview` (heading) — Overview section holding the {project_overview} placeholder for a longer project description. <!--#00ae69c98f86a6da-->
  - `Quick Start` (heading) — Quick Start section with a bash code block stubbed for install and run commands. <!--#358b911d25baaa6b-->
  - `Project Structure` (heading) — Project Structure section showing the expected directory layout (se3/, src/, tests/, and config files) of a generated project. <!--#057b89a8a6c416e8-->
  - `Documentation` (heading) — Documentation section with a table linking key files like VERSIONS.md and the base spec to their purposes. <!--#5336c849bd171379-->
  - `Version` (heading) — Version section stating the project's current version (0.1.0). <!--#2caa1c9bf3aee798-->

### `src/se3/templates/version_script.py.tmpl` (text) — A scaffolding template for a per-project version-management CLI script exposing get/bump/set commands, with semver bump logic provided and project-specific read_version()/write_version() left as NotImplementedError stubs for users to fill in. <!--#997ccfab37134d45|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/templates/versions_md.md` (markdown) — A template for the project's VERSION HISTORY changelog file, seeded with an auto-maintenance note and an initial 0.1.0 release entry, populated by se3's version_analyze and commit steps. <!--#a107f82d29b594b9|8f7146410aeb657b-->
- `Version History` (heading) — The top-level heading and intro line stating the file tracks version history, auto-maintained by se3's version_analyze and commit steps. <!--#382dba47091f371f-->
  - `0.1.0 - {date}` (heading) — The initial changelog entry template for version 0.1.0, marking the project's first release. <!--#e10dcc90f8cf1864-->

## `src/se3/templates/prompts/` — Directory holding agent prompt templates (Markdown), currently the documentation-sync prompt that directs an agent to reconcile published docs against the CLI, specs, structure, and version under strict docs-only, no-version-bump scope guardrails. <!--#e04f71f39eef32eb|69c10d0919ed52ea-->

### `src/se3/templates/prompts/doc-sync.md` (markdown) — A prompt template instructing a documentation-sync agent to reconcile all published docs (README always, plus any docs tree and localized variants) item-by-item against the CLI, specs, structure, and version, while staying within strict scope guardrails — edit only docs, report (never create) gaps, and never bump the version. <!--#7a847c4bd60f1f36|8e0db45353f552da-->
  - `Scope` (heading) — Defines what counts as in-scope documentation — every doc the project actually publishes (README always, plus any docs tree if present) — rather than a fixed required path. <!--#f1b304b8bedd824d-->
    - `README reconciliation (baseline — preserved in full)` (heading) — Specifies the baseline README contract: aligning it item-by-item with the CLI/public interface, specs, project structure, and displayed version. <!--#b042efe5d3ee0a7b-->
    - `Reporting documentation gaps (report only — never create)` (heading) — Directs the agent to report undocumented user-facing surfaces as gaps for human triage rather than authoring new doc files to fill them. <!--#9c9e901db2527ddb-->
  - `Localized documentation alignment` (heading) — Requires language variants of a document to stay structurally parallel and faithfully translated, following the dotted BCP 47 naming convention (e.g. README.zh.md). <!--#9b42e96a14a53f00-->
  - `Constraints (scope discipline)` (heading) — Lists scope guardrails: edit only documentation, never bump the version or create new doc files, and preserve existing rationale prose unless factually wrong. <!--#c209a5d5196bb9cb-->

## `tests/` — The top-level pytest/Node test suite for the SE3 system, with subpackages for CLI commands (run/merge), core helpers, the engine and its step handlers, and the WebUI frontend/server, alongside a broad set of module-level tests covering agent config/registries/runners, daemon history and aggregation, DAG scheduling, discovery, charter/code-index, confirmation and fix-loop flows, and break-glass bootstrap, plus shared fixtures (conftest.py, _authsrv.py) and issue-#209 freeze diagnosis/repro harnesses. <!--#74112c9852abddda|dea618b9012a531c-->

### `tests/ISSUE_209_FREEZE_DIAGNOSIS.md` (markdown) — A G1 diagnosis report for issue #209 that, grounded in ordered real reproductions, localizes the WebUI console freeze on discovery→analyze and retry to a starved daemon `_push_loop` and records candidate fixes, regression hooks, and temporary instrumentation for later groups. <!--#ce31c8fcf5960605|937cf4d0e4488f7a-->
- `issue #209 — WebUI console freeze on discovery→analyze / retry — G1 diagnosis` (heading) — Title/intro section stating the diagnosis is grounded in real reproduction and localizing the bug to the daemon push side rather than the frontend or server cache. <!--#5570eb393f47dc39-->
  - `Symptom (recap)` (heading) — Describes the observed symptom: the polled status bar keeps advancing while the WS-pushed conversation freezes until the session is exited and re-entered. <!--#c7aa4c30e5d9233d-->
  - `How it was坐实ed (reproductions, in order)` (heading) — Walks through the ordered chain of real reproductions and instrumentation proving each layer except the daemon push is correct. <!--#61b108926b1ebca6-->
  - `Root cause` (heading) — States the root cause: the daemon's `_push_loop` is starved under large/busy roots by per-tick synchronous engine.json parsing and per-iteration heavy awaited reads. <!--#124f112be7c6ef89-->
    - `Why specifically discovery→analyze and retry` (heading) — Explains why these two pause→resume boundaries manifest the freeze — the loaded daemon falls behind during the pause so the one post-resume incremental push never lands. <!--#4d5ac9e1a5a2edb3-->
  - `Trigger boundaries (the two the task asks to distinguish)` (heading) — Distinguishes the two triggers (new analyze jsonl vs. retry append to same jsonl) and notes a latent truncate/rewrite bug in `read_flow` not actually exercised by #209. <!--#c5a827852a521f2d-->
  - `Implications for G2 (fix) — recorded, not implemented here` (heading) — Lists candidate fix directions for the G2 group (cheapen per-tick change detection, decouple per-flow pushes, or a frontend poll-triggered reload workaround). <!--#12ed624429be8ce5-->
  - `Reproduction / regression hooks for G3` (heading) — Points to the repro script and fixtures G3 can use as before/after regression guards for the fix. <!--#faaf39a73b7ae25d-->
  - `Temporary instrumentation added in G1 (remove / demote in G4)` (heading) — Inventories the gated `SE3_HISTORY_DIAG` Python and frontend diagnostic logging added in G1 that G4 should remove or demote. <!--#fd95ca978ebdd59f-->

### `tests/_authsrv.py` (python) — Test helper module providing fixtures to build a server app seeded with an admin owner and daemon key, log a TestClient in as that admin, and construct authenticated daemon HELLO messages. <!--#a83029560578def6|138ae9367e119030-->
- `authed_app` (function) — Builds a server app pre-seeded with an admin owner and an issued daemon key, exposing them via app.state for tests. <!--#9d67901a372cc811-->
- `login` (function) — Logs a TestClient in as the seeded admin via the login endpoint, persisting the session cookie in the client's jar. <!--#98934d9f117043f0-->
- `authed_hello` (function) — Constructs an authenticated daemon HELLO message carrying the app's issued daemon key as JSON. <!--#3e0b56b990c9a04f-->

### `tests/conftest.py` (python) — Shared pytest fixtures for the se3 test suite that wire userspace-installed browser libraries onto LD_LIBRARY_PATH and provide autouse fixtures to reset config warning-dedup sets and neutralise the real code-index freshness hook so unit tests stay isolated and never trigger live LLM rebuilds. <!--#d43da4a3061b4c2d|fe85cb521c3e6302-->
- `_wire_browser_test_libs` (function) — Prepends the gitignored `.browser-libs/lib` directory to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (when present) so a child Chromium process can find userspace-installed system libraries during the headless-browser test. <!--#2fe4dfbf7269486e-->
- `_reset_config_warning_dedup_sets` (function) — Autouse fixture that dynamically clears all `_warned_*_for` dedup sets in `se3.config` before and after each test so warning-related caplog assertions stay order-independent. <!--#56a91681465d8a59-->
- `_no_real_code_index_refresh` (function) — An autouse pytest fixture that monkeypatches `ensure_code_index_fresh` to a no-op so unit tests never trigger a real, flock-taking, LLM-spawning code-index rebuild against the live repo (which previously hung the suite). <!--#dcbaa1968a2bf2b9-->

### `tests/repro_issue_209_freeze.py` (python) — A standalone reproduction harness for issue #209 that spins up an isolated se3 server, daemon, project, and fake agent under configurable daemon-load profiles (clean/loaded/heavy) to verify whether an analyze append crosses the /ws/ui WebSocket wire instead of freezing. <!--#c5433d68e0db0d67|886835cc487d4d30-->
- `_free_port` (function) — Helper that grabs an unused TCP port by binding to port 0 and returning the OS-assigned number. <!--#171e93bcd41a6242-->
- `_poll` (function) — Generic retry helper that repeatedly calls a function until it returns truthy or attempts are exhausted, swallowing exceptions between tries. <!--#e08f25e336db03f8-->
- `_synth_heavy_root` (function) — Builds a synthetic 'heavy' se3 project root (large engine.json, busy active flow, hundreds of history dirs) to simulate the daemon load that starves the push loop. <!--#3f3002f1b5415543-->
- `run` (function) — Core driver that provisions the isolated instance (server, daemon, project, fake agent, WS client), drives the discovery→analyze transition, and asserts whether the analyze append crosses the /ws/ui wire. <!--#b8c826a6ee87b3e5-->
- `main` (function) — CLI entry point that parses --clean/--loaded/--heavy-root/--wait-after flags and invokes run() with the chosen daemon-load configuration. <!--#745c2467c7705ab4-->

### `tests/test_active_flow_signature_group_status.py` (python) — Test module verifying that the daemon history reader's active-flow signature token shifts whenever a group_status line is appended to a step's history jsonl (via mtime or byte-size fingerprint, including first-write file creation) while excluding terminal/completed flows from live-status signature pushes. <!--#4c95c37a4ca33dce|796bce7e264dcc62-->

- `test_group_status_shifts_signature_via_size_even_without_mtime_change` (function) — Asserts the signature still moves on a group_status append when mtime is pinned back, proving the byte-size fingerprint component alone shifts the token. <!--#bbf0217bbee97ef4-->

- `TestLoadClaudeCommandsBackwardCompat` (class) — Test class ensuring the legacy load_claude_commands API still returns {cmd, priority} dicts by delegating to the new loader. <!--#57712e7c97c43730-->

### `tests/test_breakglass_bootstrap.py` (python) — Test suite for the break-glass bootstrap escape hatch (se3.server.bootstrap and the `se3-server bootstrap-token` CLI), covering one-time/re-issuable/TTL token issuance, the security baseline that plaintext is never persisted to the store or logged, dependency isolation so the command works on a core-only install without the [server] extra, and the end-to-end seam where a CLI-minted token is consumed by a live server on the same sqlite db. <!--#10a96aecd8ef763a|2122393ba9c40629-->

- `test_issue_is_reissuable_with_distinct_tokens` (function) — Asserts repeated issuance yields distinct plaintexts/ids that remain independently consumable (re-issue does not revoke prior tokens). <!--#f3e8600a8526c4ec-->
- `test_issue_honours_ttl_expiry` (function) — Asserts a token with a past (negative) TTL is rejected by consume while a generously-TTL'd token is accepted. <!--#d7417d2f903eb507-->

- `test_plaintext_token_never_written_to_the_store_file` (function) — Asserts the plaintext token never appears in any sqlite artifact (db/WAL/SHM) on disk — only its SHA-256 hash. <!--#fd7f66b43c1af758-->
- `test_issuance_never_logs_the_plaintext` (function) — Asserts the plaintext reaches the console stream but never the logging output at DEBUG level. <!--#f3653838c1c5f487-->
- `test_cli_bootstrap_token_prints_token_and_exits_zero` (function) — Asserts the `bootstrap-token` CLI subcommand prints a token, exits 0, and that the printed token is consumable from the same store file. <!--#f555bdbb6f6776df-->
- `test_cli_bootstrap_token_is_reissuable` (function) — Asserts running the `bootstrap-token` CLI twice yields two distinct, independently consumable tokens. <!--#5d8638473d74b4da-->
- `_run_python` (function) — Helper that runs a Python snippet in a fresh subprocess with this worktree's `src` prepended to `PYTHONPATH`, capturing output. <!--#7c663f38919d0739-->
- `test_bootstrap_token_works_without_server_extra` (function) — Asserts `bootstrap-token` mints a token in a simulated core-only install where fastapi/uvicorn/argon2/bcrypt imports are blocked, confirming it's intercepted before the `[server]` extra import. <!--#21e1f146bd82e3ef-->

- `test_cli_token_is_consumable_by_a_server_on_the_same_db` (function) — End-to-end test that a CLI-minted token is accepted by a live server (via `POST /api/auth/breakglass`) opened on the same db, mints an admin session, and is rejected on replay. <!--#695855b6de03e738-->

### `tests/test_claude_interactive_runner.py` (python) — Unit-test suite for ClaudeInteractiveRunner that uses a FakePty stand-in for pexpect to verify the class contract, interactive-mode argument building, PTY driving primitives (prompt feeding, input-readiness, draining), process-group SIGTERM→SIGKILL termination, and the full run lifecycle including normal exit, wall/inactivity timeouts, and spawn-failure handling. <!--#9aa215770033cf4a|77664b0af72825c0-->
- `FakePty` (class) — Minimal fake stand-in for pexpect.spawn that yields preset chunks then either stays alive (TIMEOUT) or dies (EOF), recording sent input and close/terminate calls. <!--#a3141a517a82d97e-->
  - `FakePty.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake PTY with queued chunks, death behavior, exit/signal status, pid, and empty sent/closed tracking state. <!--#7496fca132b41784-->
  - `FakePty.isalive` (method) — Reports whether the fake process is still alive. <!--#0e3dde0c98502e77-->
  - `FakePty.read_nonblocking` (method) — Pops the next queued chunk, or raises pexpect.EOF (die) or pexpect.TIMEOUT (stay alive) when exhausted. <!--#68ce5ea45ab2fa7d-->
  - `FakePty.send` (method) — Records sent text and returns its length, mimicking pexpect's send. <!--#a2820cc4c5b2be54-->
  - `FakePty.sendline` (method) — Records sent text plus a newline and returns its length, mimicking pexpect's sendline. <!--#2392030e03661acd-->
  - `FakePty.close` (method) — Marks the fake PTY as closed and dead. <!--#3a14be3524904ca9-->
  - `FakePty.terminate` (method) — Marks the fake process dead and returns True. <!--#9bcccaae01d66223-->
- `_make_runner` (function) — Helper that constructs a ClaudeInteractiveRunner with a default 'claude' command. <!--#219383a5bcb60303-->
- `no_kill` (function) — Pytest fixture that monkeypatches os.getpgid/os.killpg to record process-group signals instead of sending them to real PIDs. <!--#7d4c2761f1c14d6a-->
- `TestContract` (class) — Tests the runner's class contract: AgentRunner subclassing, pexpect-free construction, and legacy commands-list view. <!--#a2990995793db8cb-->
  - `TestContract.test_is_agent_runner_subclass` (method) — Asserts ClaudeInteractiveRunner is a subclass of AgentRunner. <!--#37522825bb6796df-->
  - `TestContract.test_instantiable_without_pexpect_import` (method) — Asserts the runner constructs without needing pexpect/config and exposes the expected command and setting_sources. <!--#6caf941a61772322-->
  - `TestContract.test_legacy_commands_list_view` (method) — Asserts a runner built from a legacy commands list exposes both the first command and the full list. <!--#31e38e6a71e4d153-->
- `TestBuildCallArgs` (class) — Tests build_call_args / _build_full_cmd translation of intent into interactive-mode flags (read-only tools, no print flags, stashed prompt, context dirs, prefix, session id). <!--#e715b89d18796dcb-->
  - `TestBuildCallArgs.test_read_only_adds_disallowed_tools` (method) — Asserts read-only mode appends --disallowedTools with Write/Edit/NotebookEdit/AskUserQuestion. <!--#58cdccc6a587b61c-->
  - `TestBuildCallArgs.test_writable_omits_disallowed_tools` (method) — Asserts writable mode omits the --disallowedTools flag. <!--#ddc85dc0b24b1ec4-->

### `tests/test_cli_confirm.py` (python) — Test module for CLI-subprocess confirmation-prompt handling, covering conservative prompt detection (including Chinese), the file-based interaction_calls call-writer/response-reader protocol, the make_cli_confirm_handler round trip, and on_confirm wiring through the run monitor (stdin answering, no-hang on early exit, and no-op on unrecognized output). <!--#3b063bdfcf6be598|c10d91fd5933f66e-->

  - `TestDetectConfirmationPrompt.test_known_prompts_detected` (method) — Asserts each known confirmation line (English and Chinese) is detected, returning the stripped prompt and an options list. <!--#74e1d1a2d4e66e07-->
  - `TestDetectConfirmationPrompt.test_non_prompts_are_noop` (method) — Asserts blank lines, JSON output, and ordinary prose are not falsely detected as confirmation prompts. <!--#97f9c21ef908c5ec-->
  - `TestDetectConfirmationPrompt.test_options_parsed_from_enumerated_line` (method) — Asserts numbered choices in an enumerated prompt line are parsed into the returned options list. <!--#ec624a6d740380e6-->
- `TestInteractionCalls` (class) — Test class covering the interaction_calls file-based protocol: writing cli_confirm call files, context placement of flow_id/step_id, and reading responses. <!--#412c1c6cf870d146-->
  - `TestInteractionCalls.test_write_creates_cli_confirm_call_file` (method) — Asserts write_interaction_call creates a JSON call file under se3/calls with the expected kind, prompt, options, and flow_id fields. <!--#dc3d905fc49e8fac-->
  - `TestInteractionCalls.test_handler_writes_flow_id_in_context` (method) — Asserts make_cli_confirm_handler stores flow_id/step_id/awaiting inside the call's context (not as top-level keys) so the daemon's per-flow filter can scope calls. <!--#e278efff2f800345-->
  - `TestInteractionCalls.test_response_unanswered_returns_none` (method) — Asserts read_interaction_response returns None when no response sibling file has been written yet. <!--#7f95310d05a7713e-->
  - `TestInteractionCalls.test_response_plain_sibling` (method) — Asserts read_interaction_response returns the text of a plain .response sibling file. <!--#faf0faf45cfbaeee-->
  - `TestInteractionCalls.test_response_json_envelope` (method) — Asserts read_interaction_response extracts the response value from a .response.json envelope file. <!--#56ff34f441a3d892-->

  - `TestOnConfirmWiring.test_confirm_prompt_answered_via_stdin` (method) — Asserts a child's confirm prompt triggers a call file that, once answered by a responder thread, feeds the response back to the child via stdin. <!--#1d4918b0a84d10aa-->
  - `TestOnConfirmWiring.test_child_exits_before_response_does_not_hang` (method) — Asserts that when a child prints a confirm prompt then exits without a response ever arriving, the monitor finishes promptly instead of blocking. <!--#0d43fa546dac2d14-->
