### `tests/test_code_index.py` (python) — Pytest suite for the code-index subsystem (group G1) that, using git-repo fixtures and a RecordingSummarizer test-double, verifies gitignore/se3-aware file enumeration with binary and exclude guards, deterministic AST/structural symbol extraction with per-symbol fingerprints across Python/Markdown/YAML/JSON, and the incremental build_index lifecycle covering full first builds, LLM-skipping unchanged rebuilds, change-scoped re-summarisation, preserved human corrections, prune/add of deleted/new files, force rebuilds, bottom-up synthesis, crash-resumable checkpoints, and list-fingerprint reuse. <!--#df40441c3883b9b9|e4e3f933ba56d660-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand in a given root directory, failing the test on nonzero exit. <!--#a44a1342750ce397-->
- `_init_git_project` (function) — Helper that initializes a git repo in a directory with a test user identity. <!--#6aabffa4b0cbf3dc-->
- `_commit_all` (function) — Helper that stages and commits all files in a test repo with an optional message. <!--#244569aab0134277-->
- `RecordingSummarizer` (class) — A test-double summariser that records each batch of target ids and returns deterministic `S:<name>` summaries without ever calling the LLM, with helpers (`all`, `last`, `call_count`, `reset`) to assert what work a build performed. <!--#b2000ca60427e31b-->
  - `RecordingSummarizer.__init__` (method) — Initializes the recorder's list of per-call batches. <!--#2eb12aaa30d04499-->
  - `RecordingSummarizer.__call__` (method) — Records the batch's target ids and returns a deterministic summary per target. <!--#69dbd4374dad21fb-->
  - `RecordingSummarizer.all` (method) — Property returning the union of all target ids across every recorded batch. <!--#c9050c58a5dd1c51-->
  - `RecordingSummarizer.last` (method) — Property returning the ids from the most recent batch (empty if none). <!--#c2e6d1003cf9f412-->
  - `RecordingSummarizer.call_count` (method) — Property returning how many batches the summariser has been invoked with. <!--#da34ef5d0cc65b1d-->
  - `RecordingSummarizer.reset` (method) — Clears the recorded batches (but not the on-disk md) so a test can isolate the work of a subsequent incremental build. <!--#1a52be09125e131c-->
- `project` (function) — Pytest fixture building a git-initialized sample project with source, README, gitignored files, and an se3-exclusion .gitignore. <!--#7bbbf049229b799a-->
- `TestFileEnum` (class) — Tests for file enumeration: gitignore/se3 exclusion, untracked pickup, explicit excludes, exclude matching, and binary detection. <!--#3f9745dd6015d644-->
  - `TestFileEnum.test_enumerate_respects_gitignore_and_excludes_se3` (method) — Asserts enumeration includes tracked source but excludes gitignored files and the se3/ runtime directory. <!--#b19634138c370050-->
  - `TestFileEnum.test_new_untracked_file_picked_up` (method) — Asserts a brand-new uncommitted, non-ignored file is enumerated via git --others. <!--#347b72b0ab6ec767-->
  - `TestFileEnum.test_explicit_exclude_list` (method) — Asserts an explicitly passed exclude path is omitted while other files remain. <!--#fd34608a273ac211-->
  - `TestFileEnum.test_matches_exclude_dir_and_basename` (method) — Asserts matches_exclude handles glob basenames and directory-name patterns with/without trailing slash. <!--#e84d1255bd7877c3-->
  - `TestFileEnum.test_is_binary` (method) — Asserts is_binary flags null-byte blobs as binary while text and empty files are not. <!--#f7ff6773910afa02-->
- `TestExtraction` (class) — Tests for deterministic structural/AST symbol extraction across Python, Markdown, YAML, and JSON. <!--#f4abb939fe6ee0af-->
  - `TestExtraction.test_python_drills_to_function_method` (method) — Asserts Python extraction yields top-level functions, classes, and methods but not nested inner functions. <!--#f70bde78ac49b386-->
  - `TestExtraction.test_markdown_headings` (method) — Asserts Markdown extraction yields headings with correct depth levels. <!--#9654d6c0a895e72e-->
  - `TestExtraction.test_yaml_top_keys` (method) — Asserts YAML extraction yields only top-level keys. <!--#12c5004656279e68-->
  - `TestExtraction.test_json_top_keys` (method) — Asserts JSON extraction yields only top-level keys. <!--#37c939c5af9329a7-->
  - `TestExtraction.test_structured_keys_carry_value_content` (method) — Asserts JSON/YAML top-level key symbols carry their nested value content for the summariser, not just the key. <!--#2a5f6f66a19a9830-->
  - `TestExtraction.test_make_target_summarizes_json_key_from_value` (method) — Asserts _make_target feeds a JSON key's value content to the summariser even when its line range is zero. <!--#f0c6a123355c1dfb-->
  - `TestExtraction.test_symbol_fingerprint_changes_with_content` (method) — Asserts a symbol's sha256 fingerprint changes when its body content changes. <!--#e14d1e4323c9ee2c-->
- `TestBuild` (class) — Test suite verifying the incremental build_index lifecycle: first-build summarises everything, unchanged rebuilds skip the LLM, only changed symbols are re-summarised, human md corrections survive, deleted files are pruned and new ones added, --force re-summarises all, summaries are synthesised bottom-up from children, and a mid-build crash leaves a resumable partial md. <!--#42efd8fed55117a9-->
  - `TestBuild.test_first_build_summarizes_all` (method) — Asserts a first build writes the authoritative md and summarises every file node and symbol, with a complete symbol map. <!--#bd85cd75a3c97668-->
  - `TestBuild.test_unchanged_rebuild_skips_llm` (method) — Asserts an unchanged rebuild produces no targets and does not re-invoke the summariser. <!--#5982a0bf9875c125-->
  - `TestBuild.test_changed_symbol_only_resummarized` (method) — Asserts a body-only edit re-summarises ONLY the edited symbol, since files/dirs gate on their symbol-roster list-fp (unchanged), leaving untouched siblings reused. <!--#5f050dd08968911b-->
  - `TestBuild.test_human_correction_preserved` (method) — Asserts a human-edited summary in the authoritative md survives a subsequent rebuild. <!--#45312508a4c3c2a0-->
  - `TestBuild.test_deleted_file_pruned_new_added` (method) — Asserts a deleted file is pruned from the index and a newly added module (with its symbols) is summarised. <!--#86523e7dd2a7c086-->
  - `TestBuild.test_force_resummarizes_everything` (method) — Asserts `force=True` ignores fingerprints and re-summarises every node. <!--#ee4d534a8d89d440-->
  - `TestBuild.test_summary_is_bottom_up` (method) — Asserts each node is summarised from its children's summaries — a file from its symbols' summaries (not raw source) and a directory from its child files' summaries — by capturing the content fed to the summariser. <!--#fcd5f8d30f57aec2-->
  - `TestBuild.test_checkpoint_flushes_partial_md_for_resume` (method) — Asserts a crash mid-build flushes a partial md with real fingerprints so already-summarised nodes are reused (not re-summarised) when the build resumes with a working summariser. <!--#b9b4a0ccd40fecc3-->
  - `TestBuild.test_checkpoint_flush_preserves_unchanged_file_fingerprints` (method) — Asserts a checkpoint flush preserves both fingerprints of an unchanged file not yet reached before the crash, so an interrupted build never blanks it and forces a needless re-summarisation. <!--#82a17fc3e15d60c9-->
  - `TestBuild.test_binary_file_is_file_level_only` (method) — Asserts a binary file is indexed file-level only (kind `binary`, no symbols, a 'binary' summary) and is never sent to the LLM. <!--#038d71b5868cd8f6-->
  - `TestBuild.test_load_or_build_alias` (method) — Asserts load_or_build builds and returns a populated index like build_index. <!--#1cb8b3fcc38e6c60-->
- `TestListFp` (class) — Test suite for the list-fingerprint reuse semantics: body edits touch only the symbol, roster changes (add/rename/re-kind) touch the file but not ancestor dirs, reorders touch nothing, dir membership changes touch only that dir, symbol-less files fall back to content-fp, --force cascades everything, and legacy single-fp md migrates for free. <!--#a230e3645d4aa301-->
  - `TestListFp.test_body_only_change_resummarises_symbol_only` (method) — Acceptance (a): a body-only edit re-summarises only the edited symbol while its file and all ancestor dirs reuse their cached summaries. <!--#d38332c56a3e13a5-->
  - `TestListFp.test_new_symbol_resummarises_symbol_and_file_not_dir` (method) — Acceptance (b): adding a symbol re-summarises that symbol and its file (roster grew) but not the parent dir (dir roster unchanged). <!--#364e99ebacf433b6-->
  - `TestListFp.test_renamed_symbol_resummarises_file_not_dir` (method) — Acceptance (b): renaming a symbol changes the file roster so the file and renamed symbol are re-summarised, but the parent dir is left untouched. <!--#b9c0b8820332d908-->
  - `TestListFp.test_kind_change_same_name_resummarises_file` (method) — Acceptance (b) kind component: changing a symbol's kind while keeping its name flips the roster's (kind,name) entry so the file is re-summarised, locking in the kind half of the list-fp while ancestors reuse. <!--#863a259a97a483e9-->
  - `TestListFp.test_reorder_symbols_no_resummary` (method) — Asserts the file list-fp is order-insensitive: reordering unchanged symbols leaves the sorted (kind,name) roster identical, so the file is not re-summarised. <!--#7a442e60e5fef6fb-->
  - `TestListFp.test_dir_membership_change_resummarises_dir_not_ancestors` (method) — Acceptance (c): adding a file to a subdir re-summarises only that subdir while ancestor dirs (unchanged direct rosters) reuse. <!--#8892d8b43ac45c46-->
  - `TestListFp.test_dir_child_removal_resummarises_dir_not_ancestors` (method) — Acceptance (c): removing a direct child re-summarises only that dir, with ancestors reusing their cached summaries. <!--#2e756c050505c2e9-->
  - `TestListFp.test_symbolless_file_content_edit_resummarises_file` (method) — Asserts a symbol-less file (whose constant empty list-fp would freeze it) falls back to the content-fp so a body rewrite re-summarises the file node without cascading to its parent dir. <!--#ab7ae377cb1104bf-->
  - `TestListFp.test_force_cascades_whole_content` (method) — Acceptance (d): --force ignores list-fps and re-summarises every node (symbols, files, all dirs) — the whole-content cascade. <!--#833cdfa38c84ef6f-->
  - `TestListFp.test_lazy_migration_reuses_old_md_zero_llm` (method) — Acceptance (e): a legacy single-fp md is reused for free (zero LLM) on the first rebuild, carrying old summaries forward while mechanically backfilling list-fps into the rewritten md. <!--#beefd5d4321255bc-->
- `TestDegrade` (class) — Tests for degrade-mode handling: the three-condition gate, large structureless chunking, and the oversized-structured size-cap guard. <!--#bf4f5bfdbd02d7a7-->
  - `TestDegrade._cfg` (method) — Helper returning a CodeIndexConfig with small degrade/chunk thresholds for testing. <!--#c8e5f33b8fbd6232-->
  - `TestDegrade.test_gate_requires_all_three` (method) — Asserts is_degrade_eligible only triggers when the file is large AND structureless under the configured thresholds. <!--#63f3e02c31203b39-->
  - `TestDegrade.test_large_structureless_file_chunks_with_marker` (method) — Asserts a large structureless file is chunked into degraded symbols and rendered with the degraded marker. <!--#2b74dcef5ab6f24d-->
  - `TestDegrade.test_oversized_structured_file_drops_to_file_level` (method) — Asserts an oversized but structured module is dropped to a single file-level entry rather than enumerated or chunked. <!--#1d8fcdfeec24c916-->
- `TestSummaryFlatten` (class) — Tests that multi-line summaries collapse to a single line and survive the md round-trip. <!--#b2bde80acac06f04-->
  - `TestSummaryFlatten.test_flatten_collapses_newlines` (method) — Asserts _flatten_summary collapses newlines and surrounding whitespace into single spaces. <!--#ab6d2246457f511d-->
  - `TestSummaryFlatten.test_newline_summary_survives_md_round_trip` (method) — Asserts a multi-line LLM summary becomes one md line and is fully recoverable when parsed back. <!--#5a7a705238559cd1-->
- `TestRender` (class) — Test suite for the rendering/round-trip surface: the adaptive root view lists files and dir summaries (not symbols), dir summaries survive the md round-trip and reuse independently per directory, path drill-in shows symbols or member files, and the md is self-sufficient (no json sidecar) with embedded node fingerprints. <!--#2d6b8e5df29ed89b-->
  - `TestRender.test_adaptive_lists_files_not_symbols` (method) — Asserts the adaptive root view lists file paths but omits function-level symbol bullets. <!--#3a9f305d5f06945b-->
  - `TestRender.test_adaptive_shows_directory_summaries` (method) — Asserts directory nodes carry a one-line summary in both the index and the rendered adaptive view. <!--#8866e3dbd8fb098f-->
  - `TestRender.test_dir_summary_survives_md_round_trip` (method) — Asserts directory summaries are recovered when loading the index from md for display. <!--#ee68cec64066e110-->
  - `TestRender.test_unchanged_sibling_dir_summary_reused` (method) — Asserts directory reuse is independent: adding a root-level file re-summarises only the root dir while an untouched sibling dir reuses its cached summary. <!--#74db031d2bd31040-->
  - `TestRender.test_dir_summary_not_refreshed_on_member_content_change` (method) — Asserts a pure content edit inside a file does not re-summarise ancestor directories in normal mode (dir list-fp unchanged), while --force restores the content-fp cascade. <!--#9cdc786c3b7e6d2a-->
  - `TestRender.test_render_path_file_shows_symbols` (method) — Asserts rendering a file path drills in to show its symbols. <!--#f9f2651ef457e2b5-->
  - `TestRender.test_render_path_directory_lists_files` (method) — Asserts rendering a directory path lists its files but not symbols. <!--#103aa80577e34bba-->
  - `TestRender.test_render_path_unknown` (method) — Asserts rendering an unknown path returns a no-entry message. <!--#4189b5fab8c22573-->
  - `TestRender.test_load_for_display_reads_md_round_trip` (method) — Asserts load_for_display reconstructs files, symbols, and summaries from the md. <!--#a6777337f0918b65-->
  - `TestRender.test_md_is_self_sufficient_for_incremental_rebuild` (method) — Asserts the committed md alone (no json sidecar) drives incremental rebuilds, doing zero LLM work on an unchanged tree and still rendering on its own. <!--#0b846c6a84748720-->
  - `TestRender.test_md_embeds_node_fingerprints` (method) — Asserts every rendered file/dir line carries a 16-hex content-fp (plus optional list-fp) comment that is stripped from the parsed summary, with list-fps present on file nodes but never on symbol bullets. <!--#61a973974e58fdfc-->
- `TestDoubleFpRoundTrip` (class) — Test suite for the trailing fingerprint-comment format: parsing/emitting the content-fp plus optional list-fp for file/dir lines, staying byte-compatible with the legacy single-fp form, and round-tripping both fps through render→parse without leaking list-fps onto symbol or unsummarised nodes. <!--#9a78389cb4fd1b33-->
  - `TestDoubleFpRoundTrip.test_split_fp_legacy_single_fp` (method) — Asserts _split_fp parses a legacy single-fp comment into the bare line, its content-fp, and a None list-fp. <!--#0a284f89a1837f08-->
  - `TestDoubleFpRoundTrip.test_split_fp_double_fp` (method) — Asserts _split_fp parses a double-fp comment into the bare line plus both the content-fp and list-fp. <!--#ac47db626361c765-->
  - `TestDoubleFpRoundTrip.test_split_fp_no_comment` (method) — Asserts _split_fp on a line with no fp comment returns the line unchanged and both fingerprints as None. <!--#6fa04f77e6cf5f79-->
  - `TestDoubleFpRoundTrip.test_fp_comment_round_trip` (method) — Asserts _fp_comment emits the legacy shape for a content-fp alone and the double shape when a list-fp is given, with an empty list-fp falling back to the legacy single-fp shape. <!--#243d087196d48359-->
  - `TestDoubleFpRoundTrip.test_render_parse_round_trip` (method) — Asserts render_full→_parse_md restores both fingerprints for every summarised file/dir node while symbol nodes carry only a content-fp and never a list-fp. <!--#e08ee95555fe3faa-->
  - `TestDoubleFpRoundTrip.test_unsummarised_node_embeds_no_fp` (method) — Asserts a node with no summary embeds neither fingerprint, keeping a partial md a safe resume point (treated as stale next build). <!--#dc911f1aee89a427-->
- `TestCodeIndexCLI` (class) — Test suite exercising the `code-index` CLI subcommands (index, bare invocation, show, rebuild, inspect, help) against a fake-summariser-built project with `get_project_root` monkeypatched. <!--#f8a3493da0293a96-->
  - `TestCodeIndexCLI.built_project` (method) — Fixture that builds the code-index md with a fake summariser and points `get_project_root` at the project so CLI commands resolve to it. <!--#7321282503a01e9e-->
  - `TestCodeIndexCLI.test_index_no_arg_renders_literal_root_level` (method) — Asserts `index` with no path shows the literal root level (collapsed top dirs + root files) and not one level deeper. <!--#edc365a4d57e8902-->
  - `TestCodeIndexCLI.test_bare_invocation_renders_adaptive_map` (method) — Asserts bare `code-index` renders the adaptive root map (expanding code roots) instead of Typer's 'Missing command' error. <!--#6ddcb755282417b4-->
  - `TestCodeIndexCLI.test_bare_invocation_unbuilt_errors_without_missing_command` (method) — Asserts bare invocation on an unbuilt project exits 1 with a rebuild hint, not a Typer 'Missing command' error. <!--#ac7cc4197dcec319-->
  - `TestCodeIndexCLI.test_index_with_path_drills_into_file` (method) — Asserts `code-index index <file>` drills into the file and shows its symbols. <!--#4f69a162e138f230-->
  - `TestCodeIndexCLI.test_index_with_directory_lists_files` (method) — Asserts `code-index index <dir>` lists the directory's files but not symbols. <!--#4f5c778c008153a0-->
  - `TestCodeIndexCLI.test_show_pulls_function_level` (method) — Asserts `code-index show <file>` surfaces function/method-level symbols. <!--#7230267ab2ce3244-->
  - `TestCodeIndexCLI.test_index_unbuilt_errors` (method) — Asserts `code-index index` on an unbuilt project exits 1 with a rebuild hint. <!--#7aea579c8081593f-->
  - `TestCodeIndexCLI.test_rebuild_force_full_rebuild` (method) — Asserts `rebuild --force` does a full re-summarisation via a monkeypatched fake summariser and rewrites the authoritative md. <!--#60ee9a486fe0ea70-->
  - `TestCodeIndexCLI.test_inspect_reports_stats` (method) — Asserts `code-index inspect` reports file and symbol counts. <!--#33f9ddf5a766d99e-->
  - `TestCodeIndexCLI.test_help_mentions_md_authoritative_product` (method) — Asserts the CLI help names se3/code-index.md as the authoritative product. <!--#f0dfd18b15028925-->
- `TestConcurrentRebuildSafety` (class) — Test suite asserting the incremental rebuild serializes across processes via an advisory lock, writes atomically through unique temp files, and degrades gracefully when fcntl is unavailable. <!--#d88bd69f4ce7928d-->
  - `TestConcurrentRebuildSafety.test_atomic_write_uses_unique_temp_no_fixed_leftover` (method) — Asserts the atomic md write leaves no fixed-name or stray `*.tmp` scratch files behind. <!--#7261ab11746a1c58-->
  - `TestConcurrentRebuildSafety.test_build_lock_serializes_concurrent_builds` (method) — Asserts two concurrent threaded builds both complete and produce a valid, parseable map under the advisory lock. <!--#92c9adacab9014cb-->
  - `TestConcurrentRebuildSafety.test_build_proceeds_unlocked_when_fcntl_unavailable` (method) — Asserts the build still runs best-effort when fcntl locking is unavailable. <!--#c7ce193e0880ea44-->
  - `TestConcurrentRebuildSafety.test_lock_path_lives_under_gitignored_cache` (method) — Asserts the build lock file is named `code-index.lock` and lives under the gitignored `se3/cache` directory. <!--#b1f579f6ea274ac3-->

### `tests/test_codex_runner.py` (python) — Unit tests for the CodexRunner module, covering CodexEventConverter's mapping of codex `exec --json` events to Claude NDJSON, build_call_args, infra-error detection, subprocess run lifecycle via mocks, and runner registration. <!--#8e564ce4cd9a5997|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/test_commit_step.py` (python) — Pytest suite for the COMMIT step's commit_handler, verifying version-file recovery, verbatim writing of the LLM's suggested_version, and FAILED-with-guidance behavior when suggested_version is missing or blank. <!--#0d6c6a092120d96f|646b03b8544ffc07-->
- `temp_dir` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding a fresh temporary directory Path that serves as the project root for each test. <!--#aa41b08e2a7ac2e1-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Test helper that builds a minimal FlowInstance whose change_path parent equals the given temp_dir, with a configurable task_type. <!--#df77e370fec9d9e9-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Test helper that builds a minimal COMMIT Step pre-populated with task_description, suggested_version, and bump_type inputs. <!--#40c0069baf1d4540-->
- `TestCommitHandlerVersionlessFile` (class) — Test class asserting commit_handler recovers (initializes/bumps) rather than crashing when a version file exists without a parseable version. <!--#ff7cbba6471c0e98-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerVersionlessFile.test_initializes_version_when_read_raises_value_error` (method) — Test that a versionless pyproject.toml causing read_version to raise ValueError leads commit_handler to initialize and bump rather than fail. <!--#735314a035d6c0d4-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerVersionlessFile.test_version_is_readable_after_recovery` (method) — Test that after recovering from a versionless file, the pyproject.toml holds a readable (non-None) version. <!--#b52e3d8fbb10b471-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerVersionlessFile.test_init_py_without_version_does_not_crash` (method) — Test that a Python project with a versionless __init__.py completes the commit step without raising ValueError. <!--#5d1da2675ad6f147-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerVersionlessFile.test_normal_version_file_still_works` (method) — Test that a pyproject.toml with a valid version still completes and records a bumped version output. <!--#7032d1533739de87-->
- `TestCommitHandlerSuggestedVersionDriven` (class) — Test class asserting commit_handler writes the LLM-supplied suggested_version verbatim, bypassing bump_type recomputation. <!--#49eb1fc69e8c9b46-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerSuggestedVersionDriven.test_suggested_version_written_verbatim_to_pyproject` (method) — Test that suggested_version='9.4.2' is written exactly to pyproject.toml even when bump_type would compute a different value. <!--#29c9c05dfa1ed3b8-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerSuggestedVersionDriven.test_suggested_version_supports_major_jump` (method) — Test that suggested_version can skip versions (e.g., 1.2.3 → 3.0.0) when the LLM dictates it. <!--#9fe2c664b45459f7-->
- `TestCommitHandlerMissingSuggestedVersion` (class) — Test class asserting commit_handler returns FAILED with a guided error message when suggested_version is absent or blank. <!--#fc0af8cc0c77c918-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerMissingSuggestedVersion.test_missing_suggested_version_raises_with_current_version` (method) — Test that an absent suggested_version yields FAILED with an error referencing suggested_version, current version state, and human-intervention guidance. <!--#87954cbc7b1d410c-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerMissingSuggestedVersion.test_empty_string_suggested_version_raises` (method) — Test that a whitespace-only suggested_version is treated as missing and produces a FAILED result mentioning suggested_version. <!--#69f6d568a6bc882c-->

### `tests/test_config.py` (python) — Unit tests for WorkflowConfig parsing and loading, covering from_dict default handling, type coercion, and fail-fast validation of workflow fields (max_fix_iterations, self_check_passes_required/convergence, baseline_fix_max_attempts) plus load() reading se3.yaml/se3.local.yaml. <!--#814bf59fc0ac2f7d|7a4df57571f97a04-->

  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_empty_dict_returns_defaults` (method) — Asserts an empty dict yields all default config values. <!--#f2ed21774898e0f8-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_none_returns_defaults` (method) — Asserts an empty/None-equivalent dict yields all default config values. <!--#c2ad610b1e7169e0-->

  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_custom_max_fix_iterations` (method) — Asserts a custom max_fix_iterations is honored while other fields stay default. <!--#5a25d68d37314388-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_custom_self_check_passes_required` (method) — Asserts a custom self_check_passes_required is honored while other fields stay default. <!--#ed7135967921a9a6-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_custom_convergence_enabled_true` (method) — Asserts a boolean True for self_check_convergence_enabled is preserved. <!--#2396e7b6e064a5da-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_convergence_enabled_string_true` (method) — Asserts the string 'true' coerces to boolean True. <!--#08ae92b294db922e-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_convergence_enabled_string_false` (method) — Asserts the string 'false' coerces to boolean False. <!--#2aadf16e22dca0bc-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_passes_required_string_coercion` (method) — Asserts a string-shaped integer for self_check_passes_required coerces to int. <!--#e555ed9a9ae873c0-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_passes_required_zero_raises` (method) — Asserts self_check_passes_required of 0 raises ConfigError ('must be >= 1'). <!--#4b93eb514cd94333-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_passes_required_negative_raises` (method) — Asserts a negative self_check_passes_required raises ConfigError ('must be >= 1'). <!--#6b51b557010e4e4b-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_passes_required_zero_string_raises` (method) — Asserts the string '0' for self_check_passes_required raises ConfigError ('must be >= 1'). <!--#4f89af59c2ac1d76-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_passes_required_float_falls_back_to_default` (method) — Asserts float self_check_passes_required values warn and fall back to the default. <!--#15fdd6b2fe525fa5-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_passes_required_bool_falls_back_to_default` (method) — Asserts boolean self_check_passes_required values warn and fall back to the default instead of coercing to int. <!--#e79094dbfe5e558e-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_all_fields_custom` (method) — Asserts all three workflow fields are read correctly when custom values are supplied together. <!--#f00ec665dbe9a20e-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_invalid_max_fix_iterations_falls_back_to_default` (method) — Asserts a non-integer max_fix_iterations falls back to the default. <!--#3dad8d50f53cb303-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_default_value_is_100` (method) — Asserts DEFAULT_MAX_FIX_ITERATIONS and the field default are both 100. <!--#bcb1193b0c9929db-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_max_fix_iterations_zero_sentinel` (method) — Asserts max_fix_iterations of 0 is preserved as the 'unlimited' sentinel. <!--#e98ef8da6de8af0b-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_max_fix_iterations_null_sentinel` (method) — Asserts None for max_fix_iterations is normalized to the sentinel 0. <!--#0ffc86aaa7abe97a-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_max_fix_iterations_string_zero_preserved` (method) — Asserts the string '0' for max_fix_iterations coerces to the sentinel int 0. <!--#05b0bd12de2822c5-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_max_fix_iterations_negative_raises` (method) — Asserts a negative max_fix_iterations raises ConfigError ('must be >= 0') rather than acting as the sentinel. <!--#6c0a33384d93e6fc-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_max_fix_iterations_negative_string_raises` (method) — Asserts a string-shaped negative max_fix_iterations raises ConfigError ('must be >= 0'). <!--#562caffaf9d8cc9e-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_max_fix_iterations_bool_warns_and_falls_back` (method) — Asserts boolean max_fix_iterations values warn and fall back to the default. <!--#51945d355efd2e1e-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_max_fix_iterations_float_warns_and_falls_back` (method) — Asserts float max_fix_iterations values warn and fall back to the default. <!--#533c023e2283a721-->
  - `TestWorkflowConfigFromDict.test_workflow_section_is_non_dict` (method) — Asserts a non-dict 'workflow' section causes all defaults to be used. <!--#860612c696ec353a-->

### `tests/test_config_merge_registry.py` (python) — Pytest suite verifying se3's config-merge semantics: agent registries merge per-entry (project wins on name conflicts, non-conflicting entries coexist) while llm_caller defaults and per-step overrides are wholesale-replaced by the project, using helpers to write fake global ~/.se3 and project-level config files. <!--#a9ed7953cb5cc9ec|5aa37f6b6a737e54-->

- `_write_global` (function) — Helper that writes a global config.yaml into a fake `~/.se3` directory under tmp_path. <!--#4db041cab949151c-->
- `_write_project` (function) — Helper that writes a project-level se3.yaml into tmp_path. <!--#0ac102d101a847f9-->
- `TestRegistryEntryLevelMerge` (class) — Test class asserting the agents registry merges per-entry (project wins on name conflict; non-conflicting global/project entries coexist). <!--#041b2dba843f5a23-->

  - `TestRegistryEntryLevelMerge.test_registry_merge_preserves_non_conflicting_global_entries` (method) — Asserts a global agent not redeclared by the project is preserved in the merged registry. <!--#f04b6068173aed08-->
- `TestDefaultsWholesaleReplace` (class) — Test class asserting llm_caller.defaults is wholesale-replaced by the project rather than appended to global. <!--#20780e60044193be-->

  - `TestDefaultsWholesaleReplace.test_global_defaults_used_when_project_omits` (method) — Asserts global defaults are used (resolved against the merged registry, in written order) when the project omits defaults. <!--#7aee7ab29d2b9dcd-->
- `TestStepOverrideWholesaleReplace` (class) — Test class asserting per-step llm_caller.steps overrides are wholesale-replaced and resolved independently per step key. <!--#7320680c96ef7c5e-->
  - `TestStepOverrideWholesaleReplace.test_step_override_wholesale_replace` (method) — Asserts a project step override completely replaces the global override for that same step. <!--#3d8e2709f399af16-->
  - `TestStepOverrideWholesaleReplace.test_step_override_per_step_independent` (method) — Asserts step overrides declared in different files (global 'plan', project 'implement') are each honored independently. <!--#48d39d139844ad48-->

### `tests/test_console_real_daemon_e2e.py` (python) — End-to-end test module that spins up a fully isolated se3-server + daemon stack (temp dirs, ephemeral port, seeded admin/auth) in a worktree and verifies, across HTTP, the production app.js renderer, and a headless Chromium browser, that the real daemon injects file-name-derived step_type, the paradigm renders correctly, and a CLI discovery pause can be answered from the web console. <!--#8c082bca4d036982|0b6b9e6dee2a71d2-->
- `_server_deps_available` (function) — Capability probe returning True only when the optional server extra (fastapi/uvicorn/websockets) is importable, used to skip the whole module otherwise. <!--#7101c53861230d2b-->
- `_node_available` (function) — Capability probe returning whether the `node` binary is on PATH (for the app.js node-render sub-case). <!--#bae13743c6fd1b27-->
- `_free_port` (function) — Allocates and returns an ephemeral free 127.0.0.1 TCP port so the harness never collides with the user's real daemon. <!--#b7c34f218ce22bed-->
- `_http_get` (function) — Tiny helper that issues an HTTP GET and returns the parsed JSON body. <!--#5bdc3b21b2123641-->
- `_http_post` (function) — Tiny helper that POSTs a JSON payload and returns the parsed JSON response. <!--#1be85a426842a5f8-->
- `_poll` (function) — Generic retry helper that repeatedly calls a function until it returns a truthy value or the attempt budget is exhausted. <!--#ace3ca934d426f44-->
- `_IsolatedConsole` (class) — Harness class that owns the fully isolated instance — temp dirs, free port, seeded admin/auth, and the worktree-launched se3-server and se3 daemon subprocesses — with lifecycle and isolation-guard methods. <!--#23b359e0a64bd3d4-->
  - `_IsolatedConsole.__init__` (method) — Constructs the isolated instance state: temp tree, daemon/project dirs, free port, base URL, log paths, sqlite store path, and auth placeholders. <!--#5901e9cfd3a58651-->
  - `_IsolatedConsole._env` (method) — Builds the subprocess environment that pins PYTHONPATH to the worktree src and redirects SE3_DAEMON_DIR/HOME into the temp tree to guarantee isolation. <!--#32fbdc659182b915-->
  - `_IsolatedConsole.assert_isolation_guards` (method) — Asserts every invariant that keeps the harness away from the user's real daemon (temp daemon dir, non-forbidden port, no stable-instance host/marker, loopback-only). <!--#7cf9e7c7ce2535e5-->
  - `_IsolatedConsole._seed_admin_and_key` (method) — Seeds one admin owner with a password and an issued daemon key into the server sqlite store before the server subprocess opens it. <!--#f024c5782dbb3712-->
  - `_IsolatedConsole._install_cookie_opener` (method) — Installs a urllib opener with a cookie jar so every HTTP call automatically carries the owner session cookie. <!--#6e0847d18b06bdb7-->
  - `_IsolatedConsole._login` (method) — Logs the REST/browser client in as the seeded admin and captures the resulting `se3_session` cookie value. <!--#835418c232c683eb-->
  - `_IsolatedConsole.start` (method) — Brings the whole isolated stack up in order: se3 init, seed admin/key, launch and health-check the server, log in, then launch the daemon (with external flow discovery disabled) and wait for it to connect. <!--#13c5ea3503b89612-->
  - `_IsolatedConsole._machine_online` (method) — Polls `/api/machines` and returns True once this harness's machine_id appears as online. <!--#b6a4f68c5d6728da-->
  - `_IsolatedConsole.stop` (method) — Tears down both subprocesses (terminate then kill) and closes the log file handles. <!--#7965f2d2bbf6aaf4-->
  - `_IsolatedConsole.logs` (method) — Returns the tail of the server and daemon log files for failure diagnostics. <!--#74fe8a28fd12ba6b-->
  - `_IsolatedConsole.flow_history` (method) — Fetches `/api/history/{flow_id}` and returns its list of records. <!--#e73ce55f7d7c6542-->
- `console` (function) — Pytest fixture that starts an `_IsolatedConsole`, yields it to the test, and guarantees clean teardown (subprocesses stopped, temp tree removed). <!--#fb9d06e084afa325-->
- `_write_real_history_flow` (function) — Writes a real-shaped multi-step history flow (discovery, step_completed event, group-suffixed implement, underscore version_analyze) whose messages deliberately omit `step_type`, leaving the daemon to derive it from file names. <!--#14feb0a657d8338b-->
- `test_harness_is_isolated_and_connected` (function) — Task 1 test asserting the instance is isolated (temp dir + dedicated port, no real-daemon bleed-through) and the worktree daemon/server are connected. <!--#32c1e5204237077c-->
- `test_real_daemon_injects_paradigm_step_type` (function) — Task 2 HTTP-layer test proving the real daemon injects the authoritative file-name-derived `step_type` onto each record while the inner message keeps its real (no-`step_type`) shape. <!--#9e6ec6e4ea397a6c-->
- `test_render_paradigm_via_appjs_on_real_records` (function) — Task 2 rendering test that feeds the real records through the production app.js renderer via a node helper and asserts paradigm step headers and a structured discovery card. <!--#6b843971d495bbf1-->
- `test_render_paradigm_in_headless_browser` (function) — Critical Task 2 browser acceptance test that loads the console in real headless Chromium, renders the real history records through production renderConversation, and asserts the DOM paradigm (failing loudly rather than skipping when Playwright/Chromium is unavailable). <!--#6beba69ff323d3c3-->
- `_write_fake_agent` (function) — Writes a deterministic fake Claude CLI agent that logs each invocation and returns a confirmation response for DISCOVERY prompts (pausing at the gate) and a no-op otherwise. <!--#3a39aa21c6042ed4-->
- `test_cli_discovery_pause_answered_from_web` (function) — Task 3 test that runs `se3 run --discover` under a PTY until it pauses, confirms the web console sees the pending discovery_confirm chip, answers it via `/respond`, and verifies the same live process advances and the stale chip clears. <!--#191296f035c9f63a-->

### `tests/test_critical_acceptance_gate.py` (python) — Unit and end-to-end tests for the critical acceptance test gate, covering parsing of pytest -v SKIPPED lines, verbose-flag enforcement, critical-skip/missing detection, critical_tests config loading, the test-step handler forcing REVISION_NEEDED on critical failures, and the summarize step gating completion claims on the verification result. <!--#e0157cc591f2031d|d60d4ee8fa200025-->

  - `TestParseSkippedTestIds.test_empty_when_no_skips` (method) — Asserts no skipped IDs are returned when all tests passed. <!--#67ca87cc159365b3-->

  - `TestParseSkippedTestIds.test_dedups_preserving_order` (method) — Asserts duplicate SKIPPED lines collapse to a single ID. <!--#42515d6319711576-->

  - `TestEnsureVerbosePytest.test_noop_when_no_critical` (method) — Asserts the command is unchanged when there are no critical tests. <!--#280b4ace6f4f6cd1-->
  - `TestEnsureVerbosePytest.test_appends_v_when_missing` (method) — Asserts a bare pytest command gets `-v` appended. <!--#775af5440d679738-->
  - `TestEnsureVerbosePytest.test_report_flags_are_not_sufficient` (method) — Asserts `-rs`/`-ra`/`-rA` report flags still get `-v` appended since they aren't per-test parseable. <!--#5baa85606bcfe4ee-->
  - `TestEnsureVerbosePytest.test_verbose_flag_present_is_unchanged` (method) — Asserts commands already carrying a verbose flag are left untouched. <!--#f5a00e545833c2a8-->
  - `TestEnsureVerbosePytest.test_non_pytest_command_unchanged` (method) — Asserts non-pytest commands (e.g. `npm test`) are left untouched. <!--#8641a9bcc88361d6-->
- `TestDetectCriticalFailures` (class) — Tests that `_detect_critical_failures` classifies critical tests as skipped vs missing without false positives. <!--#904082e324908cc4-->
  - `TestDetectCriticalFailures.test_skip_hit_records_critical_skipped` (method) — Asserts a critical pattern matching a skipped test is reported as critical_skipped. <!--#b5592d9ac813e863-->
  - `TestDetectCriticalFailures.test_missing_hit_records_critical_missing` (method) — Asserts a critical pattern absent from parseable runs is reported as critical_missing. <!--#f2afd412ab22b900-->
  - `TestDetectCriticalFailures.test_normal_skip_does_not_match_critical` (method) — Asserts a passing critical test plus an unrelated skip flags nothing. <!--#a3ac4422167874cf-->
  - `TestDetectCriticalFailures.test_no_patterns_returns_empty` (method) — Asserts no critical patterns yields empty results. <!--#a53c4c547f333b87-->
  - `TestDetectCriticalFailures.test_not_parseable_no_false_positive_missing` (method) — Asserts unparseable (no ran/skipped) output never falsely flags missing. <!--#e89a59664855cba1-->
  - `TestDetectCriticalFailures.test_skip_takes_precedence_over_run` (method) — Asserts a pattern matching both a skipped and a run test is reported as skipped. <!--#9c8b8b53bff6f4dd-->
- `TestCriticalTestsConfigLoading` (class) — Tests that `TestConfig.load` parses the `critical_tests` config key with sensible defaults and coercion. <!--#f55bba3f32745203-->
  - `TestCriticalTestsConfigLoading.test_default_is_empty_list` (method) — Asserts `critical_tests` defaults to empty when no se3.yaml exists. <!--#cce60e8ac101df6f-->
  - `TestCriticalTestsConfigLoading.test_loads_string_list` (method) — Asserts a YAML list of critical test patterns loads verbatim. <!--#6e124c427de7c8fd-->

### `tests/test_daemon.py` (python) — Pytest suite for the SE3 daemon package — exercising DaemonSupervisor process registration/discovery/reaping/liveness, the `_cmdline_is_se3_run` and `_scan_external` logic that distinguishes genuine `se3 run` launches from inline `python -c` stubs, `_resolve_se3_command` argv resolution, and DaemonSpawner argv construction/event-parsing/termination, using helpers and fixtures that spawn real subprocesses and write fake flow-state files. <!--#999bd8ae9d353134|b5b7fcd5aa4ae18d-->
- `_spawn_sleeper` (function) — Helper that starts a long-lived child sleep process for liveness/reaping tests. <!--#9f707aff1ef992dd-->
- `_make_engine_json` (function) — Helper that writes a minimal engine.json flow-state file under a fake project root. <!--#09ee4549be528c4f-->
- `_make_resumable_snapshot` (function) — Helper that writes a per-flow resumable snapshot under se3/state/resumable/. <!--#729fe115e994b596-->
- `_FakeClient` (class) — Minimal stand-in for DaemonClient exposing connected/last_error attributes. <!--#46848e89149937c9-->
  - `_FakeClient.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake client with given connected flag and last_error. <!--#4deadea26b6f64b5-->
- `TestSupervisor` (class) — Test class for DaemonSupervisor registration, discovery, reaping, liveness, and concurrency. <!--#ef5c28dcbde01cdf-->
  - `TestSupervisor.test_register_and_get` (method) — Verifies register returns a record retrievable by pid with correct fields and count. <!--#a67e9126cba05c15-->
  - `TestSupervisor.test_register_idempotent` (method) — Verifies re-registering the same pid updates fields without increasing count. <!--#e227d8b554d1347f-->
  - `TestSupervisor.test_discover_and_reap_dead_process` (method) — Verifies a dead process is discovered then reaped, clearing it from the supervisor. <!--#2da4f921db7e0e79-->
  - `TestSupervisor.test_exit_callback_fires_on_reap` (method) — Verifies an on_exit callback fires with the pid when a process is reaped. <!--#ff89adde164ac1f7-->
  - `TestSupervisor.test_is_alive` (method) — Verifies is_alive reports true for the current process and false for an invalid pid. <!--#324adc33dfb0d39a-->
  - `TestSupervisor.test_concurrent_registration` (method) — Verifies concurrent registrations from multiple threads are all recorded without loss. <!--#6df556ae1fe213cf-->
- `_wait_until_psutil_observes` (function) — Test helper that blocks until psutil reports the given pid with a populated cmdline, ensuring `_scan_external` regression assertions scan an actually-observable process rather than passing vacuously. <!--#80edf2d300619c7e-->
- `_write_fake_se3` (function) — Test helper that writes an executable `se3`-named shebang script running a given body, reproducing the real shebang-rewritten console-script cmdline shape (se3 at argv[1]) for psutil to observe. <!--#1b2e881221742fc4-->
- `TestCmdlineIsSe3Run` (class) — Unit-test class asserting that `_cmdline_is_se3_run` matches only genuine `se3 run` launch shapes (console-script, shebang, module forms, with -c/--change) and rejects inline `python -c` stubs and non-immediate `run` subcommands. <!--#dede7480aa5e649e-->
  - `TestCmdlineIsSe3Run.test_inline_code_form_is_not_se3_run` (method) — Asserts `python -c <code> se3 run` is rejected because se3/run are the inline script's argv, not an se3 subcommand (the ghost-session false positive). <!--#8d860a58d06824f2-->
  - `TestCmdlineIsSe3Run.test_direct_console_script_argv0` (method) — Asserts the direct console-script forms `se3 run --worktree` and `/venv/bin/se3 run` (se3 at argv[0]) match. <!--#5a0569a3c34856c9-->
  - `TestCmdlineIsSe3Run.test_shebang_rewritten_console_script_argv1` (method) — Asserts the shebang-rewritten shape `python3 /venv/bin/se3 run` (se3 at argv[1], psutil's real observation) matches. <!--#a7a0b142921f7106-->
  - `TestCmdlineIsSe3Run.test_module_form` (method) — Asserts the module form `python -m se3 run` matches. <!--#c55cededece09adf-->
  - `TestCmdlineIsSe3Run.test_console_script_with_change_option` (method) — Asserts console-script `se3 run -c my-change ...` still matches, ensuring the CLI's own -c/--change option is not mistaken for an interpreter inline-code -c. <!--#278b56d3e4949801-->
  - `TestCmdlineIsSe3Run.test_module_form_with_change_option` (method) — Asserts the module form `python -m se3 run -c my-change` matches, treating the trailing -c as the CLI option rather than interpreter inline code. <!--#59822652ba0bf299-->
  - `TestCmdlineIsSe3Run.test_inline_code_carrying_module_tokens_is_not_se3_run` (method) — Asserts `python -c <code> -m se3 run` is rejected because the interpreter-mode -c disqualifies the stray module-form tokens in the script's argv. <!--#f517a836550e1cb3-->
  - `TestCmdlineIsSe3Run.test_se3_run_as_script_arguments_only` (method) — Asserts `python script.py se3 run` is rejected since se3/run appear only as script arguments with no -m se3 and no se3 program token. <!--#da91be689e785699-->
  - `TestCmdlineIsSe3Run.test_other_se3_subcommand_with_trailing_run_is_not_se3_run` (method) — Asserts `se3 migrate run` (across console-script, shebang, and module shapes) is rejected because `run` must be the immediate subcommand, not a nested one. <!--#ddeb2b005af70f90-->
  - `TestCmdlineIsSe3Run.test_empty_cmdline` (method) — Asserts an empty cmdline list returns False. <!--#e4b9f0686cf32343-->
  - `TestCmdlineIsSe3Run.test_module_form_without_run` (method) — Asserts `python -m se3` without a trailing `run` subcommand returns False. <!--#ca974ef32391e0a0-->
- `TestScanExternalDiscovery` (class) — Integration-test class spawning real subprocesses to verify `_scan_external`/`discover_flows` registers genuine console-script `se3 run` processes while rejecting inline `python -c` stubs. <!--#55cc1c7f585ee802-->
  - `TestScanExternalDiscovery.test_inline_code_se3_run_not_registered` (method) — Spawns a `python -c ... se3 run` inline-stub process, waits for psutil to observe it, and asserts `discover_flows(scan_external=True)` neither lists nor registers its pid. <!--#2fadfd71df29a1f9-->

### `tests/test_daemon_aggregator.py` (python) — Unit/integration test suite for the daemon status aggregator, covering per-flow filtering of pending calls, stale-call pruning with retry-decision exemptions, completed-flow progress reporting, project-root enumeration with historical caching and TTL invalidation, issue collection from open/closed dirs, and worktree-run observability via MachineStatus snapshots. <!--#80c585e06b9d8af1|c0ba2d5a6cbef826-->
- `_write` (function) — Helper that JSON-serializes a payload to a file path, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#65d03e595cacafc0-->
- `_call` (function) — Factory building a PendingCall with an optional context.flow_id (sentinel '__missing__' omits the field entirely). <!--#9e798695f2db895a-->
- `test_filter_keeps_matching_flow_id` (function) — Asserts _filter_calls_for_flow keeps calls whose context.flow_id matches the target flow. <!--#2965e2e6a9b55908-->
- `test_filter_drops_non_matching_flow_id` (function) — Asserts _filter_calls_for_flow drops calls belonging to a different flow_id. <!--#16a407315ef3fa27-->
- `test_filter_drops_unattributed_calls_when_flow_id_known` (function) — Asserts unattributed (missing/empty flow_id) calls are dropped when the current flow_id is known. <!--#e6da64573e9a6581-->
- `test_filter_passthrough_when_flow_id_unknown` (function) — Asserts the filter passes all calls through unchanged when the target flow_id is None or empty. <!--#0fe641b806ffa666-->
- `_make_root` (function) — Helper that scaffolds a project root with an engine.json plus a set of call files for end-to-end snapshot tests. <!--#a5071385c00d2def-->
- `test_snapshot_filters_pending_calls_by_flow_id` (function) — End-to-end test that _snapshot_for_root surfaces only calls matching the engine's flow_id, dropping other-flow/unattributed/legacy ones. <!--#1f216e1fbd3b7191-->
- `test_snapshot_folds_legacy_top_level_flow_id` (function) — Verifies call files with a top-level (non-context) flow_id are folded into context.flow_id so the per-flow filter keeps them. <!--#1e061d16ecc30f91-->
- `test_snapshot_no_engine_json_passthrough` (function) — Asserts that with no engine.json the snapshot has flow_id None and passes all pending calls through unfiltered. <!--#99d0518fa3e58702-->
- `test_snapshot_completed_flow_reports_total_and_full_progress` (function) — Verifies a COMPLETED engine.json (index == total) yields total/total steps and progress 1.0. <!--#02c760172b2450c3-->
- `test_run_fallback_completion_advances_index_to_total` (function) — Drives run._complete_flow_via_fallback over a dangling current step and confirms it advances the index to total, yielding progress 1.0 via the aggregator. <!--#c7bb46ab42a79308-->
- `test_machine_status_project_roots` (function) — Asserts MachineStatus exposes and serializes its registered project_roots (empty list when none). <!--#907ec55ff3436564-->
- `test_get_snapshot_copies_root_set_before_iterating` (function) — Asserts get_snapshot iterates a copy of the project-root set so a concurrent add_project_root doesn't raise a 'set changed size' error. <!--#3eff3ecf8e3f2b9f-->
- `test_machine_status_project_roots_includes_historical` (function) — Verifies project_roots merges active registrations with historical (archive/history-bearing) roots, deduped. <!--#3864a8ef79ad862d-->
- `test_machine_status_project_roots_sorted_and_unique` (function) — Asserts the merged project_roots list is sorted and free of duplicates. <!--#d9666fdbef3d3209-->
- `_stale_call` (function) — Factory building a PendingCall tagged with kind, step_id, and a fixed flow_id for stale-filtering tests. <!--#c7eed47c3e390a47-->
- `_state_with_step_status` (function) — Helper producing a minimal engine state dict whose single current step carries a given status. <!--#dab21fe4a4398f0e-->
- `test_filter_stale_keeps_retry_decision_on_failed_current_step` (function) — Asserts a retry_decision call on the FAILED current step is exempt from stale filtering and stays pending. <!--#534b668a6d8e8000-->
- `test_filter_stale_drops_plain_call_on_failed_step` (function) — Asserts non-exempt (kind=call) calls still follow the FAILED-as-stale rule and are dropped. <!--#ca5fb00f0338d0d0-->
- `test_filter_stale_drops_retry_decision_on_non_failed_processed_status` (function) — Verifies the retry_decision exemption applies only to 'failed', not completed/partial/revision_needed statuses. <!--#844a90b7067b7b10-->
- `test_filter_stale_drops_retry_decision_when_flow_moved_past_step` (function) — Asserts the retry_decision exemption is scoped to the current step and drops it once the flow advances past that step. <!--#3a71135fad2c9f75-->
- `test_filter_stale_mixed_kinds_on_failed_step` (function) — Asserts that in a mixed batch on a failed step the retry_decision survives while a plain call is filtered out. <!--#453ddaec70d0a347-->
- `test_machine_status_pending_calls_unfiltered` (function) — Verifies flow snapshots are strictly flow-scoped while MachineStatus.pending_calls retains the unfiltered machine-wide aggregate. <!--#3380fa4499f6a42d-->

- `test_all_project_roots_reenumerates_after_ttl` (function) — Asserts the historical disk walk re-runs once the monotonic-clock TTL has elapsed. <!--#9a03698c94253919-->
- `test_all_project_roots_reenumerates_on_base_change` (function) — Asserts a changed base fingerprint (via set_project_roots) forces re-enumeration even within the TTL. <!--#d978b61032a5ad98-->

- `test_active_worktree_run_root_is_observable` (function) — Asserts a live --worktree run's subdir is surfaced by all_observable_roots but excluded from the dropdown-facing all_project_roots. <!--#840f408c0d6d593f-->

### `tests/test_daemon_cursor_resume.py` (python) — Unit tests verifying the daemon history reader's cursor lifecycle across rounds — that live/FAILED flows still in engine.json retain their cursor to enable append-only resume deltas, drained archived flows are pruned, and live_flow_ids is bounded to one resumable flow per project root (with legacy-provider fallback). <!--#f557ef735a1c8ce1|12875848d82db8b5-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Helper that constructs a DaemonClient wired to a given history provider and stub snapshot provider for testing. <!--#f19f94c6130c7b3c-->

  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket's list capturing sent (decoded) messages. <!--#b8b92aad379d234c-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Decodes the outgoing payload and appends it to the captured sent-messages list. <!--#7d44362527b3e749-->
- `_ScriptedHistoryProvider` (class) — Test double history provider whose per-round reads and live-flow set are scriptable, recording the cursor maps it receives so tests can assert append-continuation. <!--#d460b8347a7f3ef4-->
  - `_ScriptedHistoryProvider.__init__` (method) — Initializes the scripted provider's reads list, live-flow set, and seen-cursors log. <!--#9576faf525691821-->
  - `_ScriptedHistoryProvider.build_index` (method) — Returns an empty index (no-op stub for the provider interface). <!--#c4f69f683d154763-->
  - `_ScriptedHistoryProvider.active_flow_signature` (method) — Returns an empty signature dict (no-op stub for the provider interface). <!--#d5e6eba440e59874-->
  - `_ScriptedHistoryProvider.live_flow_ids` (method) — Returns a copy of the scripted set of live (resumable) flow ids. <!--#23771304885724d8-->
  - `_ScriptedHistoryProvider.read_active_flows` (method) — Snapshots the cursor map it was handed and returns the scripted FlowRead list for the round. <!--#01ccc7af1db29b29-->
- `_data_frames` (function) — Filters a fake WebSocket's captured messages down to history-data frames. <!--#47b939ac7698c1bb-->
- `test_terminal_flush_retains_cursor_for_live_flow` (function) — Asserts a FAILED flow still in engine.json keeps its cursor through the final flush and the subsequent record-less round. <!--#0a532ed50662e298-->
- `test_resume_continues_with_append_not_full_reread` (function) — Asserts that after resume the retained cursor is passed to the read, yielding an append delta carrying only the new record rather than a full re-read. <!--#ef4df2f2e57fb2ec-->
- `test_drained_archived_flow_cursor_is_pruned` (function) — Asserts a drained terminal flow no longer in engine.json is pruned from the cursor map while the live flow's cursor is retained. <!--#0dca867b14b922af-->

- `test_live_flow_ids_includes_failed_engine_flow` (function) — Asserts DaemonHistoryReader.live_flow_ids counts a FAILED engine.json flow as live/resumable. <!--#56e6bf31823b865e-->
- `test_live_flow_ids_bounded_to_one_per_root` (function) — Asserts each project root contributes at most its single current engine.json flow to live_flow_ids. <!--#0b05c7ceca5703fe-->
- `test_live_flow_ids_empty_without_engine_json` (function) — Asserts a root with no engine.json contributes no live flow ids (no spurious retention). <!--#5d79297fd4fb9840-->

### `tests/test_daemon_history_step_transition.py` (python) — Test suite verifying the daemon's history reader/client correctly detects and delivers incremental jsonl deltas across flow step transitions (discovery→confirm→analyze), status flips, and in-place retry rewrites (issue #209) via per-file byte cursors and whole-prefix fingerprinting, with no record loss or duplication. <!--#367a75fde0f6b12e|70a2a31e5f66e975-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Test helper that writes a list of dicts as a newly-created jsonl file at the given path. <!--#18930ad89d1ea5fb-->
- `_append_jsonl` (function) — Test helper that appends a list of dicts as new lines to an existing jsonl file. <!--#b174bd6540498b15-->
- `_msg` (function) — Test helper that builds a minimal history message record dict with role, content, and step_type. <!--#be5fea2d16df9253-->
- `_make_reader` (function) — Test helper that constructs a DaemonHistoryReader over the given project roots. <!--#808724bfc5456a05-->
- `_write_engine` (function) — Test helper that writes a minimal active engine.json giving a flow its id and status. <!--#432f8814d677f434-->
- `_hist` (function) — Test helper returning the on-disk history directory path for a given flow id under a root. <!--#c4c9473ef3f89cea-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Test helper that builds a DaemonClient wired to a real history provider/reader. <!--#6a78ec87e23c90bc-->
- `_FakeWS` (class) — Minimal WebSocket stand-in that decodes and records every message the client sends. <!--#4bcd88a41b8c0413-->
  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket's captured-message list. <!--#b8b92aad379d234c-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Async send override that decodes the protocol frame and appends it to the captured list. <!--#7d44362527b3e749-->
- `_data_frames` (function) — Test helper filtering a fake WS's captured messages down to HISTORY_DATA frames. <!--#47b939ac7698c1bb-->
- `test_signature_changes_when_analyze_step_file_appears` (function) — Asserts the active-flow signature moves forward when a brand-new analyze step jsonl appears after a discovery→analyze transition. <!--#18669b25c040eeb7-->
- `test_signature_changes_on_paused_then_running_flip` (function) — Asserts each engine.json RUNNING↔PAUSED status flip changes the signature so the daemon re-pushes around the confirmation pause. <!--#6594cd2dd02a4571-->
- `test_read_active_flows_delivers_analyze_delta_after_transition` (function) — Drives the full discovery→confirm→analyze sequence and asserts read_active_flows returns non-empty append deltas for the confirm reply and analyze records without spurious re-push. <!--#eb8779e13c85a544-->
- `test_per_file_cursor_first_full_then_append_no_loss_no_dup` (function) — Verifies per-file byte cursors give a new file a full first read while existing files append, so the union of deltas equals one full read with no loss or duplication. <!--#cc73b490a4c94793-->
- `test_history_changed_fires_on_discovery_to_analyze_transition` (function) — Asserts a real DaemonClient's _history_changed fires on the analyze-file appearance and status flips but stays quiet on an unchanged tree. <!--#d64a7814395e2cf6-->
- `test_retry_resend_same_step_jsonl_records_arrive_as_delta` (function) — Asserts retry records appended to the same step jsonl surface as a non-empty append delta even when the resent body duplicates the failed attempt. <!--#3606a7f8e76b977a-->
- `test_retry_truncate_replace_same_step_jsonl_delivers_new_records` (function) — Asserts an in-place retry that truncates the step jsonl to a shorter batch delivers all replacement records rather than skipping them against the stale line-count cursor (issue #209). <!--#74d55976441e6d7f-->
- `test_retry_rewrite_equal_size_delivers_new_records` (function) — Asserts an in-place retry rewriting the step jsonl to the same byte size but different content is detected via fingerprint and delivers the full replacement instead of seeing 'no new bytes' (issue #209). <!--#89361356232f3890-->
- `test_retry_rewrite_equal_size_preserved_boundary_delivers_new_records` (function) — Asserts an equal-size rewrite that changes an earlier record while keeping the trailing boundary record identical is still detected by whole-prefix fingerprinting (issue #209 iteration 5). <!--#c291d05f80ce3edd-->
- `test_retry_rewrite_equal_size_preserved_head_delivers_new_records` (function) — Asserts an equal-size rewrite that changes a later record while keeping the leading head record identical is still detected by whole-prefix fingerprinting (issue #209 iteration 6). <!--#2385623c2df6fefe-->
- `test_retry_rewrite_larger_size_delivers_full_replacement` (function) — Asserts an in-place retry rewriting the step jsonl larger than the old offset delivers the full replacement from the start rather than a stale-offset partial suffix slice (issue #209). <!--#14202aaa3eef0362-->
- `test_retry_rewrite_larger_size_preserved_head_delivers_full_replacement` (function) — Asserts a grow-case rewrite that preserves the leading head record still falls through to whole-prefix fingerprinting and delivers the full replacement rather than a suffix-only slice (issue #209 iteration 7). <!--#b59092b2be527bb9-->
- `test_retry_rewrite_larger_size_preserved_head_and_boundary_delivers_full_replacement` (function) — Asserts a grow-case rewrite preserving both the head and boundary windows but changing a middle record is caught by whole-prefix fingerprinting, defeating two-bounded-window detection (issue #209 iteration 8). <!--#2c5f3e84199de126-->
- `test_retry_new_attempt_file_picked_up_as_delta` (function) — Asserts a retry that writes a brand-new attempt jsonl (instead of appending) is still picked up incrementally as a delta. <!--#640e49c21ef703fd-->
- `test_history_changed_fires_on_retry_resend` (function) — Asserts _history_changed fires when a retry appends to a step jsonl because the byte-size signature component moves even with a byte-identical body and coarse mtime. <!--#46725328f8fbc9de-->
- `test_push_history_resend_is_append_not_full_reread` (function) — End-to-end test through DaemonClient._push_history asserting a retry resend ships an APPEND frame carrying only the new record, with no duplicate re-read of the prior attempt. <!--#e700ca281f2f7ded-->

### `tests/test_daemon_history_step_type.py` (python) — Unit tests for the daemon's history layer covering parse_step_type_from_step_id across all file-name conventions (seq prefix, underscore type names, _Gk group suffix, hex hash tails, legacy/non-conforming names) and verifying DaemonHistoryReader.read_flow injects the authoritative step_type into each record envelope without mutating message content. <!--#6dea2e5bdf731ce4|41717400128adbe5-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Helper that writes a list of dicts as newline-delimited JSON to the given path, creating parent directories. <!--#18930ad89d1ea5fb-->
- `_make_reader` (function) — Helper that constructs a DaemonHistoryReader whose project roots are the passed-in paths. <!--#808724bfc5456a05-->
- `test_parse_known_types_with_seq_and_hash` (function) — Parametrized test asserting known step types parse correctly from names with sequence prefix and hex hash tails. <!--#79c911c009c152e0-->
- `test_parse_underscore_type_name` (function) — Verifies type names containing underscores (e.g. version_analyze, self_check) survive hash stripping intact. <!--#231334cf06641032-->
- `test_parse_group_suffix` (function) — Parametrized test confirming the optional `_Gk` group suffix is stripped along with the hash before resolving the type. <!--#b79ffaf0e0c3b24b-->
- `test_parse_no_hash_just_seq` (function) — Asserts conforming names lacking a hash tail still resolve to their type segment. <!--#704721181b3ca59c-->
- `test_parse_legacy_name_falls_back_to_stem` (function) — Checks legacy names without a sequence prefix or hex hash fall back to the full stem rather than raising. <!--#41ced5117fbee5b3-->
- `test_parse_unknown_but_conforming_returns_middle` (function) — Verifies unknown but convention-conforming names parse to their middle segment, including multi-word ones. <!--#13372c2666174d4f-->
- `test_parse_empty_and_non_string` (function) — Asserts empty, whitespace, None, and non-string inputs all return an empty string instead of raising. <!--#33179ca1b8d3ad40-->
- `test_parse_is_pure_no_side_effects` (function) — Confirms the parser is deterministic across repeated calls and leaves its input unchanged. <!--#363b8064e9e40108-->
- `test_read_flow_injects_step_type_envelope` (function) — Verifies read_flow attaches the authoritative parsed step_type to each returned record envelope. <!--#47a8bc691d04d8fd-->
- `test_read_flow_does_not_mutate_message_content` (function) — Ensures envelope step_type injection leaves the original message dict byte-for-byte unchanged. <!--#23313986d9e05310-->
- `test_read_flow_legacy_step_completed_event_not_broken` (function) — Confirms a step_completed event already carrying its own step_type round-trips without the envelope overwriting or corrupting it. <!--#8df50aac3ebbeed1-->
- `test_read_flow_legacy_filename_envelope_falls_back` (function) — Checks a legacy-stem history file yields a graceful envelope step_type equal to the original stem. <!--#2cb9ec125a1aae1d-->

### `tests/test_daemon_history_worktree_merge.py` (python) — Unit tests for DaemonHistoryReader's worktree-aware flow resolution and history merging, verifying that split histories across a worktree and its owning main repo are resolved to the right root candidates, merged into a single ordered conversation with discovery files deduplicated (even across differing hashes), back-filled and forward-expanded correctly, read incrementally without loss, and governed by the authoritative project_root over legacy registry heuristics. <!--#a6adde14b1d74f02|33cd8650869689a6-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Helper that writes a list of dict lines as a fresh JSONL file, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#f321072562a278a4-->
- `_append_jsonl` (function) — Helper that appends a list of dict lines to an existing JSONL file. <!--#826510bf1d7d8393-->
- `_msg` (function) — Helper building a minimal conversation message dict with role and content. <!--#67f68ff7e3aa1c72-->
- `_make_reader` (function) — Helper constructing a DaemonHistoryReader whose project-roots provider returns the given roots as strings. <!--#f5fb70620f9f4765-->
- `_flow_dir` (function) — Helper creating and returning a flow's `se3/history/<flow_id>` directory under a root. <!--#2bc670cdd788413e-->
- `_make_worktree` (function) — Helper creating a `se3/worktrees/<name>` isolation dir under a main repo (with the `se3` dir present so it attributes back to the main root). <!--#043b5054157d28f3-->
- `test_resolve_flow_dirs_worktree_returns_both_roots` (function) — Asserts that resolving a worktree root returns both the worktree dir (first) and its owning main-repo dir. <!--#d8d48803f4f5c9dc-->
- `test_resolve_flow_dirs_main_root_only_self` (function) — Asserts a plain non-worktree root resolves to just its own flow directory. <!--#8503407e79f37b0a-->
- `test_resolve_flow_dirs_skips_missing_main_dir` (function) — Asserts that when the main repo lacks the flow's history, only the worktree dir is returned. <!--#7f9bbdc36f56fbf7-->
- `test_resolve_flow_dirs_empty_project_root_legacy_heuristic` (function) — Asserts that an empty project_root falls back to the legacy single first-match registry walk. <!--#ecc9a68b7cb4f1a3-->
- `test_resolve_flow_dirs_unknown_flow_empty` (function) — Asserts that an unknown flow id resolves to an empty candidate list without error. <!--#e2d13ab37c6c8ba5-->
- `test_read_flow_merges_split_history_dedups_discovery` (function) — Asserts read_flow merges main discovery with worktree steps, deduplicating the cloned discovery file into a single ordered conversation. <!--#c4e1336176352d28-->
- `test_read_flow_backfills_discovery_only_in_main` (function) — Asserts that discovery held only in the main repo is back-filled ahead of the worktree's later steps. <!--#5fc76d4574d70d9d-->
- `test_read_flow_dedup_prefers_more_complete_copy` (function) — Asserts that when both roots hold the same-named file, the larger/more-complete copy is chosen so no records are lost. <!--#b96d806fd0517c64-->
- `test_read_flow_incremental_across_merge` (function) — Asserts the incremental read cursor advances correctly over the merged file set, returning only newly appended records. <!--#71bb51107a4ae21d-->
- `test_read_flow_missing_one_root_does_not_raise` (function) — Asserts the read still succeeds when the main repo has no history directory at all. <!--#ec4e728608bd8517-->
- `test_read_flow_dedups_discovery_with_differing_hash` (function) — Asserts a discovery clone stored under a different per-step hash still dedups to a single discovery by logical step identity. <!--#329625ba501cbd3e-->
- `_write_engine` (function) — Helper writing an `se3/state/engine.json` with flow id, status, and optional worktree-mode flag. <!--#413074a99ab1cc41-->
- `test_index_records_worktree_root_for_split_active_flow` (function) — Asserts build_index records the active worktree root (not the history-only main repo) for a split active flow and that root reaches the later steps. <!--#67366e5361842d61-->
- `test_read_flow_main_root_forward_expands_into_worktree` (function) — Asserts that even when the index recorded the main root, forward expansion still pulls in the worktree's later steps. <!--#91b131cfcce93c1d-->
- `test_read_flow_authoritative_root_beats_registry_first_match` (function) — Asserts the passed authoritative project_root governs the read (yielding the full merged set) over the legacy registry first-match heuristic. <!--#d691b16372f10cda-->

### `tests/test_daemon_key_hello.py` (python) — Unit and end-to-end tests verifying the additive daemon-key auth feature: HELLO payloads carry the key when configured and stay wire-compatible when not, the key is never logged or exposed in status/pidfiles, WELCOME rejections flag auth failure and stop the run loop, transient failures keep reconnecting, and the key is resolved correctly from CLI flag, env var, and config defaults. <!--#ca2d1c3527418495|5f84981131cf8e10-->
- `test_make_hello_includes_key_when_set` (function) — Asserts make_hello embeds the supplied key in the HELLO payload alongside machine_id. <!--#e17ed1f0e4e814de-->
- `test_make_hello_omits_key_when_empty` (function) — Asserts an empty or absent key leaves the HELLO payload byte-identical to the legacy four-field structure. <!--#76d1f31e81838ada-->
- `test_make_hello_does_not_bump_protocol_version` (function) — Asserts the additive key field does not change the protocol_version in the HELLO payload. <!--#37ba0c99b622bb41-->
- `test_hello_with_key_decodes_roundtrip` (function) — Asserts a key-bearing HELLO survives encode/decode roundtrip with the key preserved for old servers to ignore. <!--#0df7d18b32ca7d6a-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Test helper that constructs a DaemonClient with default connection params and overridable kwargs. <!--#6a90ceaf2230f869-->
- `_SessionWS` (class) — Fake WebSocket stand-in that records sent messages and blocks forever on receive. <!--#f9763dd64019932b-->
  - `_SessionWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket's empty sent-message list. <!--#b8b92aad379d234c-->
  - `_SessionWS.send` (method) — Decodes and appends each outgoing message to the captured sends list. <!--#7d44362527b3e749-->
  - `_SessionWS.__aiter__` (method) — Returns self so the fake WebSocket can be async-iterated. <!--#015f3ec29184096d-->
  - `_SessionWS.__anext__` (method) — Blocks forever to simulate an idle receive stream until the session is cancelled. <!--#634859912bf87bc5-->

  - `_FakeConn.__init__` (method) — Stores the fake WebSocket to be returned on context entry. <!--#837596bb3f64d60e-->
  - `_FakeConn.__aenter__` (method) — Returns the stored fake WebSocket when entering the async context. <!--#95814d21ab06066e-->
  - `_FakeConn.__aexit__` (method) — No-op async exit that suppresses nothing. <!--#552946396ec260ce-->
- `_FakeWebsockets` (class) — Minimal stand-in for the websockets module whose connect returns a _FakeConn. <!--#cb19a33404b9b630-->
  - `_FakeWebsockets.__init__` (method) — Stores the fake WebSocket to hand to connections. <!--#837596bb3f64d60e-->
  - `_FakeWebsockets.connect` (method) — Returns a _FakeConn wrapping the preset fake WebSocket, ignoring URL and kwargs. <!--#2fc1c4e2e48510af-->
- `_run_one_session` (function) — Test helper that runs exactly one DaemonClient._session which unwinds immediately via a pre-set stop event. <!--#63a116f8fd32f116-->
- `test_session_hello_carries_configured_key` (function) — Asserts a session sends a single HELLO carrying the configured daemon_key. <!--#dd6bb87706050465-->
- `test_session_hello_omits_key_when_unconfigured` (function) — Asserts an unconfigured client sends a single HELLO with no key field. <!--#d271412f5465df71-->
- `test_daemon_key_is_not_logged` (function) — Asserts the daemon key never appears in any debug-level log record during a session. <!--#ec08330a79f48b7d-->
- `test_handle_welcome_accepted_is_noop` (function) — Asserts an accepted WELCOME leaves the auth-rejected flag and event unset. <!--#026276052ec2a101-->
- `test_handle_welcome_rejected_flags_and_signals` (function) — Asserts a rejected WELCOME sets the auth-rejected flag, records the reason, and signals the event. <!--#544426d3f294d15b-->
- `test_handle_welcome_rejected_without_reason_has_fallback` (function) — Asserts a reasonless rejection still flags auth-rejected and yields a non-empty fallback last_error. <!--#faa59c23114bf15e-->
- `test_dispatch_welcome_reject_does_not_leak_key` (function) — Asserts dispatching a rejection logs the server reason but never the daemon key. <!--#f723447424f2a897-->
- `test_run_loop_stops_after_auth_rejection` (function) — Asserts a rejected credential halts the run loop after one session instead of reconnecting forever. <!--#38be95adcc3d065e-->
- `test_run_loop_keeps_reconnecting_on_transient_failure` (function) — Asserts a transient (non-auth) failure does not set the auth-stop flag and yields a formatted last_error. <!--#08c78fcdc21cb794-->
- `test_daemon_config_daemon_key_defaults_to_none` (function) — Asserts DaemonConfig.daemon_key defaults to None and accepts an explicit value. <!--#6d5c7101f4505a1c-->
- `test_daemon_passes_key_to_client` (function) — Asserts the Daemon threads its configured daemon_key into the DaemonClient it starts. <!--#b4c12ff745b9b3f9-->
- `test_daemon_without_key_passes_empty_string_to_client` (function) — Asserts a keyless Daemon passes an empty-string key to its client. <!--#450f42b595d446ac-->
- `test_daemon_status_does_not_echo_key` (function) — Asserts daemon_status output and the on-disk pidfile/status files never expose the daemon key. <!--#e09b5f02f3df6197-->

- `test_cli_daemon_start_passes_explicit_key` (function) — Asserts `--daemon-key` on the CLI sets the resolved config's daemon_key. <!--#ca2295ddff3a43cd-->
- `test_cli_daemon_start_reads_key_from_env` (function) — Asserts the daemon key is read from the SE3_DAEMON_KEY environment variable when no flag is given. <!--#8abaae8bee3808be-->
- `test_cli_daemon_start_flag_overrides_env` (function) — Asserts the `--daemon-key` flag takes precedence over the SE3_DAEMON_KEY env var. <!--#c470766ebe352c89-->
- `test_cli_daemon_start_no_key_is_none` (function) — Asserts the resolved config's daemon_key is None when neither flag nor env var is set. <!--#6ebf2f4e1ec55b79-->
- `test_old_daemon_without_key_rejected_by_live_server` (function) — End-to-end test asserting a live auth server rejects a keyless HELLO and registers no machine for it. <!--#89ea1a0b3be64174-->
- `test_live_server_tolerates_unknown_key_bearing_hello_field` (function) — End-to-end test asserting a live server cleanly accepts a valid key-bearing HELLO, proving wire compatibility of the additive field. <!--#257f28e1e94bde0d-->

### `tests/test_daemon_spawner_path.py` (python) — Test module verifying the daemon spawner's login-shell PATH handling: unit tests for the pure merge_path_env helper (ordering, dedup, None/empty edges) and resolve_login_shell_path (subprocess parsing, failure/timeout fallbacks), plus integration tests confirming DaemonSpawner-spawned and resumed children inherit the merged PATH and degrade gracefully when resolution fails. <!--#583538c3dba6c1ff|923f7bdb83c0c5d8-->

  - `TestMergePathEnv.test_login_empty_returns_current` (method) — Asserts an empty login PATH yields the current PATH unchanged. <!--#c9cf791be4c9cc79-->
  - `TestMergePathEnv.test_current_none_returns_login` (method) — Asserts a None current PATH yields the login PATH unchanged. <!--#1d2499daf75594bf-->
  - `TestMergePathEnv.test_current_empty_returns_login` (method) — Asserts an empty current PATH yields the login PATH unchanged. <!--#57f513eaf526b4fe-->
  - `TestMergePathEnv.test_both_none_returns_none` (method) — Asserts merging two None PATHs returns None. <!--#f951c31d6258ee32-->
  - `TestMergePathEnv.test_both_empty_returns_none` (method) — Asserts merging two empty PATHs returns None. <!--#2de7f0e4b37a1996-->

### `tests/test_dag_scheduler_status.py` (python) — Unit tests verifying the DAG scheduler emits the correct ordered, once-per-group status transitions (queued/running/completed/failed/skipped) for success, failure, and downstream-skip cases, and remains robust when the status callback is absent or raises. <!--#aab236ae60a4e7a5|880dc3b1d2bca17d-->

  - `TestStatusEmission.test_failure_emits_failed_and_downstream_skipped` (method) — Asserts an upstream exception emits 'failed' and transitively skips downstream groups (queued → skipped). <!--#9f978d13064c1998-->

- `test_interactive_confirm_pause_writes_discovery_confirm_call` (function) — Verifies the programmatic-confirm gate writes a kind=discovery_confirm call with a one-click value='1' option and cleans up after a terminal '1' confirms. <!--#3dc123f708d4804f-->

### `tests/test_docs_updater.py` (python) — Unit tests for the documentation updater covering VERSIONS.md entry insertion (empty files, missing titles, duplicate dedup, and template selection/fallback), README version-badge placement around front-matter and headings, independent update_both error handling, and Template placeholder substitution. <!--#4882b435cd2ea50a|656723efcdec9b85-->
- `TestEmptyVersionsFile` (class) — Tests that an empty VERSIONS.md file correctly receives a freshly inserted version entry. <!--#8d74e2522a708f58-->

  - `TestReadmeFrontMatter.test_badge_inserted_after_heading_not_breaking_front_matter` (method) — Asserts the version badge is placed after the heading and after intact YAML front-matter, before body content. <!--#b70585e97cb48ccb-->
  - `TestReadmeFrontMatter.test_html_comment_header_is_skipped` (method) — Asserts a leading HTML comment is preserved and the badge is inserted after the heading that follows it. <!--#f4b31a0ea0bef416-->
  - `TestReadmeFrontMatter.test_no_heading_prepends_badge` (method) — Asserts the badge is prepended to the file when README.md has no heading at all. <!--#f04486d700104338-->
- `TestConfigCustomEntryTemplate` (class) — Tests that a config-supplied versions_entry_template overrides the default and drives rendering. <!--#36cc322458883448-->
  - `TestConfigCustomEntryTemplate.test_custom_entry_template_used` (method) — Asserts the custom entry template is stored and renders the version and changes into VERSIONS.md as configured. <!--#2a384d33f0504f57-->

  - `TestVersionsTemplateFileFallback.test_concrete_first_block_rejected_falls_back_to_default` (method) — Asserts a concrete (non-placeholder) first block is rejected, falling back to the DEFAULT template so the real version/changes are written. <!--#d8000cb90e87b9d2-->
  - `TestVersionsTemplateFileFallback.test_fallback_to_default_when_file_absent` (method) — Asserts that a missing versions_md.md yields None from the file helper and the updater uses the built-in DEFAULT entry template. <!--#e8346f1eeda91920-->
  - `TestVersionsTemplateFileFallback.test_config_template_wins_over_file` (method) — Asserts a config-supplied entry template takes precedence over the versions_md.md file template. <!--#872e4fe24c10ef6b-->
