### `tests/test_end_session_cmd.py` (python) — Test suite for the `se3 end-session` command covering session archival (worktree and main-branch), history-collision sidecars, flow-id resolution, live-parent discovery (via descendant cwd and pidfile), process termination/escalation/tree-kill, and defensive guards that skip destructive cleanup on mismatched flows, unkillable processes, or archive/step failures. <!--#0a7beb2a19d289cb|74818f5d65e9a38d-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Helper that initializes a git repo at the given path with a configured user and an initial committed README. <!--#1635ad85954c81ae-->
- `_branch_exists` (function) — Helper that returns whether a given git branch exists in the repo via `git rev-parse --verify`. <!--#fe856a428f75db97-->
- `_write_fake_se3` (function) — Test helper that writes an executable `se3` shebang script running a given body, so spawning it makes psutil observe the real console-script `[interpreter, /path/se3, run, ...]` argv shape that the tightened `_cmdline_is_se3_run` predicate matches. <!--#314d535317f2db8b-->
- `_make_worktree_session` (function) — Helper that builds a real git worktree session with engine.json, a resumable snapshot, and a history file for use as test fixtures. <!--#045b7a74f370c155-->
- `_make_main_session` (function) — Helper that creates a main-branch (non-worktree) session by writing engine.json and a resumable snapshot under main/se3/state. <!--#7db44937b4a1cbc4-->
- `test_worktree_session_is_archived` (function) — Verifies a worktree session is fully archived: worktree dir archived, terminal state promoted with project_root stamped, history synced to main, and branch/worktree cleaned up. <!--#2156c0f536fdc296-->
- `test_worktree_session_history_collision_uses_sidecar` (function) — Verifies that when a worktree history file collides with an existing main history file, the original is preserved and the copy lands as a `.from-<branch>` sidecar. <!--#cad015fac8b425c9-->
- `test_main_branch_session_is_archived` (function) — Verifies a main-branch session is archived: engine.json moved into archive/ and the resumable snapshot cleared. <!--#f519675a65ef9f1d-->
- `test_flow_id_resolved_from_main_engine` (function) — Verifies that when flow_id is omitted, end-session reads it from the main engine.json and archives that session. <!--#03c5521b1b361121-->
- `test_terminate_by_pid_sigterm` (function) — Verifies that end-session with `--pid` terminates a live long-running child process via SIGTERM. <!--#03b178844d9667b7-->
- `test_terminate_sigkill_escalation` (function) — Verifies that a process ignoring SIGTERM is escalated to SIGKILL after the grace period. <!--#7b9aee7aa64c72ad-->
- `test_terminate_kills_child_subprocess` (function) — Verifies that ending a session kills the whole process tree, not just the parent, so agent/test child subprocesses are not orphaned. <!--#08581e7e7cf1d8e7-->
- `test_worktree_without_branch_is_still_cleaned_up` (function) — Verifies a worktree session whose engine.json lacks worktree_branch is still cleaned up by inferring the branch from git's worktree metadata. <!--#a21bbb579ae81065-->
- `test_stale_unregistered_worktree_dir_is_removed` (function) — Verifies a stale, unregistered worktree dir with no branch is archived and fully removed via the remove-by-path fallback. <!--#1ab8ec7b239a80af-->
- `test_discovers_live_worktree_parent_by_descendant_cwd` (function) — Verifies that a live `se3 run --worktree` parent (which keeps cwd at main_root) is discovered for its flow via a descendant agent subprocess whose cwd is inside the worktree path. <!--#602105da0154f4de-->
- `test_discovers_live_worktree_parent_via_pidfile` (function) — Verifies that a live `se3 run --worktree` parent with no worktree-resident descendant is still discovered through the pid recorded in the worktree's `run.pid` marker, so the worktree isn't archived under a still-live process. <!--#7d8697af7cf82b1b-->
- `test_stale_pidfile_is_ignored` (function) — Verifies a `run.pid` pointing at a dead pid is not reported as a live process by discovery. <!--#a7650edbddf5d986-->
- `test_no_live_process_still_archives` (function) — Verifies a PAUSED worktree with no live process is still archived cleanly and its branch removed. <!--#840509fe5b1a1647-->
- `test_unkillable_process_skips_destructive_archive` (function) — Verifies that if the target process cannot be killed, the destructive archive is skipped, the worktree/branch survive, and the command exits non-zero. <!--#8689e85dd9589d5e-->
- `test_missing_worktree_degrades_to_main_archive` (function) — Verifies that with no worktree found, end-session falls back to the main-branch archival path without error. <!--#04b51133a080e5f7-->
- `test_mismatched_main_flow_is_not_archived` (function) — Verifies that ending flow A does not archive an unrelated active flow B whose engine.json occupies the main project. <!--#16bb8115fc54e639-->
- `test_unreadable_main_flow_is_not_archived` (function) — Verifies that when the main engine.json carries no readable flow_id, the destructive clear is skipped to avoid ending the wrong session. <!--#8ff6e340ec7f42a9-->
- `test_archive_failure_preserves_worktree_and_branch` (function) — Verifies that a failed worktree-archive step skips destructive cleanup, preserving the branch and worktree, and exits non-zero. <!--#64a8e5845d594a8e-->
- `test_step_failure_does_not_abort_and_exit_nonzero` (function) — Verifies that a raising sub-step (e.g. promotion) is recorded and exits non-zero but does not abort later cleanup steps. <!--#11541efbd2e030bb-->
- `test_unresolvable_root_returns_one` (function) — Verifies that an unresolvable project root causes end_session to return exit code 1. <!--#a6b850b8cf6bf46e-->

### `tests/test_end_session_protocol_daemon.py` (python) — Unit tests for the END_SESSION daemon protocol message, covering its registration/versioning, JSON round-trip encoding, the spawner's argv construction, the supervisor's request_end_session flow lookup and root/pid resolution (including worktree folding and error cases), and the client's dispatch and _handle_end_session behavior. <!--#98729dddd2b381b6|a1bc386a970e5503-->
- `test_msg_end_session_is_server_to_daemon` (function) — Asserts MSG_END_SESSION has the right name and is registered as a server→daemon message in the correct protocol sets. <!--#576fc568a0cafaa3-->

- `test_request_end_session_locates_flow_and_spawns` (function) — Verifies request_end_session looks up a supervised flow and dispatches end_session with its resolved root and pid. <!--#ae5e672bfab5d383-->
- `test_request_end_session_prefers_supplied_root` (function) — Asserts a server-supplied project_root overrides the supervisor's registered root. <!--#a1a318767822f163-->

- `test_request_end_session_unsupervised_flow_with_root_dispatches` (function) — Verifies a dangling (non-live) flow still dispatches end_session—with no pid hint—when the server supplies a root. <!--#d45b06b0ec1eea3e-->
- `test_request_end_session_empty_flow_raises` (function) — Asserts request_end_session raises ValueError on an empty flow_id. <!--#ddca5db47319cda1-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Test helper that constructs a DaemonClient with default identity/snapshot args and overridable handlers. <!--#2166366244481ca6-->
- `test_dispatch_end_session_routes_to_handler` (function) — Verifies the client's async _dispatch routes a decoded END_SESSION message to the configured handler with flow/root/reason. <!--#497088df98906f11-->

### `tests/test_end_session_server.py` (python) — Pytest suite verifying the server's end-flow endpoint, covering ownership/visibility checks (404 for unknown or cross-owner flows), state-based responses (409 for completed flows, 503 for disconnected daemons, 202 for endable flows including dangling completed worktrees), and correct dispatch of MSG_END_SESSION with project_root and a default-or-supplied reason. <!--#e949ea8183164e3e|a9e6f953651aedd3-->

- `test_end_flow_unknown_returns_404` (function) — Asserts ending an unknown flow_id returns 404 and leaks nothing. <!--#75e7bb681254ccf1-->
- `test_end_flow_cross_owner_returns_404` (function) — Asserts a flow owned by another owner reads as absent (404) and is never controllable across owners, while its own owner can end it (202). <!--#8f309a624caf502a-->
- `test_end_flow_completed_returns_409` (function) — Asserts a COMPLETED flow returns 409 (exists but already done) with no misleading end_dispatched status. <!--#b14568a5e2b2d798-->
- `test_end_flow_completed_worktree_dispatches` (function) — Asserts a COMPLETED but dangling worktree session stays endable (202 + MSG_END_SESSION) so the orphaned worktree can be archived. <!--#05337129c169e521-->
- `test_end_flow_daemon_disconnected_returns_503` (function) — Asserts a still-visible flow whose owning daemon has disconnected returns 503. <!--#b4b7567524e79b33-->
- `test_end_flow_dispatches_end_session` (function) — Asserts a non-completed flow on a connected daemon returns 202 and dispatches MSG_END_SESSION carrying the flow's project_root and reason. <!--#983a70d31a7aeb91-->
- `test_end_flow_default_reason_when_body_omitted` (function) — Asserts omitting the request body still dispatches MSG_END_SESSION with the default reason 'user terminated'. <!--#c03b08bb5443a02d-->

### `tests/test_extract_failures.py` (python) — Unit test module whose TestExtractFailuresSection class exercises the `_extract_failures_section` helper, covering FAILURES/ERRORS section extraction, tail fallback when no section exists, max_chars limits and truncation, separator boundaries, and empty/whitespace edge cases. <!--#4642e8fd8ebaf107|a35fea15630566a0-->

### `tests/test_guardrails_size.py` (python) — Test module verifying the spec-size guardrail: that `check_spec_sizes` correctly flags oversized bases, spec files, and individual requirements with size/limit evidence and deterministic, exception-safe output, and that the CLI honors the warn/enforce tier configuration (blocking or not) accordingly. <!--#0a84d0917a1dbaf4|e8ed6deec151bf41-->

- `test_three_oversize_kinds_each_produce_a_violation` (function) — Asserts that an oversized base, spec file, and single requirement each yield their respective SIZE_BASE, SIZE_SPEC_FILE, and SIZE_REQUIREMENT violation types. <!--#6025371508ce20de-->

- `test_base_reported_as_size_base_not_spec_file` (function) — Asserts a base spec exceeding both base and file budgets is reported only under its stricter SIZE_BASE type, not SIZE_SPEC_FILE. <!--#e088ba919aecdc39-->
- `test_requirement_violation_names_the_requirement` (function) — Asserts a SIZE_REQUIREMENT violation's evidence names the offending requirement (e.g. 'Huge Req'). <!--#888bd071fa438a4d-->
- `test_no_violations_when_within_budget` (function) — Asserts `check_spec_sizes` returns an empty list when all budgets are large enough to accommodate every spec. <!--#06f5b76a83fdff66-->
- `test_deterministic_output_order` (function) — Asserts repeated `check_spec_sizes` calls produce violations in the same order, confirming deterministic output. <!--#ada00add9ea79543-->
- `test_unreadable_or_empty_project_does_not_raise` (function) — Asserts that a project with no `se3/specs` directory returns no violations without raising. <!--#9c9f32f8624f5f1b-->
- `test_unreadable_spec_yields_check_incomplete` (function) — Asserts an OSError while reading a spec yields a CHECK_INCOMPLETE violation (recording exception_type) rather than being silently skipped. <!--#75f35f06371ea030-->
- `test_cli_enforce_blocks_on_unreadable_spec` (function) — Asserts the CLI under enforce tier exits 1 and reports CHECK_INCOMPLETE when a spec cannot be read. <!--#8359e3123a64dbaf-->

- `test_cli_default_tier_is_warn` (function) — Asserts that with no `se3.yaml` the CLI defaults to the non-blocking warn tier and exits 0 despite violations. <!--#214916bff7ee4aaf-->
- `test_cli_passes_when_within_budget` (function) — Asserts the CLI exits 0 and prints a 'passed' message when all specs are within budget. <!--#435a55f2a718a8d9-->

### `tests/test_history_sink_step_started.py` (python) — Unit/integration tests verifying that step lifecycle anchors (step_started/running and step_status like paused) are correctly persisted, deduplicated, re-armed after pauses, and skipped after terminal events across record helpers, HistorySink event consumption, and full run_flow orchestration, while ensuring chat-history reads ignore these non-chat anchor lines. <!--#1338b552f41987b4|b17f0c81b9dfe564-->
- `_step_path` (function) — Helper that builds the per-step jsonl path (se3/history/<flow>/<step>.jsonl) under a project root. <!--#957e6c7aeb46a4cb-->
- `_read_lines` (function) — Helper that reads a jsonl file and returns its non-blank lines parsed as a list of dicts (empty list if absent). <!--#3a7c0ef3252423a1-->
- `test_record_step_started_writes_running_record` (function) — Asserts record_step_started writes a single well-shaped step_started/running record with an ISO timestamp and no chat role field. <!--#725de4ed5b9c57f3-->
- `test_record_step_started_default_timestamp_is_iso_string` (function) — Asserts that record_step_started defaults the timestamp to a non-empty ISO string when none is supplied. <!--#d13f94ced1b36b69-->
- `test_has_step_started_event_detection` (function) — Asserts has_step_started_event returns False for absent/other steps and True only once a step's started anchor exists. <!--#0483c6793b34831d-->
- `test_get_step_history_skips_step_started` (function) — Asserts get_step_history ignores step_started lines, returning None for a started-only file and only real chat messages otherwise. <!--#b9613bca7665992f-->
- `_make_event` (function) — Helper that constructs an engine event of a given type with default flow/step/step_type fields for HistorySink tests. <!--#adcce4c55ea8b382-->
- `test_history_sink_persists_step_started` (function) — Asserts HistorySink.consume of a STEP_STARTED event persists one step_started/running anchor to the step jsonl. <!--#acb6143c8b556d43-->
- `test_history_sink_step_started_is_idempotent_while_running` (function) — Asserts repeated STEP_STARTED events while already running do not stack duplicate started anchors. <!--#43e42e3033c96e6f-->
- `test_history_sink_step_started_rearms_after_pause` (function) — Asserts a resumed (previously paused) step re-arms a fresh running anchor while still not stacking subsequent running events. <!--#f879bf7525c82bfb-->
- `test_history_sink_step_started_skipped_after_terminal` (function) — Asserts a late STEP_STARTED arriving after a terminal step_completed is a no-op, never adding a running anchor to a finished step. <!--#114a85102fdb9ceb-->
- `test_history_sink_terminal_events_unchanged` (function) — Regression guard asserting STEP_COMPLETED/STEP_FAILED/STEP_OUTPUT still persist their full step record unchanged. <!--#a3e7005ad019090b-->
- `_build_flow` (function) — Helper that constructs a single-step RUNNING FlowInstance of a given step type for run_flow integration tests. <!--#21d5b5b1ef5abf2a-->
- `_run_single_step` (function) — Helper that drives run_flow with mocked persistence/StateMachine, simulating the on_running callback to exercise orchestrator-driven step_started persistence. <!--#108fd5725e93260e-->
- `test_run_flow_emits_step_started_for_non_llm_step` (function) — Asserts a non-LLM TEST step gets one running step_started anchor at entry alongside its terminal step_completed through the full run_flow chain. <!--#eea698beb03f259d-->
- `test_run_flow_resume_after_pause_rearms_running_then_completes` (function) — Asserts running a step PAUSED then COMPLETED re-arms a second running anchor after the paused row and still lands its completion. <!--#e53666bca47fbd82-->
- `test_record_step_status_writes_status_record` (function) — Asserts record_step_status writes a step_status record carrying the given status, step_type, and ISO timestamp with no chat role. <!--#df644a53efa97e99-->
- `test_has_step_status_event_is_status_specific` (function) — Asserts has_step_status_event matches only the specific status token (case-insensitively) and not others. <!--#374e259994ed35c9-->
- `test_get_step_history_skips_step_status` (function) — Asserts get_step_history skips step_status lines, surfacing only real chat messages. <!--#6382f5e0fc7fd013-->
- `_run_discovery_pause` (function) — Helper that drives run_flow for a DISCOVERY step returning PAUSED with the interactive pause handler stubbed to exit cleanly. <!--#47bacbfd29346640-->
- `test_run_flow_persists_step_status_on_pause` (function) — Asserts a DISCOVERY step returning PAUSED persists a single paused step_status anchor alongside its running step_started anchor. <!--#78f13b15452f47e8-->
- `test_run_flow_step_status_records_paused_after_running_rearm` (function) — Asserts a multi-round running→paused→running→paused step records the second paused (after the running re-arm) so the latest persisted lifecycle status is correctly paused. <!--#1701383174e5c514-->
- `test_run_flow_step_status_dedups_back_to_back_paused` (function) — Asserts that without an intervening running anchor a re-recorded paused status is deduplicated, preventing two identical stacked status rows. <!--#fba88a107a5c51ac-->

### `tests/test_history_summary_extraction.py` (python) — Unit tests verifying that user-content extraction from prompt bodies works consistently across the CLI and daemon history views, covering three-segment marker parsing, two-segment/missing-marker fallbacks, priority ordering, list-of-text-block content, and corrupt/empty JSONL sentinels. <!--#68312e0db255f6d7|1735fdca01ccda6f-->

- `test_extract_user_content_missing_markers` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content returns None when the body contains no markers. <!--#811f5b297c2d7bd1-->
- `test_extract_user_content_two_segment_returns_none` (function) — Asserts a two-segment body (BEGIN without END) yields None since the tail is framework-injected rather than user input. <!--#db80ad8d2acad804-->
- `test_extract_user_content_empty_middle_returns_none` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content returns None when the marker-enclosed middle is effectively empty. <!--#6138357c44aa1564-->
- `test_extract_user_content_non_string` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content returns None for non-string and empty-string inputs. <!--#83f91e1b426e7884-->
- `test_extract_user_content_begin_before_template_end_is_none` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content returns None when markers appear out of canonical order (BEGIN before the template prefix end). <!--#161d4db56fc6847c-->
- `_write_first_line` (function) — Fixture helper that creates a flow directory and writes a single first-line JSONL user record to drive the extractor tests. <!--#b5d6bdb1154e1e3e-->
- `_build_cases` (function) — Helper returning a labeled matrix of prompt-body inputs paired with their expected untruncated extraction source across all three priority tiers. <!--#ab79ca9dc7ef17ff-->
- `test_cli_and_daemon_share_extraction_source` (function) — Parametrized test asserting the daemon returns the untruncated extraction source while the CLI applies the 100-char clip, both from the same source. <!--#7085829d7ab011de-->
- `test_three_segment_marker_takes_priority_over_regex` (function) — Asserts that when a body contains both USER_CONTENT markers and a Task description block, the marker-level content wins for both extractors. <!--#693c52b84afdda38-->
- `test_content_as_text_block_list` (function) — Asserts both extractors handle a JSONL record whose content is a list of text blocks rather than a plain string. <!--#d03e01122f11ca9c-->
- `test_no_jsonl_returns_no_history_data` (function) — Asserts both extractors return the '(no history data)' sentinel when the flow directory contains no JSONL file. <!--#689d081a8f1bfdc6-->
- `test_corrupt_json_returns_no_state_data` (function) — Asserts both extractors return the '(no state data)' sentinel when the first JSONL line is malformed JSON. <!--#cc7236afd112c939-->
- `test_plain_text_fallback_matches_pre_change_behavior` (function) — Regression test ensuring a marker-less plain-text first line yields the raw content (clipped to 100 chars for the CLI, untruncated for the daemon). <!--#2b24e6f312e28f5e-->

### `tests/test_implement_dag_relay.py` (python) — Unit tests for the implement step's DAG relay execution, covering LOC computation, the LOC-threshold routing between single-LLM-call and DAG-parallel paths, leaf-branch merging with LLM conflict resolution and take-theirs fallback, and the relay-plan integration (transitive reduction, leaf-only merges, and deduplicated worktree cleanup). <!--#1189b3fe475c1dce|a2bdd1fd1c07b12d-->

### `tests/test_implement_group_status.py` (python) — Unit tests for DAG parallel implement-group execution that, using fake schedulers, runners, and LLM callers, verify group_status running/completed records (enriched with step_type, agent, and model) are written to the correct main step jsonl, that on_agent_change relays fire agent-only then agent·model across attempt rotations, and that salvage never re-touches the main step file. <!--#027e077379b81da6|ffa37fff6b2d5525-->

  - `TestDagGroupStatusWiring.test_running_and_completed_records_written` (method) — Runs _run_dag_parallel with a fake scheduler and asserts each group's running and completed group_status records land in the main step jsonl tagged step_type 'implement'. <!--#dcac652550887a7b-->

  - `_AgentStreamRunner.__init__` (method) — Stores the desired success outcome and the model string to be revealed in the streamed init line. <!--#82c09b3957a7bc3a-->

- `TestLLMCallerOnAgentChange` (class) — Test class verifying LLMCaller's on_agent_change fires (agent, None) at selection then (agent, model) after parsing, with each rotated attempt reporting its own agent. <!--#09350c43c75853ec-->
  - `TestLLMCallerOnAgentChange.test_fires_agent_then_model` (method) — Asserts the first on_agent_change event is the agent-only notification and that the agent·model event follows once the model init line is parsed. <!--#d47477de3781f881-->
  - `TestLLMCallerOnAgentChange.test_rotation_reports_each_attempts_agent` (method) — Asserts that after a failed first attempt the agent rotates and each attempt announces its own agent (agentA then agentB), never carrying a stale one over. <!--#1a55f92eff1564b5-->
- `_ExecutingScheduler` (class) — Scheduler stand-in that actually invokes execute_fn (with worktree/git/LLM deps mocked) to exercise the on_agent_change relay and the status sink's agent/model enrichment. <!--#7ccc498ac6ff14f6-->

  - `TestDagAgentModelRelay.test_running_and_completed_records_carry_agent_and_model` (method) — Runs _run_dag_parallel through the executing scheduler and asserts running records gain agent then agent·model and the completed record is enriched with the same final agent/model. <!--#c86341956dfa3447-->

### `tests/test_interaction_calls.py` (python) — Test suite for the file-based interaction-call protocol, covering interject-flow message encode/decode, call-kind classification, write/read round-trips for calls and responses, idempotent draining of queued interjection requests, retry-decision call shaping, and CLI-confirm handler behavior including orphaned-child cleanup. <!--#70f764494de63e64|02aebbef3381c520-->
- `test_make_interject_flow_payload_and_direction` (function) — Asserts make_interject_flow builds the correct payload and that MSG_INTERJECT_FLOW is registered as a server→daemon (not daemon→server) message type. <!--#ce856c65ac66617e-->
- `test_interject_flow_round_trips_through_decode` (function) — Verifies an interject-flow message survives JSON encode/decode with its text preserved and project_root defaulting to empty string. <!--#ac2793896657f29a-->
- `test_call_kind_constants_are_complete_and_distinct` (function) — Checks that CALL_KINDS contains exactly the five distinct call-kind constants. <!--#1204caf6666a045e-->
- `test_decode_still_rejects_unknown_types` (function) — Ensures decode raises ProtocolError on a genuinely unknown message type despite newly added known types. <!--#398349aec6b9786b-->
- `test_decode_tolerates_interject_without_optional_fields` (function) — Confirms a minimal interject frame carrying only the required type decodes successfully with an empty payload. <!--#2ebdd7b6b0959937-->
- `_write` (function) — Test helper that JSON-serializes a payload to a file, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#65d03e595cacafc0-->
- `test_aggregator_parses_every_call_kind` (function) — Verifies the aggregator enumerates call files of each kind and preserves enriched retry-decision fields (options/context) through to_dict serialization. <!--#fb5596513692123a-->
- `test_aggregator_legacy_call_file_without_kind` (function) — Backward-compat test that a pre-feature, metadata-less call file is parsed as a plain 'call' rather than dropped. <!--#816888c6e4addb9e-->
- `test_aggregator_unknown_kind_falls_back_to_call` (function) — Asserts both an unrecognized kind and a non-object JSON body degrade gracefully to the 'call' kind. <!--#aed450fd47b2a708-->
- `test_write_and_read_call_round_trip` (function) — Checks write_call persists kind/prompt/context/options to the expected filename and read_call returns them intact. <!--#c4957825936af17d-->
- `test_write_call_rejects_unknown_kind` (function) — Confirms write_call raises ValueError when given an invalid call kind. <!--#b2d6f3ee06a79507-->
- `test_read_call_legacy_file_defaults_kind` (function) — Verifies a kind-less call file reads back as 'call' and classify_kind agrees. <!--#eb1b544ce1d51add-->
- `test_read_call_handles_missing_and_malformed` (function) — Asserts read_call returns None for a missing file and for malformed JSON. <!--#687b30bb968163c8-->
- `test_classify_kind_defensive` (function) — Checks classify_kind defensively returns 'call' for None/empty/unknown inputs and the correct kind for valid ones. <!--#092af2612a47bc38-->
- `test_write_response_round_trip` (function) — Verifies write_response/read_response round-trip a response payload for a call, with read returning None before any response exists. <!--#c4912300dcbd4448-->
- `test_read_response_accepts_daemon_response_json` (function) — Confirms read_response also accepts the daemon client's '<stem>.response.json' sibling format. <!--#50dd437fd5042d9b-->
- `test_drain_interjection_requests_consumes_and_is_idempotent` (function) — Verifies draining queued interjection requests returns them in order and that a second drain returns nothing. <!--#a32f71b7e056faf0-->
- `test_drain_ignores_non_interjection_kinds` (function) — Asserts drain_interjection_requests returns only interjection calls, ignoring plain and retry-decision calls. <!--#b906f288ae57a804-->
- `test_drain_skips_empty_text_requests` (function) — Checks a whitespace-only interjection is silently consumed (marked served) but not returned. <!--#927ebea7703ff2f7-->
- `test_drain_missing_calls_dir_returns_empty` (function) — Confirms draining when the calls directory does not exist returns an empty list. <!--#cb65df987afe9643-->
- `test_drain_unlinks_call_file_and_writes_served_sibling` (function) — Verifies drain seals each consumed call by writing a '.response' sibling (consumed/served_by/served_at) then unlinking the call file. <!--#d16e259cffce6b1c-->
- `test_drain_returns_step_id_and_step_type_when_present` (function) — Asserts drained interjection entries surface step_id/step_type from the call context plus a created_at timestamp. <!--#b32bbc00a76a8e25-->
- `test_drain_legacy_call_without_context_step_fields_empty` (function) — Confirms legacy interjection calls lacking context step fields still drain with empty step_id/step_type. <!--#e6965d334fcce5af-->
- `test_drain_second_pass_is_idempotent_after_unlink` (function) — Verifies a second drain pass finds nothing because the first unlinked the consumed call file. <!--#37022ed4194067f0-->
- `test_write_retry_decision_call_shape` (function) — Checks write_retry_decision_call derives a step-based filename and writes the retry kind, retry/skip/abort options, and context/prompt fields. <!--#8cc0d13c846f142c-->
- `test_cli_confirm_handler_returns_answer_when_response_arrives` (function) — Tests the CLI-confirm handler returns the answer once a response file appears while the child reports alive. <!--#ed27129230cab3d0-->
- `test_cli_confirm_handler_marks_orphan_consumed_when_child_exits` (function) — Verifies the CLI-confirm handler returns None and marks the orphaned call file consumed (skipped=subprocess_exited) when the child exits before answering. <!--#cd2f283da836695c-->

### `tests/test_interjection_fast_push.py` (python) — Test suite covering the daemon's fast-push interjection pipeline — the pending-calls signature computation, change detection/debouncing, interject dispatch event wiring, and the snapshot-diff tracker that emits pending/consumed interjection_event lifecycle events to UI clients. <!--#63f0876549ae4646|39ab43ca9f266bdd-->
- `_write` (function) — Helper that JSON-serializes a payload to a file, creating parent directories first. <!--#65d03e595cacafc0-->

  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket's empty list of sent frames. <!--#b8b92aad379d234c-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Decodes and appends an outgoing frame to the recorded sent list. <!--#7d44362527b3e749-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Factory building a DaemonClient with default test arguments and overridable keyword options. <!--#6a90ceaf2230f869-->
- `test_pending_calls_signature_empty_when_no_calls_dir` (function) — Asserts the calls signature is empty when a tracked root has no se3/calls directory. <!--#8abf6c1278b51914-->
- `test_pending_calls_signature_lists_each_file_with_stat` (function) — Verifies the signature lists each calls file sorted by name with populated mtime and size. <!--#741b5b020fe5ede7-->
- `test_pending_calls_signature_changes_when_file_added` (function) — Checks that adding a calls file changes the computed signature. <!--#75d8aea778091ed1-->
- `test_pending_calls_signature_changes_when_file_removed` (function) — Checks that removing a calls file changes the computed signature. <!--#da8bf7b188e78b24-->
- `test_pending_calls_signature_skips_hidden_files` (function) — Verifies dotfiles in the calls directory are excluded from the signature. <!--#4f1b3cb57ede169c-->
- `_FakeSignatureProvider` (class) — Mutable callable test double standing in for the aggregator's pending_calls_signature provider. <!--#611bef6672883121-->
  - `_FakeSignatureProvider.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake provider's mutable signature dict to empty. <!--#18a8e68f80a604da-->
  - `_FakeSignatureProvider.__call__` (method) — Returns a copy of the provider's current signature when invoked. <!--#b26d94ff89630a64-->
- `test_calls_changed_detects_signature_delta` (function) — Verifies _calls_changed reports changes on signature deltas and debounces after observation. <!--#30addebcac22bbd9-->
- `test_calls_changed_without_provider_is_false` (function) — Asserts _calls_changed returns False when no signature provider is configured. <!--#11e465f9818d0de7-->
- `test_calls_changed_provider_failure_forces_push` (function) — Verifies a provider exception conservatively reports a change so a push still fires. <!--#0c1f599c7dd33483-->
- `test_handle_interject_sets_fast_push_event` (function) — Confirms dispatching an interject flow writes the interjection file and sets the fast-push event. <!--#561992aad93b6910-->
- `test_handle_interject_no_event_when_text_empty` (function) — Verifies empty interjection text writes no file and never wakes the push loop. <!--#76a7afc61b5fe732-->
- `test_handle_interject_no_event_when_handler_raises` (function) — Verifies a failing interject handler does not flip the fast-push event. <!--#effc51a45ec3d976-->
- `_snapshot_with_interjections` (function) — Helper building a machine snapshot whose flow contains interjection-kind pending calls for the given call ids. <!--#45b0762c4fc787ca-->
- `test_tracker_emits_pending_on_first_appearance` (function) — Asserts the tracker emits a fully-populated pending interjection_event when a chip first appears. <!--#1c053a85ee4796eb-->
- `test_tracker_emits_consumed_when_call_disappears` (function) — Verifies the tracker emits a consumed event when a previously-seen interjection chip disappears. <!--#3c8fcb655f702d66-->
- `test_tracker_does_not_double_emit_same_phase` (function) — Confirms a still-present chip produces no duplicate pending event on the next diff. <!--#c072ecf3e8a2a0eb-->
- `test_tracker_ignores_non_interjection_kinds` (function) — Verifies only interjection-kind chips, not retry/call kinds, drive the event lifecycle. <!--#931c9dd65ef9d55b-->
- `test_tracker_emits_consumed_when_flow_vanishes` (function) — Checks that a flow dropping out of the snapshot emits consumed events for its chips. <!--#76bc00172c4b9ded-->
- `test_tracker_reset_machine_replays_pending_after_reconnect` (function) — Verifies reset_machine causes still-pending chips to replay as pending after a reconnect. <!--#639c8e5c9d518b1b-->
- `test_tracker_per_machine_state_is_isolated` (function) — Confirms each machine's diff state is independent so chips don't bleed across machines. <!--#b8b114d3a2ee6315-->
- `test_status_update_broadcasts_interjection_event_to_ui_clients` (function) — End-to-end test that a daemon STATUS_UPDATE introducing an interjection chip broadcasts an interjection_event on the live /ws/ui channel. <!--#bad4be5dbea5501d-->
- `test_tracker_handles_malformed_snapshots_gracefully` (function) — Verifies the tracker returns no events and never raises on missing-key or malformed snapshot inputs. <!--#847b4a02b5780a69-->
- `test_pending_calls_signature_includes_worktree_run_calls` (function) — Confirms the fast call signature also covers call files written under a --worktree isolation run's directory. <!--#7a68a7a15ed3b2a6-->

### `tests/test_invariant_check.py` (python) — Unit tests for the INVARIANT_CHECK step, verifying its two-sided anchoring discipline: cheap no-LLM passes when there's no diff or no anchors, filtering of ungrounded nits, routing of charter/why-comment-grounded violations to fix, baseline recovery of deleted why-comments, and FAILED on unparsable LLM responses. <!--#7f8ff58df7308c97|af7782bb68ee9b16-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a feature FlowInstance with a given task description and a change_path under the test's project root. <!--#ffc7ea4176dbfbe2-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Helper that constructs an INVARIANT_CHECK Step from a given inputs dict. <!--#3e4d116d5efe7203-->
- `_install_fake_caller` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches the step's LLMCaller with a scripted fake recording prompts/call counts and returning queued responses. <!--#48f66cdee783b441-->
- `_grounded_issue` (function) — Helper that builds a well-formed issue dict citing a verbatim charter quote and evidence lines in a given file path. <!--#75be8afa7a516dbd-->
- `test_no_diff_passes_cheap_without_llm` (function) — Asserts that an invariant_check with no changed files passes as COMPLETED with skipped_reason 'no_diff' and makes no LLM call. <!--#5cc2d026d2acee1f-->
- `test_no_anchors_refuses_anchorless_check` (function) — Asserts that a diff with zero recorded anchors yields a cheap COMPLETED pass (skipped_reason 'no_anchors') rather than inventing an invariant. <!--#27e66bb91cab2036-->
- `test_ungrounded_nit_is_filtered` (function) — Asserts that an issue whose verbatim_quote is absent from the anchor pool is dropped, leaving the step COMPLETED and counting it in quote_not_in_source_count. <!--#caf367740954be0b-->
- `test_grounded_violation_routes_to_fix` (function) — Asserts that a violation quoting the charter verbatim with evidence in a changed file survives to REVISION_NEEDED with fix outputs populated. <!--#49d21b341c9eecf2-->
- `test_evidence_must_point_at_changed_file` (function) — Asserts the two-sided anchoring: a valid charter quote whose evidence path is not among the changed files is dropped and counted in bad_evidence_count. <!--#b76a319f2c06bd08-->
- `test_why_comment_anchor_is_harvested_from_changed_file` (function) — Asserts that a why-comment present in a changed file enters the anchor pool, so a violation quoting it survives to REVISION_NEEDED. <!--#1eecbca80eae666d-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand in a given working directory, raising on failure. <!--#eae0deaeea597400-->
- `test_deleted_why_comment_invariant_recovered_from_baseline` (function) — Regression test asserting that a why-comment deleted by the violating diff is still recovered from the file's baseline commit via git show, so the violation can't be laundered past the check. <!--#62caab2680afaa9e-->
- `test_unparsable_llm_response_fails` (function) — Asserts that a non-JSON LLM response makes the step return FAILED with an error message set. <!--#c00d17d5f8570232-->

### `tests/test_issue209_live_append_regression.py` (python) — Regression test suite for issue 209 that replays a captured real daemon frame sequence over fixture jsonl files to verify the live-append reader delivers records with no loss, duplication, or truncation, surfaces retries and analyze/plan appends as correct deltas, and parses the ~1 MB active engine.json at most once per content change. <!--#3a53e6a559705509|aa69f71a45017b3d-->
- `_load_fixture_lines` (function) — Helper that reads each real fixture jsonl file and returns its raw newline-kept lines keyed by file name. <!--#211d170bf7b36abd-->
- `_load_captured_frames` (function) — Helper that loads the recorded daemon frame sequence (the expected per-tick read output) from daemon_frames.json. <!--#1438223a67f62bae-->
- `_ondisk_messages` (function) — Helper that returns every on-disk fixture record in file-then-line order as the no-loss ground-truth message sequence. <!--#d97b6673519977bb-->
- `_write_active_engine` (function) — Helper that writes a RUNNING active engine.json, optionally inflated with blob steps to mimic the ~1 MB parse that starved the push loop. <!--#3bfc215376d44fef-->
- `_replay_real_frames` (function) — Helper that drives the reader through the captured tick sequence, growing the on-disk jsonl files to each frame's cursor and returning the per-tick FlowRead lists produced. <!--#9f360f95e17b879c-->
- `test_real_frame_sequence_matches_captured_daemon_frames` (function) — Test asserting that replaying the real records reproduces the captured frames' mode/record-count/cursor at every tick and that analyze/plan records surface only as a final append delta. <!--#285d1e7441ec3dfd-->
- `test_real_frame_replay_no_loss_no_dup_no_truncation` (function) — Test asserting the records delivered across all replay ticks equal, item-for-item and in order, the 20 on-disk fixture records. <!--#59eb4809ac43d4fc-->
- `test_retry_after_error_same_jsonl_append_surfaces` (function) — Test asserting that retry records appended to the same plan jsonl after a step failure surface as a fresh append delta with no re-delivery of prior records and a correctly advanced cursor. <!--#b01e474d93b89856-->
- `_count_engine_parses` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches history._parse_engine_json to count actual active-engine.json parses (the GIL-bound json.loads the fix collapses). <!--#b00a8ccdf9101f77-->
- `test_real_frame_replay_parses_active_engine_json_once_per_change` (function) — Test asserting that across the unchanged-engine.json replay the ~1 MB file is parsed at most once despite all four per-tick readers touching it each tick. <!--#1f86aee91f8e0bd9-->
- `test_active_engine_json_reparsed_on_transition_and_retry` (function) — Test asserting the content-keyed parse cache serves repeats without re-parsing but re-parses when a genuine engine.json rewrite (transition/retry) changes the content, avoiding stale state. <!--#70d262a1d58807db-->

### `tests/test_issue_209_push_starvation.py` (python) — Regression lock for issue #209 (daemon push-loop starvation): tests verifying that the active engine.json is parsed at most once per actual change via an (mtime, size) parse cache shared across per-tick readers, while discovery→analyze transitions and post-error retries still stream incrementally and correctly. <!--#4e6b9d735adcea99|b7392309b695ff4e-->
- `_write_engine` (function) — Test helper that writes a flow's se3/state/engine.json, optionally padding it with many blob steps to mimic a ~1 MB long-running flow. <!--#e6104cc936b40ae9-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Test helper that writes a per-step history jsonl file containing n simple assistant-message records. <!--#bb20aacf8e3df4bc-->
- `_count_engine_parses` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches history._parse_engine_json to count actual engine.json parses, returning a mutable counter dict. <!--#1ade3412b46169de-->
- `test_active_engine_json_parsed_once_per_change_across_readers` (function) — Test asserting the active engine.json is parsed at most once across 10 unchanged ticks driving all four per-tick readers (the starvation regression lock). <!--#f8a6d13239e9ae5e-->
- `test_active_engine_json_reparsed_after_change` (function) — Test asserting the stat-keyed parse cache serves unchanged reads but re-parses once when engine.json is genuinely rewritten. <!--#4f8b51caff277baf-->
- `test_discovery_to_analyze_transition_surfaces_via_read_active_flows` (function) — Correctness test asserting the discovery→analyze new-step append still streams incrementally as an append-mode delta with the parse cache enabled. <!--#fc4a182050c46166-->
- `test_retry_after_error_append_surfaces_via_read_active_flows` (function) — Correctness test asserting retry records appended to the same step's jsonl still surface incrementally with the parse cache enabled. <!--#31f65854c7ea14aa-->

### `tests/test_llm_caller_stream_progress_chip.py` (python) — Pytest suite for StreamJSONTracker's single-chip stream_progress protocol, verifying each tool call emits exactly an in-flight chip and a terminal chip with the correct is_error flag and structured tool_detail payload (read_text, edit_diff, bash_output), that emoji CLI stdout lines are preserved, and that narrative-text progress records stay byte-identical to the legacy jsonl schema while new chip fields round-trip when provided. <!--#5bc2a231f430a845|221fa544b849b6f5-->

- `_tool_records` (function) — Test helper that filters captured records down to only those carrying a tool_use_id, dropping narrative text progress entries. <!--#858f4e18f023e307-->
- `test_read_success_emits_in_flight_and_terminal` (function) — Test asserting a successful Read produces an in-flight chip (no is_error/tool_detail) and a terminal '[Read ✓' chip with a read_text detail payload including file_path, start_line, and text. <!--#0de6e67ca0273f62-->
- `test_edit_success_terminal_has_edit_diff_detail_with_hunk_start` (function) — Test asserting a successful Edit yields an in-flight '[Edit' chip plus a terminal '[Edit ✓' chip carrying an edit_diff detail with parsed hunk start line numbers and a '@@' diff. <!--#3c04faf806769ee2-->
- `test_bash_failure_emits_terminal_with_is_error_true` (function) — Test asserting a failed Bash command produces a terminal '[Bash ✗' chip with is_error True and a bash_output detail echoing the command. <!--#116e96fdb40405e1-->
- `test_cli_stdout_emoji_lines_preserved` (function) — Test verifying the tracker prints emoji-prefixed CLI stdout lines ('🔧 Read:' on start and '✅ Read' on completion) to stdout. <!--#128ea4fd4ce8fdba-->
- `test_narrative_text_progress_jsonl_byte_identical_to_legacy` (function) — Test asserting a narrative-text progress write produces a jsonl record whose key set exactly matches the pre-extension legacy schema with no extra chip keys leaking through. <!--#abcc6d2644f83b03-->
- `test_record_stream_progress_writes_new_chip_fields_when_provided` (function) — Test asserting that when tool_use_id, is_error, and tool_detail are passed, they round-trip into the jsonl record for the daemon reader to forward to the frontend. <!--#8e517db2a718def9-->

### `tests/test_llm_trace_fsync_batching.py` (python) — Test module verifying the merge LLMTrace writer batches/throttles fsync (no per-record fsync, but forced fsync on threshold, stop/__exit__, and rotation) while keeping the jsonl stream complete and readable, plus a leaf-merge guard that fails diagnosably on a missing target branch ref and merges cleanly when it exists. <!--#e7bdfb543696079f|7e2a479aae727a88-->
- `fsync_counter` (function) — Pytest fixture that monkeypatches os.fsync in the llm_trace module with a no-op recorder so tests can count when fsync is invoked. <!--#2f60a6b8c6fdac6f-->
- `TestFsyncThrottling` (class) — Test class asserting LLMTrace fsyncs on count/interval thresholds, on stop/rotation, and per-record when disabled, rather than on every write. <!--#9297bb467922118d-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_no_fsync_under_thresholds` (method) — Asserts no fsync fires while records are written when both the count and time thresholds remain unmet. <!--#8b61fdce063fcfe3-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_fsync_fires_every_n_records` (method) — Asserts fsync fires exactly once per N records, with the batch counter resetting after each flush. <!--#d3743d17c52837f8-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_per_record_fsync_when_every_n_nonpositive` (method) — Asserts a non-positive fsync_every_n restores per-record fsync semantics. <!--#1caa0572e1f01e50-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_stop_forces_tail_fsync` (method) — Asserts stop/__exit__ fsyncs the tail even when the batch threshold was never reached, ensuring trailing records are durable. <!--#a7cdebb1b46dea89-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_rotation_forces_fsync` (method) — Asserts a file rotation fsyncs and completes the rotated-out file before opening the next one. <!--#bf371111c88e3a1d-->
- `TestRecordsRemainComplete` (class) — Test class verifying every record stays flushed, ordered, and readable even when fsync is throttled away until close. <!--#7d1bf62947363aa6-->
  - `TestRecordsRemainComplete.test_no_tail_loss_with_batched_fsync` (method) — Asserts all 50 records are written in sequence with the tail intact despite fsync being throttled to never fire mid-run. <!--#ee1914f3fb80b1cb-->
  - `TestRecordsRemainComplete.test_records_readable_mid_run_before_fsync` (method) — Asserts a record is readable from the file before any fsync occurs because each line is flushed to the OS page cache. <!--#bb6828f14f0646b6-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo path and returns the completed process. <!--#9bef257c44286ed8-->
- `repo` (function) — Pytest fixture that initializes a fresh git repo with an initial commit on the main branch. <!--#d27143b094612b5a-->
- `TestLeafMergeRefValidation` (class) — Test class verifying the leaf-merge guard fails diagnosably on a missing target ref and proceeds to a clean merge when the ref exists. <!--#59a13e887901aa84-->
  - `TestLeafMergeRefValidation.test_missing_ref_fails_safely` (method) — Asserts a non-existent leaf branch ref returns False with a diagnosable log and no leftover MERGE_HEAD before any merge is attempted. <!--#1ec994f08480c7d3-->
  - `TestLeafMergeRefValidation.test_existing_ref_proceeds_to_merge` (method) — Asserts that when the leaf ref exists the guard passes and a non-conflicting merge succeeds, bringing in the new file. <!--#a8aee8f187e14f3a-->

### `tests/test_merge_conflict_resolver.py` (python) — Unit and integration tests for the merge-conflict resolution stack, exercising StrategyDecider across SAFE/STRICT/FAST strategies, HumanCallWriter's call-file generation, and ConflictResolver end-to-end against real conflicted git repos with mocked LLM resolutions. <!--#1b7b18054c5fb876|584e22325e51db91-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo path and returns the completed process. <!--#8dcfd7712386df15-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Helper that initializes a fresh git repo at a path with test user identity configured. <!--#63bfb3f5ba420316-->
- `_commit` (function) — Helper that stages all changes and creates a commit with the given message in a repo. <!--#af29a90485ca5f27-->
- `_current_branch` (function) — Helper returning the current branch name of a repo via git rev-parse. <!--#95be0c69f317516b-->
- `_setup_conflict` (function) — Helper that builds a two-branch repo with a deliberate single-file merge conflict and returns the ours/theirs branch names. <!--#287f770ecdb793e4-->
- `_make_resolution` (function) — Factory that constructs a mock LLMResolution with configurable confidence levels, flags, and spec status for decider tests. <!--#3ac59ed3ebce187f-->
- `TestStrategyDeciderDefault` (class) — Test class verifying StrategyDecider behavior under the SAFE strategy, where only explicit flags (not confidence) trigger human calls. <!--#adb39027ee00684f-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderDefault.test_default_high_confidence_no_flags_accept` (method) — Asserts a high-confidence flag-free resolution is accepted under SAFE strategy. <!--#f67265804535fa3e-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderDefault.test_default_low_overall_confidence_accepted_without_flags` (method) — Asserts SAFE strategy accepts low overall confidence when no flags are set, treating confidence as informational. <!--#102029147f0c2852-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderDefault.test_default_requires_human_review_flag_human_call` (method) — Asserts the requires_human_review flag routes a SAFE-strategy resolution to HUMAN_CALL with a matching reason. <!--#98774beb3a154e0c-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderDefault.test_default_spec_guardrail_concern_human_call` (method) — Asserts the spec_guardrail_concern flag routes a SAFE-strategy resolution to HUMAN_CALL. <!--#a6828817ba5a5e2d-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderDefault.test_default_per_file_flag_human_call` (method) — Asserts a per-file requires_human_review flag triggers HUMAN_CALL even when global flags are clear. <!--#3288bdf3dd838298-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderDefault.test_default_medium_hunk_high_overall_accept` (method) — Asserts SAFE strategy accepts when hunks are MEDIUM but file/global confidence is HIGH. <!--#6939a188e5235042-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderDefault.test_default_low_file_overall_accepted_without_flags` (method) — Asserts SAFE strategy ignores a file-level LOW confidence rating absent any flags and still accepts. <!--#917854ef19a05c5a-->
- `TestStrategyDeciderStrict` (class) — Test class verifying StrategyDecider's STRICT strategy, which gates on confidence levels at hunk, file, and global scope. <!--#7d25c98226779196-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderStrict.test_strict_all_high_accept` (method) — Asserts STRICT strategy accepts when all confidence levels are HIGH. <!--#dabb56429791025d-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderStrict.test_strict_low_hunk_human_call` (method) — Asserts STRICT strategy routes a LOW-confidence hunk to HUMAN_CALL. <!--#5c0fd2116c61a604-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderStrict.test_strict_low_file_overall_human_call` (method) — Asserts STRICT strategy routes a non-HIGH file-level confidence to HUMAN_CALL. <!--#aad7dc7c415abffb-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderStrict.test_strict_low_global_overall_human_call` (method) — Asserts STRICT strategy routes a non-HIGH global confidence to HUMAN_CALL. <!--#deb8e0e59df05b87-->
- `TestStrategyDeciderFast` (class) — Test class verifying StrategyDecider's FAST strategy, which accepts regular files freely but aborts (REJECTs) on problematic spec files. <!--#1c7daf9474b50f40-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderFast.test_fast_regular_low_confidence_accept` (method) — Asserts FAST strategy accepts a low-confidence non-spec resolution. <!--#a966170cd45efddc-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderFast.test_fast_spec_guardrail_concern_accept` (method) — Asserts FAST strategy defers spec_guardrail_concern to post-merge guardrails and accepts. <!--#4e4f3fddfa25f3d3-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderFast.test_fast_spec_low_confidence_reject` (method) — Asserts FAST strategy REJECTs (aborts without human call) on a low-confidence spec file. <!--#19f5b9b92ff9d29c-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderFast.test_fast_spec_requires_human_review_reject` (method) — Asserts FAST strategy REJECTs (aborts) when a spec file carries requires_human_review. <!--#03d6518767ce3b4f-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderFast.test_fast_mixed_regular_and_spec_accept` (method) — Asserts FAST strategy accepts a mix of a low-confidence regular file and a high-confidence spec file. <!--#163350801be8b1bd-->
- `TestHumanCallWriter` (class) — Test class verifying HumanCallWriter's generation of merge-conflict and guardrail human-call JSON files and their printed instructions. <!--#07c8b036c91ca1fa-->
  - `TestHumanCallWriter.test_call_file_created` (method) — Asserts write_call produces a merge_conflict call file with expected metadata, options, and file entries. <!--#0c82efcc266490f1-->
  - `TestHumanCallWriter.test_call_file_prefix_distinguishes_from_merge_conflict` (method) — Asserts call files use a 'merge_' prefix distinct from legacy 'merge_conflict_' loop-mode files. <!--#e77dfac4746f413d-->
  - `TestHumanCallWriter.test_guardrail_call_instructions_differ_for_stalled_type` (method) — Asserts guardrail_repair_stalled call files include LLM-repair-attempt wording absent from standard violation calls. <!--#113195686658a997-->
  - `TestHumanCallWriter.test_print_instructions_no_evidence_shows_header` (method) — Asserts print_instructions still shows violation type, file, and message when no evidence is present. <!--#bae5fe8f9cf37864-->
  - `TestHumanCallWriter.test_print_instructions_many_violations_trailing_once` (method) — Asserts print_instructions prints the '... and N more' trailing summary exactly once for 3+ violations. <!--#179c0d10d457dd37-->
- `TestResolverStrategyIntegration` (class) — Test class exercising ConflictResolver plus StrategyDecider end-to-end against a real conflicted repo with a mocked LLM resolution. <!--#93f97a2eb197c61c-->
  - `TestResolverStrategyIntegration.test_end_to_end_mock_llm_high_confidence_accept` (method) — Asserts a full flow with a high-confidence mock resolution yields ACCEPT under SAFE strategy. <!--#dbfe5fe5c424e58f-->
  - `TestResolverStrategyIntegration.test_end_to_end_mock_llm_review_flag_human_call` (method) — Asserts a review-flagged mock resolution routes to HUMAN_CALL regardless of confidence under SAFE strategy. <!--#59cd9d601cb2eaed-->

### `tests/test_merge_context.py` (python) — Test suite for the merge-conflict context builder, covering its pure helpers (_is_spec_path, _looks_binary, _parse_hunks) and integration tests of build() against real git repos with single/multiple conflicting files, spec, and binary cases to verify it captures three-way contents, hunk line numbers, merge metadata, and spec/binary flags. <!--#32c1f2419791476e|a84b6b1d991d8baf-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo path and returns the completed process. <!--#8dcfd7712386df15-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Helper that initializes a fresh git repo at a path and sets a test user identity. <!--#63bfb3f5ba420316-->
- `_commit` (function) — Helper that stages all changes and commits them with a given message in a repo. <!--#af29a90485ca5f27-->
- `_current_branch` (function) — Helper that returns the current branch name of a repo. <!--#95be0c69f317516b-->
- `_setup_basic_conflict` (function) — Fixture helper that builds a repo with diverging ours/theirs branches and leaves a single-file conflicting merge in progress for build() to inspect. <!--#71a3e5e2647572f2-->
- `TestPureHelpers` (class) — Test class for the pure helper functions (_is_spec_path, _looks_binary, _parse_hunks) with no git dependency. <!--#45e05022d85507b1-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_is_spec_path_matches_spec_md` (method) — Asserts _is_spec_path returns True for spec.md files nested under se3/specs/<dir>/. <!--#cd6cf4ec8d81dbec-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_is_spec_path_rejects_non_spec` (method) — Asserts _is_spec_path returns False for non-spec files and spec.md files lacking the required directory nesting. <!--#5a7b4f78e45c1c54-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_looks_binary_detects_null_bytes` (method) — Asserts _looks_binary flags content with null bytes as binary and treats text/empty content as non-binary. <!--#b7e2376753e448e0-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_parse_hunks_single_hunk` (method) — Asserts _parse_hunks finds one conflict hunk and records its correct start/end line numbers. <!--#eb0d38928f821a93-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_parse_hunks_multiple_hunks` (method) — Asserts _parse_hunks identifies two separate conflict hunks and their respective line ranges. <!--#054688e471a73d3b-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_parse_hunks_diff3_marker_inside` (method) — Asserts _parse_hunks treats a diff3-style conflict (with base marker) as a single hunk spanning all markers. <!--#00704608e20b65c6-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_parse_hunks_no_markers` (method) — Asserts _parse_hunks returns an empty list when text contains no conflict markers. <!--#ac1d9924663757cf-->
- `TestBuildSingleFileSingleHunk` (class) — Integration test class exercising build() against a real repo with one conflicting file and one hunk. <!--#8d7a4c95a9f0fe37-->
  - `TestBuildSingleFileSingleHunk.test_three_way_contents_non_empty` (method) — Verifies build() captures base/ours/theirs/working contents, conflict markers, and binary/spec flags for a single conflicting file. <!--#c6e2fae734123963-->
  - `TestBuildSingleFileSingleHunk.test_hunk_line_numbers_recorded` (method) — Verifies build() records hunk line numbers that map to the actual conflict marker lines in the working content. <!--#28eb90cf322331f3-->
  - `TestBuildSingleFileSingleHunk.test_merge_metadata_populated` (method) — Verifies build() populates merge metadata such as branch names, merge base, head SHAs, and commit messages. <!--#7e2a48339f44dd0a-->
  - `TestBuildSingleFileSingleHunk.test_oneline_logs_collected` (method) — Verifies build() collects per-branch oneline commit logs containing the expected commit messages. <!--#11ef98ddc0cfc024-->
- `TestBuildSpecFile` (class) — Integration test class verifying build() correctly flags conflicting spec.md files as spec files. <!--#c2a983bfd28cdc64-->
  - `TestBuildSpecFile.test_spec_md_path_marked_is_spec` (method) — Verifies a conflicting se3/specs/.../spec.md file is marked is_spec and sets the context's has_spec_files flag. <!--#2d9d1551f24c6239-->
- `TestBuildBinaryFile` (class) — Integration test class verifying build() correctly handles binary file conflicts. <!--#f155e81294578ae3-->
  - `TestBuildBinaryFile.test_binary_conflict_marked_is_binary` (method) — Verifies a conflicting binary file is marked is_binary with no parsed hunks. <!--#f24dd050e0181d17-->
- `TestBuildMultipleFilesMultipleHunks` (class) — Integration test class verifying build() across multiple conflicting files with multiple hunks. <!--#f21b5e4000c2ba8a-->

- `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation` (class) — Test class covering end-to-end `execute()` routing in fast mode for stall, exhaustion, success, missing-SHA, call-file-write failure, and rollback-failure outcomes. <!--#db4554ef1b9eaff3-->

  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_hash_changes_exhausts_to_human_call` (method) — Verifies that oscillating hashes through `execute()` exhaust max iterations and escalate to a human call with failure_reason 'guardrail_repair_exhausted'. <!--#723dd63491ef21d4-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_missing_post_sha_fast_raises_guardrail_repair_failed` (method) — Verifies that a missing post_sha in fast mode raises GuardrailRepairFailed with GUARDRAIL_MISSING_POST_SHA and leaves HEAD unchanged. <!--#8355e5a8d2d6e39a-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_missing_pre_sha_fast_raises_guardrail_repair_failed` (method) — Verifies that a missing pre_sha in fast mode raises GuardrailRepairFailed with GUARDRAIL_MISSING_PRE_SHA and attempts no rollback. <!--#3db656da78abcb3a-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_missing_both_shas_fast_raises_guardrail_repair_failed` (method) — Verifies that both SHAs missing in fast mode raises GuardrailRepairFailed with GUARDRAIL_MISSING_PRE_AND_POST_SHA. <!--#dd55c219cecc9a2a-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_repair_success_no_violation` (method) — Verifies that a successful fast-mode repair through `execute()` produces a successful report listing the merged branch with no pending human call and an advanced HEAD. <!--#9a145eaf97f1a543-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_stalled_call_file_write_fails_aborts` (method) — Verifies that when a stalled repair's call-file write fails, `execute()` aborts with 'guardrail_repair_stalled_call_failed', no human call, and restored HEAD. <!--#108acb34bea19807-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_stalled_call_file_keyboard_interrupt_propagates` (method) — Verifies that a KeyboardInterrupt during stalled call-file write propagates uncaught while the working tree is already rolled back. <!--#cb2a7c7c5fcf6bbb-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_max_iterations_exhausted_escalates_to_human` (method) — Verifies that novel-hash exhaustion through `execute()` escalates to a human call (not an outright abort) with an exhausted-type call file and restored HEAD. <!--#82d2e7c76a467c93-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_exhausted_call_file_write_fails_aborts` (method) — Verifies that when an exhausted repair's call-file write fails, `execute()` aborts with 'guardrail_repair_exhausted_call_failed', no human call, and restored HEAD. <!--#a288838286a9b23f-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_stalled_rollback_fails_sets_rollback_failed` (method) — Verifies that a stalled repair whose rollback fails sets rollback_failed with failure_reason 'rollback_failed' while still surfacing a diagnostic human-call file. <!--#3ba4dea300241941-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_exhausted_rollback_fails_sets_rollback_failed` (method) — Verifies that an exhausted repair whose rollback fails sets rollback_failed with failure_reason 'rollback_failed' while still surfacing a diagnostic exhausted-type call file. <!--#8194aded3f64561f-->
- `TestMaxRepairIterationsClamp` (class) — Regression test class pinning the orchestrator's defense-in-depth clamp of `_max_repair_iterations` to at least one so the repair for-loop body always runs. <!--#78b60e43e42258bf-->
  - `TestMaxRepairIterationsClamp.test_orchestrator_clamps_loader_returning_zero` (method) — Verifies the orchestrator re-clamps a loader-returned 0 up to the positive module default for `_max_repair_iterations`. <!--#10a3e595f88621bb-->

### `tests/test_merge_respond.py` (python) — Unit tests for the se3 merge-respond command (process_merge_response), covering call/response file validation, choice handling (accept/abort/manual), the critical strict-mode sentinel safety check that blocks placeholder content from being written, merge commit/rollback and guardrail behavior, main-worktree lock targeting, and path/parent helpers like _first_parent_sha and _is_spec_path. <!--#8026d473575b7ff3|1dad9bbb004b9cb4-->

### `tests/test_merge_robust_cleanup.py` (python) — Tests for the `--delete-merged` archive-before-delete behavior, verifying both the low-level `_archive_worktree` helper (tracked/untracked capture, .git exclusion, collision suffixing) and the full `CleanupManager.delete_merged_branches` integration that archives a worktree into the ignored `se3/worktrees/.archive` runtime root before destroying it, preserving the worktree and branch on archive failure. <!--#dc14f7d6435f5fab|9fd431f10c54660a-->

  - `TestArchiveWorktreeHelper.test_archive_copies_tracked_and_untracked_excludes_dot_git` (method) — Asserts the archive lands in se3/worktrees/.archive, captures tracked and untracked files, excludes .git, and writes parseable metadata. <!--#af896e0ea9e75d31-->
  - `TestArchiveWorktreeHelper.test_archive_collision_appends_seq_suffix` (method) — Verifies that a same-timestamp archive collision is resolved by appending a numeric sequence suffix to produce a distinct archive path. <!--#107708e52ea3d936-->
- `TestCleanupArchiveIntegration` (class) — Test class exercising the full `CleanupManager.delete_merged_branches` path to confirm archiving is integrated with worktree/branch destruction. <!--#6fec246fd02c2628-->
  - `TestCleanupArchiveIntegration.test_delete_merged_archives_before_destroying` (method) — Confirms deleting a merged branch archives its worktree (into the ignored runtime root) before removing the worktree and branch. <!--#ed5a93a71f5667e8-->
  - `TestCleanupArchiveIntegration.test_archive_failure_preserves_worktree_and_branch` (method) — Confirms that when archiving fails (mocked copytree error), the branch and worktree are preserved and the failure is recorded in skipped_archive_failed. <!--#83e7d7d5aa1bc72f-->
  - `TestCleanupArchiveIntegration.test_delete_without_worktree_skips_archive_cleanly` (method) — Confirms a merged branch with no bound worktree is deleted cleanly with no archive entry and no archive-failure entry. <!--#4e90fd5e0250b85b-->
- `TestCleanupReportFields` (class) — Test class checking that the CleanupReport dataclass exposes the new archive-tracking fields. <!--#2e304771abce3c6f-->

### `tests/test_merge_strategy_consolidation.py` (python) — A pytest module verifying merge-strategy behavior end-to-end: safe mode escalates to a human after exhausting LLM iterations, strict mode skips the LLM entirely, 'fast' is the default strategy for both run_merge and the CLI, and legacy strategy names ('robust', 'default') are rejected by both MergeStrategy.from_str and the CLI; includes git/repo/conflict-file/BatchContext fixture helpers. <!--#c84e169ac35515f6|dc1e0c223b3b838a-->

- `test_safe_exhausts_iterations_escalates_to_human` (function) — Verifies that safe mode, when the LLM never clears markers, escalates to a human call after exhausting iterations while preserving conflict markers on disk. <!--#1d6e43bbb56f484b-->
- `test_strict_skips_llm_and_routes_to_human` (function) — Verifies that strict mode routes conflicts directly to a human call without ever invoking the LLM (zero iterations). <!--#19198f079fd16273-->

- `test_legacy_robust_strategy_name_rejected` (function) — Asserts that `MergeStrategy.from_str('robust')` raises ValueError mentioning the legacy name and the 'fast' replacement. <!--#c4b9add2aba39870-->
- `test_legacy_default_strategy_name_rejected` (function) — Asserts that `MergeStrategy.from_str('default')` raises ValueError mentioning the legacy name and the 'safe' replacement. <!--#8cef9c1bf92e2003-->
- `test_cli_rejects_robust_strategy` (function) — CLI test confirming `--strategy robust` fails fast with a non-zero exit and never invokes run_merge. <!--#1973cd073c1ba355-->
- `test_cli_rejects_default_strategy` (function) — CLI test confirming `--strategy default` fails fast with a non-zero exit and never invokes run_merge. <!--#821ebd3e1ef21f88-->

### `tests/test_merge_unlock.py` (python) — Unit and CLI test suite for the merge-lock subsystem, verifying that inspect_lock correctly classifies missing/alive/dead/empty/corrupt locks read-only, that break_lock_file and release_merge_lock handle stale (dead-PID, holderless, corrupt), live (refuse without --force, release with), and unlink-denied (failed_remove) cases, and that the se3 merge-unlock CLI reports the right outcomes and exit codes for each. <!--#9842c412b9f52ed2|c4bcaa327c7c11d4-->
- `_lock_path` (function) — Helper returning the absolute merge-lock file path (`se3/state/merge.lock`) under a given project root. <!--#db4c4674fe3e9a27-->
- `_write_lock` (function) — Helper that creates the lock file with the given body content and returns its path. <!--#4a20343d55e0ce24-->
- `_dead_pid` (function) — Helper that scans downward from a large number to find a PID confirmed non-existent via `os.kill(pid, 0)` raising ESRCH. <!--#fde38f4d452aeeab-->
- `test_inspect_lock_missing_file` (function) — Asserts `inspect_lock` reports a missing lock as non-existent, holderless, and reclaimable (stale). <!--#8a000da44494f371-->
- `test_inspect_lock_alive_holder` (function) — Asserts `inspect_lock` recognizes a lock held by the live current process as alive and not stale. <!--#06604a0f76c53a6c-->
- `test_inspect_lock_dead_holder` (function) — Asserts `inspect_lock` treats a lock owned by a dead PID as not-alive and stale. <!--#3ea9cee0acd1c667-->
- `test_inspect_lock_empty_file_is_stale` (function) — Asserts an empty lock file is reported as existing but holderless and stale. <!--#9ceaee7d60ac0c2e-->
- `test_inspect_lock_corrupt_record` (function) — Asserts a non-numeric lock body is reported as corrupt, holderless, and stale. <!--#145a85cf4fabd8fd-->
- `test_inspect_lock_does_not_write` (function) — Asserts `inspect_lock` is read-only by verifying the lock file bytes are unchanged after inspection. <!--#f6c84c8238682557-->
- `test_break_lock_file_removes_existing` (function) — Asserts `break_lock_file` deletes an existing lock and returns True. <!--#774a993f5bfb8c9c-->
- `test_break_lock_file_noop_when_absent` (function) — Asserts `break_lock_file` returns False and is a no-op when no lock exists. <!--#0fffa971484c7f9c-->
- `test_release_no_lock` (function) — Asserts `release_merge_lock` returns the `no_lock` outcome with exit code 0 when no lock is present. <!--#da7f3c75b57e39e8-->
- `test_release_stale_dead_pid` (function) — Asserts a stale lock held by a dead PID is released (`released_stale`) without requiring `--force`. <!--#b7dc02044944394d-->
- `test_release_stale_no_pid` (function) — Asserts an empty (holderless) lock is released as stale without force. <!--#b6ad97ef2781937f-->
- `test_release_stale_corrupt` (function) — Asserts a corrupt lock record is released as stale, with the outcome flagging corruption. <!--#795092016b95b8d9-->
- `test_release_refused_when_alive_without_force` (function) — Asserts release is refused (`refused_alive`, nonzero exit, lock preserved) when a live process holds the lock and `--force` is absent. <!--#ecaf17f195d49934-->
- `test_release_force_removes_live_lock` (function) — Asserts `--force` releases a lock held by a live process, yielding `released_force` and removing the file. <!--#219aa438c6f6b448-->
- `_make_unremovable` (function) — Helper that strips write permission from the lock's parent directory so unlinking the file raises PermissionError. <!--#ff724d541bbdd637-->
- `_restore` (function) — Helper that restores normal (0o700) permissions on the lock's parent directory after an unremovable-file test. <!--#b369467d8e93b67e-->
- `test_release_stale_failed_remove_when_unlink_denied` (function) — Asserts a stale lock that cannot be unlinked yields `failed_remove`, nonzero exit, and the file remaining on disk. <!--#0d36005306b6a72c-->
- `test_release_force_failed_remove_when_unlink_denied` (function) — Asserts a forced release whose unlink is denied yields `failed_remove`, nonzero exit, and the file remaining. <!--#5840a05f6d4c480b-->
- `cli_project` (function) — Fixture that monkeypatches `get_project_root` to point the CLI at `tmp_path`. <!--#cb249ba1ae611144-->
- `_run` (function) — Helper that invokes the `se3` Typer app with given args via CliRunner and returns the result. <!--#23b50511ac6e6535-->
- `_flat` (function) — Helper that collapses rich-rendered newlines and spaces so output can be substring-matched. <!--#3f2ff121b29cf474-->
- `test_cli_no_lock_reports_and_exits_zero` (function) — Asserts the CLI reports no lock to release and exits 0 when none exists. <!--#4ba317c686c41159-->
- `test_cli_refuses_live_holder` (function) — Asserts the CLI refuses (nonzero exit) a live-held lock, printing the holder PID and a `--force` hint while preserving the file. <!--#f007af9f69db8fe7-->
- `test_cli_force_flag_releases_live_holder` (function) — Asserts `merge-unlock --force` releases a live-held lock, prints a WARNING, and removes the file. <!--#8dd64165bd391644-->
- `test_cli_short_force_flag` (function) — Asserts the short `-f` flag behaves like `--force` in releasing a live-held lock. <!--#b8716ef7108d0ab2-->
- `test_cli_stale_cleanup_without_force` (function) — Asserts the CLI cleans up a stale (dead-PID) lock without force, reporting "Released stale" and exiting 0. <!--#3a6792b68e9bccc2-->
- `test_cli_failed_remove_reports_error_and_nonzero` (function) — Asserts that when a stale lock cannot be unlinked, the CLI reports an ERROR, exits nonzero, and does not falsely claim the lock was released. <!--#f576f5430fb87325-->

### `tests/test_merge_version_aggregator.py` (python) — Unit tests for the merge version aggregator, covering max_bump selection, _diff_bump SemVer precedence rules (prerelease/build-metadata), the InferResult dataclass, infer_branch_bump's end-to-end pyproject version-diff inference per branch, and aggregate_and_apply's bump aggregation with version writing, commit amending, and failure handling, supported by git/pyproject test helpers. <!--#c25334796f6868e7|9025a32a8658039c-->

### `tests/test_migrate.py` (python) — Test suite for the `se3 migrate` command and its first spec-to-new-system migrator, covering the migrator registry (register/list/get with duplicate rejection), CLI wiring of the `migrate` sub-app, and the fault-tolerant migration pipeline that writes the charter exactly once, injects colocated why-comments, builds the authoritative code-index, deletes salvaged specs only after success, and idempotently rewrites .gitignore with root-deny whitelists that protect tracked top-level paths. <!--#6ff5fef47d2e581b|4ef8b1d225aebcd4-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand in the given project root, raising on failure. <!--#881bf8d1b379498d-->
- `_init_git_project` (function) — Helper that initializes a git repo with a test user identity in the given root. <!--#6aabffa4b0cbf3dc-->
- `FakeSummarizer` (class) — Deterministic stand-in code-index summarizer that maps each target to a fixed `S:<name>` string instead of calling the LLM. <!--#35adba97abbabfe3-->
  - `FakeSummarizer.__call__` (method) — Returns a dict mapping each target's id to a deterministic `S:<name>` summary. <!--#1d61334eb28ddb92-->
- `_make_salvager` (function) — Factory returning a fake salvager callable that ignores its input and yields a fixed `SalvageResult` (charter body + colocations). <!--#59b18ab05a11927b-->
- `project` (function) — Pytest fixture building a committed git project with base/non-base/changelog specs, one source file, and a baseline .gitignore. <!--#5ae2f30166d70517-->
- `test_registry_has_first_migrator` (function) — Asserts the `spec-to-new-system` migrator is registered and bound to `run_spec_to_new_system`. <!--#cd2233b643f97a14-->
- `test_registry_register_and_duplicate_rejection` (function) — Verifies migrators can be registered and that re-registering a duplicate id raises `ValueError`. <!--#c9c23b945b202a87-->
- `test_list_migrators_sorted` (function) — Asserts `list_migrators` returns migrators ordered by id. <!--#a17aab8ec2db6e4a-->
- `test_cli_registers_migrate` (function) — Checks that a `migrate` sub-app is wired into the main CLI's registered groups. <!--#c1033f71af03974e-->
- `test_migrate_list_command_runs` (function) — Asserts `se3 migrate list` exits cleanly and lists the `spec-to-new-system` migrator. <!--#8f51c77c8e15f79b-->
- `test_migrate_run_unknown_id_errors` (function) — Asserts `se3 migrate run` with an unknown migrator id exits with code 1. <!--#880bbbdf3d97f7df-->
- `test_full_migration_happy_path` (function) — End-to-end test asserting that a full spec-to-new-system migration writes the charter, injects colocated why-comments into source (keeping it parseable), builds the authoritative code-index.md with no JSON sidecar, deletes the salvaged specs, and rewrites .gitignore accordingly. <!--#584a226c5fd5333f-->

### `tests/test_protocol_history.py` (python) — Unit tests for the session protocol's version-2 message constructors, exercising registration/direction tables and encode/decode round-trips for history index/data/request, spawn-flow (discover and resume), and issue-command messages, plus error handling for bad modes and unknown types. <!--#1a14ef6b8dd5df3d|91d0c8cb625739a3-->

- `test_history_index_request_type_registered` (function) — Checks the history-index-request type is server-to-daemon only and never sent back to the server. <!--#fe65f847ae6110c0-->
- `test_make_history_index_request_round_trip` (function) — Confirms make_history_index_request produces an empty-payload re-push trigger that survives encode/decode. <!--#ef2bd936d51d230e-->

- `test_make_history_request_with_cursor` (function) — Verifies make_history_request preserves a per-stage byte-offset cursor through the round-trip. <!--#f67024e99736f136-->

- `test_make_history_data_append_with_cursor` (function) — Confirms make_history_data in APPEND mode round-trips records, the advancing cursor, and the seq number. <!--#f5bca4b43def2be4-->
- `test_make_history_data_rejects_bad_mode` (function) — Asserts make_history_data raises ProtocolError when given an invalid history mode. <!--#eb6b0938307aedd1-->
- `test_decode_unknown_type_raises_protocol_error` (function) — Asserts decode rejects an unrecognized message type with ProtocolError rather than crashing. <!--#6460f879cf60220a-->
- `test_decode_unknown_type_is_catchable` (function) — Shows known frames decode while unknown ones raise a catchable ProtocolError, enabling forward/backward peer tolerance. <!--#4c2d88e7a8fada6b-->
- `test_make_spawn_flow_discover_defaults_false` (function) — Verifies make_spawn_flow sets the discover field to False by default and round-trips it. <!--#4b85f3c1b0ebd829-->

- `test_make_issue_command_edit_round_trip` (function) — Confirms make_issue_command for an edit operation round-trips issue_id and description while omitting empty fields. <!--#020423f3b51e05dd-->
- `test_make_issue_command_close_with_reason` (function) — Confirms make_issue_command for a close operation round-trips the issue_id and close reason. <!--#b25a1f484512a702-->

### `tests/test_read_only_injection.py` (python) — Unit test module verifying the read-only step mechanism end-to-end: that every STEP_POOL entry carries a correct read_only flag, that get_read_only_injection()/is_step_read_only correctly classify analysis steps (discovery/analyze/plan, sync_scan/sync_analyze, pure-data code_index/migrate) as read-only versus mutating steps (implement/commit/sync_resolve), and that LLMCaller.call() injects the READ-ONLY constraint text into prompts across strict and two-phase JSON modes. <!--#f109b9f74917c1a1|979bc3b9c9459164-->
